<a id="c231"></a>
### C231 — Audit the funnel per market and per channel — storefronts diverge on billing and funnel stage, not on the product, and written reviews are a complaint channel that under-rates it against public ratings

**Certain** · 42 apps · 302 cards · positive in 11 apps · negative in 19 apps · tied to a purchase in 1 apps

*Why Certain:* 42 apps, same direction (unresolved, 75%), 19 reports label it high-priority

Report 24: Latin-American and Gulf storefronts (Brazil 4.266, Mexico 4.381, Peru 4.511, Ecuador 4.593; bill_core 2.35–6.42%) carry the same product that rates 2.1–2.6 in the US/UK/AU/CA during 2024–26 at 42–52% billing disputes; Brazil stays at 4.002 through the worst era. Language-neutral ratings rule out a classifier artefact. Whatever is different in how the product is sold there is the model — and rich English-language markets were the worst, not the best. Report 25: Argentina (mean 2.95, monetisation friction 40%, billing 10%) and the Spanish-language block (blocker 36% more common, paywall register markedly more hostile) vs Great Britain (mean 4.06, zero blocker, zero confusing-UX) — the same product, different market experience; check Argentine pricing display and trial mechanics. Report 26: Germany (63.6% 5★, 19.83% friction), France (20.37%), Australia (18.52%) and Canada (cap 10.09%) vs Russia (85.3% 5★, 7.34% friction) and Vietnam (86.8%, 5.15%) on the same product — though Russia's low friction may be a payment-availability effect: if users cannot reach the paywall, low friction is not satisfaction. Report 28: China (n=12) has zero ad complaints while its three critical reviews are all localisation — if ad inventory does not serve there, CN is a natural control for the ad-free product. Report 30: Russia is the product's real market (only continuous 13-month stream, most purchase attempts, most nuanced feedback, substantive mean 3.20) and where the payment flow is visibly breaking; Spanish-language organic reviews (AR/MX/UY, 0/6 templated, mean 2.33) are the harshest in the corpus while ES/CL are 16/24 templated at 4.75. Report 31: Australia shows the monetisation and integrity story without the crash wave (friction 43.5%, entitlement 14.0%, billing 19.7%, launch 9.3%); Canada is the worst large storefront (2.10, 57.7% 1★); Brazil and Mexico are wave-dominated (launch 28.6% / 28.1%, upsell only 2.2% / 3.5%); Switzerland was offered 10 CHF and charged 59 CHF; Hong Kong and India show 26.7% / 17.1% entitlement failure. Report 33: storefronts differ sharply — cn blocked (57.8%), de subscription-averse (price 14.7%, subscription 9.2%), kr the account-deletion centre (5.5%), jp highest payer share (16.0%) and Watch / update complaints, ru Mac/web 10.1%, vn happiest (4.61). Report 42: Brazil (41.8% cap complaints, 9 of 12 lag reports), the US (all six multi-count complaints, near-zero cap), Russia (5 of 7 crashes, 4 of 6 data losses, no payment rail) and Japan (both reviews 1★ on price) each fail differently on the same product. Report 43: 18 of 20 crash reports are US (4.40% vs 0.87%) — more likely a reporting-behaviour artefact than a device fact, unresolvable from reviews. Report 46: the same product is loved and disputed differently per storefront — Germany 3.95 with every monetisation theme 2–4× global, Russia 4.43 calling the price fair, China objecting to the payment shape not the cap, India negotiating, Turkey regional price, Spain the harshest cap objection (mean 2.00) beside Catalan praise. Report 47: Japan (mean 3.54) carries almost all the monetisation shock and the payers; Korea (4.33) requests and forgives (6 of 13 KR crash reviews still 5★); the same product rates 3.70 in JP + KR and 4.25 elsewhere. Report 48: 'Praise is remarkably uniform; grievance is local' — simplicity and flexibility land within a few points everywhere while price sensitivity clusters in CA / AU / DE / CN and localization in RU / CN; China splits sharpest (crash 12.33%, localization 12.33%, simplicity at 5.00★). Report 50: the cap change is invisible in the US (all four US cap statements say 5) and concentrated in Turkey, Australia and Mexico (four of Mexico's five reviews in 18–24 Aug 2026) — hypothesis: it lands hardest where the subscription is expensive relative to local purchasing power. Report 53: Spanish- and Portuguese-language storefronts carry 34.1% monetisation friction against 21.3% globally; Germany's top theme is price (18.00%); Taiwan's is reliability (37.5%) with only 8.9% friction. Report 54: payer and cap-complaint rates are identical in the high-volume group and globally (11.9%), so those are product properties, while price objection (CN 16.7%), restore failure (non-US) and outcome language (US 24.4%) are market-specific. Report 57: the same product shows three market problems — Korea (tenured base worn down by regressions), the US (top-of-funnel lost to a 30-second ad; ads and uninstalls 15.15%), Japan (would convert at ¥2,000, converts at zero at ¥4,500). Report 59 (Tappsk): monetisation pain is geographic and product love is not — without the Russian storefront praise (76.8%), ease and the free-limit objection are unchanged while billing falls 3.2% → 1.4% and payment access 0.7% → 0.0%; billing 3.7% in Russian-speaking storefronts vs 1.0% in English-speaking; high-star reviews hide support tickets (CONTRA_RATING 155: 102 are 4–5★ reviews whose text reports a crash, charge or refund request — 'Возможно ли вернуть деньги после списания', 5★), so star-filtered monitoring misses refund requests. Report 60 (Mindway): the US vs rest-of-world split is a funnel-stage split — the US has bought and been disappointed (under-built 7.92% vs 1.74%, billing 9.90% vs 0.87%), the rest of the world has been stopped at the door (paywall cap 11.30% vs 5.94%); whether the billing rate improved after 2024 or the US share of reviews simply fell (85.3% → 26.8%) cannot be separated from review text (Q3). Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): 45 written reviews vs 536 public ratings (8.40%), written mean 3.111 vs public 4.52 — 'the written corpus is a complaint channel, not a satisfaction measure'; per storefront the gap runs to −3.56 (UA: 39 ratings at 4.56 vs two 1★ reviews) and Ireland's one 1★ review is its entire public rating; Argentina is the one storefront where the June burst shows in the public number (3.82). (Consolidation after report 62: the title was widened from 'Audit the sales funnel per market — the same product can rate 4.3 in one storefront and 2.1 in another on billing alone' to cover the channel dimension the batch added; the original storefront finding stays in the statement.) Report 64 (Critique AI): written vs public gap −1.84 to −2.92 in every storefront with ≥ 5 reviews (US 180 @ 2.66 vs 9,557 @ 4.73); high-spend ('rich') markets carry the friction (2.53, 47.9% 1★) against volume markets (2.91, 34.3%) — the paywall binds where the creator's audience is; the US argues the amount (price 30.0% > hardwall 29.4%) and is where people get in (22.2% vs 11.5%), while GB argues the wall's existence (40.0% vs 20.0%); the app ranks worst in the US (48th) where 43% of written reviews come from. Report 65 (Rabit): written 3.677 vs public 4.76 (−1.08; −0.30 Vietnam to −2.10 Portugal) — 'both are correct, and the store number is the better estimate of average satisfaction while this report is the better guide to what is broken'; six 5★ reviews carry price complaints or crash reports — here stars under-report dissatisfaction; non-Brazilian reviewers left faster over the 2023 changes. Report 67 (Habio): corpus mean 2.35 vs US public 4.28 (3,932), gb 3.68, ca 4.04, au 3.71, fr 3.05, de 2.65, mx 3.31, es 2.93; 'the complaint does not depend on the market' — non-seeded means near 1★ everywhere, only the mechanism varies (workbook gb / es, language bait fr / de, cancellation and support au / de); the US is two corpora (555 of 886 flagged; non-seeded US 1.35). Report 68 (Ultiself): public exceeds corpus mean in 12 of 20 storefronts; kz 4.04 corpus mean but 2.38 outside E5, il 4.48 carried by 51 Hebrew 5★ one-liners, ng 4.98 all praise with 8 shared bodies and the 'post one review per day' text; the harm concentrates in ae (2.02, 72.0% billing), by (2.78, 26.3% web billing), ua (2.98) and cl (3.04 vs public 4.26) — the ua + kz + by group outside E5 is 61.5% billing against 29.9% for the US outside E5. Report 69 (TheFor): a positive-skew corpus — 71.25% 5★, written 4.525 against ~4.87 US public on a 30% write rate; storefront inversions (za 2.50 vs 4.40; de 5.00 vs 4.13) each explained by one or two reviews; 29 probed storefronts with zero reviews read as absent distribution, not rejection. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): a corpus that agrees with its public rating (4.73 vs 4.78) because reviewers are mostly those who succeeded; 17 contradictions are all 1–3★ with wholly positive text. Report 71 (MyStreaks): the written corpus stops 648 days before extraction while the app shipped 9 more releases (Challenges, Persona Notifications, Journal) — 'this report describes the app as it was up to late 2024'; the silent public raters are harsher (a 2★ and two 1★ with no text); zero paying reviewers, so every monetization data point is a refusal; GB, CA, AU and VN hold ratings but no text. Report 72 (Habit Hearts): 85.20% 5★, 27.20% low-information reviews rising to 36.00% in 2026 ('the informative corpus is closer to 180 reviews than 250'), zero feature requests in 2026, a grant cohort of 15 all 5★, 21.5% of public ratings written; the Christmas cluster contains six 1★, so it is seasonal, not solicited. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): Japan's 103 text reviews are 3.27% of its 3,151 ratings and carry a 24.27% 1★ share against 3.11% public; JP written 3.49 vs rest of world 4.31 is 'engagement depth, not national sentiment' (27.08% of non-JP reviews are sentiment-only; every churn, defect and friction report is Japanese); Brazil holds 100 public ratings but 4 short reviews. Report 75 (Habit Streak): 41 text reviews on 451 public ratings — ratings-weighted 4.67 vs corpus 4.00 (France −1.34: 3.40 vs 4.74); 4 of 25 5★ carry a monetization objection and two are wholly negative in substance ('Me gustaría que fuera gratuito', author handle 'Gratuito porfa') — 'Star rating is unreliable as a sentiment proxy in this corpus'; gb and jp rate but write nothing. Report 76 (Way of Life): a praise corpus (any-praise 81.88%, 1–2★ 3.67%) where a 'Meaningful' complaint is dozens of reviews; CONTRA_RATING 47 (0.61%) — 29 high-star reviews reporting problems, 7 low-star praise ('I absolutely love this app', 1★); the public mean exceeds the corpus mean in 21 of 22 storefronts; E6 is both the highest-rated era (4.70) and the most polarised (1–2★ 5.2%); removing burst days shifts no headline by more than 0.4 pp. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly, 71 reviews): (1) one review is 1.41% so the spec's bands cannot discriminate — every headline carries a Wilson CI, 'where a band and an interval disagree, trust the interval'; (2) 14 of 71 (19.72%) are content-free 5★ and 3 more 5★ are complaints — 17 of 50 five-star reviews (34%) evidence no satisfaction; excluding low-info makes both the strongest positive and the strongest negative larger; (3) money complaints changed register, not volume — 7 at 1.57★ before v3.0, 7 at 3.86★ since, so 'the recent ratings no longer carry the monetization problem' (2026 Q3: 5 of 9 money-negative at 4.44★); (4) 18 of 28 storefronts contributed exactly one review, averaging 3.33★, and five of six 1★ come from them — where almost nobody writes, the one who does is the annoyed one; (5) 71 text reviews on 339 public ratings, 4.31★ vs 4.58★, the US public base has zero 1★/2★ across 37; (6) zero refund / cancellation / renewal mentions is 'a genuine blank, not a clean bill of health'. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker, 172 reviews): 937 public ratings vs 172 text (18.4%), 4.781★ vs 4.599★; France 57 ratings / 2 text; the distribution is prompted (in-app review request) and the tail is inverted — 11 one-star, 6 at 2★+3★ — 'the signature of a transaction failing rather than a product gradually underperforming'; 10 edited reviews carry their last-edit date; 5 rating-vs-text contradictions (a 5★ 'given in advance', a 5★ whose body is only a complaint, a 1★ that calls it a 'Great app'); a 'six seven' meme review kept; the rating decline (4.89 → 4.02) cannot be separated from a composition shift as the YouTube/Reddit launch cohort aged out. Report 82 (Lasting Change, 175 reviews): corpus 1.880★ vs public 3.838★ — a 1.958★ gap, over two stars in every high-volume storefront ([[C300]]); 72.00% one-star; the Anglophone UK+AU+CA block is the most negative population (mean 1.20★, 94.0% 1★, praise 2%, trust_collapse 84%) with a plausible mechanism — they can read the English listing, T&Cs and warning reviews and have consumer-protection routes they use; 90.9% of the corpus comes from high-spend markets, consistent with a $50–$131 funnel targeting high-ARPU geographies; a rising era mean (1.69 → 2.41) is a measurement artefact — nine of fifteen late positives are under 60 characters while money harm hit its highest share; the developer's home market (Lithuania) is the only storefront perfect on both measures; no rating elasticity ('they are asking for their money back'), no rating recovery, no defence of the company by any user. Report 83 (Roubit, 500 reviews): the positively selected case — public 4.658★ vs corpus 4.156★ (+0.502), small in Korea and the US, +1.13★ in Japan where the text turned during bug waves while the cumulative rating still read 4.48★ — 'the text reviews are the more negative signal, and they lead it'; 31 of 33 rating/text contradictions are four- or five-star bug reports and 19 of 40 blank-screen reports are 4–5★ — 'star ratings understate dissatisfaction during bug waves'; reviews used as a support desk (SUPPORT_QUESTION 43); 145 reviews (29.00%) under 60 characters; 17 of 31 voted reviews are Japanese, 10 of them bug reports; seven solicited or invite-code reviews, all 5★. Report 84 (HabitGrid, 86 reviews): the zero-gap case — corpus 4.930★ vs public 4.939★ over 311 ratings (+0.009), every large storefront within 0.12★; 'the corpus is a complete census of text reviews and, on rating, is not distinguishable from the silent majority'; zero 1–2★ text reviews in 451 days (the only trace of a very dissatisfied user is one textless US 1★); 28 one-line 5★ (32.56%), all five-star; no churn statements; no storefront reaches 50. Report 85 (Habitica, 3,445 reviews over eleven years): the US listing shows 4.27★ from 3,324 ratings against a US corpus mean of 3.76★ and the public mean exceeds the corpus mean by 0.26–0.78★ in all eleven eligible storefronts — 'people write when something breaks'; the distribution is bimodal (5★ 44%, 1★ 14%); CONTRA_RATING 46 — 44 are 5★ reviews reporting a defect, 42 of them before 2022-12 and cn over-represented, 'consistent with reviewers treating the star field as a contact form'; single days hold 49 (crash), 22 (feature day) and 20 (outage) reviews and excluding them moves no headline more than 5.4 points; three authors on >1 storefront; 'great app!' recurs across three authors years apart. Report 86 (Today, 1,785 reviews over ten years): corpus 3.97★ vs every public storefront 4.5–4.8★ — 'do not present 3.97★ as the app's rating'; the corpus is front-loaded (45.32% in E1, 645 reviews from 2016) so 'any global percentage is mostly a statement about 2016–17'; volume decayed 45× (59.1 → 1.3 per month); CONTRA_RATING 46 — 40 are 5★ whose text is only a complaint ('Blank Screen after IOS update' — entire text) so the public average is inflated 'by a measurable population of users who write a complaint and tap five stars anyway'; Japan reports the most defects (42.11%) while rating above the mean — 'any market-health read that uses the rating alone will systematically under-weight Japanese defect signal'; RATING_LEVERAGE 16; 40 five-star reviews contain no praise at all; 152 reviews carry both praise and a bug code — 'people who like the app describing what is broken in it'. Report 88 (GetHabit, 490 reviews): a 2020–21 corpus (98.16%) about a product sold under another name (HabitBox), 87.55% negative, 72.45% one-star; text 2.38% of the rating base and 2.64★ below it; the review gate, pre-use five-stars and inverted vote pattern make the public rating itself suspect; volume collapsed from 92 reviews in April 2021 to 6 in May, so the disappearance of the in-app dark patterns after May 2021 is 'weak evidence that they were removed'; some charge complaints may be the reviewer's own mistake and several say so ('my own fault'). Report 89 (Check Calendar, 253 reviews, 40 storefronts): only the US (61) and Japan (60) reach 50; corpus 3.58% of 7,065 ratings and 1.34★ below them; half the corpus is non-English (Japanese 59); Japan carries the highest paywall share (50.0%) with the least fraud language (3.3%) and the most precise, polite descriptions, the most buyers (18.3%), the most specific praise (51.7%), all the record-integrity defects and all three unkept-promise reviews, and 17 of the 21 voted reviews; the US is 'the same paywall share but more accusatory' (non-disclosure 18.0%, scam language 11.5%, both double the rest) and says 'does what I need' more than 'simple'; storefronts with ≥10 reviews carry the paywall problem (46.5% vs 33.3%) and the public-rating gap tracks it by storefront. Report 90 (Quit Bad Habits & Addiction, 614 reviews, 37 storefronts): a Russian-language corpus — 516 reviews (84.04%) in Russian across 23 storefronts, including 41 of the 56 US-storefront reviews, so 'the US findings describe mostly Russian speakers using US App Store accounts'; only RU (407) and US (56) reach 50 and 17 storefronts hold one review; the request pattern is Russian-speaking (REQ_WIDGET 16.7% in RU vs 8.7% elsewhere; 27 of 28 tree-growth requests; SUPPORT_QUESTION 3.4% vs 0.5%; all six perceived-paywall reviews) while the crash concentrated in the high-spend group (19.3% vs 9.2%, driven by the US); 'language, not storefront, organises this corpus'.

<a id="c082"></a>
### C082 — Ads in the free tier — viable only off the logging path, off the launch path and out of harmful categories, and they turn 'free' praise into the churn segment

**Certain** · 23 apps · 76 cards · positive in 15 apps · negative in 12 apps · tied to a purchase in 6 apps

*Why Certain:* 23 apps, same direction (act on it, 61%), 9 reports label it high-priority

| | reaction positive | reaction negative |
|---|---|---|
| **app makes it free** | free-praised — 4 apps | free-expected-but-broken — 4 apps |
| **app makes it paid** | paid-converts — 1 apps | paid-resented — 0 apps |

**Verdict from the table:** mixed — conditions decide

A mild negative and a minor purchase reason in report 2; 'no ads' is the best-rated topic in report 1. Report 18: an interstitial ad on every check-off (Oct 2022) drew 17+ protests in weeks and was softened by December; the surviving minimal ads were tolerated. Report 25: six reviewers volunteer 'show me ads instead' of a paywall — ads-as-alternative is requested, not complained about; the app has none. Report 26: three teens independently ask for a rewarded-ad path to extra habits ('I will watch ads all day long if I have to') while 7 reviews (mean 5.00) praise having no ads. Report 27: 12 reviews (8.70%, mean 4.83) praise the absence of ads by name; an ad tier is 'contradicted by evidence'. Report 28 (the strongest counter-evidence in the set): an ad-supported free tier whose interstitial fires on every check-off is 19.98% of reviews at mean 2.73 vs 4.35 for the rest, 52.4% of all 1★, and rose from 3.5% (2021H2) to 39.6% (2024H2) before easing to 16.7%; three reports of non-dismissible ads and one of 'decline the rewarded ad, get a forced ad anyway' are store-guideline risks; an app rated 4+ with 40 reviews from or about children (ages 8–10 self-declared) serves untargeted network ads including AI homework-cheating and Temu wigs; 6 reviewers praise the ads as light and rewarded ads for carrots are accepted — the placement, not the existence, is the damage; the CN storefront (12 reviews, zero ad complaints) may be a natural ad-free control. Report 42: zero mentions of ads; upsell interstitials play the role ('the popups for premium are annoying and difficult to click out of'); one would rather see ads than pay €1.99/month (report 34). Report 47: the corpus is its own before-and-after on ad format — top-and-bottom banners were a mild theme (11, 1.87%, mean 3.55, 2019 – Apr 2024) whose reviewers mostly asked to pay to remove them; a video ad per check-in (May–Dec 2024) averaged 1.46 and generated exits ('1アクションに1回結構な長さのゲーム広告'; '元々入力するのに1分もかからないのに広告も1分じゃ'; 'an ad after every single entry is excessive… worse option than the notes app'); rewarded video for cosmetic colours (2022) was reported neutrally in a 14-vote 5★ — placement on the completion action, not ads as such, is what reviewers punish. Report 48: no ads in any era — 33 praise it, zero complain; two reviewers propose ads instead of the paywall, which the report reads as hostility to the cap rather than endorsement of ads. Report 52: the counter-case at scale — a nine-year Chinese tracker ran splash ads (2019–21, AD_NEG 3.4% / 2.8%) and in-flow ads from June 2025 (35.0% of reviews in six months, the lowest month in nine years); a ¥8 one-time ad-free SKU is accepted by those who find it ('but 8 yuan removes ads forever', 5★) and read as the motive for hostile ads by others; recovered to 5.8% in 2026 with complainants possibly churned. See [[C269]]. Report 64 (Critique AI): with no free tier, 12 (2.86%, mean 1.58) propose an ad-supported way in, one proposes an ad-supported base of a three-tier ladder; a 2★ defends the price as the alternative to 'annoying ads'. Report 76 (Way of Life): the free tier carried ads 2011 → ~2018 (NEG_ADS 54, mean 3.06★, 5.03% of 3★); removing them was the #3 purchase trigger ('Worth the upgrade to get rid of the ads', 4.6% of purchasers, 6.59× lift); ads gone from the free version by 2018 ('Now without ads even in free version', 5★) and NEG_ADS is 0.0% of E6; the price objection was highest while the free tier had ads (E2–E3) and fell after. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): no ads; the only ad mention asks for them as a paywall alternative — 'would like to have more freebies or maybe ads instead of the payment wall' (5★). Report 83 (Roubit): a free tier with ads that reviewers praise as generous (PRAISE_FREE_GENEROUS 14: 'literally gives you supportive letters every day FOR FREE'; PRAISE_NO_ADS 6) until 2026 put ads on open, on diary write and on past-day check-off — then ads became a stated churn reason; no reviewer says they paid to remove ads. Report 84 (HabitGrid): the no-ads, no-IAP counter-case — zero price or ad complaints in 86 reviews, all 23 price hits and 9 ad hits are praise. Report 89 (Check Calendar): the free-with-ads option is 'offered but not selectable' for one reviewer (2024-07), used with a top banner by another (2024-10), 'useless without premium' for a third (2026-06) — the corpus cannot establish whether the ad tier works; PAY_PREFER_ADS 2 would take it over the wall. Report 90 (Quit Bad Habits & Addiction): ads are the app's only revenue apart from two ad-removal subscriptions, and the corpus prices that trade-off — U:money_any 36 (5.86%), 20 of them ad complaints; FUTURE_MONETISATION_WORRY 3 wrote before the ads arrived ('just don't ruin it with ads'), and they were right: the ad rollout produced the churn segment and, in July 2026, the crash ([[C306]]). (Consolidation after report 90: title widened from 'Ads in the free tier' to state the three placement constraints and the churn finding; see [[C240]], [[C269]], [[C306]], [[C307]].)

<a id="c101"></a>
### C101 — Milestones, achievements, celebration

**Certain** · 21 apps · 32 cards · positive in 10 apps · negative in 9 apps

*Why Certain:* 21 apps, same direction (unresolved, 61%), 5 reports label it high-priority

| | reaction positive | reaction negative |
|---|---|---|
| **app makes it free** | free-praised — 2 apps | free-expected-but-broken — 0 apps |
| **app makes it paid** | paid-converts — 0 apps | paid-resented — 0 apps |

**Verdict from the table:** only free-tier evidence

The largest positive-intent request in report 3 (2.21%, six years); shipped Aug 2026. Report 23: the gold-theme completion state — the whole screen turns gold when every task is done — is named by 80 5★ reviews; rewards, badges and milestones requested 136 times by happy users. Report 31: celebration on completion requested by 44 (mean 3.98), while achievements/trophies added in Apr 2023 were unwanted by long-time users. Report 46: the colour saturation itself is the reward — no badges needed; a gentler decay on a miss is asked for by 6 (mean 4.67) but must be tested against the neurodivergent segment. Report 50: badges / achievements requested (1). Report 57: a big confetti pop-up on check-off 'gives me ALL the dopamine' with no penalty for missing. Report 58: an ADHD reviewer asks for 'more of celebration for those who like dopamine hits' while 7 of 8 neurodivergent reviewers praise restraint — make it off-by-default and measure. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): reviews are written to mark milestones — streaks of 500 days, 1,000 days, a year or more; OUT_STREAK 617 (26.94%). Report 75 (Habit Streak): streak-milestone visuals requested (background changes at 7, 30, 60, 90 days, citing chess.com) — reinforces the Duolingo mental model users arrive with. Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_GAMIFY 16 (rewards / achievements, 4.06★) and REQ_SCORE 4 — small against PR_CHAINS 129; the listing ships a scoreboard. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): Badges & Achievements shipped 2025-09-29 → 2025-11-02 and no reviewer mentions them; UX_NO_ACHIEVEMENT_FEEL 1 ('lacks to give you the feeling of achievement for completing the tasks') predates them. Report 90 (Quit Bad Habits & Addiction): REQ_MOTIVATION_CONTENT 14 (2.28%) — achievements, quotes and congratulation at milestones; 'no daily motivation, notifications or congratulations … after three days I forgot it existed' (2★); against a counter-signal — one reviewer finds plain numbers calmer than praise — so §8.4 makes milestone notifications optional and off by default. Research: Quit Habit Decision.md — in the leading quit tracker's 10,621-review corpus the happiest reviews (4.77★ average) are milestone screenshots, which makes the milestone screen simultaneously the retention moment and the organic-sharing surface; specified milestones are 1/7/30/90 days plus money saved.

<a id="c015"></a>
### C015 — Shared / group habits

**Certain** · 18 apps · 34 cards · positive in 6 apps · negative in 13 apps · tied to a purchase in 1 apps

*Why Certain:* 18 apps, same direction (unresolved, 79%), 3 reports label it high-priority

| | reaction positive | reaction negative |
|---|---|---|
| **app makes it free** | free-praised — 2 apps | free-expected-but-broken — 0 apps |
| **app makes it paid** | paid-converts — 1 apps | paid-resented — 0 apps |

**Verdict from the table:** mixed — conditions decide

Strong purchase driver where it exists, but the worst-executed feature — demand is proven, execution is the risk. Report 23: task sharing / accountability partner exists but is described as weak and one-way; social layer requested by 28 (0.39%). Report 24: in-app community ('Circles', 370, mean 3.897) and time-boxed group challenges exist; the word 'God' being blocked in Circles drew 14 complaints. Report 25: friends / accountability / leaderboard requested by 10 fans (mean 4.80); no social feature exists. Report 26: eight Chinese reviewers ask for the community features of the discontinued '种子习惯' (Seed Habit) app. Report 31: social / shared lists / family to-do requested by 49 (mean 3.27); a parent tracking attention to each child. Report 33: challenges, friends and sharing (2022+) are mixed (challenges 19, some gated), and the report recommends hiding them until enabled. Report 48: shared / partner accountability requested by 22 (mean 4.45), including a coach who would move 100 clients onto the app if it existed. Report 59 (Tappsk): REQ_SHARED 65 (0.43%) never stops across eight years; the listing advertises sharing a task to a friend's Tappsk, praised by only 5. Report 71 (MyStreaks): sharing streaks with a spouse, family and students (SOC-SHARE 3) — 'share with friends, students and people I want to be accountable to or vice versa' (a teacher / coach use case); comment replies and posting into Groups requested or buggy (2023). Report 85 (Habitica): parties that fight quest bosses together, where a missed Daily damages the whole party, are the strongest social-accountability mechanic in the series — PR_PARTY 158 (4.59%), party praise held at 5.0% of reviews even after the public community was removed; 'In my group, we keep each other motivated'; NEG_SOLO 16 want a party finder; BUG_SOCIAL 78.

<a id="c300"></a>
### C300 — A headline star rating that sits far above its own written reviews is a signal to audit, not a satisfaction figure — find where and when star-only ratings are collected before trusting them

**Certain** · 8 apps · 35 cards · positive in 0 apps · negative in 3 apps

*Why Certain:* 8 apps, same direction (act on it, 71%), 8 reports label it high-priority

Report 82 (Lasting Change): the text corpus averages 1.880★ while the ratings-weighted public mean across the same 26 storefronts is 3.838★ (848 ratings, 673 star-only) — a 1.958-star gap, and more than two full stars in every one of the four high-volume storefronts (us 2.00 vs 4.10, gb 1.09 vs 3.27, ca 1.31 vs 3.72, au 1.29 vs 3.55); 72.00% of text reviews are one-star, at least one 5★ is a fraud warning, and the public 4.1★ 'does not reflect the content of the reviews underneath it'; two readings the report does not choose between — text-writers are a negatively selected minority, or star-only ratings are collected in a context text reviews are not — and §8.8 asks where in the lifecycle and from whom the stars are gathered. In ordinary corpora the gap is a few tenths (report 79: +0.18; report 77: +0.27; report 76: up to +0.38 per storefront); a two-star gap across every major market is the signature of a rating stream and a review stream describing different populations. Related: [[C231]] (written reviews are a complaint channel — audit the funnel), [[C094]] (ask for reviews well), [[C076]] (never seed the launch rating). Report 83 (Roubit): the counter-case — here the written reviews lead the public rating downward during a bug wave (Japan text 3.36★ vs public 4.48★) because loyal users file bug reports at five stars and the cumulative star base lags; §8.10 'don't read cumulative 4.66★ as current satisfaction'. Report 84 (HabitGrid): the no-gap baseline — +0.009★ between public and text means for a free app with no billing surface; the two-star gap in report 82 is a billing-surface artefact, not a property of star ratings. Report 85 (Habitica): public exceeds corpus by 0.26–0.78★ in every eligible storefront for an app with an eleven-year defect history — the ordinary 'people write when something breaks' gap, an order of magnitude below the report 82 anomaly. Report 86 (Today): public 4.5–4.8★ vs corpus 3.97★ — a 0.6–0.8 gap on a ten-year corpus with a collapsed review rate; 'the true signal is in the text, which is why every finding here is text-derived'. Report 88 (GetHabit): the largest gap in the series — corpus 1.714★ vs 20,597 public ratings at 4.355★ (+2.641★), at least +2.3★ in every storefront with ten or more reviews; US 1★ is 6.76% of public ratings but 76.85% of text; the corpus shows two mechanisms — a rate-to-unlock gate and five-star texts written before use — plus a vote pattern in which one-line 5★ reviews carry the most votes; 'it is enough that the 4.355★ public rating should not be used as evidence of satisfaction for this app'. Report 89 (Check Calendar): corpus 3.332★ vs 4.676★ over 7,065 public ratings (+1.344★); the gap tracks the paywall share by storefront (Canada +2.82, Vietnam +2.78, Brazil +1.65, Japan +1.47, US +1.38 vs India +0.55, UK +0.19); seven five-star reviews carry negative text ('(1 STAR RATING) DO NOT INSTALL THIS' at 5★); very short reviews rose to 44.9% of 2026 reviews as the US rating base grew 258 → 868 → 1,492; one complaint of a review request every day — §8.7 find how often the prompt fires and at what point in the trial: 'if it fires before the trial ends, the public rating mostly reflects the pre-wall experience'. Report 90 (Quit Bad Habits & Addiction): the counter-example — corpus 4.397★ vs 4.913★ over 14,806 public ratings is only +0.515★, and before the crash week the corpus averages 4.647★; 'text reviews and public ratings agree that the app is liked; the difference is the crash week, whose one-star reviews barely move a cumulative public mean'; the largest per-storefront gaps (RU +0.58, US +0.70) are the storefronts that carried the crash. Report 90 (sensitivity): dropping the one crash week lifts the corpus to 4.650★ — within 0.26★ of the 4.913★ public mean — so this app's written-vs-public gap is almost entirely one release, not a rating mechanism.

<a id="c064"></a>
### C064 — Price level — where 'fair' turns into 'too expensive'

**Strong** · 52 apps · 183 cards · positive in 8 apps · negative in 44 apps · tied to a purchase in 4 apps

*Why Strong:* 52 apps, directions mixed (open 84, act 53, paid 19)

| | reaction positive | reaction negative |
|---|---|---|
| **app makes it free** | free-praised — 1 apps | free-expected-but-broken — 1 apps |
| **app makes it paid** | paid-converts — 1 apps | paid-resented — 11 apps |

**Verdict from the table:** evidence leans free (paid is mostly resented)

Both coexist for one price; split follows market, payment rails and year. Report 20: $39.99/year for a checkbox app was rejected in every market and language for seven years; Spain, which arrived after the conversion and lost nothing, objected to price (16.9%) but not revocation (2.8%) — the grievance follows arrival date, not nationality. Report 23: price objection 123 (1.69%, mean 2.21, 50.4% 1★) with au 5.7%, de 3.8%, ca 3.6% vs us 1.3%; flat across a 2.5× price rise; China's 1★ reviews are almost uniformly '¥25/30 for a reminder'; Germany objected to €3.99 at launch ('99Ct wären OK'). Report 24: price objection 791 (1.82%, mean 2.248) is about magnitude relative to category ($40/quarter, $80–100/month with bundles vs $5–20/yr rivals), opacity and targeting (premium wellness pricing for people with executive dysfunction and low income) — not the existence of a price; a distinct group calls $20/yr worth every penny. Report 25: only ~12 of 55 price objections are about the level ('£25 for a basic box checker'; '$40??? it's a simple app'); ~8 are stated inability to pay (a student, a child); US names the highest figures ($13/mo, $49 lifetime); Argentina (n=40, mean 2.95, friction 40%) is the most hostile storefront. Report 26: price objection 29 (0.76%, mean 2.76) vs 57 defending the price — 2:1 in favour; high-spend markets (de 19.83%, fr 20.37%, au 18.52%, ca 15.60% friction) are where price-defence arguments are also most articulate. Report 28: 16 price objections (1.95%, mean 2.88) at ~$10–15 consumable tiers — 'too expensive for an unproven, ad-saturated experience, sold as an opaque bundle, with no way to try it'; 'not the level of quality that this kind of money gets you with apps like procreate'; students and minors cannot pay ('strict parents and only my mom knows my Apple ID'); the winning position is 'more affordable alternative' to Finch — do not raise the price. Report 30: the price objection (5, mean 1.40) is price ÷ what you get free — 'Es un check list CARÍSIMO'; 'The price is too high for this quality'; 'para ser de pago es demasiado simple' — while three say the price itself is acceptable, two of them rating 1★/2★ for the cap; 'do not cut the price'. Report 31: 'a subscription for a checklist is unjustifiable' ('almost the price of Disney+!'; 'In this economy?'; 'How is this app worth $499.99?') — price objection 379 (7.31%, mean 1.79), 4.1% (E1) → 13.0% (E2); Canada has the highest price objection (11.6%); do not conclude 'lower the price' alone — restore a trustworthy low-commitment path and make it work. Report 33: price objection 203 (5.15%, mean 2.64), highest in Germany (14.7%), Turkey (10.5%) and France (10.4%) — '269 roubles … I pay 400 for Netflix'; '43 euro … for an agenda???'; '€40 … vous vivez où, Monaco?'. Report 34: ~$9/mo, ~$20/yr, ~$40 lifetime — price objection 25 (mean 3.16), many 'great app, too expensive' at 4–5★; €9.99/month called 'completely of the charts'. Report 36: ~$15/£15/€18 a year for Habits alone and ~$30 for the suite (2022–25) rising to $59–70 by 2026; price objection 36 (mean 2.31) and 'not worth it' 21 (mean 2.24, zero 5★). Report 41: lifetime moved €22 (2021) → €28 (2023) → €22–25 / $22.99 (2026) and price objections tracked it (4.2% 2022, 4.6% 2025, 0% 2026); reserve prices named €10, <$5, £3.99. Report 42: $39.99–$59.99/yr (US), ¥6,900 (JP, both reviews 1★), R$79.90 per 12 weeks (BR) vs 500₽ (RU, 'that's nothing'); price objection 18 (mean 1.67, never above 3★) — 'you pay that much for barely any technology'; 'the subscription price is unreal for what the app delivers'. Report 43: at $2.99 the price objection (36, 5.64%, mean 2.31) was almost entirely an objection to being stopped, not to money ('you can easily set timers on your phone for free'; 'I'm a college student so I'm ~broke~'), and it vanished with the cap. Report 46: $12/year (2019) → $4.99/mo or $30/yr (Jan 2020) → $7.49 / $29.99 / $99.99 lifetime (2023); pricing-model union 212 (9.73%, mean 2.92); Canada's CAD $39.99 / $129.99 sharpens it ('Are you out of your mind???'). Report 48: one-time requesters name $10–$20; the lifetime at $79.99–$149.99 is rejected by 28 who accept the model; Canada is the most price-sensitive storefront (9.47%) with praise intact — 'Canadians like the app and resent the deal more than anyone else'. Report 52: a nine-year price ladder ¥6 → ¥12/¥18 → ¥88 lifetime → ¥98, with a Nov 2019 tier rise (¥8→¥12, ¥12→¥18) and price rise complaints 42 (3.19). Report 53: one-time $4.99 → $7.99 → $12–13 → $19.99 (2017–22), then annual only $39.99 / over €40 / AU$99.99; price is Germany's top theme (18.00%, 'why €14?'). Report 55: reviewers name $5–$10 one-time or a $2.99 download as acceptable against ~$19.99/yr (text sub-cut). Report 57: lifetime roughly tripled between 2020–22 and 2024 (₩9,900 → ₩29,000; ¥1,600 → ¥4,500; $13 → $30–35) before a shift to subscription. Report 59 (Tappsk): the monthly at ~300 ₽ is called too high — 'Месячную подписку можно было бы сделать хотя бы 150р, а не 300'; 'Люди куда охотнее отдадут 100р в месяц'; 'Рублей 199-299' — while the lifetime at 449–600 ₽ on sale (list 1,490–2,500 ₽) sells; MON_PRICE 252 (1.66%), distinctive in France (2.16×) and Turkey (4.49×). Report 60 (Mindway): price points $7/week, €8/week, $39.99–40/year, '$60 a year', a $0.99 paid trial; 'a bit expensive for something I could do myself' (payer, 3★); the objection is relative to free substitutes, not to a number ([[C277]]). Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): three reviewers volunteer that the price is good ('The price is also very affordable considering the features it offers'; 'the subscription prices are very good'; 'reasonably priced' — and still did not buy, over the sync gap) against two one-line objections ('It's paid'; 'Asked for a payment in simple app like this') — §8.5: do not raise prices and do not cut them. Report 64 (Critique AI): PAY_PRICE 105 (25.06%, mean 1.94) against 11 defenders (2.63%, mean 4.55: '$40 bucks a year is a steal. A human trainer could cost as much as $40 a week!'; 'way cheaper than others'); PAY_PRICE jumped 19.2% → 34.0% in the latest quarter while defect themes stayed flat and defenders rose 0.8% → 8.7% — 'Contested pricing became a topic on the listing itself'; a price rise, a trial withdrawal or an audience widening past willingness-to-pay cannot be separated without pricing history. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): '¥980 is far too much. I'd happily pay around ¥300'; 'It's ¥980 a month as of April 2023, which feels a bit expensive'; MON_PRICE_HIGH 20 and MON_NO_PAY 17 (students, minors: 'my family says no in-app purchases'). Report 75 (Habit Streak): price level (4, mean 3.50: 'like 11 Dollars… I would download it then delete it'; 'man muss zu viel bezahlen') vs structure (7, mean 2.29) — structure carries all the hostile language; one defends the price against 'apps that charge up to $70 a year'. Report 76 (Way of Life): the $4.99 objection peaked when the app was young and the free tier had ads (MON_PRICE 6.7% E2, 6.5% E3) and fell to 1.6% in E5 as it matured; prices users volunteer — 12 yuan (cn), 200 roubles (ru), '.99 for an extra goal' (a per-item micro-price), 'up to £50 for lifetime' (gb); the price objection carries mean 3.71★ and is 23.49% of 3★ — 3★ reviews are the longest because they argue price. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): price level is the smallest of eight upgrade barriers — MON_PRICE_LEVEL 2 (2.82%, mean 3.00★: 'just wastage of funds', 1★; 'a little bit pricey, basic function still worth using it', 5★) against 3 who volunteer the price is right ('really affordable compared to others'); the inference (n=3) is that the app converts against a reference price the user has already formed elsewhere, not against zero; one affordability barrier at 5★ ('the moment I can afford it'). Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): price level is not the barrier — MON_PRICE_FAIR 10 (5.81%, 5.00★) including four written after the price rose from $10 to €23 ('der Preis für die Vollversion sehr fair'; 'Simple, barata y eficaz'), against U:price_objection 5 (2.91%, 3.20★: '18€ is way too much for a tracker lmao, pc games cost less than this', 1★; 'etwas teuer', 5★); the five objectors are Italian, Slovak, German, German and Czech — high-income European markets; 'A price cut would buy less than four sentences of disclosure'; the load-bearing case: a German 4★ who 'wanted to buy to support the developer' and did not at €23 'for a single app with one function'. Report 82 (Lasting Change): ~$30.99/month or ~$42–56/quarter for a companion app, billed off-store — the amount is objected to by 4 of 175 and called fair by 2; the entire objection is consent and structure. Report 83 (Roubit): monetisation friction is mild (U:paywall_friction 61, 12.20%, 3.85★) and the free tier is praised more than attacked; the objection is format and the yearly anchor, 'not the value of the character or the letters'; WOULD_PAY_INTENT 11 of 246 in Korea vs 1 of 254 elsewhere; one Korean 3★ payer mainly uses Todo Mate, 'cheaper and works with Apple Watch'. Report 85 (Habitica): MON_PRICE_HIGH 8 — '12 month usage cost as much as a tripple AAA vid game title' (2★); 'I'd gladly pay $10-$15 for the full program but nickel and diming users is off-putting' (2★); regional pricing in Russia and 'a bit expensive' in Turkey; MON_PRICE_FAIR 6; 'I'm a subscriber now, it's not expensive'. Report 86 (Today): $4.99 one-time was defended by reviewers against each other (MON_DEFEND 44; 'a steal at £5'; 'just a cup of coffee') and objected to as 'premium' at CA$7; German reviewers accept the pricing below the global rate (7.79% vs 10.98%); the objection that stuck is structure ($299.99 beside $9.99/yr), not level. Report 89 (Check Calendar): $3.99 → $4.99 and 600円 → 800円 (¥780 listed) between July 2025 and mid-2026, inferred from reviewer-quoted prices because the listing does not date it; no reviewer compares before and after — 'no price elasticity'; the only lower-price ask in 253 reviews is 'a couple of hundred roubles'.

<a id="c022"></a>
### C022 — Apple Watch app (done properly: timer, two-way sync)

**Strong** · 48 apps · 152 cards · positive in 19 apps · negative in 40 apps · tied to a purchase in 8 apps

*Why Strong:* 48 apps, directions mixed (act 50, paid 34, open 33)

| | reaction positive | reaction negative |
|---|---|---|
| **app makes it free** | free-praised — 1 apps | free-expected-but-broken — 2 apps |
| **app makes it paid** | paid-converts — 0 apps | paid-resented — 3 apps |

**Verdict from the table:** evidence leans free (paid is mostly resented)

Small volume, very high purchase intent; a half-built Watch app draws 2–3★. Report 20: an Apple Watch app was the highest-mean capability gap (62 requests, mean 4.15), asked for by the happiest users and named in churn-to-Streaks reviews; never shipped. Report 23: the Watch is the app's strongest differentiator and most fragile surface — 626 mentions (8.61%), 241 negative (mean 3.13) vs 385 positive (mean 4.35); it breaks on each watchOS generation (2016, watchOS 7, 2021–22 mirroring, watchOS 10 complications, 2024–26 blank complications); in Korea (13.5%) and Japan (13.3%) it is the dominant topic; 'I bought this for the Watch and it doesn't work' are the highest-value churn events. Report 24: in a 43,469-review coaching corpus the Watch (69, 0.16%) and widget (53, 0.12%) are marginal — the surface matters where the product is a checklist, not where it is content. Report 25: the Watch app (21 mentions, mean 4.48, 0 1★) is part of a praised Apple-platform surface (Watch + Mac + widgets + Shortcuts + Health), but one reviewer says it was 'suddenly removed' (Oct 2025) and another that the listing advertised Watch support that could not be installed. Report 26: no Apple Watch app throughout; requested by 8 (0.21%). Report 27: Apple Watch, Apple Health and macOS are each requested once (4★ 'Would be perfect with watch support'); the report says a paid tier, if ever, should attach only to such not-yet-existing capability. Report 31: the Watch app and complication were broken for long periods — 60 reviews (mean 2.33); support asked for a video, then silence; ''update coming soon'. 6 months later'; the v2 rebuild (Mar 2022) broke it and restored it months later. Report 33: the Watch app broke with iOS 13, would not launch after Habitify X, its complication broke with iOS 15.1 and sync lagged until 'finally' fixed Jan 2024 — 100 reviews (2.84 mean), 6.8% of E3, Japan 5.0% ('Streaks costs a tenth and works'); single-tap logging and area complications were removed. Report 36: Apple Watch requested by 9 (mean 4.11), one wanting the haptics on the wrist. Report 41: the Watch app shipped in 2021 on request (discussion peaked 13.7% then normalised); a privacy-minded payer cancelled because Watch sync requires iCloud and will return for 'easy normal Bluetooth sync between the phone and the watch'. Report 43: Apple Watch requested by 12 over five years (May 2019 'Not using your app due to lack of iwatch' → Jan 2024), the listing now ships Watch, and no request appears after Jan 2024. Report 46: Apple Watch shipped Mar 2021 and the request stopped (3 → 2 → 0 → 0); Watch ↔ phone sync is then a failure surface ('finished goals on the watch won't show up on the phone and vice versa… a deal breaker'). Report 47: Apple Watch requested by 6, all 2020–22; the listing shows iPhone, Mac and Vision only. Report 48: Watch app and complication praised by 24 (4.67) when working, faulted by 12 (2.33) when blank; 8 want a complication. Report 50: a Watch app shipped Jan–May 2025 after requests ('almost perfect, it just needs a watch app'); one 1★ calls it useless — no habit complication, notifications not working. Report 52: Apple Watch check-in requested every year since 2019 (PLAT_WATCH 256, 1.24%, 4.52) — 'one reviewer bought a Watch for this app'. Report 53: Watch complications configurable 'almost like watch faces themselves' are a purchase trigger (WATCH_GOOD 43, 4.70) while WATCH_BUG 62 (2.85) — duplicate water entries, sync, the Watch app crashing on launch in 2025–26; F6: re-certify the Watch app on every iOS release. Report 54: no Watch app (9, 4.22) — 'now I'm forced to use another app' (DE); 'lemme know if you're working on the watch app and I'll be the first one to buy this app' (PK). Report 55: no Watch app (PLATFORM_WANT 24). Report 56: an Apple Watch app requested once. Report 57: a Watch app shipped ~Mar 2020 ('moved to see it on the Watch') and hung on 'Loading…' for 26 (19 in 2020–21), then was largely fixed (0.94% of 2024–26). Report 59 (Tappsk): REQ_WATCH 81 fell from 4.7% of the launch year to 0.0% of the latest era as PR_WATCH 37 appeared — a request that stops is the trace of a shipped feature. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): an Apple Watch app requested once (UZ, 4★); treated as absent as of Jan 2026, lowest priority of the set. Report 65 (Rabit): REQ_WATCH 5 (1.00%, mean 3.80) — two frame the Watch as how they would actually get reminded. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): 'will make it 5★ if Apple Watch is supported' (REQ_WATCH 5). Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_WATCH 54 (0.70%, 4.30★) appears from 2015-08 and replaces the iPad request from 2016 (E5 1.8%); §8.5 ranks it after iCloud sync to iPad. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): REQ_WATCH 1 (5★). Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): REQ_WATCH 3 (4.33★, 2024-12 → 2026-06) — 'quasi unentbehrlich' for fast capture; 'Bitte ganz nach oben auf die Prioritätenliste!!!! (dann gibt's auch ✱✱✱✱✱)' (4★); the listing is iPhone-only; §8.3 'the app's whole value is low-friction check-in and the Watch is where that friction is lowest'; §8.7 whether the Watch actually converts or is a stated preference. Report 83 (Roubit): Apple Watch requested only from Korea (within REQ_IPAD_WATCH_MAC 15); a paying user defected to a rival 'cheaper and works with Apple Watch'. Report 84 (HabitGrid): REQ_WATCH 2 (2.33%), both recent; the developer told one reviewer he would try; 'two requests do not justify building one' — check the developer's own Discord/Reddit where requests are cheaper. Report 85 (Habitica): REQ_WATCH 67 (1.94%), in every era from 2015-12-07 to 2026-04-29 — the longest-running unshipped request in the corpus; a Wear OS version exists ('It doesn't make sense that Habitica hasn't released for Apple Watch but Wear Os'); §8.8 a watchOS companion for checking off Dailies and Habits. Report 86 (Today): the Watch app was requested for 14 months (REQ_WATCH 34 from 2016-03-11), shipped ~May 2017, and never worked properly — BUG_WATCH 88 (4.93%, 2.98★) vs 21 praising it: check-ins revert ('I tap an icon to say I've done it, then 20 minutes late it's unchecked again!!'), phone and watch disagree, the complication works on one watch face; Infograph complication requests recur for seven years unanswered; watchOS 5 broke it ('Broken since iOS 12 / watchOS 5… App hasn't had an update in nearly 2 months'); a purchase trigger for one ('I bought this app for the watch incorporation') and a condition for others ('I will gladly pay for the full version but I really need it to work on my watch') — 'a shipped-but-unreliable companion app is a larger negative than its absence'. Research: Feature Gating vs Quantity.md — Apple Watch support is named first in the set of capabilities habit apps conventionally gate.

<a id="c172"></a>
### C172 — Per-day / per-habit notes and journal text

**Strong** · 44 apps · 77 cards · positive in 18 apps · negative in 28 apps · tied to a purchase in 1 apps

*Why Strong:* 44 apps, directions mixed (free 30, open 28, act 9)

| | reaction positive | reaction negative |
|---|---|---|
| **app makes it free** | free-praised — 5 apps | free-expected-but-broken — 1 apps |
| **app makes it paid** | paid-converts — 0 apps | paid-resented — 1 apps |

**Verdict from the table:** mixed — conditions decide

A note field on each check-in is pure upside and requested by happy users (reports 2, 3, 7); a single cramped line is the common complaint; charging for journal text while mood is free drew complaints (report 9). Report 20: notes per day was the single most-requested feature in the corpus (79, mean 3.66) and never shipped. Report 23: per-completion notes were requested from 2015 (43, 0.59%) and shipped ~Mar 2023; the residual ask is navigation between notes. Report 25: a notes / journal / mood field per day requested by 7 (mean 4.43). Report 26: a journal / gratitude note requested (~4). Report 27: daily memo prompts exist and their value is disputed ('simply yet engaging daily memo questions' vs 'the note taking doesn't really have a point to it'); a fuller daily log is wanted. Report 28: journal/notes per day and mood tracking used by 38 (4.63%, mean 4.29). Report 31: notes/journal per entry and timestamps (added Jan 2017) — 82 mentions (mean 3.52); 'last done / minutes ago' removed in 2022–23. Report 33: per-habit per-day notes / journal moved to Premium in Apr 2019 (free users lost 300 days of notes) and in Dec 2024 – Jan 2025 lost back-dating and editing (1,000+ gym days logged in memos). Report 34: notes per completed day are Premium (praised 11, mean 4.91); notes on missed days and opening a note from the calendar requested by 9 (a 'No Spend' habit). Report 36: notes on a habit requested by 3. Report 43: journal / per-day notes praised by 9 (mean 4.44) — but a journal prompt forced on every skip in the 2025 redesign drew a 1★ from a long-time payer. Report 46: journal / per-day notes shipped Dec 2023 (praised 12, mean 4.67) after 9 requests. Report 47: a per-day memo attached to each check-in is the diary feature Korean and Japanese reviewers name as the differentiator (memo + photo 32, 5.43%, mean 4.75); a note-length limit is asked by 3; one user stopped writing memos after the 2026 data loss. Report 48: per-entry notes praised by 21 (4.95), requested by 14; whether notes are free is disputed in-thread. Report 50: see [[C268]] — the journal is a primary reason to choose the app and its editor the worst-quality surface. Report 52: check-in notes are the largest unmet need (JRNL_WANT 668, 3.24%, very strong) and a praised micro-diary with 'on this day in past years' (234, 4.85). Report 54: notes per habit requested (3, 4.67). Report 56: per-habit description / notes requested by 3 — ship a short label first; journaling is a separate question. Report 57: notes allowed only on successful check-ins — 9 ask across six years and three languages to write why they failed ('I want to write down why I couldn't do it on the days I failed'). Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): a per-day value / note ('walked 5k, then 7k') requested by a 4★ reviewer. Report 64 (Critique AI): a notes space requested (ch, 5★). Report 65 (Rabit): a notes / description field per habit (REQ_DESC 2) and calendar notes on why a habit was missed (S7). Report 67 (Habio): the daily reflection journal is one of the two things the corpus says to keep. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): a note per check-in requested (REQ_MEMO 7, mean 4.43). Report 72 (Habit Hearts): a free-text note / link on a habit (3 — one to attach a yoga video link), the largest request. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): the memo written on the check cell itself (9, 4.67) — 'The memo isn't tucked away, it's on the check itself, so when you scan back you don't have to open them one by one… the memo usability really is one of a kind'. Report 75 (Habit Streak): a daily note / journal and completion timestamps requested by one 4★. Report 76 (Way of Life): per-day notes are free and praised (PR_NOTES 174, 2.24%, 4.86★, 1.53× among purchasers); friction is reaching and searching them (REQ_NOTES_VIEW 13, NEG_NOTES_UX 4) and photos (REQ_PHOTO 9). Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): REQ_NOTES 2 (Aug–Sep 2024) shipped as check-in notes / Journal in v1.9.0 (2025-08-14). Report 83 (Roubit): a diary with mood logging is the emotional core (PRAISE_DIARY 24); REQ_DIARY_FEATURES 10 — photos, more moods, memos, more than one entry a day ('I pay so letters are unlimited, which is good, but I can only write one a day'). Report 84 (HabitGrid): notes shipped in 1.0.5 and were praised eight months later; 'add a note' is part of the ideal described by a 5★. Report 86 (Today): a journal card exists (PR_JOURNAL 24) yet a note per check-in is the second-most-upvoted request (31 up / 47: 'to record it at that point in time. That way you can know yourself more accurately', cn 5★; REQ_NOTE 12) — never shipped. Report 89 (Check Calendar): PRAISE_NOTES 4 ('I use the short note for listing my weight'); DEF_NOTES_ERROR 2 on consecutive days in January 2024 ('10.1.0でメモが書けない'; 'Something went wrong'); notes are what the trial wall locks ('I can't even copy the notes I had written down').

<a id="c009"></a>
### C009 — Basic widgets, icons and colours are free

**Strong** · 39 apps · 150 cards · positive in 27 apps · negative in 27 apps · tied to a purchase in 5 apps

*Why Strong:* 39 apps, directions mixed (free 76, act 48, open 10)

| | reaction positive | reaction negative |
|---|---|---|
| **app makes it free** | free-praised — 10 apps | free-expected-but-broken — 3 apps |
| **app makes it paid** | paid-converts — 4 apps | paid-resented — 8 apps |

**Verdict from the table:** evidence leans free (paid is mostly resented)

Loved, drives 5★, and re-paywalling widgets backfired. Report 7: with every widget Pro, the widget paywall was the only theme with zero 5★ reviews, while widgets were the best-loved feature; users proposed one free widget, more with Pro. Report 12: widget requests appeared only from Nov 2024 and came from retained payers ('I forget all the time to use this app cause I don't have a widget') — the highest-mean complaint theme. Report 23: custom app icons and theme colours (324, 4.46%, mean 4.51) are 'a small feature with an outsized delight response'; 54 more ask for more/custom icons. Report 25: widgets (Home, Lock Screen, Control Center) are almost purely positive (30, mean 4.43, 0 1★); custom icons and colours with hex input; one lifetime buyer asks for a minimal heat-map widget like HabitKit/Ripples. Report 26: a garden-view home-screen widget, reminders, a timer and day-of-week scheduling are free (21 widget mentions, mean 4.14). Report 29: colour coding per habit is free; 4 ask for a wider palette and custom colours. Report 34: widgets requested for 3.5 years (11.1% of E3) became the top new praise on launch (11.2% of E4), then were paywalled for some users ('Cant use widgets without subscription', 1★) — the report's advice is to keep at least one widget and basic colours free. Report 36: widgets gated in Oct 2023 (WIDGETGATE 14, mean 2.64) are load-bearing for adherence — '62 days in a row … wouldn't be possible without this app and it's widgets'; 'Ojalá los widget fueran gratuitos eso mejoraría el apego' — and reviewers accept paid skins but not paid widgets ('I can understand locking skins behind a paywall but ALL widgets???'). Report 41: interactive widgets (111 mentions, 13.62%) are the most-praised surface, stronger in the US (17.4%) and GB (18.8%) than DE / CA (~9.9%). Report 42: no widgets at all, framed as a competitive deficit — 'it has no widgets, so it loses against the rest of similar apps'; 'It's a paid app, so I have higher requirements… PLEASE add a WIDGET section' (a payer). Report 43: the widget is what makes the app work for the ADHD / accessibility segment — 'if I have to seek it out a lot of the time it's not happening. I can miss notifications, but not if it's on my Home Screen' — and is named a protected surface. Report 46: interactive widgets are free (contested) and rose from 0.81% to 3.98% of praise — 'I barely even open the app'; the widget holds four rows and the free tier three. Report 47: a widget was requested by 20 (3.40%) in every era 2019–2026 — the most-requested capability — and shipped in 2025 as a free surface; 'please make a widget that makes me want to continue', Duolingo the benchmark. Report 48: widgets arrived ~2020 and interactivity was later removed (12 praise at 5.00, 20 requests, 14 widget bugs). Report 52: premium icons, themes and some colours are paid and are both a purchase reason (161 payers at 4.50; DES_THEME lift ×3.65) and the top payer request (DES_ICON_WANT 561, lift ×2.83) — icons removed in 2024 and 2026 are asked back. Report 54: colours, pots and reminders gated resented (8, 3.00); more icons / colours / pots / themes requested (17, 4.35). Report 56: widgets free where 'free apps often have chopped widgets, or widgets just gated behind a subscription'; cosmetic limits (icons, colours, descriptions) cost two of four 4★ — 'i would have a 5 star rating if a few small changes could be made'. Report 57: dark mode Premium-gated ('shell out $13 for premium just for dark mode') against a photosensitive user; a colour picker praised by 22. Report 58: icons / emojis and colours / themes are the only repeat request (3 + 2) and what a 3★ asks for ('I feel like the app is depressed I hope you add colors') — ship the baseline expansion free first, and only then consider paid packs, because selling what a 3★ calls missing reads as a paywall on a deficiency. Report 69 (TheFor): 'having the free widget is awesome'; WID_GOOD 4 at a perfect 5.00. Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_WIDGET 41 (0.53%) from 2014-11; the 2023 removal of the old Today widget drew NEG_LOST_FEATURE 7 ('Any updates on when the widget will be fixed?', 3★); widgets shipped for iOS 17+. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): the widget arc — requested by the very first review (2025-01-10), shipped and praised 33 days later ('Great widget too for each habit'), then reported behind the paywall ('You have to pay for widgets', pt 1★, the whole review, single-source) and found too narrow (one habit per widget); U:widget_gap 5 (7.04%, 3.80★); §8.2.2 'a widget is the cheapest daily-retention surface a habit tracker has, and this one is gated and limited to a single habit at the same time as the free tier is limited to a single habit'; §8.6 E7 ungating the widget. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): interactive, stackable widgets are the app's perfect-score feature (PRAISE_WIDGET 27, 15.70%, 5.00★: 'The widgets are a game changer'; 'thanks to the widgets, I was able to easily keep a track of my study habits'; 'Widgets work effectively without needing to go back into the app'); gating them in 2025 produced the angriest reviews (MON_WIDGET_GATED 2) and a proposed compromise of two free widget sizes; REQ_WIDGET_MORE 5 (smaller/compact widgets) shipped in v2.5.0. Report 84 (HabitGrid): free interactive widgets are the third concrete strength (PRAISE_WIDGETS 8: 'keep a widget on my home screen, and tick the specific habit… and that's it!') and the only feature on both sides — 2 of the 7 problem reports involve them (a counter increment landing on the next day; only one widget with one habit); a reviewer asked for widgets five months after the first widget praise; §8.4 do not move widgets behind payment. Report 86 (Today): the Notification-Centre widget shipped Oct 2016 after a day-two request and became the main way many used the app ('son Widget super bien pensé'); the home-screen widget never shipped in 5.5 years — 'they urgently need a widget and I swear I'd pay premium' (mx 4★); 'its lack of a widget means I'll probably need to look for something else'; a reviewer asks for one 'for IOS 26'. Report 90 (Quit Bad Habits & Addiction): REQ_WIDGET 86 (14.01%, mean 4.53★) is the single most-requested thing in every era from 2023-02-06 to 2026-08-25 in an app that has no widget at all; 30 of the 87 four-star reviews ask for one and say it is the missing star ('without a widget the app is pointless', 3★; 'no home-screen widgets … deleting', kz); the reason is the mechanism — 'without one you can forget the app is even installed' — so §8.3 ships the counter widget free and tests premium *styles* inside the ad-free subscription: 'gate styling, not the number'.

<a id="c024"></a>
### C024 — Streaks / gamification

**Strong** · 38 apps · 91 cards · positive in 30 apps · negative in 12 apps · tied to a purchase in 1 apps

*Why Strong:* 38 apps, directions mixed (free 36, act 22, open 17)

| | reaction positive | reaction negative |
|---|---|---|
| **app makes it free** | free-praised — 8 apps | free-expected-but-broken — 1 apps |
| **app makes it paid** | paid-converts — 1 apps | paid-resented — 0 apps |

**Verdict from the table:** mixed — conditions decide

High-priority praise, moderate purchase factor. Report 10 (contested): streaks added to a non-punitive pet app generated their own defect stream (171, growing 74×) and pressure stream (96) — net-negative in the written record for an ADHD audience. Report 20: a streak counter was requested 71 times (mean 3.72) — always alongside, never instead of, the decaying strength score. Report 23: streak psychology is the highest-satisfaction theme (902, 12.41%, mean 4.75, 0.7% 1★ — reviewers get out of bed to preserve a streak); rewards/badges/levels are requested by fans (136, 1.87%, mean 4.43). Report 24: streak counters with 'freeze' passes and certificates; Duolingo is named for its streak freezes. Report 27: streaks are the core praised mechanic in a deliberately non-gamified app — no pets, no flashy graphics, no urgency; behaviour-change outcomes ('I'm on a 9 day vacuuming streak!') rose 0% → 11.9% across eras. Report 28: gamification (carrots, levels, rooms, a pet) is the differentiator in an 821-review corpus — but 10 (mean 2.40) say 'it's a game, not a tracker', an expectation mismatch the listing could pre-empt. Report 31: motivation through bars filling, streaks and sounds is praised by 200 rated 4–5★ ('an adult sticker chart!'); removing the streak count from the main list in v3.0 drew 52 complaints (100% E4), including medication and 30-day pill-cycle users; the report proposes a streak-on-list toggle and testing its default on logging frequency. Report 33: motivation / streaks praised by 130 (mean 4.75); non-daily streaks broke and the streak count on the complete button changed in redesigns. Report 47: the streak resets to zero on a miss — praised as motivating by 3 (5.00) and non-punitive framing praised by 4 ('scoring points, not losing them') vs empty squares demotivating 1; a cumulative total was added by 2025 after 2020–21 requests. Report 48: streak motivation 144 at mean 4.96 — the highest of any theme with n > 100 ('I can't bear to see it go'); 507-day and 1,000-day streaks; gamified rewards requested by 17 (4.47); a 2013–14 points system was disliked (10). Report 55: 'I completed a task because I didn't want to break my streak'; 'over 10K pushups… because I don't want to disappoint the app' — motivation layer 362 (17.89%, 4.86). Report 56: do not add streak pressure, scores or gamification to a product chosen for restraint — one streak request against 'no subscription, no guilt' and 39 restraint reviews. Report 58: streaks praised by 5 ('It's so fun every time I get a streak'). Report 60 (Mindway): the absence of streaks or any progress view is what payers name when they call the product under-built — the 'encouragement' and 'tracking consistency' they expected and did not get. Report 64 (Critique AI): XP, quests and leaderboards are 'unambiguously liked' (8, 1.91%, mean 4.00) and proposed as the free hook ('keep the workout and XP/leaderboard free'), with one sharp dissent that generated tasks 'seem more like XP grabs than anything else'. Report 76 (Way of Life): chains shipped 2015-11 and turned a request into praise — PR_CHAINS 0.3% E1 → 3.2% E4 (56 reviews, 'Chains is going to change my life') → 3.2% E6; REQ_STREAKS fell 18 → 3; REQ_GAMIFY 16 (4.06★) stays small; the red cell, not a reward, is the motivator ('I hate to break a winning steak'). Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): gamification — acorns, a squirrel, foxes, achievements, Badges (v2.6.4) and a purchasable Habit Forest (v3.0) — PRAISE_GAMIFY 5 (4.60★), REQ_MORE_GAMIFY 1; a Korean 3★ questions why the squirrel/acorns and the Focus tab exist; Badges are mentioned by no reviewer and the Forest by exactly one, eight months after shipping — 'two headline features, one mention between them'. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): the counter-position — no imposed gamification is praised (PRAISE_NO_GAMIFICATION 2, 5.00★) and zero reviews ask for social, leaderboard or AI features; v2.4.0 added a toggle to disable streak/consistency stats. Report 83 (Roubit): gamification at its most effective in the series — 'habit app × gacha game' called 'excellent' even by a user uninstalling; PRAISE_GAMIFICATION 76 (15.20%, 4.68★); META_CALLS_IT_GAME 6; Duolingo named both as a nag to avoid ('it's not gonna harass you like Duolingo') and as a widget model. Report 84 (HabitGrid): weekly and monthly streaks shipped in 1.0.16 and no review mentions them; the year grid, not a streak, is what reviewers call motivating. Report 85 (Habitica, 3,445 reviews): the fullest gamification in the series — PR_GAMIFY 468 (13.58%, mean 4.72★ vs corpus 3.71); three mechanisms: instant reward (XP and gold on the tick), consequence (missed Dailies cost health, and in a party hurt friends: 'I still have adhd but now I feel anxious that my team could get dmg because of me not doing the dishes'), collection (eggs, pets, mounts: 'I am constantly doing chores just to earn food for them'); U_OUTCOME 502 (14.57%, 4.70★); PR_STICKY 78; the cost side: long-term players say the game runs out ('they are all essentially the same'; 'A progressão fica meio estagnada'), REQ_CONTENT 79 asks for battles and an endgame, and non-gamers still find value (SEG_NONGAMER 21: 'Best habit tracking app, even without the gamification'). Report 86 (Today): 'It doesn't give you confetti or a cookie' is praise; badges and milestones exist and are unremarked; NEG_REDESIGN objected to a shrunken calendar mark — the visual record, not a reward, is the motivator. Report 90 (Quit Bad Habits & Addiction): the counter *is* the gamification — 'breaking big numbers hurts far more than the urge to smoke'; 'seeing the numbers clearly calms me more than a pile of praise' — and the app has no streak badges, levels or rewards at all; the requests are for a growth visual and milestones (U:motivation_layer_request 49, 7.98%), not for points.

<a id="c080"></a>
### C080 — Colour themes / dark mode

**Strong** · 37 apps · 82 cards · positive in 15 apps · negative in 24 apps · tied to a purchase in 2 apps

*Why Strong:* 37 apps, directions mixed (free 23, act 23, open 20)

| | reaction positive | reaction negative |
|---|---|---|
| **app makes it free** | free-praised — 3 apps | free-expected-but-broken — 0 apps |
| **app makes it paid** | paid-converts — 1 apps | paid-resented — 3 apps |

**Verdict from the table:** evidence leans free (paid is mostly resented)

'Only green' draws requests; cheap. Report 10: dark mode requested since 2022 as an accessibility need (migraine, light sensitivity). Report 20: dark mode moved from free-ish to paid in the 2021 conversion (89 reviews, mean 2.69) and was a named purchase trigger. Report 24: dark mode requested by 43, 58.1% of them 4–5★ — cheap and asked for by advocates. Report 29: dark mode absent — 15 requests (4.10%, mean 4.67, the highest-satisfaction request group), India 8.77% (2.9× global), 'it's what's missing for 5 stars'. Report 31: dark mode / themes 18; a German visually impaired reviewer: 'no accessibility features, no dark mode, no localisation … unusable'. Report 33: dark mode and themes were Premium in 2019–20; 48 request themes / colours. Report 43: per-habit colours / icons requested by 4 (mean 4.50); dark mode praised. Report 46: dark mode paywalled (2020, June 2024) — the report's #7 fix returns it to the free tier. Report 47: dark mode must keep every control legible — time-picker digits were unreadable in dark mode (2); more colours requested 3 (2019–20), later unlocked by watching a video. Report 48: dark mode requested by 11 (4.64). Report 50: colour coding, app-wide font, text size, dark mode, week-start day and per-habit units praised (customisation 25, 4.80); hex colours, longer habit titles, hide streak count requested. Report 52: dark mode requested (70, weak). Report 54: dark mode requested (5), once for light sensitivity. Report 55: dark mode shipped mid-2020 with 'black writing on the black background' (BUG_DARK 10, 1.90). Report 56: a dark / OLED design praised ('Cool OLED and Minimal Design'); dark mode (Feb) and light mode (Jul) requested five months apart. Report 57: dark mode Premium-gated (US) against a photosensitive user's accessibility need; white text on a white background with Premium themes. Report 59 (Tappsk): REQ_DARK (13) ends in 2021-10, consistent with a dark theme shipping; REQ_THEMES 70, REQ_ICON 20, REQ_FONT 21 continue. Report 72 (Habit Hearts): dark mode (2, both 2024–25; nobody since — verify whether it shipped). Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_THEMES 54 (0.70%, 4.22★) across the whole span 2011 → 2026; themes shipped 2019-07 (Dark, Serenity, Retro C64, Light, Rose; PR_THEMES 14 at 4.86★) with some sold (MON_BUY_ITEMS 27, 16.48× among purchasers); 'this app keeps its dark mode theme locked behind a paid upgrade' (3★). Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): REQ_DARKMODE 1 (5★). Report 89 (Check Calendar): dark mode was moved behind payment in 2022 (PAY_FEATURE_REVERSAL, 1★) and is praised when present (PRAISE_DARK_MODE 3: 'I love the OLED black color'); DEF_DARK_FLASH 1 — 'dark mode flashes on every open' (cn, 2021). Research: Quit Habit Decision.md — a literal, fixable contrast defect in the #1 app: quit habits set to 0 per day render as 'nothing is readable because of the all dark colors', so the zero-target state needs its own dark-mode check.

<a id="c020"></a>
### C020 — Data export / backup / CSV

**Strong** · 35 apps · 87 cards · positive in 11 apps · negative in 27 apps · tied to a purchase in 3 apps

*Why Strong:* 35 apps, directions mixed (act 39, free 22, open 11)

| | reaction positive | reaction negative |
|---|---|---|
| **app makes it free** | free-praised — 2 apps | free-expected-but-broken — 1 apps |
| **app makes it paid** | paid-converts — 2 apps | paid-resented — 3 apps |

**Verdict from the table:** mixed — conditions decide

Requested a lot from happy users, rarely a purchase trigger — charging for it generates requests, not revenue. Report 18: export was asked for from the app's fifth month to its last, named as a purchase condition twice ('add export and I'll subscribe for life'), and is the honest answer to five years of unresolved data-loss reports — it lets users protect themselves. Report 20: export never shipped (9 requests, mean 4.44). Report 23: CSV export is included in the one-time price. Report 25: CSV export exists but is described as weak (3). Report 27: data export is praised ('export data for nerdy kind') and the one-tap note export was removed in 2025, producing the only 2★. Report 28: no export mentioned; cloud sync paid. Report 29: add a local CSV/JSON export to Files, account-free, so a date bug can never again mean total loss — three independent export/backup requests. Report 31: backup to Dropbox/iCloud and CSV export were manual only with a repeated backup nag; export hangs ('I can't export my data to move to another app because it hangs on the CSV export') — export is the exit door, keep it open and fast; export to Google Drive was a purchase trigger. Report 33: CSV export was removed with Habitify X (Aug 2020) and back from 2022. Report 34: CSV export disabled in Feb 2026 ('Out of nowhere … years of data are stuck in this app'; 'Vendor Lock', 1★) and a paid backup required before deleting (1★) — both data-lock-in reviews are 1★ (mean 1.00) in a no-account app where export is the only exit. Report 41: CSV export shipped Feb 2023 after a year of requests ('Now that the developer has added CSV export… the app is 5-star awesome for me') and is named as a purchase reason ('so my data is safe'); praised by 14 (mean 4.71). Report 42: no export or backup; history beyond ~2 weeks paywalled ('if you don't pay you won't see last month's result'). Report 43: CSV / PDF export requested by 2; no export exists in a local-storage app that lost four-year histories. Report 46: export / backup / print requested by 3 in an app that lost users' history. Report 47: sharing / export requested by 3, RecStyle named as the CSV model. Report 48: CSV export is premium, praised and occasionally broken (16 requests, 4 export bugs). Report 52: data export requested (59, weak). Report 55: CSV / Excel export is paid and bought for; 5 of 15 export reviews report failures. Report 57: backup is manual Dropbox (Jan 2020) and Premium-gated — 'so you can't back up at all unless you buy — this is practically blackmail'. Report 65 (Rabit): backup moved behind the paywall in 2023 while restore failed for payers; zero export requests in six years. Report 76 (Way of Life): CSV/Excel export is free and praised (PR_EXPORT 50, 4.84★); NEG_EXPORT_FORMAT 4; REQ_IMPORT 6. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): CSV export praised as 'no lock-in' (PRAISE_EXPORT 1); REQ_IMPORT 2 (5.00★) — data import / migration 'directly reduces switching cost into the product, and pairs with the existing CSV export'. Report 83 (Roubit): no export or backup request appears in 500 reviews — until the diary tab blanked; §8.1 offer diary export as the fallback for a multi-year personal record. Report 84 (HabitGrid): import/export exists per the listing and is mentioned by zero of 86 reviews; the one data-safety warning and the one account request both come from users who did not find it. Report 86 (Today): 'Manage Data' export/delete shipped May 2018 ('Kudos for the new Manage Data section… If only more companies would follow suit'); REQ_EXPORT 14; a twenty-item 2016 request list asked for Excel export. Report 89 (Check Calendar): CSV export is in the listing and §8.2 relies on it — keep it available after the trial so locked history can leave; REQ_LOCAL_EXPORT 1 asks for a non-cloud export on privacy grounds.
