<a id="c023"></a>
### C023 — Interactive widget check-off

**Strong** · 35 apps · 98 cards · positive in 10 apps · negative in 27 apps · tied to a purchase in 2 apps

*Why Strong:* 35 apps, directions mixed (act 44, free 21, open 15)

| | reaction positive | reaction negative |
|---|---|---|
| **app makes it free** | free-praised — 2 apps | free-expected-but-broken — 1 apps |
| **app makes it paid** | paid-converts — 1 apps | paid-resented — 0 apps |

**Verdict from the table:** mixed — conditions decide

Mark done without opening the app; small volume, very high intent. Report 18: 'let me check off without launching the app' was the single most-repeated widget request across five years and every language; some builds fixed it (Jul 2025) and then it regressed. Report 23: an interactive Today-view widget shipped Jan 2017 to enthusiasm, was lost at iOS 14 (Sept 2020) and asked for back continuously for five years (36 named requests) — one of the top three reasons for a downgrade from a previously-happy user; restore it via App Intents. Report 26: an interactive widget to tick from the home screen requested (~5); the garden-view widget is free. Report 27: reviewers wrote the widget spec — 'a small widget that just showed the current streak count for a single goal'; 'a streak counter on the widget like duolingo'; 'a grayed out version if it's still to do and a coloured version if it's done'; tappable to check off — requested in 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026; in a streak app the widget is the retention surface. Report 28: an interactive check-off widget requested continuously for four and a half years by satisfied users (mean 4.64, zero negatives). Report 29: a Home Screen widget showing today's list requested by 16 across 26 months, 7 of them in 2026. Report 31: a tappable Today-view widget (2018–2021) was replaced in Oct 2021 by a non-interactive home/lock-screen widget limited to 4 habits (a user with a memory disability 'requesting a refund'); before that, the app had no iOS 14 widget for a year — 73 of 451 reviews (16.2%) Sep 2020 – Sep 2021 and 14.0% of E2 asked about it; the widget peaks in the 4★ band (12.6% vs 3.8%). Report 33: the 2016 Today widget was removed ('the entire reason I paid'), iOS 14 widgets were non-interactive, and the May 2025 redesign removed compact, incremental (+1) and streak widgets — widget complaints 6.3% of 2025, the one surface still worsening; interactive widgets named as the 4★ → 5★ piece. Report 34: 7 interactive-widget requests, all after static widgets shipped (Mar 2024) — 'The widgets still aren't interactive' (Feb 2026). Report 36: 'instead of taking advantage of the iOS 17 update with interactive widgets, they preferred to make that option paid' (2★); interactive widget requested by 4. Report 48: widget interactivity was removed after arriving ~2020; the request persists (20). Report 50: widgets with check-off shipped by Nov 2024 after a Mar 2024 request; interactive check-off, quick-append journal, compact and weekly-progress widgets still requested (3); widget lag (1). Report 52: 'Maybe the most important features of ShineDay are its widgets. Being able to check off completed habits without opening the app' — when iOS 14 replaced tap-to-check with a ring that opens the app (Oct 2020) 55 widget-bug reviews arrived in one month; check-in was removed from the widget again in 2026. Report 53: check off from the widget, hide completed, more habits per widget (WIDGET_WANT 18). Report 54: the top request (41, 11.11%, 4.29; P1 7.5% → P3 17.6%, open since Oct 2020, first asked one month after iOS 14), 19 of them five-star and a named purchase blocker for 3 of 5 ('If there were a home-screen widget I'd open it far more often — then I'd be more willing to buy', TW); framed as retention by ADHD and autistic users ('once it's closed i never use it'); D3: build it as a completion surface, not a display surface. Report 55: widget or notification check-off requested (WIDGET_WANT 16). Report 56: per-habit home-screen widgets with one-tap completion are the differentiator (9 of 67 name them; 'the empty dots on my home screen guilt trip me into being productive and honestly? it works'); a multi-habit widget designed in detail (dates across, habits down), more than 4 widgets and transparency requested; a widget tap that opened the app instead of completing broke the most-praised interaction (fixed in v2.3.2). Report 57: the widget tap launched the app instead of checking in from the iOS 14 rewrite (Nov 2020) until Dec 2023 — 16 reviews ('if it's a widget the check should happen right there — why is the app launching?'; 'give us back checking from the widget'), zero after. Report 58: 'THE WIDGET that is clickable?? the best ever'; 'The widget option is legit a life saver!'. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): a widget that shows the next unfinished habit is requested (UZ, 4★); widgets are credited with the strongest outcome statement in the corpus. Report 69 (TheFor): after the free widget shipped, the next ask (the most recent review, 2026-09-02) is interactive — 'a widget that allows me to see all my habits and their progress and allows me to check them off'; B2. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): some users keep the habit and lose the app — 'I couldn't even keep up opening this app every day' (12 votes); 'This is no different from a game's daily login bonus'; widget requests (17, 0.3% → 2.4% of eras) ask for the goal to be visible without opening the app (§8.8). Report 71 (MyStreaks): 'Home Screen widget for quick check-off… that is literally my only feedback' (5★, Apr 2023) — still absent after 25 releases, 'the cheapest item… open the longest', aligned with the most-praised mechanic, the 3-click check-off. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): a widget requested 2023 → 2026 while the listing now claims widgets — possibly discoverability. Report 75 (Habit Streak): three of the first six reviews asked for a widget; it shipped by May 2025; demand then moved up the stack — complete a habit from the widget ('aus dem Widget heraus… als erledigt markieren'), the streak on the Lock Screen ('el fuego con el numero de días… en la pantalla bloqueada'), milestone widget art at 7 / 30 / 60 / 90 days citing chess.com; 8 of 41 (19.51%, cohort mean 4.75) touch the widget — 'the retention surface'; what users want on it is the streak number itself. Report 89 (Check Calendar): REQ_WIDGET 5 (2022-01 → 2025-01) stopped once widgets appeared in the listing — and not one of 253 reviews praises the widget; the one 2026 widget request asks to tick several habits from it (REQ_WIDGET_MULTI); §8.9 widgets are not a priority. Report 90 (Quit Bad Habits & Addiction): the widget requests are for visibility of the count on the lock and home screen (second- and third-most-voted reviews in the corpus, 33 and 32 votes), not for interaction; one 2026 request asks to mark progress from it.

<a id="c073"></a>
### C073 — Manual reordering, renaming and editing of habits/tasks — free

**Strong** · 35 apps · 86 cards · positive in 5 apps · negative in 28 apps

*Why Strong:* 35 apps, directions mixed (act 39, free 26, open 6)

| | reaction positive | reaction negative |
|---|---|---|
| **app makes it free** | free-praised — 1 apps | free-expected-but-broken — 1 apps |
| **app makes it paid** | paid-converts — 0 apps | paid-resented — 1 apps |

**Verdict from the table:** mixed — conditions decide

Trivial, requested for years by 5★ users; best effort-to-goodwill ratio. In report 4 rename/reorder was gated and it was the top complaint among paying users. Report 25: habit/group order resets itself (11, 0.84%) — two long-term users left over it; make reordering a drag gesture. Report 26: reorder habits / per-habit gardens / categories requested by 18 (0.47%). Report 27: habit reordering shipped (between Sept 2024 and Aug 2025) and the order does not stick ('they keep getting jumbled up and going back to the wrong spots'); one user avoids reordering for fear of data loss; another wants grouping by the time a habit is set for. Report 29: 'This could be my perfect habit tracker if I could only reorder the list of tasks… Without it the app is virtually useless' (2★); two of four ask to sort by reminder time, which needs no new data model. Report 31: custom order and forced grouping (22) and an edited habit jumping to the top of the list drew complaints — restore custom ordering and stop moving edited habits. Report 33: custom ordering that sticks requested / broken in 47 (90 routines; broken in v10.7.4–10.7.5 and again in 2026). Report 36: cannot delete or rename a habit easily (10, mean 3.00) and a habit-name character limit (3). Report 43: drag-to-reorder within time windows requested by 7 and shipped Nov 2025 ('The ability to program your day windows and reorder items in time windows is fantastic'); bulk edit across a group 1. Report 46: cannot reorder habits (10, mean 4.10); a limited history view (9). Report 47: reorder / sort habits requested by 6 (all JP, mean 4.33); habit order scrambled by an update in 2022 (5). Report 48: can't edit / delete a log entry 32 (3.22); backfill history praised by 13. Report 50: an August 2026 update removed editing or deleting a single occurrence of a recurring habit ('I love this but I was really disappointed in the update that took away ability to modify time or delete single reoccurring events in a day') — fix F5: a straight revert. Report 54: reorder / drag habits (13, 4.54; 5 payers). Report 55: in 2026 habits cannot be deleted or deactivated. Report 56: reorder requests (4) stopped dead once reordering shipped, because it is visible in the list. Report 57: 27 could not find how to delete or edit a habit though the function exists ('How on earth can you make a habit app and not be able to delete the habits'; 'I got angry and deleted the app'; 'I almost threw my phone') — a user documented it publicly; 'it should be a clear option when viewing the habit detailed view'. Report 68 (Ultiself): 'sort those habits chronologically' — REQ_REORDER 7. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): row reordering (4) named as the thing blocking one purchase — possibly already available via long-press. Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_REORDER 16 (0.21%, 2011 → 2025) and NEG_EDIT_NAME 3 ('cannot edit items', 2012 → 2015) — both long since fixed but they recur for years. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): REQ_SORT 1 (5★) — sort or organise habits. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): REQ_REORDER 1 shipped in v2.4.2/2.5.0 and is still reported broken by the corpus's final reviewer; editing an existing board reported as paid by one 2★ ('You don t let me modifie my habits whitout paying'). Report 86 (Today): reorder/sort was added but 'slow' (two reports); parent/child habits requested in a 2016 twenty-item list. Report 88 (GetHabit): FUNC_LIMITED 13 — 'you can't change the name of a habit, you can't add more habit categories, you cant change the order of habits within a category' (mx); §8.8 editable habits as table stakes.

<a id="c010"></a>
### C010 — Backfill missed days / edit start date

**Strong** · 34 apps · 74 cards · positive in 13 apps · negative in 24 apps · tied to a purchase in 1 apps

*Why Strong:* 34 apps, directions mixed (act 33, free 28, open 5)

| | reaction positive | reaction negative |
|---|---|---|
| **app makes it free** | free-praised — 4 apps | free-expected-but-broken — 1 apps |
| **app makes it paid** | paid-converts — 0 apps | paid-resented — 0 apps |

**Verdict from the table:** only free-tier evidence

Users accept a bounded free backfill window. Report 8 contests it: a ~7-day backfill window in a free app with weak history views was the worst-rated request (mean 3.52). Report 16: logging only today and yesterday cost earned streaks ('I forgot to log 2 days ago… my streak is permanently reset'); 33 requests from mostly 3–4★ users, unshipped for 31 months. Report 19: 'I did the habit so why can't I go back and track it?' — back-dating a completed habit was broken or absent. Report 23: 'today or yesterday?' retroactive completion and calendar backfill are included; backfill older days still requested 76 times (1.05%). Report 24: cannot undo a tick or backfill a missed day (70, mean 2.700) — the emotional cost is disproportionate because it breaks streaks the product made meaningful. Report 26: backfill the previous day and a configurable day boundary (29 verified, 0.76%) — night-owl and after-midnight complaints recur across five years; a next-day 'did you do it?' prompt exists and is praised. Report 27: backfill by tapping past dates is praised (and broke for the annual grid in 2025); two reviewers want to import an existing streak by start date ('the streak being automatically completed from that date, moving to a new phone was a bit tedious'). Report 30: editing history works inside the current month but not for prior months (asked politely by a 5★). Report 34: back-filling and long-press to mark yesterday praised by 10 (mean 4.90); editing days from the month calendar requested by 6, and one US reviewer left over it. Report 41: a payer upgraded specifically to backfill an 8-day streak and backfilling did not exist (1★); can't backfill / edit past days 5 (mean 3.40). Report 43: backfilling a day after it has passed requested by 4 (mean 3.75). Report 47: back-dating shipped 29 March 2020 after being 16% of 2019 reviews and is praised as available by 7 (all JP); the start-date-before-creation option exists but is hidden — 21 requests (3.57%), last July 2026, two reviewers could not find it after reading it existed; see [[C262]] for the 2024 video gate. Report 54: backfill only to yesterday — 15 (4.07%, 3.67); 'deleted on the second day because of the issue' (UA); if the schedule says Mon/Wed/Thu and you worked out Tuesday, you cannot record it at all. Report 55: log earlier days including before install — part of the praised tracking model. Report 56: back-dating existed but was hard to find — requested in June, 'a little hard' in July, 'super easy' in August. Report 57: past-date check-in went from top complaint (13, 2019–20: 'if you forget to track something you're just out of luck') to differentiator (4 praise at 5.000: 'ridiculously easy to add data for previous dates') — the one confirmed fix-to-differentiator in the corpus. Report 59 (Tappsk): REQ_BACKFILL 62 (rising to 0.8% in the latest era) — unfinished tasks roll to today and cannot be marked done for the day they were done ('если я выполнила задачу в 00:01 и хочу отметить её выполненной за предыдущую дату' — did it at 00:01 and want to mark it for the previous date); the report's experiment: mark done for a past date. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): any past day can be edited and a premium buyer was actively using the edit-previous-day buttons when the June build broke them; the counter-request is a lock, not removal. Report 65 (Rabit): marking the previous day was the capability premium took at launch (Nov 2020). Report 75 (Habit Streak): no backfill — 'j'ai commencé une habitude il y a une semaine et pour l'instant j'ai 0 % de réussite… j'ai pas la possibilité de marquer ce que j'ai fait avant… ça me décourage' (5★, the only helpful-voted review, asking twice for a reply) — 'the only request in the corpus that is demonstrably causing disengagement'; E5 measure D7 retention of users who backfill. Report 76 (Way of Life): NEG_BACKFILL 39 (0.50%, 3.79★, 2012 → 2024, 'hard to log past days'; jp 4.22×) against PR_BACKFILL 8 at 5.00★ once possible; REQ_FUTURE_ENTRY 9 want to mark future days; REQ_DAY_ROLLOVER 9 want a custom day end. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): back-dated entry exists but bulk back-entry is painful (UX_BULK_ENTRY 1, 5★). Report 84 (HabitGrid): marking past days is praised ('You can mark progress for past days and add a note. Ideal'). Report 86 (Today): REQ_BACKFILL 18 (2016 → 2021) — 'partially, then made harder'; the Nov 2018 redesign made checking in for an old day three taps. Report 89 (Check Calendar): PRAISE_BACKFILL 1 (5★) — editing past days is part of U:calendar_core (4.72★).

<a id="c013"></a>
### C013 — Cloud sync / multi-device as the paid differentiator

**Strong** · 33 apps · 87 cards · positive in 12 apps · negative in 26 apps · tied to a purchase in 8 apps

*Why Strong:* 33 apps, directions mixed (act 27, paid 21, open 14)

| | reaction positive | reaction negative |
|---|---|---|
| **app makes it free** | free-praised — 0 apps | free-expected-but-broken — 1 apps |
| **app makes it paid** | paid-converts — 5 apps | paid-resented — 2 apps |

**Verdict from the table:** evidence leans paid (paid mostly converts)

Strongest true differentiator among buyers (lift ×9.8). Report 7: absent for 3+ years, sync was the #1 3★/4★ theme with named willingness to pay; ship it opt-in and end-to-end (CloudKit private database) to keep a no-account privacy promise. Report 28: cloud sync is bundled with any purchase ('I now realize just buying anything gives u cloud access'; 'il faut payer pour jumeler les comptes'); multi-device sync is named as the advantage over Finch. Report 30: iCloud sync and colour themes are advertised paid features that no reviewer in any market or period mentions. Report 33: one purchase covering iPhone, iPad, Watch, Mac, web, Android and Windows is a leading purchase trigger — and every platform that lagged became a support case (see C251). Report 47: account-based e-mail backup and sync (beta 2020, free in 'version 2.0', Feb 2024) spans iPhone, Android and iPad ('애플이랑 삼성 연동'); cross-platform sync unreliable in 2022; sync / backup failures 16 (mean 2.25, 7 in 10–18 Dec 2019 — '同期中ですとの表示が一向におわらず'); a platform bundle is a stated purchase condition ('Macのリリース、ウィジェット導入、iPadとの同期を求めます。そしたら課金します', 2026). Report 48: cross-device sync is the paid feature most often named as the purchase reason; multi-platform praise recovered from 0.78% to 3.13% with the Mac app (Mar 2022), yet sync failure is the one reliability theme that never improved (11 / 12 / 12 / 13 per era) and is the most common reliability complaint in 2022–26. Report 50: one account across iPhone, iPad and Mac, free within the cap. Report 54: iCloud sync / backup absent (8, 4.12) — 'I don't give it 5 stars because it lacks iCloud sync'. Report 55: cross-device sync was the headline paid feature and the most often named purchase reason (19 of 165 payers), mostly in 1–2★ because it failed ('If you are about to buy it for the sync option. I suggest you keep your money'; 'Paid £17.49 to sync phone/iPad/watch and it doesn't work'); SYNC_BUG 62 (1.90) with a 7.12× payer lift and 'servers are dead' by 2019. Report 56: optional iCloud sync shipped free and headlines a positive review ('Simple, free, privacy friendly - optional icloud sync'). Report 57: cross-device is the largest unmet need in the product's history — 72 (9.24%): sync 44, iPad 21, Mac 8, backup 17 — flat across eras (29 / 28 / 27) and 84% Korean; one JP report of iCloud working (2024) against six later Korean 'it doesn't'; a Premium user in 2026 'I bought Premium and iPad doesn't seem to sync'. Report 58: cross-device use requested by 2 (a 3★ whose whole review is 'so I can work in two different places') against 2 who chose the app because it has no account — if sync ships it must be optional and never a precondition for first use; accounts and servers bring the 1★ failure classes the corpus is free of. Report 59 (Tappsk): iCloud sync between devices is Premium and reviewers ask for it free ('в бесплатной версии синхронизировать устройства нельзя'; 'оставить синхронизацию в бесплатной версии'); the Mac app was sold separately in 2020–22 (MON_PER_DEVICE 59: 'Она платная для тех кто уже премиум?') and later folded into Premium. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): 'looked really promising and reasonably priced, but does not let you sync between your Phone and iPad' (US, 1★) — a willing buyer who did not buy solely for this; 'revenue-blocking, not cosmetic'. Report 65 (Rabit): platform_gaps 55 (11.04%, mean 4.25) — widget, Watch, iPad, desktop, sync — 'Rabit exists on exactly one surface'; SYNC_REQ 4 (4.75) and the entitlement failures share a root, no reliable account layer (S6). Report 69 (TheFor): sync_any 5 (6.25%, mean 4.20) — the corpus's only 3★ ('Love that the free version includes unlimited habits. And the paid version is a great price. However, needs to be able to sync across devices'), two 4★ iPhone ↔ iPad failures, two 5★ 'lack of iCloud sync… a notable drawback'; every one otherwise positive — 'the cheapest kind of rating to recover'; rising 0% → 7.0% → 11.8%; M2 / X1: sync is 'the classic additive premium feature' and Pro's first describable benefit. Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_SYNC 139 (1.79%, 4.01★) in every era for 14 years, second most frequent request, 2.72× over-represented among purchasers; 'at this point I would pay to sync' (5★); 'A five star app without iCloud support is a one star app' (gb 1★); 'Five stars if I could open the app on any device and see my data' (3★); REV_STAR_TACTIC 19 make the fifth star conditional; §8.5 ship iCloud sync to iPad before a Watch app — sync is the paid feature reviewers say they would pay for. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): REQ_ICLOUD 2 (4.50★) — iCloud sync / backup / an account; the only account mention in 71 reviews is a request for one; 'I totally recommend it' from the 4★ who wants sync between devices. Research: Feature Gating vs Quantity.md — device sync/backup is named as one of the four capabilities habit apps conventionally gate (with Apple Watch, widgets and detailed analytics), and a Zapier review of free project managers is cited for the same split: unlimited tasks and collaboration drive free adoption while premium monetises cloud sync and reporting.

<a id="c016"></a>
### C016 — Skip / holiday / pause mode (pause a habit or counter without losing history)

**Strong** · 33 apps · 83 cards · positive in 9 apps · negative in 22 apps · tied to a purchase in 2 apps

*Why Strong:* 33 apps, directions mixed (act 38, open 18, free 11)

| | reaction positive | reaction negative |
|---|---|---|
| **app makes it free** | free-praised — 3 apps | free-expected-but-broken — 1 apps |
| **app makes it paid** | paid-converts — 1 apps | paid-resented — 0 apps |

**Verdict from the table:** mixed — conditions decide

Minor purchase factor; free or paid open. In report 3, pause/stop/archive is the highest-leverage missing feature (44 requests at mean 4.02, 'the only thing between me and 5★'). Report 23: pausing a task and un-pausing it marked the paused days as missed and destroyed the streak — the defect defeats the feature's entire purpose; reported 2023–24 with no visible fix (57 archive/pause mentions). Report 25: vacation/pause, skip-a-day ('Jump'), mark-not-done ('Cancel') and archive all exist and are praised. Report 26: a vacation/pause mode is requested with flexible recurrence (12). Report 27: a goal end date so a completed goal stops repeating but stays visible, and habit archiving, were asked for by a 3★ reviewer — both appear on the listing and were not findable. Report 28: 'the only way to remove a habit from view is to delete it, but that results in losing all its data'; one wants to mark a routine as 'established' and retire it. Report 29: an end-date / no-end-date control requested (4) — set a habit with no end and change it later. Report 30: there is no habit end-date, so deleting a finished habit wipes its history, and Skip breaks the daily completion ring so users feel they failed a day they completed — one frequency + end-date feature closes both. Report 31: every-N-days, bi-weekly, skip, vacation mode and end dates requested by 84 (mean 3.12) — 'lose a 100+ day streak because … vacation'; a streak freeze is named as the missing piece between 4★ and 5★. Report 33: pause / vacation mode never existed (18 requests; a 'reschedule' swipe) — the report asks for a pause that preserves streaks. Report 34: skip / pause / sick day requested by 5 ('i am sick and cannot swim … i dont want to loose my results'). Report 46: skip marks — a half-square and a triangle — with a 'don't skip twice' rule are praised by 41 (mean 4.93: 'no punishment other than a break in the color gradient') and confuse 19 for seven years ('What does the triangle and squares mean?????'; a subscriber who will 'cancel until this is fixed') — a legend reachable from the grid. Report 48: no skip / vacation mode (13) and weekly goals that still demand a daily answer (21 weekday-scheduling) are 'the two structural scoring complaints', sustained across all five eras from otherwise-happy users — report's change #10. Report 50: streak freeze / habit pause is the most-requested missing capability (3, mean 4.33) and archive (2) — 'It makes me feel guilty for losing my streaks, but like sometimes your routine has to change for a few days!'; 'it's much easier for me to continue a streak when it's large rather than from ground zero'; skipped days visually distinct (1) — the report's S4: ship freeze / pause / archive together as retention mechanics. Report 53: the most-upvoted review in the corpus (274 votes) asks for archive / pause — 'to keep my page organized I have to delete some habits, which means losing all the records'; skips that don't count as failures (CORE_SKIP 20, 4.20). Report 55: a sick / skip day that keeps the streak (CORE_SKIP 5). Report 57: a skip / rest day shipped mid-2024 ('which I've been eagerly waiting for') but only reachable from the calendar step and still requested after. Report 65 (Rabit): S3 — skip / exempt a legitimately impossible day without killing the plant (CORE_SKIP 2), 'turns the gamification's biggest liability into a fair mechanic'. Report 68 (Ultiself): 'flagging a day as sick day' (4★). Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): a two-day-miss reset with no pause — 'sometimes you can't do it when you're unwell' (1★); 「生理が来ると、2日くらいお休みしたい人も中にはいるのです。」 (period); a school trip; REQ_PAUSE 10; §8.6: a limited honest rest day (e.g. two per cycle) plus an optional strict mode — 'Both camps have existed since 2018, so a single rule will keep losing one of them'. Report 76 (Way of Life): a skip state that keeps the chain is loved — 'skip option for when you have days where you need to skip without breaking your chain'; PR_SKIP 99 (1.28%, 4.66★); the request REQ_SKIP (7, 2011) stopped the moment it shipped (2012-05). Report 85 (Habitica): 'rest in the inn' pauses the health penalty but is undiscoverable (PR_REST 6, REQ_PAUSE 7); §8.9 an illness mode. Report 86 (Today): REQ_SKIP 11 (illness, travel, a bad mental-health day) + REQ_ARCHIVE 11 — the corpus's most-upvoted request (22 up / 36): 'could you add a way to stop a habit? Sometimes a habit is already formed or no longer needed, but currently you can only delete it, and all the data goes with it' (cn 5★); 'the design forces a user who succeeded to destroy their record of succeeding'; a skip exists and 'nobody understands it'. Report 90 (Quit Bad Habits & Addiction): REQ_RELAPSE_OPTIONS 4 — 'you can't pause and keep your progress'; users instead log a slip as a note to avoid zeroing two weeks ([[C308]]).

<a id="c019"></a>
### C019 — Quit-habit / bad-habit mode — a counter that counts up from the last relapse, with its own vocabulary, relapse record and non-punitive reset

**Strong** · 30 apps · 75 cards · positive in 17 apps · negative in 14 apps

*Why Strong:* 30 apps, directions mixed (act 24, open 18, free 16)

| | reaction positive | reaction negative |
|---|---|---|
| **app makes it free** | free-praised — 4 apps | free-expected-but-broken — 0 apps |
| **app makes it paid** | paid-converts — 1 apps | paid-resented — 0 apps |

**Verdict from the table:** mixed — conditions decide

Well received where shipped; see Quit Habit Decision research doc. Report 23: negative ('don't') tasks shipped in v3.0, Jul 2017. Report 25: a 'bad habit' mode exists and counts against the cap; a bad-habit limit exceeded at 200% is scored as success; a long review asks whether to name it 'smoked' or 'didn't smoke'. Report 31: build and quit habits in one list is praised by 96 ('the ONLY app I've found that does that'); quit-to-zero goals were removed in Mar 2022 and Jan 2023 (sobriety tracking), and 30 find quit/zero-goal habits confusing — restore them. Report 33: bad-habit / limit tracking done well requested by 23 — a tap per cigarette, auto-fail over the limit. Report 34: bad-habit / quit tracking 6 — 'I'd rather not see TO DO next to bad habits'. Report 36: a quit-a-habit inverse mode requested once. Report 41: break-a-bad-habit mode (max units per day) praised by 36 (mean 4.69); Screen Time as a trackable bad habit requested by 4. Report 43: negative / 'avoid' habit tracking requested by 3. Report 46: a habit-breaking mode (colour fades when the bad habit is logged) is praised by 42 (mean 4.98) — alcohol, sugar, screen time — though its logic is unclear to some. Report 48: bad-habit / 'less is better' tracking (a limit, not a goal; red / green inverts) praised by 105 (2.39%, 4.81) — a quit-smoking reviewer benchmarked 10+ rivals; yes / no semantics turn ambiguous in bad-habit logging (12). Report 50: a quit / reduce mode with a reset-on-relapse counter praised by 6 (4.83) — trichotillomania ('The fact that I have to reset the tracker every time I "fall back" gives me the more motivation'), drinking. Report 52: bad habits that deduct reward points (78, weak, mean 4.8). Report 53: limits and zero goals — 'no more than 3 coffees', count-down counters (CORE_BAD 21, 3.76). Report 54: quit-habit tracking requested (4). Report 55: quit-habit use for smoking, alcohol, nail-biting and NoFap (USE_QUIT 46, 4.83) via 'not more than' goals — 'a nail biter for 26 years but getting to tap yes! everyday is exactly what I needed to finally stop'. Report 76 (Way of Life): good and bad habits in one grid, colours inverting for habits to avoid — 'it reverses the red/green colours for yes and no' (5★); PR_YESNO 73; USE_ADDICTION 46 at mean 4.96★ ('Today marks 1 month clean'); REQ_NEUTRAL_HABIT 5 want a third, neutral kind. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): REQ_NEGATIVE_HABIT 2 (5.00★) — negative / inverse boards, both German, 17 months apart, same design (smoking; unfulfilled days as the streak) — 'opens the quit-habit use case the product currently cannot serve'. Report 86 (Today): a limit-type habit is the missing shape — 'if I only want to limit my intake to, say, two sodas a day, I can't both log each drink and show success for not going over the limit' (5★); REQ_BREAKBAD 15; USE_QUIT 16 (soda, meat, smoking, drinking). Report 90 (Quit Bad Habits & Addiction, 614 reviews, 4.40★): a pure quit-tracker — time since quitting to the second, unlimited habits, a personal record, an attempts counter, a relapse button with a dated note — earns U:praise_any 476 (77.52%) and U:outcome_any 118 (19.22%, mean 4.92★: 'not smoking for 2 years'; 'quit smoking and drugs with the app'); what is quit: smoking or vaping 17, self-harm 13, alcohol 10, drugs 8, food or weight 8, sexual 3, plus phone addiction, face picking, nail and lip biting, swearing and a habit that caused stuttering; the mechanism is the number itself ([[C308]]). (Consolidation after report 90: title widened from 'Quit-habit / bad-habit mode' to name what the mode consists of; see [[C308]] for the relapse-logging rule and [[C307]] for the ad-category rule that follows from the audience.) Research: Quit Habit Decision.md — the decision memo for this point, and it settles three things. (1) Quit is parity, not differentiation: 8 of the top 40 habit trackers explicitly market breaking bad habits, including Habit Tracker (#1), HabitKit, Streaks and Simple Streak, and the #1 app already ships a Quit tab — 'Shipping it doesn't differentiate you. Not shipping it is starting to look like a gap.' (2) The differentiation is in the implementation, because the leader's is defective in five named ways (wrong streak count on quit habits; an alcohol ceiling of a one-month maximum period with a two-drink minimum; unreadable dark colours when the target is 0 per day; a form error on the Quit tab; 'Bad for quitting habits') — see [[C310]]. (3) The build spec, five items: a days-since counter rather than a streak ('Quitting is days clean, not did it today'); a relapse that does not wipe history — the most-repeated complaint across the 10,621-review Days Since corpus — logging the slip, keeping the record and showing best-ever beside current ([[C308]], [[C216]]); allowances rather than only zero, because '2 drinks a week' is a real goal and the leader's one-month cap draws loud complaints ([[C048]], [[C108]]); milestones with meaning at 1/7/30/90 days plus money saved, which is where the leading quit corpus is happiest — milestone-screenshot reviews average 4.77★ ([[C101]], [[C100]]); and readable in dark mode ([[C080]], [[C171]]). What people actually quit, from 10,621 Days Since reviews: alcohol 5.0%, smoking/vaping 3.7%, social media/phone 2.0%, sugar/junk food 1.0%, weed/drugs 0.7%, nail biting/caffeine/gambling 0.6%, porn 0.2% — the top two are locked up by the verticals and phone/social-media use is the one quit niche with genuine room. Ship it as a habit type in this app, not as a second listing ([[C309]]).

- Narrowed at consolidation after report 90 (batch end, 76-90): was *Quit-habit / bad-habit mode* — report 90 is the first dedicated quit-tracker corpus in the series (614 reviews, mean 4.40, U:praise_any 77.52%) and it specifies the mode the old one-line title only named: time since quitting to the second, unlimited habits, a personal record, an attempts counter and a relapse button that stores a dated note with a reason; the mechanism is loss aversion on a large number ('breaking big numbers hurts far more than the urge to smoke'), the audience includes self-harm (13), drugs (8) and clinical contexts (3), and the vocabulary itself is a design surface ('the words refusal, bad habits, relapse are so-so')

### C044 — Mac / desktop / web app

**Strong** · 30 apps · 70 cards · positive in 9 apps · negative in 25 apps

*Why Strong:* 30 apps, directions mixed (open 19, act 16, paid 14)

| | reaction positive | reaction negative |
|---|---|---|
| **app makes it free** | free-praised — 0 apps | free-expected-but-broken — 1 apps |
| **app makes it paid** | paid-converts — 0 apps | paid-resented — 0 apps |

**Verdict from the table:** only free-tier evidence

Strongest 3★ driver; users volunteer to pay extra for it. Report 23: the Mac app was a separate purchase in 2020–21, then included in the universal purchase from late 2021 (≥8 reviews, a classifier miss at 1); one unverified report of the Mac app creating millions of files and locking the user out. Report 25: a Mac app is part of the included platform surface (8 mentions, mean 4.00). Report 27: a macOS app requested once, 5★. Report 31: iPad / Mac / landscape / web / Android wanted by 98 (1.89%, mean 3.49), peaking in the 4★ band (7.5%) and in E1 (5.3%), falling to ~1% after 2021 as those users left. Report 33: a Mac app (sold separately in 2018), a menu-bar mini app, web, Android and Windows exist; the Mac app could not sign in or sync through 2021–22 (Mac/web 18.5% of 2022, Russia 10.1%) until macOS 13.0.1. Report 34: no iPad / Mac / web app (8) — 'The only reason i'm going with a competitor … is because I don't always want to use my phone'; 'I'd even pay for separate versions as long as they synced'. Report 43: a macOS / desktop app requested by 3 (mean 4.67); the listing claims Mac (M1+) — possibly discoverability. Report 46: a web app and Chrome new-tab extension pre-dated the iPhone app and held the early community ('I have it as my default Chrome tab page'; 'I am not allowed my phone at work'), fading 2.15% → 0.23%; the Mac build is criticised as slow. Report 48: a Mac app from ~March 2022 was welcomed by long-term users and lifted multi-platform praise to 3.13%; the web app (2015 – ~2019) was discontinued and its removal is still resented — 17 want it or Android back (0.84% of 2022–26), Windows users in particular lost access. Report 49: iPad and Mac builds exist but layouts are broken (device incompatibility 15, mean 1.27). Report 50: Mac and iPad companion with one account (praised). Report 52: a Mac build exists but cannot bind the WeChat account the membership lives on. Report 55: no Mac or web app (PLATFORM_WANT 24). Report 57: Mac requested by 8 (all Korean). Report 59 (Tappsk): U_PLATFORM_REQ 385 (2.54%) — REQ_DESKTOP 208, REQ_WEB 104, REQ_ANDROID 28; desktop requests fall from 6.0% of the launch year to 0.6% after the Mac app and hold near 1% since, shifting to Windows and the browser ('Сделайте версию для ПК на WINDOWS 10'; 'нужна веб версия, товарищи'); the report's experiment is a read-mostly web view priced into Premium to test demand before a full client; REQ_WATCH fell from 4.7% to 0.0% after the Watch app shipped. Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_MAC 23 (4.52★), REQ_WEB 14 (4.43★), REQ_ANDROID 3 — the highest-rated requests in the list, from users who already love it. Report 86 (Today): REQ_MAC 14 (2016 → 2021) — never; Momentum's desktop sync envied ('I like their desktop sync, wink!').

<a id="c021"></a>
### C021 — Apple Health integration

**Strong** · 28 apps · 79 cards · positive in 12 apps · negative in 24 apps · tied to a purchase in 5 apps

*Why Strong:* 28 apps, directions mixed (open 20, paid 18, act 15)

| | reaction positive | reaction negative |
|---|---|---|
| **app makes it free** | free-praised — 0 apps | free-expected-but-broken — 1 apps |
| **app makes it paid** | paid-converts — 1 apps | paid-resented — 0 apps |

**Verdict from the table:** mixed — conditions decide

Small volume, very high purchase intent. Report 23: HealthKit auto-completion (277, 3.81%, mean 4.35) is 'the single highest-leverage integration in the category' — it removes the friction that killed every other habit app the reviewer tried; a weak tail of misfires (auto-completing without action 11; Health data miscounting 9). Report 25: two-way Apple Health is a purchase trigger (32, 2.44%) with a weak tail of demonstrably wrong mappings — weight read as an entry count, steps off by 568, running only measurable in minutes, step counting starting at 04:00 (9, 0.69%). Report 27: Apple Health integration (exercise, water, steps, sleep) requested once, 4★. Report 31: Apple Health integration covers ~10 preset tasks (steps, sleep, exercise minutes); 79 mentions (mean 2.85); Health sync named as the missing piece between 4★ and 5★. Report 33: Apple Health auto-logging and Fitbit, Strava, screen-time and NFC habits, described as both free and Premium; Health integration complaints rose to 2.2% of E5 and Garmin / wearable auto-completion is requested. Report 36: Apple Health requested by 3 — a 10,000-step habit that auto-completes. Report 41: Apple Health auto-completion (53 mentions) is a switch reason ('Coming from Grit, I almost instantly bought it because the Apple Health habits actually work') and a payer failure ('I paid for it specifically for synching with the health app'); Health gaps 8. Report 43: Apple Health integration requested once. Report 48: Apple Health auto-logging of steps / weight and Siri Shortcuts voice logging praised by 17 (rising to 1.56% of 2022–26); 3 Health sync bugs. Report 50: Health auto-tracking of steps, calories, distance and exercise with historical import praised by 7 (4.71, 5 US); 5 (4.60; 4.50% of US) want weight, sleep, mindful minutes and Apple Fitness session types synced instead of hand-entered — one says weight sync would move the rating to 5; a Health sync break after an update (1). Report 53: Apple Health integration is what reviewers could not find elsewhere (HK_GOOD 40 — the Watch Breathe app 'automatically marks that as complete'; calories logged from the wrist) and they ask for more sources — sleep, running, calories, blood pressure, Fitbit, Garmin, Strava (HK_WANT 31). Report 54: Health app / Fitbit sync requested (2). Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): 'It doesn't communicate with iPhone Health-fitness; it said it did' (TR, 2★) — if the listing promises it, an expectation mismatch, worse than an absent feature; I5: make the link work or remove the claim, the cheapest immediate fix. Report 64 (Critique AI): Apple Health and Hevy sync requested with exercise animations (us, 3★). Report 68 (Ultiself): Apple Health integration and automatic tracking are the long-term users' top asks (REQ_HEALTH 9, REQ_AUTO_TRACK 2); §8.8. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): Apple Health integration exists and is the only subsystem with more than one failure — the connection 'has not worked' for a lifetime buyer (2★) and 'the app crashes when adding Active Energy' (inside a 5★) — while a third asks for more of it (REQ_HEALTHKIT 2, 5.00★): wanted and, at least twice, broken; no reviewer says which tier it needs. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): REQ_HEALTH 1 (4★). Report 86 (Today): PR_HEALTHKIT 38 — 'EVERYTHING that is in your Apple Healthkit can be displayed and values for can be entered… I tried all popular health dashboards and activity tracker, but this is miles ahead'; a weight graph and a distance-swum card (jp); REQ_AUTOCHECK 11 (auto check-in from Health) never shipped.

<a id="c048"></a>
### C048 — Flexible units / partial progress

**Strong** · 25 apps · 66 cards · positive in 9 apps · negative in 16 apps · tied to a purchase in 1 apps

*Why Strong:* 25 apps, directions mixed (open 23, free 18, act 15)

| | reaction positive | reaction negative |
|---|---|---|
| **app makes it free** | free-praised — 2 apps | free-expected-but-broken — 0 apps |
| **app makes it paid** | paid-converts — 0 apps | paid-resented — 0 apps |

**Verdict from the table:** only free-tier evidence

Drag to 60% instead of a binary tick — a named reason for choosing over competitors. Report 23: 77 reviews (1.06%) in seven languages ask to record effort beyond the goal or short of it — over-achievement is discarded ('goal 30 minutes, read 90, it stops at 30') and partial progress renders as failure ('6 of 8 glasses shows an ✗'); the two most-upvoted reviews in the 7,270-review corpus (313 and 126 votes) are this request; 'do 30 push-ups' breaks on a 25 day where 'push-ups per day' would record 25 and preserve momentum. Ship floor-without-ceiling goals and a partial-progress calendar state without changing the streak rule. Report 25: measurement units — count, minutes, distance, custom steps — and track-only habits with no goal number. Report 29: quantity/unit tracking (steps, litres, reps; one proposes a slider) requested by 4 — only as an optional habit type outside the default flow. Report 31: unit tracking with custom increments (dollar amounts for business referrals) is praised; a custom-count input bug added an extra unit ('I type in 50 pages … it counts 55', 16). Report 33: goals with units and multiple check-ins per day shipped in Aug 2020; custom units (kg, kcal, metric) and icons still requested (56). Report 34: quantity / partial completion requested by 11 — 'I Drank 80oz … I wanna be able to track that'; '8 of 10 glasses counts as progress'. Report 36: multiple completions per day / quantity targets (water in ounces) requested by 5. Report 43: multiple completions per day with 0/2, 0/4 counters (water, reps) exist free and are a purchase trigger ('the 0/2, 0/4 etc feature that visually shows you how far behind you are… it made me buy it'); praised by 14 (mean 4.71). Report 46: several completions per day (12) and numeric targets — glasses, steps, pages (9, mean 4.56) — requested. Report 48: numeric Target and rolling Average trackers are the reason 485 reviewers chose the app; flexible units requested by 13 and true time-duration HH:MM by 8 — see [[C265]]. Report 53: US units only for water, weight and distance ('Stuck with Dopey American units'; 'In Europe we have no idea what a US Fl Oz is!'; notifications in ounces with litres selected — DES_UNITS 47, 20 storefronts); log beyond the goal (CORE_OVER 10). Report 55: numeric habits with 'at least', 'exactly' or 'not more than' success rules alongside yes/no — 'counting habits like 8 glasses of water a day'. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): 'store a value or note per day (walked 5k, then 7k) and see it over time' (ZA, 4★) — the same data-model change as within-day counting (P5). Report 69 (TheFor): a numeric goal set by a scroll wheel capped at 10,000 — 'I want to be able to type the number for my goal instead of having to scroll for a minute'; 'Хотела выставить цель:12000 шагов - максимально выдает 10000' — two independent users two years apart; F6: 'a one-afternoon fix'. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): enter numbers, counts or durations instead of a check (2) and more than one check a day (2). Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_COUNT 129 (1.66%, 4.22★) quantities / several times a day, in every era (0.8–2.9%); NEG_YESNO 36 want a partial or 'yellow' state; §8.4 test an optional count per day as a separate journal type, keeping yes/no as the default. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): check-in of amounts with custom units (PRAISE_FLEXIBLE 7, 4.71★: 'a task with a completely open schedule'); notes + custom units were the roadmap items one buyer waited for. Report 89 (Check Calendar): REQ_QUANTITY 1 — numeric values per day (5★). Research: Quit Habit Decision.md — quit habits need allowances, not only zero: "'2 drinks a week' is a real goal", and the #1 app's ceiling (a maximum period of one month with a two-drink minimum) draws loud complaints; moderation is a distinct tracking mode from abstinence.

<a id="c008"></a>
### C008 — Daily check-in and reminders are free — never paywall the reminder

**Strong** · 24 apps · 47 cards · positive in 16 apps · negative in 11 apps · tied to a purchase in 1 apps

*Why Strong:* 24 apps, directions mixed (free 21, act 19, open 3)

| | reaction positive | reaction negative |
|---|---|---|
| **app makes it free** | free-praised — 10 apps | free-expected-but-broken — 0 apps |
| **app makes it paid** | paid-converts — 0 apps | paid-resented — 4 apps |

**Verdict from the table:** evidence leans free (paid is mostly resented)

Core loop must be free; it draws no complaints when it is. Report 13: exact-clock reminder times behind the paywall was the single most resented gate in an eleven-year corpus (227 requests); free users got only Morning/Afternoon/Evening buckets. Report 25: a specific clock time per habit with a notification at that time — not a generic reminder — was absent and is the top request from satisfied users (29; 4★ band 9.0%). Report 47: reminders free throughout and praised by 10 (all 5★ — multiple times per habit, editable text). Report 48: unlimited custom reminders per tracker with the user's own message text are free and praised by 224 (5.09%, 4.87) — reminders faulted by 78 at a stable ratio. [Merged from C257: Report 42: reminders sit behind the paywall and are the feature most often named as the thing behind the wall (5 reviews, mean 2.60 — 'I just wanted to use the habit reminder feature and that would cost me 40 a year? Come on. That's insane!'), while working reminders are praised at mean 5.00 (6); three reviewers independently conclude the phone's own tools substitute — 'better to use the native Lista app on iPhone… doesn't freeze and is free'; 'the paid version adds a reminder — you can set that in the calendar too'; 'Your alarm or reminder on your phone can do everything this app does. Wasted $20!' The report calls un-paywalling reminders 'the most defensible single paywall change'. Report 43 (counter-case): reminders, including the nag, are free and the app's reason to exist; only the habit count was ever gated. Report 46 (contrast): reminders are free; the paid gates are habit count, dark mode, offline use and sync.] Report 65 (Rabit): notifications were never gated, yet a reviewer asks whether they were — when the reminder breaks for everyone, free users read it as a paywall. Report 72 (Habit Hearts): 'you're only allowed to set 3 habits and you can't even get notifications for them' (Nov 2024) — 'a habit tracker whose free tier cannot remind you is not a smaller product, it is a different one'; §8.1 #3 verify and ungate. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): notifications were absent and requested in 2023–24 ('有料でもいいので' — 'even if paid'), then praised as present in 2026. Report 76 (Way of Life): reminders are free and praised (PR_REMINDERS 351, 4.83★) but the praise fades from 6.6% of E1 to 1.8% of E6 as reminders become table stakes; per-item reminders were requested for eight years (REQ_REMINDER_PER_ITEM 51, 2011 → 2019) and the request stopped when they shipped. Report 89 (Check Calendar): REQ_NOTIFICATIONS 5 (2021-08 → 2025-08: 'Notifications are missing.'), none after the listing added them; no notification failure in the corpus.

<a id="c066"></a>
### C066 — Focus timer

**Strong** · 22 apps · 38 cards · positive in 7 apps · negative in 11 apps · tied to a purchase in 1 apps

*Why Strong:* 22 apps, directions mixed (open 15, act 10, free 6)

| | reaction positive | reaction negative |
|---|---|---|
| **app makes it free** | free-praised — 3 apps | free-expected-but-broken — 0 apps |
| **app makes it paid** | paid-converts — 0 apps | paid-resented — 0 apps |

**Verdict from the table:** only free-tier evidence

Meaningful in the US, emerging globally. Report 23: timed tasks and a built-in Pomodoro exist; the Pomodoro break cycle was reported broken in 2022 and timers desync between devices. Report 24: a deep-work ramp-up ritual and per-habit timers are named by long-tenure users as the reason they renew. Report 25: a built-in timer that keeps counting past the goal is praised at mean 4.60 (15, 1.15%). Report 28: a timer with auto-mark-complete exists; three want it to run in the background / on the lock screen. Report 36: a timer / pomodoro requested by 4 (mean 2.50), one because a screenshot habit was named 'Run 15 minutes'. Report 41: a per-habit timer with Live Activities praised by 27. Report 43: multi-step timed routines (morning routines, workouts, kids, ADHD) with background-music fade and voice prompts are a core differentiator and the mechanic the ADHD segment names most. Report 47: timers / time tracking requested by a payer for study logging (average and total study time). Report 48: a built-in timer requested by 5–6; time-duration HH:MM units by 8. Report 52: a pomodoro / count-up focus timer linked to habits (FOCUS 390, rising to 5.5% of 2026) — accepted but ranked below check-in speed; the app-block list works backwards; a solid-red focus page redesign (Aug 2026) clashed with the calm style. <a id="c170"></a>
### C170 — Configurable day boundary and hemisphere seasons

**Strong** · 21 apps · 41 cards · positive in 3 apps · negative in 17 apps

*Why Strong:* 21 apps, directions mixed (act 14, free 9, open 5)

| | reaction positive | reaction negative |
|---|---|---|
| **app makes it free** | free-praised — 1 apps | free-expected-but-broken — 0 apps |
| **app makes it paid** | paid-converts — 0 apps | paid-resented — 1 apps |

**Verdict from the table:** mixed — conditions decide

Report 10: 146 reviews say the app assumes a conventional daytime schedule and northern-hemisphere seasons; night-shift workers and southern-hemisphere users ask for a movable day boundary. Report 18: a configurable day-end time was requested ~15 times across KR, JP and US, and the timezone stayed on Korean time for diaspora users from 2021 to 2024 (US daylight saving unhandled). Report 23: day-boundary / midnight reset requested (54, 0.74%, emerging, mean 4.02). Report 25: a day-start time setting exists for shift workers but is capped at 11:45. Report 26: a user-set day boundary requested alongside backfill (29); persistent across five years. Report 27: a Monday week-start setting asked twice in early 2024 (DE/AU) and never again. Report 31: a day-start offset for late sleepers and shift workers (capped at 5 am) was later removed; day-start / midnight rollover 18. Report 34: 'My day always ends after midnight' — a configurable day start, citing Habitica's setting. Report 41: custom day-start and week-start shipped May 2025 after being requested from 2021; night-shift day reset 5. Report 46 (counter-signal): none; the grid's day boundary is not raised. Report 49: the wake-time control permits only ~5–10am, excluding night-shift, graveyard and FIFO workers — 31 reviews at 3.42 (well above the corpus), 23 stating their shift, US +2.15pp, several saying they want the product while uninstalling; the daily recap closes the day at a fixed ~9pm (10) — 'the cheapest high-value fix in the report'; a partial fix turned a 4★ into 5★. Report 52: night owls' check-ins after midnight land on the next day — 50 text mentions ask to end the day at 2–4 am. Report 53: end the day at 1–5 am and handle time-zone travel (CORE_DAYSTART 9). Report 59 (Tappsk): NEG_DAY_BOUNDARY 19 — 'Как быть совам' (what about night owls, 1★); the report proposes a user-set day boundary alongside back-dating. Report 65 (Rabit): 'My day does not start or end at 12am… I track my water usage past midnight and it doesn't reset after I sleep??'. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): the previous day is recordable until 3 a.m. — praised as grace (PR_GRACE 41) and by a night-shift worker ('choosing yesterday or today after midnight is welcome for night workers'), yet late studiers and shift workers get caught ('if I record at 15:00 one day, I can't record at 10:00 the next'; NEG_DAYBOUNDARY 11, REQ_DAYBOUNDARY_SET 6) — Japan's specific rule friction. Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_DAY_ROLLOVER 9 (custom day end, 2014 → 2024). Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): REQ_DAY_START 1 (custom start of day) shipped in v2.4.0; REQ_BEDTIME 1. Report 83 (Roubit): 'not getting carrots for tasks done after midnight kills motivation' (kr) — a later day boundary requested. Report 84 (HabitGrid): 1.0.19 'Custom week start' shipped after two week-boundary defects (a weekend tick toggling both days). Report 85 (Habitica): NEG_DAYSTART 16 — the custom day start interacts with a server-side rollover that sometimes fails (BUG_RESET 93). Report 86 (Today): day-start time requested in 2016 (a twenty-item Japanese list); a time-zone check-in bug fixed 6.5 years after the first report.

### C050 — One-off to-dos alongside habits

**Strong** · 17 apps · 36 cards · positive in 5 apps · negative in 10 apps · tied to a purchase in 1 apps

*Why Strong:* 17 apps, directions mixed (open 16, act 12, free 2)

| | reaction positive | reaction negative |
|---|---|---|
| **app makes it free** | free-praised — 0 apps | free-expected-but-broken — 0 apps |
| **app makes it paid** | paid-converts — 0 apps | paid-resented — 1 apps |

**Verdict from the table:** mixed — conditions decide

Emerging request. Report 18: routines and one-off to-dos interleaved in one time-ordered list was a named purchase trigger and 'MyRoutine's one advantage' over to-do apps; to-do parity (carry-over, subtasks, tags, priority, undated, recurring) was requested ~30 times. Report 25: one-off, non-repeating tasks in a separate list or tab requested by 10 (7 of them 4★) alongside the time-of-day request. Report 28: a to-do checklist exists separately from habits and users want it to earn carrots (9, mean 4.44 — 'the more irksome and time consuming tasks that you procrastinate on'). Report 31: one-off tasks / today-only items requested by 28 (mean 2.86). Report 33: one-off tasks requested by 10. Report 50: tasks / to-dos and 'Lista' sections alongside habits (requested May 2024, shipped); the list section reported broken (MX, Aug 2026). Report 52: to-dos (小事) shipped ~2024 and rose to 3.0% of that year's reviews — welcomed, then sorting and hiding regressions. Report 59 (Tappsk): the strongest evidence yet for the hybrid — a daily to-do list with a habit row on the same screen is what 15,176 reviewers praise: PR_ALLINONE 293 (1.93%), PR_HABITS 445, and the most-voted review in the corpus (156 votes) is 'Задачи и привычки в одном приложении - гениально' (tasks and habits in one app — genius); switchers come from Notes/Reminders, Todoist, Trello, Notion and Things. The to-do half brings its own design decisions: today / tomorrow / this week / later buckets (PR_SECTIONS 134, PR_ONE_SCREEN 82; Germany praises the one screen at 8.92×), automatic carry-over of unfinished tasks (PR_AUTO_CARRY 69 — 'all your unfinished today's tasks move to tomorrow') which the report says to keep as the default but with a per-task opt-out because recurring tasks carrying over is unwanted by 28 and recurring tasks invisible on future dates by 32; and the missing event time ([[C276]]). Report 65 (Rabit): a separately paid to-do list — 'só o todo-list que não é [gratuito], achei meio injusto' — that vanished for a payer and has no reminders ('die sinnlose Aufgabenliste ohne Erinnerungsfunktion… Total sinnfrei'). Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_SUBTASKS 6 (to-dos / subtasks, 2014 → 2018).

<a id="c089"></a>
### C089 — Promos, giveaways and gift codes must work exactly as advertised

**Strong** · 17 apps · 39 cards · positive in 8 apps · negative in 13 apps · tied to a purchase in 4 apps

*Why Strong:* 17 apps, same direction (act on it, 81%)

| | reaction positive | reaction negative |
|---|---|---|
| **app makes it free** | free-praised — 0 apps | free-expected-but-broken — 1 apps |
| **app makes it paid** | paid-converts — 1 apps | paid-resented — 0 apps |

**Verdict from the table:** mixed — conditions decide

Inflate early sentiment; when the promo fails to apply it produces 2–3★ from would-be buyers. Report 5's '1+1' gift code could not be used by the buyer and expired in three months — six years of disputes. Report 9: an advertised 3-month money-back guarantee was not honoured (17 reviews); withdrawing the claim zeroed those complaints and halved refund complaints. Report 26: China App Store shows a ¥38 tier with no in-app purchase path. Report 31: '83–90% off' first-year offers ($8.99–$9.99) checked out at $59.99–$99.99 through 2022–23, and a $19.99 'lifetime' was shown against anchors of $399–CA$499.99 that charged without unlocking. Report 34: the ~29 Jun 2023 free-lifetime giveaway left one reviewer calling it a 'Scam of free life time subscription' (1★) and another asking when the next limited-time free offer comes. Report 42: a promotional R$39.90/year shown, R$99.90 charged at confirm (1★, 'I'm waiting to adjust my rating of the app'). Report 43: a promo-free, ad-free one-time model produced zero unexpected charges, trial traps or chargebacks in 638 reviews. Report 46: a Black Friday €15 price; a December discount honoured after it expired ('Joan still hooked me up with the discounted subscription', 5★). Report 53: a splash screen offering ~90% off the annual plan while the App Store sheet shows the full price, in more than ten currencies ($7.99 → $79.99; €6.99 → €69.99; ¥900 → ¥9,000; 199 → 1,999 TRY) — PAY_PROMO 35 (mean 1.83), Jan 2023 → Feb 2026, 13 with no support reply and 9 asking for refunds; some reviewers did get it, suggesting eligibility rules; the most concentrated trust-destroying pattern in the corpus; F1: show the exact first charge and renewal on the offer screen and never show an offer the viewer can't redeem. Report 68 (Ultiself): a 2022 Sweatcoin promotion for lifetime access brought users who were then asked to pay. Report 76 (Way of Life): MON_SALE 3 (5.00★) — discounts are welcomed; 'only offer a reduced price in the first days after installation' (br 5★) is the complaint about timing. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): an AppAdvice free-lifetime promotion (2025-02-25) that could not be redeemed produced a 1★ (MON_PROMO_FAIL) from a user who also could not find directions; a competition-win giveaway produced a disclosed, neutral 5★ — 'a promo that fails is worse than no promo'. Report 82 (Lasting Change): 'you have the option to buy either the personalized book only… or, at a marginally higher [price], the book plus a 3-month-subscription' — a bundle priced so the subscription is effectively forced (ACQ_BOOK_PRICE_GATE 3: 'they hiked the price of the book if you don't buy a subscription'); a 'free month of membership' that 'will begin charging you monthly many months afterward'.

<a id="c107"></a>
### C107 — Widget variants and customisation as the paid layer

**Strong** · 15 apps · 45 cards · positive in 6 apps · negative in 10 apps · tied to a purchase in 4 apps

*Why Strong:* 15 apps, directions mixed (free 19, act 9, open 5)

| | reaction positive | reaction negative |
|---|---|---|
| **app makes it free** | free-praised — 1 apps | free-expected-but-broken — 1 apps |
| **app makes it paid** | paid-converts — 3 apps | paid-resented — 3 apps |

**Verdict from the table:** mixed — conditions decide

Base single-counter widget free forever; multi-counter widgets, custom art, progress rings, reset-from-widget can be paid — and were report 3's #1 purchase trigger. Report 30 (counter-evidence): a paid widget in a capped tracker lost a user to a competitor with a free widget and is the only named paid feature besides more habits; the report proposes testing widget free vs paid as an acquisition driver. Report 36: once widgets were paid, widget-improvement demand peaked (titles, colours, streak display, interactivity) — 'now that widgets cost money, people want them to do more'. Report 41: widgets are icon-only — 'When you have +10 habits, one habit widget with only icon and no clue to remembering the habit is a pain'; one runs a competitor alongside for text labels (8 requests); widget icons 'Make them bigger and it is 5 stars!'. Report 43: per-habit notification sounds are 'too few' — 'hearing the same sound for every habit… mentally makes me mush all my tasks together'; 'you can't use the notification or ringtone sounds from your iPhone'; a snooze wanted (16, mean 3.94). Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): the large heat-map widget is the only named purchase trigger in the corpus ('I bought the paid version of the app (single month), because I wanted to use the larger widget showing the entire heat map and i absolutely love it') and the credited retention mechanism ('Without it I would underestimate the progress and tend to give up… I was able to successfully track and build new habits for the first time with this app'), while a lifetime buyer's only complaint is that it is too basic ('no dark themed widget? Widget so basic? Please step it up, I just paid for lifetime access') and another wants it to surface the next unfinished habit; M3: make the widget the explicit centre of the paid offer; P2: dark theme and a next-unfinished mode — 'highest leverage per unit of work'. Report 65 (Rabit): REQ_WIDGET 43 (8.63%, mean 4.30), first asked days after iOS 14 widgets launched (Jan 2021) and still asked Aug 2025, never shipped, top theme of the 4★ band, twice as hot outside Brazil; four purchases made conditional on it — 'I'll definitely buy the lifetime plus version if you add widgets'; 'If this app had them I would 100% buy the lifetime'. Report 72 (Habit Hearts): 'более 50 виджетов на выбор' ('more than 50 widgets to choose from'); WID_GOOD 9 at 5.00 rising 2.38% → 6.00% — and the listing does not mention widgets. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): widgets reportedly paid (n=1, a 1★ whose whole text is 'You have to pay for widgets'); the paid layer is the widget itself, not a variant — and it shows one habit only. Report 90 (Quit Bad Habits & Addiction): the one conditional purchase intent in 614 reviews is a widget — 'ready to buy a subscription, but please add widgets' (2023, 5★) — and §5.6 refuses to call it a result: 'no finding that a widget would sell subscriptions… an experiment to run'. Research: Feature Gating vs Quantity.md — widget access is named as one of the four capabilities habit apps conventionally gate, and 'widgets' appears in the document's list of non-essential extras users expect to pay for once they have invested time. (Final consolidation: distinguish [[C167]] — a widget is a functional visibility surface and in reports 3 and 62 it is the named purchase trigger and the credited retention mechanism; C167 is decoration bought after engagement. Gating a functional surface and gating decoration are different decisions with different risk.)

### C116 — Content library (workouts, meditation, sleep, journal) as the paid layer

**Strong** · 13 apps · 42 cards · positive in 10 apps · negative in 6 apps · tied to a purchase in 2 apps

*Why Strong:* 13 apps, directions mixed (paid 12, free 12, act 7)

| | reaction positive | reaction negative |
|---|---|---|
| **app makes it free** | free-praised — 2 apps | free-expected-but-broken — 1 apps |
| **app makes it paid** | paid-converts — 3 apps | paid-resented — 1 apps |

**Verdict from the table:** evidence leans paid (paid mostly converts)

Gives a routine app something to sell beyond the core loop and separates it from 'a fancy Reminders list'. Report 13 (contested): Challenges/Explore content tabs added in 2020 drew 'please let me hide them… I will not pay for an app that is 50% useless content'; nobody in 19,850 reviews asked for content, coaching or AI. Report 24: three narrated coaching pieces a day, multi-week Journeys, meditations, a deep-work ritual, music and soundscapes are what paying users value (coaching praised 6,095, 14.02%, mean 4.483; life-changing 4,468, mean 4.799); repetitive content 103 (mean 2.660); the content must be saveable and replayable. Report 26: background music and nature sounds (559, 14.57%, mean 4.68), daily quotes (58, mean 4.74), themes, backgrounds, seasons, app icons and extra gardens are the content layer — partly free, more paid. Report 46: a free Learn tab (articles, videos, James Clear material) and 7-day e-mail course were praised as 'like a life changing book' by early users (107, mean 4.82) and faded 11.02% → 3.30% as the audience turned mobile; English-only; the report's E6 resurfaces it after day 14. Report 48: a free goal-setting course / handbook is credited by 27–29 reviewers (4.93) and several convert from it — a companion-content funnel rather than a paid layer. Report 67 (Habio): articles, courses and quotes criticised far more than praised (57 vs 12 non-seeded) — 'all the typos and language errors'; a therapist 'would never recommend for a client'; 'essentially charging 1 euro per page'; NEG_SHALLOW 102 'You literally pay to track your own habits'. Report 88 (GetHabit): printable PDF checklists and challenge packs sold on top of premium — the content library as the paid layer, at $9.99 a pack, on a product whose challenges were 'laughable'. (Final consolidation: see [[C233]] — this point asks whether a content layer sells; C233 is the reliability requirement on content already sold, and report 24 shows the second failing while the first succeeds.)

### C234 — Statistics stay readable on the free tier — gating the progress view removes the motivation loop the category sells

**Strong** · 13 apps · 22 cards · positive in 3 apps · negative in 8 apps

*Why Strong:* 13 apps, directions mixed (free 9, act 7, open 2)

| | reaction positive | reaction negative |
|---|---|---|
| **app makes it free** | free-praised — 2 apps | free-expected-but-broken — 0 apps |
| **app makes it paid** | paid-converts — 1 apps | paid-resented — 2 apps |

**Verdict from the table:** evidence leans free (paid is mostly resented)

Report 25: statistics of any kind were paywalled in every era and the calendar view by 2026 ('Pay to even look at calendar'); the reviews that name it average 1.40 and one explains why — for someone at rock bottom, free statistics are the motivation; gating it removes the reason to upgrade rather than creating one. The report predicts, counter-intuitively, that free statistics increase conversion and proposes the A/B. Sits beside C011 (paid weekly/monthly/yearly reports): the basic progress view is free, the deep report is the paid layer. Report 31: statistics (145 mentions) and charts were a paid unlock and a purchase trigger in the one-time era. Report 46: statistics free; richer stats requested by 11. Report 60 (Mindway): the paid product has no progress view at all — 'thought this would give more feedback on completion percentage - tracking consistency. It's just a basic to do list'; 'very little flexibility or encouragement'; no reviewer in 216 describes a streak, chart, score or progress view; D3: build the tracking layer — 'the largest non-pricing gap in the report' and the capability that justifies a subscription because it cannot be replicated in Notes (E4: completion %, current streak, 30-day grid). Report 69 (TheFor): the one monetization backlash in 80 reviews is a long-tenured user who lost free stats and 'see which days were tracked' to a subscription; the listing still advertises 'Comprehensive Weekly Overview' — M3: audit what is actually gated and reconcile with the listing. Report 76 (Way of Life): charts, trends and overview are free for the 3-item tier and are the second-largest praise (PR_INSIGHTS 838); friction is about range and depth (REQ_STATS 72, REQ_DATE_RANGE 22, REQ_CALENDAR 29, NEG_CHART 38), not access. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): v2.4.0 (2026-04-27): 'Advanced analytics, which was previously part of paid Ripples+ plans, is now available to everyone' — corroborated by a free-tier user four months later ('súper útil con analíticas y todo', 5★). Report 84 (HabitGrid): week / month / year statistics are free and among the top three concrete strengths (PRAISE_STATS_VIEWS 9); a yearly percentage counted from the habit's start rather than the year is the one stats complaint (arguably a design choice; §8.2 an option rather than a fix). Report 86 (Today): PR_STATS 65 free; the statistics screen is undiscoverable ('I only stumbled on the charts in the profile section by accident!'); nobody reports buying for statistics.

<a id="c117"></a>
### C117 — Mascot / companion character

**Strong** · 10 apps · 46 cards · positive in 9 apps · negative in 3 apps · tied to a purchase in 1 apps

*Why Strong:* 10 apps, directions mixed (act 16, free 13, open 7)

| | reaction positive | reaction negative |
|---|---|---|
| **app makes it free** | free-praised — 2 apps | free-expected-but-broken — 0 apps |
| **app makes it paid** | paid-converts — 0 apps | paid-resented — 0 apps |

**Verdict from the table:** only free-tier evidence

Small, pure praise in report 4; category norm in pet-style apps. Report 10: the pet is the causal story users tell — 'I will do for the bird what I will not do for myself' — at 70,041-review scale (companion 1,309, cute design 10,074); the same attachment makes data loss feel like bereavement. Report 28: the rabbit is the emotional object — 40 (4.87%, mean 4.15) describe attachment ('I named him Paul'; 'so I dont abandon my rabbit child'), the room-cleaning loop is 'an externalised progress bar with an emotional stake' (60, mean 4.25), 244 (29.72%) describe concrete behaviour change ('made me lose 80 pounds'; 'I take my iron pill just to check it off'); the cute art survives even in 12 of 84 one-star reviews; a bug that made the rabbit drift off-screen when tapped ('I WAS TAPPING ON THE BUNNY AND IT FLEW AWAY') drew 12 reports; users want to pet and feed it (9). Report 49: a character / hero mode with equipment, loot and battles shipped late 2025, cut 'just a checklist' to 1.0% of E4 and immediately generated its own bug theme (5). Report 54: an avocado mascot with facial expressions (9, 4.78 — 'the little avocado characters really motivate me'). <a id="c167"></a>
### C167 — Cosmetic and colour variety as the paid layer

**Strong** · 9 apps · 22 cards · positive in 7 apps · negative in 3 apps · tied to a purchase in 5 apps

*Why Strong:* 9 apps, directions mixed (paid 9, act 6, open 6)

| | reaction positive | reaction negative |
|---|---|---|
| **app makes it free** | free-praised — 0 apps | free-expected-but-broken — 0 apps |
| **app makes it paid** | paid-converts — 3 apps | paid-resented — 1 apps |

**Verdict from the table:** evidence leans paid (paid mostly converts)

Report 10: buyers name extra colour options, seasonal items and a larger shop as the specific hook ('I started getting finch plus solely because I found the extra color options… very motivating'); restricting palettes later (Aug–Sep 2026) drew a backlash. Report 36: cosmetic gating (≈10 premium skins) is 'broadly accepted when it is the only gate' — 'So far the app is mostly free aside from cosmetics (understandable)' — and 3 of 34 payers bought for skins; selling skins separately on top of the membership reads as double-charging ('$15 for permission to buy a $10 skin'). Report 47: more colours unlocked by watching a video (2022) — the one rewarded-ad surface reviewers accepted. Report 52: themes sold separately (~¥6 each, 2018) then made free for members — a buyer was refunded. Report 76 (Way of Life): paid themes / add-ons (MON_BUY_ITEMS 27, 4.44★) are bought — 16.48× over-represented among purchasers — but gating dark mode specifically drew a 3★. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): PAID_INAPP_CONTENT 1 — 'Love the bonus of buying and planting a forest' (5★): cosmetic content bought in-app rather than a tier; the only purchase in the corpus tied to a named thing. Report 83 (Roubit): 'Ultimate' yearly plan adds exclusive themes and outfits; Gold Carrots sold as consumables ($0.99–$9.99); PAYWALL_COSMETICS 4 (0.80%, 'A bit greedy') vs REQ_CUSTOMISE_CHARACTER 14 at 5.00★ — cosmetics are wanted and lightly resented as a paid layer. Research: Feature Gating vs Quantity.md — Habitica is the document's worked example that a fully free, unlimited core is compatible with a paid tier provided the paid tier is decoration: all core features free and unlimited, only cosmetic 'Pro' perks sold, and users 'buy the paid tier only for cosmetics'. (Final consolidation: distinguish [[C107]] — cosmetics are the safest paid layer precisely because they are not the mechanism; a widget that shows the number is, so it carries the base-free rule in C107 while pure decoration does not.)

### C227 — A 'graduated' state — keep tracking a mastered habit without it occupying an active slot

**Strong** · 8 apps · 17 cards · positive in 1 apps · negative in 5 apps

*Why Strong:* 8 apps, directions mixed (act 5, open 3, free 2)

Report 23: the single most persuasive argument for more capacity, made repeatedly, is that people want to keep tracking a habit that has become automatic while starting a new one; a mastered/graduated state that keeps history but frees the slot answers it without raising the cap. Report 48: end dates and archiving requested by 23 (4.09). Report 50: archive completed habits requested (2) — a completed short-term goal cluttering the screen. Report 53: archive without losing history (274-vote review). Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): 'Once you complete 30 days and start a new habit, the old habit is no longer notified' (3★) — §8.5: after a cycle offer 'keep tracking this quietly' beside 'set the next goal', graduated habits kept as a low-key streak while one goal stays active; measure 60- and 90-day continuation, not goals created. Report 76 (Way of Life): archive exists (PR_ARCHIVE 14 at 4.93★, 'pause habits') with NEG_ARCHIVE_UX 5 ('cannot find archived items', 4.80★) and REQ_ARCHIVE 10 ('keep data of removed habits'). Report 86 (Today): REQ_ARCHIVE 11 restated across five years and four languages — a formed habit can only be deleted, taking its history; the most-upvoted request in 1,785 reviews.
