<a id="c065"></a>
### C065 — Paying customers are the highest 1★ risk — every paid feature must work

**Certain** · 59 apps · 267 cards · positive in 7 apps · negative in 53 apps · tied to a purchase in 3 apps

*Why Certain:* 59 apps, same direction (act on it, 92%), 40 reports label it high-priority

Paid cohort rates a full point lower; 28% of payers leave 1–2★; confirmed buyers ×6.7 on 1★. Report 10: paid-cohort mean fell 4.40 → 2.96 across 2022–2026 while the corpus mean barely moved; the five highest paid lifts are all billing mechanics, not price. Report 16: 17 confirmed payers rated 1.21 stars below everyone else; five of the seven billing complaints in the corpus came from them. Report 18: 161 confirmed payers rated 0.30 below the corpus with 21.7% at 1★; their rates of entitlement failure (9.94% vs 1.22%), data loss (12.42% vs 6.01%) and billing dispute (14.29% vs 7.03%) were roughly double the global rates, and by the last era 4.36% of all reviews came from someone who had paid and could not use what they bought. Report 19: 64 of 105 reviewers were confirmed payers and 63 of them left 1★; one third said they could not get their money back and just under one third that they could not stop paying. Report 20: 908 reviewers with payment evidence averaged 1.55 against 3.61 for everyone else — 2.06 stars lower; 76.8% of revocation complaints, 62.1% of widget complaints and 65.5% of support complaints came from the ~22% who paid; the damage was also concentrated in the high-spend storefronts (revocation 19.3% vs 8.1% in ru/ua, broken widget 7×). Report 23 (everyone paid): reviewers who discuss the transaction average 3.52 vs 4.27 for the rest — a dissonance signal; 'I bought this for the Watch and it doesn't work' are the highest-value churn events. Report 24: reviewers who discuss the transaction average 2.006 against 4.356 for the rest. Report 25: explicit payers' mean fell 4.23 → 3.16 → 2.68 across eras (n=13/25/19) while the headline fell 0.27; 14% of payers raise a billing dispute, 8.8% lost access to something bought, 8.8% hit a reliability failure; 52 of 302 one-star reviews (17.2%) show paid evidence — failed customers, not non-buyers venting. Report 26: explicit payers (72) rate a full point below the corpus (3.56 vs 4.570), flat across five years; their top problems are losing the purchase (16.7%) and paywall friction after paying (23.6%). Report 28: identifiable payers rate 3.75 vs 4.03 and 41.7% of them report a failed purchase; a 5★ payer still getting ads writes 'Maybe it just needs to sync up'. Report 30: of the six reviewers who reached payment, five had a bad outcome and none describes a satisfactory purchase; the corpus cannot see quiet happy payers. Report 31: explicit payers went from the happiest segment (E1 mean 3.76) to the angriest (E4 1.35) while their share of reviews rose six-fold to 25.0%; 17.2% of 1★ reviews are from people who say they paid; within 625 payers: not granted 48.6% (1.21), support unresponsive 34.2%, still upsold 31.5%, lag 13.3% ($79.99, freezes on the third habit); a share bought only to make the pop-up go away. Report 33: 427 explicit payers (10.84%, mean 3.16) are polarised — 212 rate 4–5★, 172 rate 1–2★; their mood tracks integrity events, not price (E2 3.77 with a stable lifetime app; 2018 2.83 with 25 purchases not applied; E3 2.78 after Habitify X); after paying: reliability 42.6%, integrity 26.7%, support failure 11.9%, regressions 11.5%; nearly one 1★ in five is a payer. Report 34: payers are satisfied (51, mean 4.63) and E5 is their weakest era (4.23) because every low-rating E5 payer reports a broken paid thing — widget, reminders, lifetime entitlement — not price. Report 36: payers are the least satisfied identifiable group — 34 payers average 3.794 (23.5% 1–2★) vs corpus 4.039 and free-tier praisers 4.88 — because paying exposes no sync (9 of 34, 26.5%), entitlements that don't travel, billing edge cases and bugs ('please fix the bugs (paying user)'). Report 41: 5 of 29 1★ (17.2%) are payers whose specific purchase rationale failed — backfill, Mac sync, Watch sync without iCloud, Health sync, refund; 10 of 60 payers report a post-purchase failure. Report 42: payers (29) rate 2.72 vs non-payers 3.20, 44.8% of them 1★, none 4★ — 'no such thing as a mildly satisfied paying customer'; 9 of 29 hit a defect after paying (freezing '5 minutes to mark two tasks', a launch crash, disappearing habits, premium stats miscalculating). Report 43: payers (48, 7.52%) rate 3.58 vs 4.05 and are 1.9× as likely to give 1★; 11 of 48 (22.9%) hit a defect after paying and 10 of 76 one-star reviews are payers — every one a delivery failure (re-buy after reinstall, restore failed, 'Had it for two minutes after I paid for it and it's glitching', won't open with data gone despite iCloud, a lifetime payer with no support reply, the 2025 popup regression). Report 46: payers (97) rate 3.95 vs 4.35, 1.7× as likely to leave 1★ and 2.9× 2★; 21 of 97 (21.6%) hit a defect after paying; every payer at 1★ (12) is a delivery or billing failure, none a design objection. Report 47: 13 identifiable payers (2.21%, 12 JP) average 3.23 vs 3.83; nine of thirteen report a billing, entitlement or reliability problem (ads reappearing, charged twice, crash after paying, the month view showing a week, the AI toggle stuck off, the rating prompt shown to payers); 4★ holds most of the payers — 'one fix from five'. Report 48: 172 payers (3.91%) average 3.92 vs 4.24 — 84 (48.8%) also report a problem (billing 12, refund 8, no support reply 8, crash 9, sync 6); 31 one-star reviews are from payers — 'the most expensive failure mode in the corpus'; 'The paid experience fails at exactly the moments it matters.' Report 49: 106 payers average 1.92 — 97 (91.5%) carry a complaint; reliability 41.5% of payer reviews vs 13.4% of non-payers; login failure 11.32% vs 1.30%; 57 payers at 1★ 'the most serious group in this report'. Report 50 (counter-case): payers are happy — 9 direct at 4.11 (7 at 5★), 13 with probable at 4.23 vs 4.27 for non-payers; both unhappy payers were hurt by billing, not the product; a Premium user who lost data still wrote a 2,020-character defence — 'Every monetization change should be evaluated against whether it risks converting this segment into the angry-payer segment that most competitors have.' Report 52: payers are the most satisfied segment (306 value-reporting payers at 4.92) until something breaks — entitlement broke 80 at 2.62, data loss 33 at 1.73, support silence 52 at 1.92, reliability 286 at 3.04. Report 53: payers went from 143 at 3.44 (2017–22) to 54 at 2.15 (2023–26); paid and reliability failure 82 at 2.46, statistics broken 24 at 2.25, entitlement withdrawn 10 at 1.50. Report 54: confirmed payers average 3.091 against 3.981 and are 3.3× more likely to leave one star (27.3% vs 8.4%); 12 of 31 one-stars are payers — 'the one-star population is, disproportionately, the company's customers'; the payer segment holds nearly all of six failure themes (10 of 12 value gap, 6 of 6 never unlocked, 6 of 7 restore, 5 of 5 refunds) — 'Free users complain about the gate; paying users complain about the goods'. Report 55: payers are the unhappiest group — PAY_BOUGHT 165 at 2.56, 96 (58.2%) at 1–2★, paid mean 4.24 → 2.78 → 1.91 → 1.41 across eras; 41.8% of payers report a data & account continuity failure, 25.5% support silence, 21.8% sync failure; the continuity chain — crash or new phone → reinstall → login fails → data and premium gone → e-mail support → no reply → refund request and 1★; 'Two online reviews that premium customers had posted convinced me not to'. Report 57: 31 of 99 payers (31.31%) report a purchase-side failure, rising 12.9% (2019–21) → 27.3% → 45.7% (2024–26); payers are 12.71% of reviews but 20.8% of one-stars; in 2026 8 of 12 payers report a failure — the rising payer share may be measuring anger, not adoption; refunds rare (2 genuine) because unhappy payers write a 1★ and stay broken. Report 59 (Tappsk): 147 of 1,090 purchasers (13.5%) rate 1–2★; among purchasers BUG_PURCHASE lifts 8.43×, MON_PAID_TWICE 8.89×, SUP_NONE 6.09×, BUG_SYNC 5.71×, NEG_DEV_PROMISE 4.43× — the paid segment concentrates every failure class; 'написано, что поддерживается семейный доступ' (it says Family Sharing is supported) is a paid-twice complaint. Report 60 (Mindway): the extreme case — 13 explicit payers (6.02%), mean 1.38, 11 of 13 at 1★, zero at 5★; 'not one paying reviewer describes getting value for the money… the most consequential single number in the report'; every refund request, cancellation failure and unexpected-charge report in the corpus comes from this segment; five of thirteen say the paid product is a list, not a tracker; the responsible reading — the segment is biased toward the aggrieved — still leaves 'the only payer voices the store shows prospective buyers are 1★'. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): 5 of 6 self-identified payers report a defect or shortfall — two entitlement failures, two hit by the June build, one lifetime buyer disappointed by the widget; only one paid reviewer is unreservedly happy ('Worth every penny'); notably neither failed purchaser asked for a refund — both asked for a fix. Report 64 (Critique AI): 13 self-stated payers average 1.85 (10 at 1★) against 3.87 for users who got in without stating payment — access more than doubles satisfaction and stating that you paid halves it again; 12 of 13 report a defect or shortfall. Report 65 (Rabit): 49 self-stated payers average 2.061 against 3.677 (27 of 49 at 1★, 3× over-represented), and the 1★ band's top theme is PAY_PAID (29.67%) — 'the one-star band is mostly composed of (a) people who could not get into the app at all and (b) people who paid and could not get what they paid for. Neither group is a pricing problem'; payer complaints peak in 2023, the cap year; only 2 say paid was worth it against 16 who say not. Report 67 (Habio): 35 deliberate buyers (mean 1.23) report the same failures as everyone else plus locked premium; praise among money-left reviewers has a 0.06× lift. Report 68 (Ultiself): 331 of 392 deliberate purchasers (84.4%) carry a billing complaint and 26 (6.6%) rate 4–5★; refund requests 221 (4.90%): refused or ignored 120, received 27 (18 in 2026), partial 4 — 69.7% driven by a charge the reviewer did not expect, not dissatisfaction with the app. Report 69 (TheFor): 'the paid path is the only part of this product with a majority-failure account, and it is the part that generates revenue' (3 of 4 stated payers). Report 75 (Habit Streak): zero self-identified purchasers in 41 reviews — 'this corpus cannot see the post-purchase funnel at all'; §8.6 instrument conversion, refunds and churn 'because the next version of this analysis should not have to say no purchase evidence exists'. Report 76 (Way of Life): 1★ (181) is where purchases go wrong — MON_PAID 16.57%, BUG_PURCHASE 11.60%, MON_SUBSCRIPTION 8.29%, MON_REGRET 7.18%, MON_DISCLOSURE 7.73%, SUP_NONE 6.08%; MON_REGRET is the lowest-rated money code (21, mean 1.52★); 40 of 349 purchasers (11.5%) rate 1–2★; on cn 11 reviews in one week of 2015-01 report crashing immediately after buying premium ('the money was taken and it started crashing, endlessly'). Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): the four stated payers average 3.75★ (0.56 below the corpus) — a lifetime purchaser whose app crashes on every launch and whose Apple Health connection does not work ('maximum spend, zero delivery — the worst outcome in the corpus'), a premium buyer who uninstalled after 20 days over missing feedback loops, and two satisfied 5★; PAID_ENTITLEMENT_FAIL 1 ('Leider werden mir die Optionen nicht angezeigt', a 5★ titled 'Problem Premium'). Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): the 11 purchase-evidence reviews average 3.55★ vs corpus 4.599 — the only substantial segment below the corpus — produced entirely by four broken transactions: five of nine stated payers 5★, four 1★, none 2–4 ('paying this developer is, on the evidence of this corpus, a binary experience'); satisfied payers praise craft at the corpus rate; titles 'Estafa' and 'No part of the app is free' are what a prospective buyer reads. Report 82 (Lasting Change): U:paid_evidence 125 (71.43%) averages 1.224★ — 116 × 1★, 0 × 4★ — 92.8% of everyone with purchase evidence rated one star; BILL_NO_CONSENT, REFUND_REFUSED, TRUST_ESCALATED and SUP_NO_REPLY occur only in one-star reviews ('a person who is charged without consent and refused a refund gives one star, without exception, in 1080 days across 26 storefronts'); U:trust_collapse 97 (55.43%): TRUST_SCAM_WORD 65 across seven languages, TRUST_WARN_OTHERS 67 — the largest code — written to warn the next buyer. Report 83 (Roubit): PAID_EXPLICIT 27 (5.40%, 3.67★) — 44.4% satisfied, 51.9% report a defect (one who paid for the letters then lost the diary: 'if it seems fixed after a while I'll subscribe again', 2★), 4 regret ('abandoned a year's subscription as clunky'), 3 not unlocked, 4 churned — 'the product broke under paying users'. Report 85 (Habitica): stated purchasers (55) average 3.25★ and 15 of 55 report a purchase that went wrong — paid then the app would not open ('Paid for premium but can barely use it as it constantly crashes', 1★), gems not credited ('I got a month subscription and the gems didn't credit to my account', 1★), could not cancel ('Habitica keeps charging for new subscriptions', 1★), left over the 2023 changes; MON_PAID_UNHAPPY 17. Report 86 (Today): paid reviewers (188, 10.53%) average 3.69★ vs 3.97 and report defects at 34.57% vs 26.27% — they use it longer with more habits, the condition under which it degrades; 12 of 55 data-loss reviewers paid for the backup that lost their data; MON_PAID_EXPLICIT is 16.13% of 1★ — 'paying does not make people kind'; U:purchase_friction 51 (2.61★): restore 18, IAP failure 11, regret 12, refund 7 (two refused by Apple), overcharge 2, features taken back 3. Report 88 (GetHabit): of 182 who chose to pay, mean 1.18★ and 161 gave one star; 51.1% hit a post-purchase problem (unwanted charge 28.0%, content still locked 16.5%, no access 13.7%, support failure 23.6%), 35.7% regret, 27.5% asked for a refund, one is satisfied; PAID_NO_ACCESS 28 ('Despite that I cannot access app: Error. There was a problem with App Store'); 'buyers rate lower than everyone' — the public 4.355★ is not produced by its paying customers. Report 89 (Check Calendar): PAID_EXPLICIT 31 (12.25%, 3.48★) — 15 of 31 (48.4%) report a post-purchase problem (restore 9, data loss 5, ads after paying 2, refund request 1, disputed charge 1) against 0.5% of non-buyers; four of the seven one-star reviews without a paywall code are paid users — 'outside the paywall, what earns one star is losing, miscounting or being re-charged for records the user paid to keep'; three-star is the paid-user band (8 of 26 buyers, 7 problems).

<a id="c034"></a>
### C034 — Data must never be lost on update, reinstall or phone change

**Certain** · 55 apps · 192 cards · positive in 2 apps · negative in 52 apps · tied to a purchase in 1 apps

*Why Certain:* 55 apps, same direction (act on it, 94%), 30 reports label it high-priority

Data loss is ×10.6 over-represented among buyers; local-only storage is the cause. Report 10: from 2025 the dominant story became app-initiated — 'it told me my pet data got corrupted' — with no automatic backup to fall back on. Report 14: data lost on update was the only theme with a perfect 1★ record and the corpus's only 'stay away' review; it recurred 5.5 years later ('backdate all my progress by memory (again)'). Report 18: data loss sat between 6% and 8% in every era after the first, five years running — the single most durable defect in a 2,048-review corpus — and hit 12.42% of confirmed payers; 'if I'd known records could all disappear I wouldn't have paid.' Report 20: update 1.41.0 (13 Mar 2025) erased habit histories globally — 126 of 161 reviews in the following seven weeks (78.3%) reported losing 2–5 years; the advertised fix did not work, a second bug wiped prior progress on the next check-off, iCloud backup was itself a paid, manual feature ('Why should a premium subscriber even have to think about whether a backup was created?'), and there was no communication. The same migration-bug class had fired in Jan 2021. Report 23: data loss 81 (1.11%, mean 2.17, 45.7% 1★), 60 of them after the 2022 sync rewrite (3.38% of post-2022 reviews, mean 2.03; 2024 peak 22) — the only theme that destroys a long-tenure customer outright ('my 3+ years record to null'; 'It's like I'm a brand new user'); an in-app backup existed and was discovered by support, not the user. Report 24: progress lost on device change with no restore (257, mean 2.693) is the most-cited reason a multi-year user stops. Report 25: data loss / reset to zero 12 (0.92%), flat ~1%; archive/delete destroys history (4) — 'archive losing history defeats the point of archiving'. Report 26: with no account or sync, a support-recommended reinstall deleted 'all the lovely growth you have achieved' along with the purchase. Report 27: the one observed churn — 'It doesnt open with the update, ive lost all my progress, guess its time for a new app' — is reliability plus data loss, not price. Report 28: 12 data/progress-loss reports (1.46%, mean 2.42) entangled with the game's intentional decay — 'on challenge mode… run out of health it resets ALL of your progress… level 278… resets you to level 1'; 'My Account is gone, I was at a high Level'; an intentional decay mechanic and an unintentional data-loss bug are indistinguishable to the user. Report 29: 9 data-loss reports (mean 2.11, the lowest-rated theme) came from the calendar bug plus a workaround users taught each other — reinstall — which wiped local-only history ('just sad I lost my data from uninstalling it'); 'the bug fix alone does not close this loop — an export or backup path does'. Report 31: data / streaks lost or reset in 94 reviews (a 109-day no-wine streak; sobriety 40 → 16 days; 200+ day streaks to 0); counts corrupted by v2.7.1/2.7.2 in 107 (58,720 — 'Do not download 2.7.2!!!'); a habit tracker's only durable asset is the user's history, which users treat as health data — gate releases on data-migration tests and stage every rollout. Report 33: v2.0 (Nov 2016) wiped history and Premium for many ('30 routines gone'); Habitify X erased 4 months of time logs; data lost 55 reviews (mean 2.25). Report 34: local-only storage lost data on reinstall, factory reset or 'for no reason' (4; 'thought this app supports iCloud sync and re-installed app … lost all data as this app needs backup file'). Report 36: 'everything you save and track is reset when the app is deleted … I do not recommend' (1★); DATALOSS 3 (mean 1.67); a new phone met the new cap ('5 habits on the old phone, 1 on the new'). Report 41: 6 data-loss reports (0.74%, mean 3.33) — 'After 215 days of tracking… everything… deleted, all history lost! No chance to restore'; 'deleted from BOTH old and new device' on migration; one recovered only by the developer by hand; a 6-month total loss filed at 5★. Report 42: data loss 6 (mean 1.33, acted on regardless of share) — 'last night it updated… All my data and tracking… is gone'; 'I had 90 days of progress on every habit, now it's all gone and became 9 days'; 'I used it for many years… After the last update progress isn't visible… looking for a replacement' — the update → restart → history-truncated pattern recurs, four of six Russian. Report 43: data loss is the most severe and accelerating defect — 12 (1.88%, mean 2.08), 0 in 2016–18 → 7 in 2022–26 (4.55%); in July 2026 two German users four days apart lost four years of locally stored history when the UI changed ('I used HabitHub for four years and after an update my locally stored data was gone'), got immediate support replies, and had already migrated — 'If I could change anything, I would sync my data to the iCloud to be sure'. Report 46: data loss 24 (1.10%, mean 2.12), doubling across halves and 8 from payers — checked squares, streaks and history silently rewritten ('marks from a couple of days or even a week ago disappear'; 'the results for habit one are somehow already displayed for habit three'; 'suddenly reset and lost all my data. What am I paying $29.99/year for'); all four 2026 cases from the Russian storefront in 23 days — 'for an app whose entire value is an unbroken visual record, silently rewritten history is the highest-severity failure possible'; the fix asked for is a per-habit change history with 'undo last 7 days' and conflict resolution that never deletes a completed mark. Report 47: data loss 16 (2.72%, mean 1.94), all Japanese, 8 of them in 3–20 August 2026 after an update — '7年間使った結果がこれ… アプリ更新したら勝手にデータ上書きされて今までの記録消えた' (seven years overwritten); '2022年から毎日つけていたトピックが消えていました'; '登録していたメアドに復旧のための確認メールは来ない' (no recovery mail); one user stopped writing memos because losing them hurts too much; the data-integrity union rose from 1.1% of reviews (2019–21) to 13.0% (2025–26) while crashes fell 13.8% → 4.8% — 'more stable to open and less trustworthy to rely on'; the report's fix #1: run it as an incident, restore server-side, guard sync against overwrite, ship a visible restore path. Report 48: data loss 58 (1.32%, 1.67), 25 in the 2015 sync rewrite; 36 of the 484 one-stars; Australia over-indexes (3.23%). Report 49: progress reset or lost 36 (14.15% of payers vs 2.92%) — an update or logout restarts a 66-day programme at day 1: 46 of 66 days lost, a 177-day streak lost, six accounts lost within 48 hours in June 2025 (window mean 1.92) — 'destroys the exact asset the product is selling'. Report 50: 'the app just pushed an update and erased all my data without any warning or options to save' (1★, May 2026); a Premium user's to-do entries lost and unrecoverable (Apr 2026) — no reviewer in 205 mentions a backup; fix F6: visible backup / restore and no destructive migrations. Report 52: DATA_LOSS 229 (1.11%, 2.73; 37.1% 1★) persistent every year; 56 tie loss to an update or crash — 'four years of to-do records all gone… I bought lifetime membership for this'; payers with data loss average 1.73. Report 55: 'now I lost my account including years worth of data' (BUG_DATA 35, mean 1.31); 'I'm a premium user and have already lost all my data twice' (br); reinstalling to escape a crash often wiped data. Report 56: a sync update deleted a user's habits (4★, the only severe defect) — the history is the asset outcome reviewers keep the app for. Report 57: 12 data-loss reports (8 since 2024, 6 at 1★) — 'today's update wiped all my previous data. If recovery is impossible, shouldn't you warn people before the update?'; 'I adjusted the count on one habit, saved, and every other habit's check-ins collapsed to one'. Report 59 (Tappsk): U_DATA_RISK 104 (0.69%) — 'но все мои задачи пропали' (all my tasks disappeared); 'Нигде не указано, что задачу надо обязательно сохранить' (nowhere does it say a task must be saved) — an unsaved-edit loss reads as data loss. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): 'After several months of usage all my habits disappeared upon app launch' (UA, 1★); a repeating last-week wipe on update (KZ) — two reviews (4.44%) promoted under the severe-data-loss rule. Report 65 (Rabit): 'it continuously wipes all my habits, tasks, everything and I have to start over. I have the paid version!'; 50 list items saved one by one and 'simplesmente sumiu tudo!'; 'não restaura o que tinha antes' (DATA_LOSS 10, mean 1.70; data_continuity 21, 4.22%). Report 69 (TheFor): 'Eu comprei o app. Desinstalei e na hora que fui instalar novamente, sumiu tudo o q estava lá e pediu novamente para comprar' — data and entitlement lost on reinstall (2★); F2: never lose local data on reinstall. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): 'my five minutes of effort couldn't be recorded and went to waste' (1★) — a lost check-in is lost data in a streak product. Report 71 (MyStreaks): the streak record is the asset users protect — 'I depend on it to keep track of my Streaks…that record is extremely important to me!'; streaks of 823 and 900+ days; zero data-loss, crash or login complaints in six years (thin but genuine). Report 72 (Habit Hearts): 'Всё сбросилось в бесплатной версии спустя месяц. Подскажите, так и должно быть?' — a month of free-tier tracking gone and the user cannot tell bug from policy; §8.2 #10 'Either answer is a product decision; silence is the only wrong one'. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): three data-loss reports inside 48 hours after an October 2022 update, never recurring — yet in January 2024 a buyer withheld a star purely because of them: 'Old data-loss reviews keep costing stars long after the bug is gone'. Report 76 (Way of Life): local-only storage with manual backup — U_DATA_RISK 123 (1.58%, mean 3.04★): BUG_DATA_LOSS 38, NEG_BACKUP_MANUAL 13, BUG_BACKUP 10; long histories gone on update or phone change ('using Way of Life daily for over four years… I downloaded an update and all of my data disappeared', 2★; 'for the third time, I've lost my data because I forgot to backup my data', 3★; 'I lost all my habits when I got a new phone even though I paid for the app', 5★); a 2017-07 release wiped some histories; 12 of 181 1★ are data loss. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): DEF_DATA_LOSS 3 (1.74%, mean 2.00★), all in the last seven months — 'All data gone after updating to ios 18.4' (1★; later recovered by iCloud sync), 'Han borrado los datos previos de antes del cambio de nombre' (1★, attributing the loss to the rename), 'My old boards got taken down in an update… Is there anyway I can get them back? I had a nice streak going' (4★, matching a v2.6.2 stability fix for year-old builds); 'for a habit tracker, whose entire value is an unbroken record, this is the most damaging defect class'; an archive/restore feature shipped in v2.3.0 and nothing suggests users know it exists. Report 83 (Roubit): the diary holds years of personal writing and was unreachable for weeks in two waves — DATA_LOSS 11 (2.20%, 2.91★): 'this app holds two years of my memories' (5★); 'I'd at least like to see the diary I wrote for a year, but I can't'; 'after updating, all my diary entries disappeared' (1★); 'It lost all my fragments. I had dozens.'; §8.1 treat the diary as irreplaceable data — release gate, fallback read-only view, export. Report 84 (HabitGrid): no actual data loss in 86 reviews; one warning it could happen on a phone change (4★) and one request for an optional account for backup — for a local-only app the fear itself costs a star. Report 86 (Today): U:dataloss_any 55 (3.08%, 2.67★): BUG_DATALOSS 33, BUG_BACKUP 28, BUG_ICLOUD 17 ('iCloud was clearly on but there was no automatic backup — all the data is gone', cn 1★), BUG_SAVE 12; 'these people have lost ALL my information on 2 occasions' (pe 1★); §8.4 restore must never destroy the backup it is reading, a failed restore must leave existing data intact, covers must survive a restore; REQ_ACCOUNT 3 want a login so history is not hostage to one device — but on-device data is praised, so 'optional account-based sync, not mandatory'. Report 89 (Check Calendar): DEF_DATA_LOSS 6 (2.37%), 5 of them buyers — 'i took the premium version of the app for 1 reason: so they store my data and i don't loose it, i changed my phone and lost evrything' (1★); 'bought premium for automatic backup; it failed; notes lost' (br, 5★ with negative text); 'stopped working after 2 years of tracking and wouldnt open' then a reinstall lost data and the purchase; U:device_change_fail 12 (4.74%) consistent 2022 → 2025; last report 2025-09-04 while the listing now advertises backup and restore 'even across different devices' — 'whether that fixed it is not established'. Report 90 (Quit Bad Habits & Addiction): REQ_BACKUP_SYNC 4 (0.65%) — 'if I change iPhone, will my progress be saved?' — with no account and no sync; DATA_LOSS 3 (a habit that deleted itself, a 1000-day count reset after a week, and the crash-week fear of losing 'lots of statistics and notes').

<a id="c043"></a>
### C043 — Flexible / custom frequency — N times per week, specific weekdays, counts — with non-scheduled days neutral in the statistics

**Certain** · 53 apps · 194 cards · positive in 17 apps · negative in 46 apps

*Why Certain:* 53 apps, same direction (act on it, 69%), 20 reports label it high-priority

Every X days, specific weekdays, bi-weekly, quarterly, yearly, total-over-a-window — the #1 unmet functional need and highest 4★ lift. Report 12: weekday-only repeats were asked for in Jul 2022 and still missing in May 2026 — three years and ten months. Report 20: frequency was 'N times in M days' only — specific weekdays ('Gym Mon/Wed/Fri') were never expressible in seven years (22 requests) and drove a share of the notification complaints. Report 23: times-per-week, per-day, per-month and every-N-days shipped incrementally; still absent after eleven years — yearly goals, arbitrary intervals (every 6 weeks, quarterly, a shift worker's 4–5-day rotation) and specific dates of the month (101 requests, 1.39%); a non-daily habit also consumes a daily slot under the cap. Report 24: per-weekday / shift-work scheduling requested by 31, 51.6% of them 4–5★. Report 25: flexible scheduling primitives are a stated reason to choose the app — an every-N-days reminder ('the ONLY APP I've found'), N×/week, skip, vacation mode, a custom day-start for shift workers (capped at 11:45); a weekly habit cannot be pinned to a chosen day. Report 26: flexible recurrence ('3× per week') and a vacation/pause mode ('exception periods' while travelling) requested by 12 (0.31%); only per-habit day-of-week scheduling exists. Report 27: flexible weekly frequency shipped ~2025 and is praised ('tasks that can be completed a few times a week rather than everyday'); per-weekday scheduling ('run 1 mile per day during the week, and skip Saturday + Sunday') remains a request; a Monday week-start setting was asked twice in early 2024 and never again. Report 28: a weekly-target-only model — monthly, every-other-week, multiple-times-per-day and specific-weekday scheduling requested by 15 (1.83%), one explicitly blocking a purchase: 'I can't see myself purchasing without being able to make these distinctions'. Report 29: weekday checkboxes only — x times per week without naming days ('practice golf 3 times a week but it doesn't matter on which days'), every other week ('My off days Fri, Sat, Sun every other week… its frustrating' — the only feature-driven 1★), monthly and custom intervals (14, 3.83%) — the one structural gap persisting across all five half-years. Report 30: non-daily scheduling (days of week, x per week, weekly, monthly) is the only feature gap with multi-market evidence — 4 storefronts, 4 languages — and the only build item the report supports. Report 31: 'N times per period' with no fixed days is praised by 81 (a monthly view prevents 'feel bad' spirals); removing monthly and yearly frequencies (Dec 2022 – Jan 2023) drew 58 requests still arriving in 2026 ('This was the ONE reason I used to love this app'; contact lenses monthly, weight loss yearly; 'call friend once a month or take a vacation three times a year'; deep-clean the oven monthly). Report 33: 'N times a week' and every-N-days frequency are named differentiators (flexible scheduling praised 79, mean 4.80); 'N per week' was removed in Habitify X and restored; monthly nth-weekday and end dates are still requested (82; haircut, bills on the 15th, can't end a 30-day challenge). Report 34: x-days-per-week added on request (Apr 2019), flexible frequency praised by 13 (mean 4.92); every-other-day and monthly targets still requested (7). Report 36: flexible schedules (every N days, N×/week or month) requested by 7 in E1–E3 and not since Dec 2024 (probably addressed); habits shown on unscheduled days (3, all 4–5★). Report 41: 'X times per week, any days' / 'every N days' (13) and seeing which day a weekly habit was done (9) — one request asked twice, every year 2021–2026, 8 of 13 at 4★: 'I would like the option of doing something 3 times a week, not necessarily on the same day'; the app models which-days and how-many-times as alternatives. Report 42: setting which days, dates and repetition is Premium ('task repetition is paid-plan only', JP 1★); 'Tue & Thu' and shifting a habit to another day requested. Report 43: scheduling flexibility is the longest-running unaddressed request (29, 4.55%, mean 3.38; Jan 2017 → Jan 2025) — intervals beyond one month ('Wish I'd known that before I paid for it'), Nth weekday ('1st Tuesday of each month'), 'X times per week' without fixed days, every other week, a due date rolling from last completion; a redesign regression made 'every 2/3 weeks' habits show every week. Report 46: every-N-days, X-per-week without fixed days and monthly schedules are the longest-running functional request (34, mean 4.09, every era Sep 2019 → Jul 2026) — 'a medicine I must use every other day and I can't put it on this app'; a shift worker on trial calling it 'potentially a deal breaker'; 'most of my habit are repeated every 3 days… Apple reminders is WAY more efficient' (churned). Report 47: X-per-week and monthly habits requested by 8 (mean 4.12) — absent, and a 5★ requester withdrew the request to protect simplicity. Report 48: arbitrary cadences such as every-other-day requested by 35 (3.97); weekday scheduling — weekly goals that still demand a daily answer — 21 (3.57). Report 50: 'at least N per week' goals missing (2, 5.00 — a weekly goal marked complete at Mon–Thu cannot record Friday and Sunday); every-other-day, future start date and 15-minute increments requested (4). Report 52: monthly, every-other-day and N-per-week rules (299); weekly-N habits spoil a '100% day'. Report 53: '3 times a week, any day', every other day, a day of the month (CORE_FREQ 54, 3.76); a 3×/week habit fails Monday and Tuesday and support's Skip 'skips that task for the week'; '2 times weekly' must be done twice in one day. Report 54: 'X times a week without naming the days' — 24 (6.50%, 3.79); two call the scheduling model 'unusable' ('I don't care or know when those days will be but this app makes you designate them'; shift workers, DE). Report 55: 'You set your own standards (every day, certain days a week, or a number of days in a week/month)… it doesn't disqualify you if you don't do each habit every single day' (CORE_FLEX 148, 4.82 — the named differentiator); gaps: weekly totals, monthly periods, custom week start, optional end dates. Report 56: non-daily scheduling is the oldest request (day one) and the only one with a rating penalty — the corpus's only 3★: 'Great daily but no weekly… I love the daily tracking for free with no premium version, but I feel like we need a weekly/monthly/select days option!'; five of six forms reduce to 'this habit is not daily' (x per week, weekly, monthly, select days); a deadline request is a different product (D1). Report 57: every-N-days, monthly, yearly and month-end scheduling requested (7). Report 58: times per day, per weekday ('only make habits show up on specific days for my gym sessions'), biweekly and monthly — 4 reviewers, 4 storefronts, one gap in a weekly-goal model. Report 59 (Tappsk): REQ_HABIT_OPTIONS 113 (0.74%) and REQ_RECURRENCE 51 — habit scheduling and count options are a steady request beside REQ_CUSTOMIZE 234, the largest single request (80 of the 4★ reviews). Report 60 (Mindway): recurrence limited to daily / weekly / monthly is the largest functional request — R_REPEAT_OPTIONS 3 and R_CUSTOM_TASKS 4 of only 10 requests: 'I don't need to flip my mattress every month, but that's the only option I'm given'; hourly hydration, every 2 weeks, every 6 months, haircuts; plus fixed 28/38-day programme pacing the user cannot control ('neden tüm planları kendimiz hemen o gün yapamıyoruz'); D5: fix the recurrence model before adding anything else — four of ten requesters ask for flexibility in different words. Report 65 (Rabit): CORE_FREQ 9 (1.81%, mean 4.11), all Brazilian over five years — 'Preciso estudar música 3x por semana (0/3)… (1/3), (2/3) e (3/3)'; 'minha rotina não permite sempre me exercitar nos mesmo dias'; 'Sem isso a assinatura não vale a pena' (a conditional purchase); with skip, partial multi-per-day, reset time and week start, 15 reviews (3.01%) describe one model limitation — fixed weekdays; S2; research: why only Brazilians ask. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): strength-training users — rest days are part of training, so a daily rule does not fit (REQ_FREQ 8). Report 72 (Habit Hearts): more repeat intervals — 'cada 15 días … o una vez al mes'; 'add monthly as a repeat option' (2). Report 76 (Way of Life): the one structural request for fifteen years — U_FLEX_REQ 347 (4.47%, mean 4.13★) = REQ_FREQUENCY 214 (weekdays, N times a week, weekly/monthly) + REQ_COUNT 129 (quantities) + NEG_YESNO 36 (a partial state); present in 15 of 16 calendar years and in every era (1.8–4.5%); the most frequent code in 4★ after generic praise (96 of 1,281) and 2.39× more common among purchasers than the corpus; a 2016 reviewer was 'waiting for the promised weekly/monthly options' and they never came (NEG_DEV_PROMISE); users emulate it with skip, which distorts the percentages they value (NEG_CHART 38); §8.4 schedule on weekdays or N/week with non-scheduled days neutral and excluded from percentages, counts as a separate journal type, yes/no as the default, guarding against bloat (PR_KEEP_SIMPLE 64). Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): 'x times per week' scheduling is the only feature requested twice by otherwise-happy 4★ users, 11 months apart ('3 veces a la semana o 2 veces al mes'; ''x-mal pro Woche' zu definieren anstatt 'a Tag x und y'… Mich verwundert, dass es das nicht gibt'); scheduling is weekday-only; the use case is 'go to the gym three times a week, any three days'; 'an app built on missing a day is fine still forces users to name the days' — a scheduling-model gap that contradicts the product's own thesis; §8.8 one of the three things to do. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): REQ_WEEKLY_SCHEDULE 3 (4.67★, 2024-10 → 2026-07), partial only (v2.4.0 lets you disable streak/consistency; no weekly target): 'a gym habit done 3×/week can never build a streak, so the app's core feedback loop breaks for non-daily habits'; 'Wenn ich einzelne Tage skippen könnte, oder ein Wochenziel festlegen… Das wäre der 5. Stern für mich' (4★) — one of only two pre-committed-star requests in the corpus. Report 83 (Roubit): REQ_FLEX_SCHEDULE 10 (2.00%) — every N days, weekly counts, reps ('if it's 10 planks a day'), recurring deadlines, a pomodoro timer. (Consolidation after report 83: title widened from 'Flexible / custom frequency' to name the three shapes and the statistics rule; the earlier evidence stays in the statement.) Report 84 (HabitGrid): REQ_FREQUENCY 5 (5.81%), the only recurring request, in five variants (N per week without fixed days, specific weekdays, every N days, monthly, custom interval), one attaching rating elasticity ('if it appears, this app will have no equal'); all five predate 1.0.15 'Smarter habit goals' and none of the 27 reviews after repeats it; §8.5 check each variant against the shipped goals — where present, the fix is discoverability. Report 85 (Habitica): REQ_FREQ 45 (1.31%) — '3 times a week'; 'there being no option for truly weekly tasks' (1★); REQ_DUE 12; REQ_REPEAT_TODO 9; §8.6 'N times per week' Dailies. Report 86 (Today): scheduling covers daily / weekdays / N per week (max 6) or month (max 25) / multiple check-ins a day — the most complete in the series — yet REQ_FREQ 27 still ask for every-N-days ('If the app had this capability, I would rate it 5 stars and purchase the full version') and weekday-only reminders ('add weekday-only reminders and I'll pay immediately', cn). Report 89 (Check Calendar): FRICTION_CHECK_INPUT — touching a future date checks it by accident (jp, 4★); a yes/no calendar without a schedule has no non-scheduled days, so every mis-tap is a record.

<a id="c033"></a>
### C033 — Restore purchase and entitlements must work immediately

**Certain** · 45 apps · 193 cards · positive in 3 apps · negative in 44 apps · tied to a purchase in 1 apps

*Why Certain:* 45 apps, same direction (act on it, 96%), 21 reports label it high-priority

Charging and not delivering is the second-fastest route to 1★ (×13.9). Lifetime buyers told to subscribe, subscribers who cannot find their tier, premium members still upsold. Report 11: 3 of 3 paid reviewers lost purchased access — a lifetime non-consumable expired, a subscription re-locked after a week and reinstall did not restore, an active annual term was re-charged — and two titled their reviews 'scam' and 'Purchase fraud'. Report 12: 40% of self-identified payers reported that payment did not grant access (paywall re-appears, 'no subscription found', Restore Purchase redirecting to the privacy policy, HTTP 400 at login, re-purchase demanded on a new device) — rising to 12.6% of all 2025 reviews. Report 18: 25 entitlement failures (mean 2.44★; 9.94% of confirmed payers; every Japanese instance 1★) — lifetime buyers denied Pro, a PayPay lifetime never applied, a subscription active in iOS settings with premium unusable, and a lifetime holder whose entitlement was deleted when they cancelled an accidental annual plan. The worst case: a power cut reset a lifetime buyer to onboarding, wiped every routine, then demanded a subscription. Report 19: 5 of 105 paid and could not use the product — 'I can log in on my laptop but no apps'; iPhone login error 300 with no message while iPad worked; account access lost once cancellation was started. Report 20: legacy lifetime entitlements often did not survive a device change; restore-purchase failures (91, mean 1.59) recurred for years after the 2021 revocation, and 75.8% of them came from confirmed payers. Report 25: 'already paid, asked to pay again' — 8 reviews across a 16-month window (Mar 2025 → Jul 2026), including a lifetime purchase that restore does not recognise ('every time I enter the app it tells me to remove them or to buy the subscription to keep my habits'); emerging by rate, severe by kind, and the persistence argues against a one-off outage. Report 26: purchase lost or not delivered is the top paid-user failure (24, 0.63%; 12 of 72 explicit payers = 16.7%) by three mechanisms — the 2022 repricing withdrew a purchased unlock, restore-purchases fails or the button is dead, payment succeeded but premium never activated. Report 28: 10 of 24 identifiable payers (41.7%) report a purchase not delivered or not restorable — a $9.99 pack that never appeared with 'no Support button in the app. Nor on developer's website'; restore failing on a new device with the same account; a purchased cosmetic that reverted; consumables cannot be restored the way non-consumables can. Report 30: 'Списаны деньги за подписку, премиум функция не открылась' — charged with premium never unlocked — 'unambiguously a bug and should be treated as a P0 incident, not a review'; both billing failures are Russian, the only market with continuous purchase attempts. Report 31: 468 reviews (9.02%, mean 1.23; 304 explicit payers) say Premium they paid for was not granted — 2023 200, 2024 200 — including 295 'lifetime' buyers who stayed on Basic (mean 1.14, 89.5% 1★): the post-purchase 'gift' / Growth-Bundle screen appears to drop the entitlement when dismissed ('by not finishing this flow and purchasing the upsell, I think it doesn't recognize I purchased it'); one clean success ('I was successful at purchasing and using a lifetime premium upgrade') suggests a code-path defect that ran at least 16 months — make the entitlement grant atomic with the purchase and show any cross-sell after. Report 33: entitlement failure is small (69, 1.75%) and mostly portability — web (Paddle) purchases not unlocking the iPhone, a lifetime tied to one e-mail and paid twice, guest → account, a new or stolen phone, 18 days without activation, 6+ weeks and 20+ e-mails to resolve, a lifetime holder asked to subscribe on the Watch — plus a Jan 2018 wave (21, 11 in Japan) fixed within two weeks; the report asks for one entitlement per person recognised on every platform, with guest and account purchases merged automatically. Report 36: entitlements don't travel — skins 'unlocking them on each device'; a payer who cannot find out whether the subscription covers one device. Report 41: premium bought on iPhone never reached the iPad (2022) and premium intermittently reverted to free with Restore Purchases failing (2025) — 'a paying customer being shown a paywall is the most damaging possible bug'. Report 46: entitlement not recognised across devices or after a trial — 4 payers ('App does not recognize it… even after refreshing the subscription with the provided link'; '明明都在pad己開通高級版，Iphone上卻不給用'; one resolved only by refund and re-purchase); the report's #3 fix is one entitlement across iPhone, iPad, Watch, Mac and web with a visible subscription-status screen. Report 47: premium status reverted to free with ads reappearing (3 payers, January 2021); a 'purchase failed' loop on every open (Jul 2026); the report's fix #3 is entitlement recognition. Report 49: restore purchase fails 5 — every one a paying customer locked out of what they bought, all 1★ — 'the most severe five-review theme in the corpus'. Report 52: PAY_RESTORE 190 (0.92%, 2.61; payer lift ×3.21) — an iPhone membership not recognised on iPad, memberships lost after reinstall, and a reinstall path where restoring one's own data asks for a membership that does not restore. Report 53: PAY_RESTORE carries the highest payer lift (6.32); a lifetime buyer about to post a bait-and-switch review tapped Restore Purchase and 'the app went back to normal and no more pop ups' — so part of the 2026 legacy cluster is a restore failure the app could fix by restoring on launch (F2). Report 54: 'for a one-time-purchase product, restore-purchases is not a feature, it is the product's warranty' — 7 restore failures (every one 1★) across BR, ES, GR, TH, UA×2, US, 2021 → 2026, P3 rate 4.2% (five-fold rise), 6× more concentrated outside high-spend storefronts; F1: a visible, labelled Restore button — the single largest source of one-star reviews. Report 55: premium gone after a new phone or reinstall (PAY_RESTORE 18, 1.11, lift 10.22) because premium was tied to an e-mail account; F1: restore-purchase tied to Apple ID. Report 57: 8 restore failures, all from 2024 ('I changed phones and my Premium purchase is gone'; 'after reinstalling I get ads again'); 3 whose entitlement never applied; a July 2026 release (3.1.0) broke Premium activation and restore — 8 reviews in 5 days, six 1★, one still broken on 3.1.1, externally corroborated by the release notes. Report 59 (Tappsk): BUG_PURCHASE 142 (0.94%, 2.81★, 8.43× among purchasers) — 'оплачено 990руб за подписку, но работать в этой программе нельзя пока ещё 1499 руб не заплатите' (990 ₽ paid but you cannot work until you pay another 1,499 ₽); a lifetime unlock listed in the phone's subscriptions as 'for a year'; the fix: restore the lifetime unlock from any receipt, on any device, on the Mac, after a reinstall, with no annual charge in between. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): 'I paid for subscription monthly but still not working. Is this scam?' (BR, 1★) — two of six self-identified payers had an entitlement failure, 'the worst ratio in this report'; I2: audit the purchase-unlock path end to end, including a charged subscription that still behaves as free. Report 64 (Critique AI): paid but still gated — the paywall popup persists after purchase (age 15), restore fails ('I can't restore my purchase so basically I can't do anything now'), reinstall demands payment again, and a second device refuses login ('you have to pay for each device') — 4 of 13 payers (30.8%), 3 of 13 fully gated (23.1%) — 'converts a completed sale into a 1★ and a fraud accusation'; F4. Report 65 (Rabit): PAY_ENTITLE 9 (1.81%, mean 1.56) — 100% payers, Sep 2021 → Mar 2026: 'Fiz a assinatura do plano plus anual e o app não reconhece!'; a subscriber still capped at five habits; a buyer's to-do list locked; lifetime charged but 'O app consta como se eu não tivesse o pacote'; ads and 'upgrade to premium' prompts after paying; a new phone offered only a new plan; an account 'não existe' after reinstall; F2: audit fresh install, new device, reinstall and Android→iOS, and make Restore Purchases reachable. Report 67 (Habio): U_ACCESS_FAIL 97 (4.73%, mean 1.02) — cannot log in / email not found 52, paid but no premium or restore fails 43, purchased PDF not delivered 10; 'even i payed for subscription 350 kr but everything is locked'; §8.4: link web purchases to app accounts automatically. Report 68 (Ultiself): paid access never unlocked (BUG_PURCHASE 18) and login failures often after a web purchase (BUG_LOGIN 41). Report 69 (TheFor): 3 of 4 self-stated payers describe a failure (mean 2.75 vs 4.62 for non-payers) — 'I payed for an annual subscription but the app is still prompting me to pay. Hitting restore purchase does not help'; a reinstall that lost the purchase — 22 months apart on two storefronts, 'a persistent weakness in the receipt-validation / restore path'; F1: validate the receipt on launch, never paywall a Pro owner, show entitlement state in-app. Report 72 (Habit Hearts): an accidental sale-pop-up purchase not recognised after delete-and-reinstall — 'still asking me to purchase the thing I already accidentally purchased' — §8.1 #6 restore after reinstall, findable. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): both restore failures had paid — a tablet upgrade that did not appear on the phone (no support contact found) and 'Doesn't let you transfer purchases from one OS to another. Waste of money' (1★) — 'the most costly review type there is'. Report 76 (Way of Life): BUG_PURCHASE 54 (0.70%, mean 2.69★) runs the whole 16 years and is 9.48× over-represented among purchasers and 11.60% of 1★; 'money were taken but nothing had changed' (ru 1★); 'es gebe nichts zum wiederherstellen' (de 1★); rose after the model change (0.91% → 1.55%); ru over-indexes 3.29×. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): U:paid_broken 4 (2.33%), mean 1.00★ — the only theme where every review is one star, and 4 of 11 1★ overall: 'I paid for the pro features but still features are not unlocked. Restore purchase is also not working' (2024-11); 'Lifetime purchase doesn't work. Restore purchases doesn't work. Developer doesn't respond' (2026-01); 'Estafa — Pagué por la versión premium pero no puedo usarla en mis dos celulares' (2026-06); a recurring class over 19 months, not one build; 3 of 9 stated payers; §8.8 #1 'make purchases and restores work, everywhere, including offline'. Report 83 (Roubit): PAID_NOT_UNLOCKED 4 — 'I was stuck with only 8 even after paying' with no support reply (us 1★); 'despite paying for the ¥6,000 annual plan, none of the paid features applied… 詐欺に近い対応です' (jp 1★, refund requested); membership 'sometimes drops'; one fixed by support via Restore Subscription; SCAM_LANGUAGE is otherwise absent (2 in 500). Report 85 (Habitica): BUG_IAP 9 — subscription benefits and gems not credited after payment; §8.4 restore/credit checks and a preview of paid backgrounds. Report 86 (Today): MON_RESTORE 18 (2016-03-28 → 2021-02-12), a nine-year unresolved defect — 'I bought it last year — why does it charge again after reinstalling?' (cn 5★); 'I delete the app, now I install it again (on the same phone) and I have to buy the features again' (nl 4★); '¿Es una estafa?' (es 1★); 'I paid for the Premium twice' (2★); China carries 8 of the 18; one reviewer found Settings → Restore Purchases himself — 'the function exists and is undiscoverable'; MON_IAP_FAIL 11 incl. a March 2018 cluster where the product showed as 'no longer available' ('I am trying to give you $4.99… It keeps failing. I wrote for help and no response', 1★); §8.2 'surface restore at the paywall, not buried in Settings'. Report 89 (Check Calendar): DEF_RESTORE_PURCHASE 9 (3.56%), all buyers — the failure point is the device change: 'I have the premium version but had to change devices… it's asking me to pay again' (br); 'I already PAID and now it wants me to pay again???' (ca); the restore button 'does nothing' on a new iPhone; a buyer cannot use Premium on their iPad; three buyers used the review to ask how to restore; 15 of 31 buyers (48.4%) report a post-purchase problem; none reported in 2026 (5 buyers) — §8.3 treat the silence as unconfirmed, test iPhone → iPhone and iPhone → iPad restore of both purchase and records, and make Restore purchase and backup status visible in settings.

<a id="c029"></a>
### C029 — Billing must be exactly right

**Certain** · 43 apps · 160 cards · positive in 5 apps · negative in 40 apps · tied to a purchase in 1 apps

*Why Certain:* 43 apps, same direction (act on it, 97%), 21 reports label it high-priority

Wrong amount, double charge, surprise renewal are the fastest route to 1★ (×21 lift); single price shown, no trial-to-charge traps, refunds honoured, receipts clear. Report 19: a 105-review corpus that was 91% one-star and 71% about money — charged after cancelling (19), charged with no recognised subscription (19), double-billed (16), charged ≠ agreed ($29.99 annual agreed, $59.99/month billed), and terms permitting weekly renewal made 'again and again every week' structurally possible. Report 23: nothing supports deceptive billing on a single Apple payment; refund friction (79, mean 1.75, 70.9% 1★) is Apple's process, and reviewers address Apple through the review field. Report 24: charged after cancelling 1,620 (3.73%, mean 1.085), duplicate charges 584, charge without consent 338 (mean 1.047), not visible in Apple Subscriptions 125 — all consequences of billing outside Apple IAP; 1,412 edited reviews are mostly downgrades after a later charge. Report 31: billing-dispute language in 403 reviews (7.77%, mean 1.24) — refund, scam, fraud, estafa, arnaque, Abzocke, 欺诈 in eight languages — with 13 calling on Apple to remove the developer; billing & entitlement integrity rose 1.6% (E1) → 34.5% (E4) → 25.4% (E5): 768 reviews (14.81%, mean 1.30); discount offers checked out at full price in 69 (49 actually charged; '$59.99 crossed out and … $9.99 … My card was charged full price'; support: 'a bug that happens sometimes') — make the displayed price the charged price and audit introductory-offer configuration per storefront (CA, AU, GB, DE first). Report 33: billing integrity 147 (3.73%, mean 2.22) — charged more than shown (¥4,900 shown, ¥5,150 charged; a $39.99 offer charged $48.97; monthly chosen, annual charged; lifetime then an annual charge); billing-dispute register 「詐欺アプリ」, 'Abzocke', 'CON ARTISTS', 流氓. Report 36: all 3 billing reviews are 1★ — a cancellation link that returns 'Cannot cancel subscription' ('roach motel'), an unauthorised annual charge on a disabled reviewer, and five annual fees for one bundle membership with two refunds denied (China) — triaged regardless of 0.56% share as the only consumer-protection records. Report 42: three payers charged without intending — 'immediately charged for a subscription upon opening the app for the first time'; 'auto-selected a package and deducted money… hadn't even tried it' (499k₫); a promotional R$39.90/year that became R$99.90 at checkout — plus a trial that 'won't get the refund even if you cancel two minutes after'; 11 of 29 writing payers (37.9%) request refunds. Report 46: 13 billing failures (0.60%, mean 2.31) — charged on day one of a 7-day trial (twice), a subscription the app would not recognise ('App does not recognize it and won't let me add more than three habits, even after refreshing… On to the next app'; premium on iPad not on iPhone), a wrong amount (CHF 40.45 for 29.95), four refund requests — vs 2 refund references in report 43's one-time corpus. Report 47: 8 billing failures (1.36%) in a 13-payer corpus — premium reverting to free with ads back (3 in January 2021), '400円を2回も騙し取られた' (charged ¥400 twice), 'アプリを開くと毎回「購入に失敗しました。」' (a purchase-failed loop, Jul 2026), an unintended half-year subscription, a crash the moment a trial payment went through. Report 48: billing problem 23 (2.52) — 1 / 4 / 6 / 12 by era, the fastest-growing monetisation fault: charged $39.99 instead of the agreed $4.99; charged the full year at the start of a 7-day trial; charged twice after cancelling before the trial ended, blocking other App Store purchases; 'another active subscriber using the same receipt'; paid subscription not recognised after an update (3); 23 refund requests at mean 1.04★ — the lowest-mean theme with n > 10. Report 49: every overcharge review is a payer — €1.99/month becoming €30 at once, $2/month becoming $70, £25 on top of £29.99, a year charged during a trial, seven months of charges after cancellation (9; payers 8.49% vs 0.73% globally). Report 50: 3 reviews (mean 1.00, all 1★, Aug 2024 → Jan 2026) charged an amount not matching the quote — '$14.99 for the yearly membership' vs a $31.01 bank charge; 'said to be $14.99 after the free trial but I was charged $30 before my free trial was up. This app is a scam'; ~$50 annual auto-charge — the same ~$15 advertised vs ~$30 charged 17 months apart; 'The app does not accept any of my cards' (2 cannot pay) — the only defect class with a 1.00 mean and no exceptions; fix F1 and experiment: instrument price displayed vs charged per storefront. Report 52: 2018–2020 billing defects (261, 83.5% in those years: purchases that spin forever, double charges, ¥12 shown but ¥31 charged); a gb 'lifetime' purchase billed as £12.99/month (2023); a tw buyer of the NT$390 lifetime unlock charged NT$220 when the concurrent trial converted (Aug 2026); an SMS login that subscribed a user to ¥55/month of carrier services (single report, legal exposure). Report 53: unexpected charges PAY_CHARGE 34 (mean 1.38, 85.3% 1★); a one-week trial billed for a year (kr); an accidental purchase on first open. Report 54: a purchase that never unlocked ('I paid for the app and absolutely nothing. It's exactly as it was before', AU; 'Still telling me Become a habit pro!', KR) — 6, mean 1.17. Report 55: 'BEEN TRYING FOR MONTHS TO CANCEL MY SUBSCRIPTION'; auto-renewal on an account the user can't log in to; charged after a trial (PAY_CHARGE 7). Report 57: listed ₩29,000 but the card was charged ₩44,000; ₩3,994 charged after a redeem code. Report 59 (Tappsk): U_BILLING 485 (3.20%, mean 2.30★) is the largest negative that is neither a price objection nor a product defect; even the reviewer's own missed cancellation ('забыла отменить подписку', 5★) lands as a support ticket in the reviews, and refunds are reported both granted ('Все вернули! Оперативно') and refused ('Деньги, естественно, никто не возвращает'). Report 60 (Mindway): billing operations failing is 'a store-risk problem, not a pricing problem' — 11 of 216 (5.09%, mean 1.27, 10 of 11 US): charged for a year without subscribing ('this needs to be reported and i want my money back'), charged after cancelling with screenshots of inactive status, a $0.99 'free trial' billed $39.99 within hours, a 3-day trial that billed a week after cancelling on day two, monthly implied but the whole year drafted; the corpus cannot prove the charges were unauthorized, but eleven users could not tell what they had agreed to or how to get out, and seven of them used a public review as their support channel; all 13 confirmed payers are the only source of every refund, cancellation and surprise-charge report — 'the corpus contains no post-purchase success story at all'. Report 64 (Critique AI): 'On the website it said cancel anytime but it immediately billed me'; 'They say that they give a three day trial but charge you for the full year upfront'; reinstall charged again — PAY_BILLING 8 (1.91%, mean 1.50), 6 of 13 self-stated payers. Report 65 (Rabit): billing_failure 28 (5.62%, mean 1.75) nearly all payers; PAY_REFUND 8 at mean 1.12 — the lowest of any theme — for crashes after an annual subscription, reminders not working after Plus, ads despite paying, a post-trial charge, and two unanswered refund emails. Report 67 (Habio): U_BILLING_HARM 878 (42.81%, mean 1.04; 60.05% of non-seeded) — charged after cancelling 351, trial conversion 173, workbook 189, charged with no subscription 164, duplicate charges 157, amount above shown 55; U_ESCALATION 196 (9.56%): bank / card / PayPal disputes 118 and regulator / police / legal threats 94 (BBB, FTC, ACCC, state attorneys general, OCU, Sernac, Verbraucherzentrale — 'Abofalle'); a card statement under the company name the customer had to research ('Tuve que investigar que aplicaciones tenía GOTOTOP LTD'). Report 68 (Ultiself): MON_EXTRA_CHARGE 632 (14.01%, 2021-02-28 → 2026-09-06, every era), MON_SCAM 747 (16.56%); MON_ESCALATE 189 (4.19%) — card blocks, chargebacks, reports to Apple, police, regulators and lawyers; reviewers teach each other to block the payment in their bank app (REV_TIP 5); 'Leaving is rarely the story; being unable to leave is' (deletion 8 vs escalation 189).

<a id="c039"></a>
### C039 — Reminders fire reliably, once

**Certain** · 42 apps · 106 cards · positive in 9 apps · negative in 37 apps

*Why Certain:* 42 apps, same direction (act on it, 88%), 13 reports label it high-priority

Reminders that work are a top praise item; not firing or spamming is a 1★ driver. Report 23: 97 (1.33%, mean 3.48, 18.6% 1★) — reminders that don't fire (Thailand 4 of 22, 18.2%, limited evidence), fire for already-completed tasks, fire all at once at night, ignore Do Not Disturb, or interrupt a meditation to say meditate; the 'smart' auto-timing algorithm is widely disliked. Report 24: notification volume/control 744 (1.71%, mean 2.437) — users turn all notifications off, which disables the product; give per-notification-type control. Report 27: the reminder fires for a goal already marked complete today — 'a notification that contradicts app state actively trains users to ignore notifications'. Report 28: notification annoyance 5 (0.61%, mean 2.80) — decay-guilt pushes ('YOUR BUNNY'S LOSING HEALTH'). Report 29: reminders that never fire, deleted reminders that keep firing (surviving delete-and-reinstall), and changed times that don't take (6, mean 3.17) — one problem: the notification schedule is written once and never reconciled against the habit's state; cancel scheduled notifications on delete and stop the day's reminders on check-off. Report 30: a user wants an alarm, not just a notification — 'receives an alarm from the app itself and doesn't need another alarm on the phone'. Report 33: reminders praised by 91 (repeat every 30 min until done) and broken in 68, notably when iOS 13 broke notifications. Report 34: the reminder time picker broke for a paying user ('I payed for this app … I might just cancel my membership', Dec 2025) and again Mar 2026; a 2019 buyer got no notifications and returned the purchase. Report 43: an iOS 15 notification regression ran five public weeks (13 Oct – 10 Nov 2021: firing after completion, double notifications, 'I don't think the solution is to have us individually email tech support. It's clearly a bug'; a payer 'over a month and a half… no bug fix'); ghost habits — deleted habits still firing at midnight after reinstall and a new phone (2); notification bugs 15 (2.35%, mean 2.60) on the app's signature feature. Report 46: a deleted habit's notification kept firing (the most-voted review in the corpus, 25 votes); reminders not firing 7; finer reminder control (per day, stop once done) requested by 9. Report 47: reminder time-setting buggy Jan–Feb 2021; non-scheduled weekdays notified until fixed by June 2026 — notification bugs 11 (1.87%). Report 48: notification bugs 78 (1.77%, 2.64) at a stable ratio against 224 reminder praise; notification overload 12 (2.33). Report 52: reminders were why people installed (and in 2017 what they reviewed to unlock), so REM_FAIL carries a 3.62× payer lift — silent mode kills the sound, reminders keep firing after the habit is done (23 votes), archived habits still remind, changed sounds revert. Report 53: in an app named HabitMinder reminders are tied to a time-of-day section, not a clock time — an evening habit reminds at 8 am ('the only reminder that can be set is for 8am'), a 30-reminder list hits iOS's scheduled-notification cap so some habits are never reminded, and reminders fire for habits already done (REM_CONTROL 56, 2.88; REM_ANNOY 28; REM_FAIL 13). Report 54: notification defects — no badge, nagging after completion, wrong sound (6, 2.50). Report 55: medication reminders that fail; push instead of sound-only in silent mode. Report 59 (Tappsk): BUG_REMINDER 96 (0.63%, 2.78★) in every era — 'unless you open the app every other day, the reminders you set will stop working'; 'за весь день дай бог словить хотя бы 2 уведомления' (lucky to catch two notifications a day); PR_REMINDERS 401 shows the same feature is a top praise when it works. Report 65 (Rabit): the ledger's clearest reminder regression — REM_FAIL 66 (13.25%, mean 2.91), 10.8% of launch-era reviews, 0.8% for the next 25 months, then 45.7% of everything written from Nov 2023 to Sep 2026 and still open at the last review; 14 reviewers (2.81%) report the app is absent from iOS Settings → Notifications altogether, across iPhone and iPad, seven storefronts and five languages, after reinstalls — 'almost certainly a missing or failing UNUserNotificationCenter authorization request'; 'Qual o sentido de fazer um app de habitos e nao ter notificação?'; 15 of 66 are 4★ and 9 are 5★; REM_GOOD (a perfect 5.00) fell 8.1% → 0.8%; the loop a reviewer described — cue (notification), routine, reward (the tree) — loses its first step; three abandoned lifetime / subscription purchases, 10 of 49 payers, three refunds; F1: confirm the authorization request on a current device before anything else. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): missing, duplicated and phantom reminders across 2017 → 2026 (BUG_NOTIF 38) against 203 reviews crediting the reminder (PR_NOTIF, 4.84) — 'The second notification arrived at a moment as if it had seen through my laziness'. Report 72 (Habit Hearts): 'приходят не все уведомления о привычках' (3★ — the only rating reduction from a plain defect); a 5★ titled 'Notification bug' resolved individually by support — handled per-user rather than systemically (§8.2 #11). Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): multiple reminders — asked by three reviewers in 2024 — shipped in v2.2.0 (2026-03-01) and generated two reliability complaints five and six weeks later (DEF_NOTIF_FAIL 2, 3.50★: 'maybe is a bug I would like a anwser') — a newly shipped requested feature created its own defect class. Report 86 (Today): BUG_NOTIF 63 (3.53%, 2.57★), 2016-04-04 → 2025-02-10 — ten years never fully fixed ('notifications are straight up not working for habits. I have 3 set up and they never go off'; 'out of ten habits it notifies one or two, and for days no notification is delivered', br); 10 of 63 say it makes the app unusable; a specific reproducible behaviour reported independently in 2017 and 2021 — 'if I don't check in every single day, the reminders stop all together'; 'surely this is the most important time to have a reminder?' — §8.3 'a habit app that goes quiet precisely when the user lapses has inverted its own purpose'. Report 88 (GetHabit): DEF_REMINDERS 18 (3.67%) — 'the habit notifications are sent at the complete wrong time'; 'it goes back to the default time so the reminders don't work properly'; §8.8 'reminders that fire at the set time… are table stakes in the category'.

<a id="c175"></a>
### C175 — Updates must not break function or wipe progress

**Certain** · 38 apps · 110 cards · positive in 3 apps · negative in 35 apps

*Why Certain:* 38 apps, same direction (act on it, 100%), 21 reports label it high-priority

'Then Boom… updated! Now… the progress is gone' (report 4); a nine-week window of hard functional failures (report 8); an update broke chronological sorting across four countries in one week (report 9); near-daily forced updates are themselves a complaint (report 10). Report 18: a July 2026 update told a mid-term subscriber to buy a new plan; lag, solved by 2025, regressed sharply (1.83% → 5.38%) as routine modes, intensity levels and note/tracker features were added. Report 26: the 2022 'music cannot be turned off' defect (10 reviews, May–Nov 2022) was fixed and stayed fixed — a clean, closed defect; the later inverse (music won't play) is 3 reviews. Report 27: the 2025 update broke launch on iOS 26 and removed the one-tap note export, the day-tap record popup, the single-screen annual overview and backfill from the annual grid — the same update that shipped multi-check-ins and flexible frequency; 'feature removals in this app are more expensive than feature absences'. Report 28: a listing version ten months older than the newest reviews coincides with 2026 freezing, crashing and broken-login reports — 'verify the app on current iOS and ship an update'; the 2022 rabbit-off-screen, can't-clean-the-room and orange-screen bugs were fixed and stayed fixed. Report 31: v2 rebuild (Mar 2022) brought 10–30 s tap lag, a broken Watch app and removed past-entry editing (restored in 2.0.8); v3.0 (Jan 2023) brought a week-start bug and a custom-count +1 bug. Report 33: v2.0 (Nov 2016) wiped data and Premium; Habitify X broke the Watch; 'update made it worse' spiked 7.6% in 2020 and 5.8% in 2025. Report 43: regression after update 16 (2.51%) — 3 → 4 → 9 by era, eight of the nine recent inside Oct 2025 – Jul 2026; three updates in two days then 'I can no longer access the app… All the I spent created things are lost'. Report 46: 'The new IOS update has wiped all of my historical and tracking data' (GB, 1★, Sep 2022); a Sep 2020 'won't open after the update' cluster of six reviews in three days across five storefronts. Report 47: an update in August 2026 overwrote years of history (8 reviews in 3–20 Aug); an update in 2022 scrambled habit order (5); the back button vanished in Nov 2020; 'アプリ更新したら勝手にデータ上書きされて'. Report 48: paid subscription not recognised after an update (3); the 2015 v3.0 release lost data for 25 and duplicated trackers for 20. Report 52: an update that could not be downloaded or reinstalled produced 12 reviews on one day (31 Jul 2023); BUG_UPDATE 524 (2.54%, 3.26). Report 53: re-certify Watch app and widgets on every iOS release — iOS 11.3, iOS 13 and iOS 18/26 each broke a surface. Report 55: crash waves after the July 2017, 2018 and 2020 updates; fixes reported twice, the second after nine months. Report 56: a sync update deleted habits; defects clustered in the Jun–Jul build cycle. Report 57: 'an update broke it' is constant for seven years (update_regression 59, 7.57%) — a Sep 2020 release broke the note keyboard (21 reviews in three days, mostly still 5★) and a Jun 2020 release stopped launch (8); 'every update breaks something that worked. Please just leave it alone'. Report 59 (Tappsk): BUG_UPDATE 103 (2.83★) and the four release-clustered regressions ([[C031]]); the quietest release era (E4, 2022-03 → 2023-05) is also the best-rated (4.70★, praise 80.3%, defects 3.5%), and the regression era that followed the lowest since launch on crashes. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): 'Seems like each time when it updates the habits progress for the last week wipes. These happened two times already' (KZ, 2★, Aug 2026) and a total loss on launch ten months earlier — present before the June regression and still present after it was fixed; I4: treat habit history as migration-critical data with an integrity check on upgrade — 'in a streak product, destroyed history destroys the only thing the user has accumulated'. Report 65 (Rabit): plants purchased under Plus re-locked behind a padlock after an update; 14 reviewers attribute a regression to a specific release (BUG_UPDATE, mean 2.71). Report 76 (Way of Life): U_UPDATE_REGRESSION 84 (1.08%, mean 3.08★); BUG_UPDATE_BROKE 54 (2.80★) — 21 from 2012-11/12 (a release that left the app unusable or corrupted data: 'latest release has left this application unusable'), 12 from 2016-05/06 (crash on 'updating journal' at launch; reviews from six countries within two days), a 2017-07 release that wiped histories ('Latest update deleted my entire history', 5★), the 2014-06 v3.0 flat redesign called awful and greedy (NEG_UPDATE_WORSE 17), the 2023 loss of the Today widget; 10.50% of 1★; the two worst months in 16 years (2012-11 at 4.38★, 2015-01 at 4.36★) are both regressions. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): 'now we have reached a point with the new update, where the app can't even open without crashing' (dk 1★, 2025-08-26) — the only reliability regression, and it opened the 70-day window holding all six of the corpus's one-star reviews; defects then fell to zero for 37 consecutive reviews. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): U:defect_any 0.9% (E1) → 0.0% → 19.5% (E3, mean 2.50★); 8 of 9 defects after v2.1.0 (2026-02-11), 'a major internal overhaul' whose own notes warn 'widgets and custom shortcuts need to be re-configured', followed within four days by a 'Deduplicate data' tool 'as some people reported duplicated boards and check-ins'; a crash on board creation fixed by name 11 days later; a self-described daily user: 'I loved how easy it was to use, how reliable it was… Now UI bugs have made it unusable' (1★); the two worst-rated eras follow a rename and an overhaul. Report 83 (Roubit): 'new bugs seem to appear with every update, so I'm thinking of switching apps' (3★); two blank-screen waves coinciding with releases (6.1.24 'Dreaming Idol' theme; 6.4.50 ad-rewards) — timing not proven cause; BUG_UPDATE_LOOP 7 — a forced update that cannot be installed (2022, Feb–Mar 2025, Mar–Apr 2026); widget removed in July 2025 for a paying user; U:defect_any 14.7% (E1) → 73.5% (E4); 'the product broke under paying users' — 14 of 27 payers report a defect. Report 85 (Habitica): U_BUG_ANY 1428 (41.45%, mean 2.81★) over eleven years — BUG_CRASH 415, BUG_REGRESSION 201 blame a specific update; the waves are dated: 2016-11 (72 reviews, 54 crashes on the Rewards page), 2017-10 (86, 45 crash on launch), 2021-08-20 (49 reviews in one day, 47 crashes: 'crashes and auto closes in a matter of seconds'); crash reports fall to 2.1% from 2024 but the newer defects are quieter and more corrosive — Dailies not resetting (BUG_RESET 93), taps on the wrong task, widgets not refreshing; 386 of 488 1★ carry a defect; §8.1 'a staged rollout with crash-rate gating would have contained 2016-11, 2017-10 and 2021-08-20'. Report 86 (Today): five datable crash waves in ten years — launch Mar 2016 (Editors' Choice, 21 crash reviews in three weeks, 'Great crash simulator'), iOS 9/10 Oct–Nov 2016 (18), Face ID / Touch ID Mar 2018 (enabling the paid lock crashed the app), iOS 12 / watchOS 5 Sep 2018 (the Watch app), and the black-screen build 1.9.63 of 2022-11-09 with the next release 1,030 days later; BUG_UPDATE 42 (2.55★); the mean fell 4.16 → 4.14 → 3.59 → 3.51 → 3.07 across five eras — 'reliability, not features, is what destroyed this product'; the pre-2019 vs 2019-onward gap is 0.61★ over 458 reviews, 'not a bad week; it is the product's trajectory'.

<a id="c075"></a>
### C075 — Skippable, replayable onboarding tour and an in-app help screen — searchable FAQ and per-setting explanations for anything richer than the daily check-in

**Certain** · 37 apps · 98 cards · positive in 6 apps · negative in 30 apps · tied to a purchase in 1 apps

*Why Certain:* 37 apps, same direction (act on it, 86%), 17 reports label it high-priority

Hidden gestures (swipe-to-complete, mode toggles) confuse new users; a US-specific 6% complaint in report 2. Report 12: an unskippable narrated intro drew 21 complaints peaking at 16% of 2024 reviews, then fell to one review after a skip control landed — the corpus's clearest fix — while the same intro is praised as a conversion asset. Report 17: a product with its own vocabulary ('what is a sequence? What is a block? What is an activity?') asked for 'a day of experimenting'; users who got through the first day gave 5★, those who didn't quit at 30 minutes — while the paywall demanded payment before that day. Report 18: a five-year vocabulary muddle (습관 vs 루틴 vs 모드) and an onboarding that re-ran on existing and paying accounts with no skip button — a restore-purchase loop returned users to the questionnaire. Report 23: an icon-only first run left new users unable to delete, edit or undo — 63 of 650 1★ reviews; a 66-upvote review asks for plain-language in-app instructions; replace it with a short text-labelled walkthrough covering add / complete / edit / delete / undo / pages. Report 25: confusing/no-guidance 27 (2.06%, mean 2.70); two Brazilian reviewers ask for a tutorial video; comprehension failures worth designing against — how to structure a bad habit ('smoked' or 'didn't smoke'), pinning a weekly habit to a day, stopping a repeat, whether the app is iOS-only. Report 27: a real first-run comprehension cost — four of five confused reviewers got past it and stayed ('a lil hard to figure out at first but now super easy'), the fifth gave 1★; a 30-second skippable explainer is a low-risk fix that does not compromise minimalism. Report 28: 38 onboarding complaints (4.63%, mean 3.24) with one unchanged content for four and a half years — the tutorial teaches the fiction (bunny, mess, carrots) but not how to add, edit or delete a habit ('The tutorial is pointless as they don't show you how to create a task'; 'a steep learning curve with all the unlabeled icons'); 11 more report the add/edit controls genuinely broken and the app cannot tell which it is receiving; the fix is a labelled, skippable tutorial that demonstrates habit CRUD. Report 36: onboarding complaints 16 (mean 1.81, 12 of 16 1–2★), 7.9% of E1 → 1.9% of E5 — 'Is there no manual? Or user guide? I see no way to add new items like a + sign'; 'Is it a game or some kind of something else?' Report 41: onboarding 8 (mean 2.88, lowest non-monetisation) — 'How to use this app🤡 :: Is there a tutorial?'; could not find how to edit a habit; a paying user never started because the skip / miss / stats model was opaque; the report proposes a one-screen 'how this app models habits' card. Report 42: 'Endless screens asking unnecessary questions with no option to skip. I deleted the app after about 15 non-shippable screens, never got to use it'; '~30 questions before I gave up' (both 1★). Report 43: 20 reviews over nine years say there is no tutorial, FAQ or help (see C259). Report 46: onboarding confusion 19 (mean 3.95); the skip-symbol legend is missed at first run and cannot be found again ('I missed the intro and can't find it again'). Report 47: onboarding confusion 9 (mean 2.44) — two could not find back-dating after reading it existed in the update notes, a third the hidden start-date options; today's done / not-done status unclear 5. Report 49: onboarding too long 29 (1.55), rising every era to 4.1% — some abandon during the questionnaire before any price is shown. [Merged from C259: Report 43: no guide / tutorial / FAQ / help (9, mean 2.78) plus a learning curve (14, 3.36) — 20 reviews (3.13%) requested continuously from Feb 2017 ('There must be some tips or suggestions in start') to Aug 2026 ('I don't understand nothing') and never addressed: 'There is no help option in settings which makes at least one action I want to take impossible… I can't find instructions for this in the app, on YouTube, or through a Google search'; 'I have had to contact support twice on things that could have explained up front'; 'it took me an hour or so to figure out how to make it work… I'd pay for this if it had some adjustments in usability'.
