<a id="c038"></a>
### C038 — Dates, streaks and statistics correct on every surface — month boundaries, week starts, DST and timezones

**Certain** · 36 apps · 109 cards · positive in 6 apps · negative in 31 apps

*Why Certain:* 36 apps, same direction (act on it, 98%), 13 reports label it high-priority

Miscounts are ×10.2 over-represented among buyers. Off-by-one dates across app/widget/Watch were report 2's longest-lived bug. Night routines that cross midnight must log to the day they started, honouring a user 'day ends at' setting. Report 23: un-pausing a task marks paused days as missed and resets the streak; a completion 'un-completes' seconds later under sync conflict. Report 25: over-achievement carries into the next day (exceeding a goal pre-completes tomorrow) and logging a bad habit at 200% is rewarded as success (7, 0.53%). Report 29: a month-rollover and weekday-header-offset bug was the dominant defect — 37 reviews (10.11%, mean 2.95 vs 4.73), 78.4% filed on days 28–3 against a 27.6% baseline ('On the last day of every month the app has no idea what day it is… April 30 defaulted to Feb 28'); 62.5% of all 3★; users taught each other to reinstall, which wiped local-only data. Test every date surface at month end, leap day and both week starts. Report 31: time-zone travel rewrote 600- and 1,500-day streaks (13); the week-start setting was ignored and weeks reset on Sunday, including in widgets (30; a 3-year premium user 'begging'); store completions against the local calendar day, not a UTC timestamp. Report 47: calendar weekdays off by one day for reviewers outside the Japan / Korea time zone — 14 (2.38%), 13 from China, Italy, France, Spain and Australia, 2019 → April 2021 ('4 January 2021 is a Monday and it says Tuesday'; 'it lost 29 February'); habit order scrambling (5, 2022), counts displayed wrong (5, 2025–26), late-night check-ins leaving a gap (fixed); a Sunday week start added on request. Report 48: timezone / date bugs 26 (3.35, 2014–22); wrong counts / stats 85 (2.59) across every era; day-boundary 2. Report 49: the day counter advances wrongly — 20 reviews, flat Oct 2024 – Jun 2026, never fixed; the daily recap closes scoring at a fixed ~9pm (10). Report 54: the paid calendar rings show the wrong completion — two reviewers on two continents tie it to the long-press undo not propagating to the calendar (9, 2.56, 5 payers). Report 55: 'not more than' goals saved as 'at least' — inverting success for quit-smoking and drinking goals ('Smoke not more than 10 cigarettes… they actually show as requiring you to do the task at least that many times'); streaks reset at the year change in 2018 and 2020; editing a frequency rewrites history; a traveller's completions shift days; a July 2020 update marked taps on the wrong day. Report 56: 'the calendar is a day out so when you complete a dot on the Monday it highlights the Sunday before' (GB, rated 5★) — F2: verify week-start and timezone handling (Europe/London vs UTC feed); the UI switched to Chinese unprompted. Report 57: 'Display on' per-weekday filter shipped and silently ignores selections for 8 users over five years ('I set Tue/Thu/Sat and it shows every day'). Report 65 (Rabit): completed habits reported as missed — 'Tengo un hábito cumplido todos los días y mi planta sale muerta y con 0 días de racha' (BUG_STREAK 7, mean 2.43); week start offered only as Friday or Saturday, never Monday (3); a calendar mapping dates to the wrong weekday; F7, F9. Report 69 (TheFor): 'Even though I completed around 75% of my test, only 20%. Why?' (3★, 2026 — the only open bug that year); F4: verify the completion percentage before deepening analytics — 'Deepening a view that computes the wrong number is the wrong order'. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): no date is shown on the ring — 'because no dates are shown, from about day 3 I lost track of whether I'd recorded or not, got confused and uninstalled'; 'unrecorded' flags on unscheduled weekdays; §8.1: show the date being recorded on the ring. Report 75 (Habit Streak): 'Have a 6 day streak and it says day 4. Best streak says 5, current streak says 4… it just frustrates you instead of encourages you' (2★) — three mutually inconsistent numbers on the one metric the product exists to show, the highest-severity open defect; with the no-backfill 0% case: 'the app's record of what the user did disagrees with the user's own record, and the app wins'. Report 84 (HabitGrid): DEF_DATE_LOGIC 2, the only defect reported twice — a tick on Saturday or Sunday 'fills in/unfills both days'; a widget increment lands on the following day; both week/day-boundary errors; 1.0.19 'Custom week start' touches week boundaries and whether it fixes either is not established; §8.2 test completion writes across the week boundary, across time zones, and from widgets. Report 85 (Habitica): BUG_RESET 93 (2.70%) — 'the app will tell me it started a new day, but it hasn't cleared out my dailies' (3★); NEG_DAYSTART 16; in the latest era day-rollover failures rank fourth among defects; §8.1 make 'start new day' (cron) idempotent and visible and never let a failed rollover block ticking tasks. Report 86 (Today): a time-zone check-in bug first reported Feb 2019 was fixed Oct 2025 — six and a half years later; a day-start-time setting was in a 2016 twenty-item request list. Report 89 (Check Calendar): DEF_COUNT_WRONG 2 ('some checked days aren't counted in the total'; monthly cumulative and this-month totals 'often don't match'), DEF_DATE_STALE 1 ('date doesn't become today unless the app is closed'), DEF_CHECK_LOST 1 ('checks sometimes vanish on reopening') — all Japanese, 2024–2026; U:record_integrity 20 (7.91%, 2.60★) once locked and lost records are included. Report 90 (Quit Bad Habits & Addiction): BUG_COUNTER_ATTEMPTS 5 — the count follows the device clock ('changing the phone's date changes the count'), an attempt was not recorded, a deleted relapse still counts, and a wrong day count appeared after the update; DATA_LOSS 3 includes a 1000-day count reset after a week away and a habit that 'deleted itself' — in a sobriety counter the number is the product, so a wrong number is a total failure.

<a id="c109"></a>
### C109 — A free trial must be a real trial

**Certain** · 36 apps · 119 cards · positive in 2 apps · negative in 34 apps · tied to a purchase in 2 apps

*Why Certain:* 36 apps, same direction (act on it, 79%), 19 reports label it high-priority

It must apply to whichever plan the user picks, and the confirmation must show the exact charge date and amount; a trial that bills at once produced 789 reviews at mean 1.35 in report 4 and must be verified per storefront (Brazil ran 7–11× the global rate). Report 10: 149 users believe they were charged at trial START (mean 1.79) and trial length varied between 2 and 7 days across users. Report 12: a 3-day trial introduced around 2024 shows as subscribed but 'doesn't move past the subscription screen' — the complaint changed shape from 'there is no trial' to 'the trial doesn't work'. Report 13: a trial that cannot start without first authorising a subscription, defaulting to the most expensive annual tier, produced 1,102 auto-charge reviews at mean 1.20 (999 one-star) — the single most damaging mechanic in a 19,850-review corpus; involuntary-charge reviews equalled voluntary-purchase reviews 1:1. Report 18: trials that converted immediately ('in my case there was no free period'; asked for monthly, charged annual; frozen since minute 10, charged a full year) in KR, JP, TW, ID, BR and DE; trial length shrank from 3 weeks to 7 days to 2–3-day variants. Report 19: a 'free trial' that charged (10 of 105) — '$45 for the initial trial', 'free 7 days charged trial' — with the price hidden at decision time and no renewal warning; four non-payers refused precisely because there was no way to try first. Report 24: the 'free trial' charges a 'pay what you can' set-up fee ($1 / $10 / $16.41) on a donation-style screen, classed in the terms as non-refundable — 506 reviews (1.16%, mean 1.136) say the trial was not free and 100 name the fee mechanism (mean 1.110). Report 25: the trial is a net-negative topic (21, mean 2.62, 10 1★) — card required up front, charged inside the window ('it says cost 0 in the trial selector and they charged me 1,500 pesos'), renewal into the wrong plan, and uncertainty about whether cancelling is possible; billing disputes stepped up ~5× after 2024 (0.8% → 3.9%). Report 26: a '3-day free trial' that charges immediately (incl. a lifetime tier charged instantly with no trial disclosed), cancelled before trial end and charged anyway, renewal with no notice — 23 disputes at mean 1.48, the lowest-rated theme in the corpus, and the source of the only accusations of deception ('Scam company. Impossible to cancel and tricks you into renewing'; 'Estafadores'). Report 30: no trial at all, so an annual charge is the first real use. Report 31: a 'free trial' that was actually a paid first year ('told I would be getting one year, 365 days free … now only … a month'), a trial renewing into the most expensive plan, and a trial not visible in iOS subscriptions. Report 33: 2025–26 trials converted to an annual charge unexpectedly ('I signed up for a free trial and somehow got converted to paid'; 'a 7- or 14-day trial, then charged a full year of Pro'). Report 46: two charged on day one of a 7-day trial ('Offerred 7 day trial, but I got charged the same day'); after a trial ends the extra habits are locked, not archivable ('I can't delete them… it falsifies the statistics') — the report's #8: let the user choose which 3 stay and archive the rest. Report 47: no refund requests, but one user cancelled after discovering a half-year plan they did not remember agreeing to ('契約した覚えがないので、もしかしたら無料期間を忘れたのかもしれない。気をつけた方がいいです', 1★, Jan 2026); the fix: a clear notice before a trial converts. Report 48: trial terms 26 (1.65) — charged the full year at the start of a 7-day trial; charged twice after cancelling before the trial ended; refund requests concentrate in 2019+ trial and auto-renew disputes. Report 49: 'I signed up for the 1 week free trial and was immediately charged AU$17.98'; 'immediately charged for one year. It does not show up in your Apple subscriptions and there is no way to cancel your trial!'; cancelled a day early and still charged $50; 'a loop so you can not use the app if you don't accept the free trial'; a 7-day trial only on the annual plan billed €14.99 immediately. Report 50: 'I was charged $30 before my free trial was up'; 'They absolutely DONT SEND THE REMINDER when the trial is about to finish… they charge you automatically the whole year'. Report 53: 7-day trials that several reviewers say billed a full year; M4: charge date and amount on the trial screen and a reminder 24 hours before conversion. Report 55: charged after a trial; a trial that can't be cancelled (PAY_TRIAL 8, 2.12). Report 59 (Tappsk): the 7-day trial that charged immediately or on day six is the largest single source of 1★ reviews across eight years — MON_AUTO_CHARGE 229 (1.51%, mean 1.82★) carries 163 of the 674 1★ (24.2%), co-occurs with MON_TRIAL 111 and MON_REFUND 113; a year's fee (999 ₽ named 73 times) taken at once ('при выборе бесплатной недели сразу списали деньги за год'; '«7 дней бесплатно», а сами втихую списываете на 6 день' — you quietly charge on day 6), charges after deletion ('Списывают деньги, даже если приложение удалено'), peaked 2.9% of 2020 and still 1.2% of 2024–26; the fix list: no charge before day 7, a visible countdown, one-tap cancel inside the app, a confirmation e-mail with the renewal date; a card-required trial is itself a barrier ('полная версия в пробном периоде требует привязки карты'). Report 60 (Mindway): three distinct trial failures from three users — a $0.99 paid trial converting to $39.99 within hours ('with NO EXCEPTIONS OF A REFUND'), a '3 day free trial' that billed a week after cancelling on day two (a 4★ that would otherwise be 5★), and no trial offered at all before purchase ('I'm just out the money now') — 'a flow problem, not three user errors'; F2: audit the trial-to-charge flow end to end. Report 64 (Critique AI): a 3-day trial that requires card details up front, charges the full year on expiry without warning ('it didn't let me know that it was over so it took my money'), cannot be cancelled in-app, and is not reached at all by others — PAY_TRIAL 26 (6.21%, mean 1.58), persistent across 17 months; 3 days cannot test a habit product ('Getting into stuff like this will take at least a month to stick'); M4: 14 days, no card. Report 65 (Rabit): a 7-day trial reported charging the monthly price at once ('isso é propaganda enganosa'), never starting (the subscribe button spins), charging R$199.90 after the app was deleted, and ending free use on day two (PAY_TRIAL_BAD 5); M3: 'the highest-trust-cost surface in the product'. Report 67 (Habio): a $1 / €1 / £1 3-day paid trial (MON_TRIAL_1DOLLAR 148) converting to $40+ plans — MON_TRIAL_CHARGE 173 (8.43%, mean 1.03): 'Factually their 3 days trial for 1,00 Euro is actually a 2 two days trial'; MON_PRICE_MISMATCH 55 charged more than shown; 'they've also never mentioned in their add that the currency is not in AUD'. Report 68 (Ultiself): paid intro trials on the web that auto-convert (MON_RENEWAL_SHOCK 227, 5.03% — an intro plan becoming $39.95–$87 recurring; MON_TRIAL_CHARGED 19); §8.6: replace paid intro plans with a free trial that ends without charge unless confirmed, measuring chargebacks and 90-day retention. Report 82 (Lasting Change): BILL_FREE_CLAIMED 7 (4.00%, 1.57★) — an app presented as free or as a trial that then bills: 'offers what appears to be a free month of membership, but they hide the fact that they will begin charging you monthly many months afterward'; 'I really thought I was going to get a 7 day trial. But, instead it wanted me to pay'; whether a trial exists or its length could not be established from any source. Report 83 (Roubit): BILL_UNEXPECTED_CHARGE 2 — 'I started a 7-day free trial and was charged ₩4,400'; 'suddenly ₩55,000 for a year was charged' (5★, refund requested); TRIAL_USER 4; a trial-ad problem fixed via Restore Subscription. Report 88 (GetHabit): a paid or card-gated trial — $0.49 / £0.49 / 0,49€ for the first week, three days free with card details, a '$1 verification of funds' / €0.01 / $0.99 on the web (PAY_PAID_TRIAL 29: 'Was met with a $0.49 charge to even enter the app'); ad-promised trial lengths (a week, 28 days, a month) then a charge within days — BILL_TRIAL_SHORTER 8, BILL_TRIAL_CONVERSION 35 ('they offer you a 3 day subscription but charge you $31 immediately'; 'the trial that said ONE MONTH… automatically charged 20€'); PRIV_PAYMENT_DETAILS 8 object to card details for a 'free' trial ('Don't use their trial with your card details. This is a trap!'). Report 90 (Quit Bad Habits & Addiction): TRIAL_USER 1 — 'even though I deleted it and cancelled, they still try to charge me for the free subscription' (ru, 2025-12, 1★); the listing shows no trial, so what the reviewer saw could not be confirmed. (Final consolidation: distinguish [[C063]] — that point weighs whether to offer a trial; this one governs a trial that already exists. Report 12 is the case that shows they are sequential, not alternative: the complaint there changed shape from 'there is no trial' to 'the trial doesn't work'.)

<a id="c040"></a>
### C040 — Widgets must not go blank, stale or disagree with the app

**Certain** · 35 apps · 103 cards · positive in 4 apps · negative in 29 apps · tied to a purchase in 2 apps

*Why Certain:* 35 apps, same direction (act on it, 88%), 14 reports label it high-priority

Broken widget is ×7.8 on 2★. Report 10: the widget rendered as a grey box for five years (117 reviews) — reported mostly by fans, so it never generated pressure. Report 18: the widget went from the top request (31 reviews at 4.77★ before launch) to the top defect surface (214 mentions, 10.45%) — blank, missing from the picker, wrong weekday, false 'all done', check-off opening the app, routine widget rendering to-dos. Report 20: the widget was the top defect surface for five years and the 2★ band's peak theme (13.0%). Report 23: widgets rendering blank or losing configuration (57 explicit widget-bug reviews, mean 3.16; 20 blank/config reports) alongside the interactive-widget regression. Report 25: widget stopped working / not interactive / font fixed (6, 0.46%). Report 27: the widget is the most consistently under-delivering surface and the only one to produce a 1★ on its own ('Widget does and shows absolutely nothing… Just says 0% ALL the time'); 9 gap/defect reviews (6.52%, high-priority) across every one of five years vs 5 praising it. Report 28: no widget at all — 14 requests (1.71%), mean 4.64, zero negative ratings, continuous April 2022 → September 2026, 'i want to be able to click on the widget and shortcut to check a habit as done'; the clearest uncontested gap in the corpus. Report 29: no widget at all — 16 requests (4.37%), the only absent feature with demonstrated substitution (a user on 'Check Me' because it has one) and the one explicit payment offer ('add widget support happy to pay for a lifetime'); three withhold a star for it. Report 30: the Home Screen widget is paywalled and a documented switch followed — 'I downloaded it only for the widget. Turned out it's a paid feature… competitors include it free — I went there'; the widget shown in the store screenshots is not the widget the app provides; the one user who has it is the happiest reviewer. Report 31: widget mentions 195 (3.76%) — positive in E1, demand in E2, complaint after the Oct 2021 downgrade; the widget ignored the week-start setting. Report 34: widget rendering broke with the iOS 18 tinted home screen (white), two of six widgets didn't show days, 'keeps getting disabled' — 5 reviews, 3.0% of E4, one payer 'waste money'. Report 46: widgets blank, stale or wrong — 21 (mean 3.33): 'I deleted the Dry January task but the widget still shows it'; 'every day the home-screen widget colour blocks get scrambled'; 'The widget is the heart of the application' (1★ after contact); interactive widgets also record accidental taps ('marks the completion of that day by mistake… Not great for a paid app') — the report: keep it, add a lock / view-only mode. Report 47: the 2025 widget gets stuck at 0 or goes blank (5, all 2025–26: 'ある日突然ウィジェットがずっと0表示になってしまいました'); the report's fix #2 pairs it with wrong month-view counts. Report 49: the same blank / stuck-on-day-1 widget reported in Mar 2025, May 2025, Nov 2025, Dec 2025 and the final week of the corpus (8). Report 50: widget lag (1, 5★). Report 52: widget defects 454 (2.20%), 62.8% in 2020–21; a widget renders blank on iOS 26 Clear / Tinted home screens. Report 53: widgets blank on tinted home screens and no longer interactive on iOS 18/26 (WIDGET_BUG 5.1% of 2025, 7.5% of 2026). Report 56: a widget tap that opens the app instead of progressing the habit (BE, 4★). Report 57: the widget is both the most-loved feature and the largest defect surface — 129 (16.56%) raise a problem: 50 won't appear or go blank (rising 3.89% → 6.67% → 10.80% by era), 25 don't reflect check-ins, 9 show a live group as 'deleted' (Apr 2024 – Dec 2025), 6 clip items; 58 of 90 defect reviews are 4–5★; 'every single update breaks the widget'; 'I have to reinstall five or six times a month'; 23 of 99 payers affected; a Premium payer considering switching over three widget layouts. Report 58: widget habit icons render as white boxes in iOS clear / tinted icon mode — the only functional defect in 91 reviews, with a stated repro. Report 59 (Tappsk): BUG_WIDGET 100 (0.66%) — widgets blank or stale after updates and not changing at day change ('при переключении дня задачи на виджете не меняются'; 'каждый раз обещают направить разработчикам, но проблема остается' — each time they promise to pass it on, the problem remains); fix: widgets that refresh at day change without opening the app; the 2.6.2 release notes list 'faster widgets'. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): the widget is the paid hook, so its gaps are voiced by the highest-LTV buyer — no dark theme, 'so basic' — from a lifetime purchaser. Report 69 (TheFor): widget won't launch the app unless it is already backgrounded, and doesn't show already-completed tasks (BUG_WIDGET 2) — refresh / state bugs on an asset praised at 5.00. Report 83 (Roubit): BUG_WIDGET 15 (3.00%; KR 4.9%) — routine order reversed in the widget (developer promised a fix for October 2024); in July 2025 'with this update the iPhone widget seems to be unsupported' for a paying user; REQ_WIDGET 9. Report 84 (HabitGrid): 'incrementing a counter through the widget doesn't increase the count, or increases the count for the following day (possibly a time zone mismatch?)' (4★) — the most detailed bug report in the corpus, from a reviewer who calls widgets 'a huge plus'; 'can't add several widgets with different habits — it only gives one… please tell me how' (5★); widget praise stops in the final era (8 → 0). Report 85 (Habitica): widgets arrived and became a defect source — BUG_WIDGET 22 (all from 2021), 15 of them in the latest era where widget failures rank sixth among defects; REQ_WIDGET 68 (1.97%). Report 86 (Today): BUG_WIDGET 35 (1.96%) — 'the widget has a bug on iOS 10; purple blocks keep appearing' (5★); the 3D Touch widget reveals the habit list past the paid lock.

<a id="c112"></a>
### C112 — In-app cancellation

**Certain** · 33 apps · 101 cards · positive in 1 apps · negative in 31 apps

*Why Certain:* 33 apps, same direction (act on it, 97%), 16 reports label it high-priority

Cancel-by-email with no reply converts recoverable disputes into permanent 1★, legal threats and denied refunds. Report 13: in Korea 24.7% of reviews say they cannot cancel and two reviewers published how-to-cancel guides for other users; an in-app 'Manage subscription' link would address a quarter of that storefront's reviews. Report 19: cancellation required email rather than a button, used bold 'stay' and small 'cancel' buttons, ~10 confirmation steps, was split across two subscriptions, and locked the user out of the account mid-flow; 24 of 105 (22.86%) described it and three asked simply for a cancel button inside the app. Report 20: refund requests ignored in Feb 2021 (Apple refunded where the developer would not), 'cannot cancel' reports 2022–2025 with one alleging an FTC-transparency breach, and accidental Touch-ID purchases during onboarding; 125 reviews at mean 1.28. Report 24: cannot find or complete cancellation 1,146 (2.64%, mean 1.115, 0.3% 5★) because the subscription lives on the developer's website; move billing into IAP or surface the web subscription in-app with one-tap cancel. Report 25: two reviewers could not find subscription settings in the app at all — 'I looked for five minutes… Is that even legal?' Report 26: two reviewers could not find any way to unsubscribe; 'well hidden there is a way to contact support… but the button is not enabled'. Report 30: an accidental subscription with no route to a refund (MX, 1★) — the reviewer blames the app even where the flow is Apple's. Report 31: 66 cannot cancel / charged after cancelling (mean 1.39, mostly E4) — no subscription found in iOS Settings; 'cancelled … TWICE and I'm still being charged'; put 'Manage subscription' in the app. Report 33: web-billed (Paddle) subscriptions had no in-app cancel ('payments … through a third party and there's no unsubscribe button'), 13 cannot-cancel reviews at mean 1.62; a deleted account was still charged; cancelling a renewal after a trial ended current access — show renewal date, price and a cancel link for every billing channel, and keep access through the paid period. Report 36: 'Dark pattern: roach motel … Clicking on link In email returns Cannot cancel subscription' (1★). Report 41: 'I would like to unsubscribe and delete the app but there are no means to do that via the app'. Report 42: two cancelled; one could not find how to refund; 'Don't fall for the free-trial trap.. you won't get a refund even if you cancel two minutes after'. Report 43 (counter-case): a one-time purchase produced zero cancellation complaints; the only refund refusal was inside the EU 14-day withdrawal window. Report 46: six cancellations threatened or described, one on the last day of the trial after a developer reply; 'I just cancelled the subscription. That's $29 down the drain'. Report 48: cancellation difficulty 4 (1.25), retained as compliance-adjacent. Report 55: M4 — disclose cap, trial length, annual price and how to cancel inside the app. Report 59 (Tappsk): MON_CANCEL_TROUBLE 73 (1.0% of the latest era, its peak) — the subscription is hard to find and cancel, and the direct-card route for Russian users has no cancellation at all because App Store subscription management no longer shows the app ('В Айфоне в подписках вас у меня нет' — you are not in my iPhone subscriptions, 1★); a cancellation that works without the App Store and stops retries after deletion is an immediate fix. Report 60 (Mindway): M_CANCEL_DIFFICULTY 4 (mean 1.00) plus one who cancelled and was charged anyway — 'There is no way to cancel'; 'Please help me unsubscribe'; 'I am getting no help and stopping the subscription'; an AU reviewer still asking how to cancel 14 months after the first report; F1: make cancellation one tap from the main screen and confirm it in writing — 'the cheapest star recovery available' and 'the highest-severity item in the report'. Report 65 (Rabit): 'Comprei por engano e não consigo cancelar, não tem suporte, não tem orientação como faço?' (PAY_CANCEL 3); M4. Report 67 (Habio): MON_CANCEL 361 (17.60%, mean 1.01) and MON_CHARGED_AFTER 351 (17.11%) — an in-app cancellation confirmation screen with no persistent cancelled status, an emailed cancellation link that expires in 20 minutes, 'email not found' when cancelling, deleting the app believed to cancel (CHURN_DELETE 66); §8.1: every subscription visible in app settings with status, next charge date and amount, one-tap cancel with an on-screen and emailed confirmation, an emailed request effective at receipt. Report 68 (Ultiself): MON_CANCEL_HARD 592 (13.12%, mean 1.10) — 'you can't unsubscribe by your own, you have to email them' (kz); cancellation emails sent on time and ignored; 'Cela fait 2 mois que je demande l'annulation de mon abonnement'; a Manage-subscription button that leads nowhere for web buyers. Report 69 (TheFor): a subscriber used a public 1★ to ask to be unsubscribed and for written confirmation — an Apple-side action the developer cannot perform, but the missing Manage-subscription row is a surface the developer can add. Report 82 (Lasting Change): zero reviews in 1080 days describe a working in-app or web cancel control; CANCEL_NO_PATH 27 (15.43%: 'not… via your App Store account, their website or from within the app itself'), CANCEL_EMAIL_ONLY 12, CANCEL_DARK_PATTERN 2 ('You will forget.'); charged again after cancelling 12, after deleting the account 5 ('They confirmed cancellation and a month later they were charging me again'); cancellation honoured 3 of 175; §8.2 a self-service Cancel control in the account screen and on the web with on-screen and email confirmation — 'the only change that deals with all of the top five 1★ drivers'. Report 85 (Habitica): MON_CANCEL_HARD 4 — 'Habitica keeps charging for new subscriptions' (1★); §8.4 a visible cancel path and clear App Store subscription management. Report 88 (GetHabit): BILL_CANT_CANCEL 34 (6.94%; 25.0% of the web-checkout era, 44.4% of the tail), BILL_CHARGED_AFTER_CANCEL 21 ('I sent three emails asking to cancel that night and one the following day'; 'they've been charging me for months', 2022; 'the payment still running in my credit card', 2024); the 2022 terms describe cancellation through Apple or Google only while 2021 web buyers say that route did not exist for them.

<a id="c035"></a>
### C035 — Account system from day one

**Certain** · 29 apps · 68 cards · positive in 3 apps · negative in 21 apps

*Why Certain:* 29 apps, same direction (act on it, 85%), 8 reports label it high-priority

Root cause of lost purchases, lost data and failed sync; requests rise as users change phones. Report 20: 'no account, no signup' was praised — and was the root cause of the 2025 data loss; the account/backup layer must exist even if signup stays optional. Report 26: no account system anywhere in the corpus — a device change, a reinstall, or support's own advice to reinstall destroys both progress and entitlement ('It also deletes the purchase price of the app if you bought it as there is no account to sign into'); absent accounts every other entitlement bug is unrecoverable — the root cause behind the top paid-user complaint. Report 27 (counter-evidence on the signup side, not the durability side): no account is praised — but iCloud sync exists and is invisible, so three reviewers fear data loss and one churned after an update lost progress; the account layer's job here is legible backup, not signup. Report 28: an account with e-mail verification exists (29 mentions, mean 3.66, mixed); a verification reset by support turned a 1★ into a 5★. Report 29 (counter-evidence): no account, no email, no login is named as the reason to choose the app; the report's rule is backup yes, account no — local-first. Report 33: guest mode is a data trap — 26 users who never created an account lost everything on update, reinstall or Mac sign-in ('Never use guest mode'; a ¥6,000 lifetime bought as a guest) — while forced login since 2016 is itself a privacy complaint. Report 36: no account at all; Chinese-market users ask for login specifically ('希望可以登陆', 17 helpful votes, third most-voted). Report 41 (counter-evidence): no account is praised (privacy / no account 10, all 5★: 'Pas de compte à créer, pas de données collectées'), and the report lists 'do not require an account' among what not to change. Report 43 (counter-evidence): no account required is listed among reasons to buy ('No subscription · Very reasonable one-time purchase price · Great data privacy (no data collected) · No ads'). Report 46: an account was required 2018–2022 (8 complaints, mean 1.50; the first review in the corpus could not sign up; login failures mean 1.89) and optional by 2024 — the complaint stopped when the requirement did. Report 48 (counter-evidence on mandatory accounts): forcing an account and online sync on a local tracker in Jan 2015 drew 39 reviews at mean 1.64 — 'a privacy objection, distinct from price' — strongest in Germany (5.04%, the largest over-index of any theme in any storefront; one review invokes German consumer law); iCloud sync later replaced the account; login / account failures 21 (1.86). Report 50 (counter-evidence): a mandatory account limited to Sign in with Apple or Google before first use lost two GB users at the gate — 'Why would I want to expose every aspect of my life to data mining in this way? Stay clear.' and 'unable to login with apple' — 'a conversion risk and a single point of failure'; S6: consider a local-first trial mode. Report 52: WeChat login cannot be bound on the Mac build for five years (12 reviews, among the most-upvoted) and QQ vs WeChat logins split Android and iOS memberships. Report 55: an optional account (e-mail, Facebook; later Apple, Google) whose January 2018 registration spinner, 'email invalid' and reset e-mails that never arrive (ACCT_BUG 57, 1.68; US 34 of 57) broke premium; F6: registration optional and robust, never block first use. Report 58: no account and no e-mail sign-up named as adoption reasons by 2 ('It makes it quick and easy to start using'). Report 76 (Way of Life): a counter-example — no account, no sync, local-only for 16 years at 4.62★; the cost shows as data loss on phone change (U_DATA_RISK 123, 1.58%) and REQ_SYNC 139 in every era, not as a sign-up complaint; PR_PRIVACY 12 praise the absence. Report 82 (Lasting Change): the account system is the product's one reliability defect class — DEF_LOGIN 14 (8.00%), no crash reports at all; a paid web account must be linked to the app login by the purchase email with creation and recovery paths on the sign-in screen. Report 84 (HabitGrid): the no-account counter-case — 'No sign-in. No servers. No cloud.' is a headed section of the listing, praised for privacy, and the cost is one 4★ who believes data dies with the phone and one request for an optional account; the website mentions opt-in authentication and cloud backups that appear nowhere else. Report 88 (GetHabit): the absence of an account meant a web purchase could not unlock the app (8 of 19 web buyers) and a reinstall required paying again — §8.3 'link it to an account that unlocks the app'. Report 89 (Check Calendar): the no-account design is the reason every buyer failure is a device change — purchase not recognised, records empty, 'how to use that account on my ipad?' — and the reason 'Unable to backup on new phone since it is not allowing me to login' is written as a 5★ review with no other channel.

<a id="c113"></a>
### C113 — One stable, disclosed price — no discount wheels

**Certain** · 28 apps · 80 cards · positive in 3 apps · negative in 25 apps · tied to a purchase in 3 apps

*Why Certain:* 28 apps, same direction (act on it, 87%), 13 reports label it high-priority

Users in the same market reported $19.99–$59.99 for the same thing; that inconsistency is what 'scam' language attaches to; a rigged or broken gimmick makes it worse. Report 10: household members quoted $34.99 vs $41.99 on the same day, support could not explain a $19.99–$99.99 range — perceived as discriminatory pricing inside families. Report 18: four to five concurrently live annual prices per storefront produced 'I paid, then it showed me a cheaper price' — charged ₩33,000 and ₩25,000 both, '40% off' banners not honoured, ¥2,900 checkout billed ¥4,150 — and fraud accusations in six languages; Taiwan (2.60★) was almost entirely this; a Dutch user watched the displayed price move 'from over 200 to 68 to 19.90'. Report 20: the app advertised $5.99 / 499₽ / 85%-off and charged $39.99 / 3,150₽ — 28 reports across eight storefronts, Dec 2021 → Apr 2025; below threshold on volume, a consumer-protection exposure by nature. Report 23: a weak cluster (7, 0.10%) says the price shown and the amount debited differed (au, ru, tr, mx) — most likely tax or currency conversion, but a recurring, avoidable trust event. Report 24: annual, quarterly, 'bimonthly', monthly and weekly cycles at overlapping prices ('this page says $59 for a year… it's $40 billed every three months'), different prices on different screens, and a cancel flow that discounts $19.99 → $12.99 → $5 → $2/month; the inconsistency of what users believe they bought is the direct cause of 'charged twice' reports. Report 25: $24.99 shown and $42 charged; €29.99 lifetime followed by two further €6.99 charges; a German purchase sheet showing no price at all; Mexican reviewers unable to tell whether the price is pesos or dollars (four say so in the review) — show the local currency unambiguously and confirm displayed equals charged. Report 30: two yearly SKUs at different prices ($44.99 and $29.99) beside a $59.99 Lifetime produced 'they tell you the plan is for life and it's only for a year'; the monthly option could not be bought ('it charges for a year'). Report 31: reviewers quote 60+ price points across 15 currencies; a 'Christmas' $11.99 → $39.99, perpetual 72-hour countdowns that reset, 83–90% off banners and $399 anchors — and 69 say the advertised price was not the charged price. Report 33: charged more than shown in ~6 cases (¥4,900 → ¥5,150; $39.99 → $48.97; monthly chosen, annual charged). Report 49: a countdown discount that does not apply (an 80% notification resolving to 70%) and 'limited time offers' that tipped purchases (misleading checkout 17). Report 52: price seen as unstable — ¥18 / ¥28 / ¥88 reported in the same months, a ¥12 buyer finding lifetime at ¥98. Report 53: a perpetual 'limited-time' discount offer (2023–26) reads as deception rather than a deal. Report 59 (Tappsk): the discount that sells the lifetime unlock also generates disclosure complaints — 'Kurz nach dem Kauf wurde der Preis durch einen Zufallsgenerator reduziert' (shortly after the purchase the price was reduced by a random generator); the same lifetime named at 449 ₽ and 2,500 ₽ within a year; offers that vanish ('Предложение куда-то исчезло и желание купить пропало') and a buy button that is inactive; the report's fix: one price per region and no re-pricing within days of a purchase — a predictable seasonal sale rather than random rotation reconciles the two findings ([[C003]]). Report 64 (Critique AI): the same year quoted as $40, £40, £24, 40–45€, $39.99, $45, $50, $60, $100, $192, $200 and ₦69,900, plus weekly and monthly SKUs and an exit discount (£2.08/mo advertised, £24/yr charged) — PAY_SCAM 21 (5.01%, mean 1.05). Report 67 (Habio): 13 price points from $0.49 to $79.99 in the US listing, charges above the price shown (55), and currency not disclosed ('never mentioned in their add that the currency is not in AUD'). Report 68 (Ultiself): MON_BAIT 55 (1.22%, mean 1.05) — 'Ofrecen 4 semanas a 0.35 usd la semana y resulta que cobran 9.92usd por 7 días'; 'Cada que entro a la app me da un costo diferente' (MON_PRICE_SHIFT 6); 'it takes forever to figure out how much it costs a month'. Report 72 (Habit Hearts): two different 'Lifetime' SKUs ($9.99 and $15.99) and two prices quoted to one Russian reviewer in one session; reviewers report €10, €9.99, €25, £10, $10–16, R$124.75, 129 kr and 899 ₽ — one checks the 'no further cost' claim with scepticism ('så är jag skeptisk'). Report 76 (Way of Life): 'last week the price was $29, this week is $99' (4★) in the subscription era; §8.1 one stable price per region stating whether it is monthly, annual or lifetime; 'only offer a reduced price in the first days after installation' (br 5★) penalises evaluators. Report 86 (Today): a $299.99 lifetime SKU beside a $9.99 annual — 30× — reads as 'either a mistake or contempt' next to a history of paying customers losing their purchase; regional launch pricing (CA$7 vs US$4.99) drew its own cap complaint in Canada ('$7 in the app world is premium', 2★).

<a id="c171"></a>
### C171 — Accessibility stack: VoiceOver, motion, sound and light sensitivity, text size

**Certain** · 26 apps · 45 cards · positive in 5 apps · negative in 19 apps

*Why Certain:* 26 apps, same direction (act on it, 74%), 4 reports label it high-priority

Report 10: 597 accessibility reviews (0.85%, mean 4.56) from blind, mobility-limited, chronically ill, motion-, sound- and light-sensitive users; dark mode is argued as an accessibility need, not a preference ('Cute clothes for the bird were apparently shippable'). Report 23: accessibility / VoiceOver 19 (0.26%, mean 3.79). Report 24: accessibility (vision, font, VoiceOver) 129 (0.30%, mean 3.101). Report 26: a detailed, actionable VoiceOver defect report — images without alt text, focus loss, elements announced only as 'botão' — plus larger text and low-contrast reports; dynamic type was added and praised; promoted on inclusion/legal grounds at 5 reviews. Report 31: no VoiceOver support, small fonts/buttons (19) — ship VoiceOver labels, Dynamic Type and 44 pt targets. Report 33: memo input breaks under Japanese IME. Report 36: respect the silence switch and add a global audio toggle (2, one an uninstall). Report 41: the Mac app has no text zoom — 'text and icons are too small on my 27-inch display' (the only accessibility report). Report 42: premium pop-ups 'difficult to click out of' alongside a text-size accessibility complaint. Report 43: 'this app works with voiceover since I am a voiceover user' (the only screen-reader confirmation); 'The text is small, I can not see to read it!' Report 46: accessibility requests 8 (font size, VoiceOver, reading needs — 'unique reading needs' from a dyslexic 5★); a VoiceOver regression on iOS 15 (IT). Report 47: time-picker digits unreadable in dark mode (2); the skip key hidden by the keyboard (Jul 2025); the settings button hidden by long tab names (a payer). Report 48: accessibility 6 (3.50). Report 53: VoiceOver compatibility shipped on request (2022) for blind users. Report 54: a detailed VoiceOver report (many fields and buttons unreadable, DE, 1★, offering to re-review once fixed) and Dynamic Type text cut off — 'below the 1% bar, but flagged under the standing exception for accessibility, and cheap to fix'. Report 57: dark mode paywalled against photosensitivity. Report 60 (Mindway): time entry on a 24-hour clock only, no AM/PM option — 'This confuses me a lot'; F6: add AM/PM time entry, 'one review, one line of work, and it is the only reported input-level usability defect in the corpus' — respect the user's locale time format. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): an app that cannot be operated by tapping is an accessibility failure in effect — the June build; zero explicit accessibility requests otherwise. Report 76 (Way of Life): the listing ships a colour-blind mode; REQ_COLORBLIND 1; REQ_FONT 2; REQ_LANDSCAPE 9 (3.44★). Report 86 (Today): accessibility evidence is absent — 2 incidental mentions in 1,785 — 'an evidence gap, not an all-clear'; a full-screen-photo app with text over imagery has obvious contrast risk and 'unreadable text on light wallpapers' was reported in 2016. Research: Quit Habit Decision.md — the #1 app's quit habits at a 0/day target are unreadable in dark mode, a contrast failure that appears only in that state and would be missed by a check of the default states.

<a id="c110"></a>
### C110 — An obvious 'continue free' path on the paywall — the free/paid boundary must be legible

**Certain** · 25 apps · 57 cards · positive in 4 apps · negative in 19 apps · tied to a purchase in 1 apps

*Why Certain:* 25 apps, same direction (act on it, 84%), 12 reports label it high-priority

Users wrote 75 reviews teaching each other where the hidden X was while 1,903 said the app was paid-only; legibility of what is free is a rating decision. Report 24: a real free tier (~3–4 habits, coaching locked) exists behind a small 'X' or 'skip' on the trial splash and is hard to find; 77 reviews (mean 4.442) call it generous once found. Report 34: the wall arrives at habit #3 during setup — 'I added 2, tried to add the third and was prompted to pay'. Report 48: 48 reviews (mean 1.65, rising 0.49% → 2.05% of E5) invested setup effort before meeting an undisclosed 3-tracker wall — 'I lost my time encoding 3 trackers for nothing'; 'Wish i knew before i downloaded and set everything up' — the report's fix #1: disclose the limit on the listing and at first run, 'the cheapest 1★ in the corpus to eliminate… about the surprise, not the price'. Report 49: no 'continue free' path exists at all — 256 say the only free thing is the questionnaire and its result. Report 50: a pop-up 'insisting I pay for premium every time I open the app… it stops me from just being able to use the app' (GB, 1★) — the only report of the paywall obstructing ongoing free use; 'it takes 15 Seconds to ask you for 5,99 every month' (DE). Report 52: 2026 onboarding requires picking 5 habits and choosing a 3-day trial; reviewers ask to skip both and for a visible back control on every paywall screen (M6). Report 54: 'told to upgrade, no way to' (1). Report 59 (Tappsk): paywall surprise 64 at 1.70★ — the lowest-rated monetization code — from users who thought the app was free. Report 64 (Critique AI): with no free tier the 'continue' path is only a dismiss control, and a tenth of the corpus cannot find it — 'you are stuck In the buy screen. You literally can't do anything but just stare at it'. Report 76 (Way of Life): MON_UPSELL 13 (2.85★, 'upsell nags', 2014 → 2023); MON_PAYWALL 22 (2.68★). Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): 'What's the point of making a free app if it's unfunctional unless you buy a premium plan' (1★) — the free/paid boundary is illegible at install and at the wall. Report 89 (Check Calendar): an ad-supported free option that reviewers say exists but cannot be selected — PAY_FREE_OPTION_BLOCKED 2 ('The whole app is basically useless without premium', 4★ 2026-06), FREE_TIER_OK 3, PAY_PREFER_ADS 2 ('You could just show ads so that we can use it freely'), MODEL_FREE_CLAIM 2 — 'the corpus cannot tell whether a working ad-supported tier exists'; the free/paid boundary is illegible enough that reviewers disagree about whether a free tier exists at all. Report 90 (Quit Bad Habits & Addiction): every feature is free and six Russian reviewers still believe the app is paid — PAYWALL_PERCEIVED 6 (0.98%, all RU): 'you can't even see the interface; a fully paid app' (1★); 'nothing but ads, and everything only for a month' (1★); 'the app is good, pity it's paid' (5★); the report cannot establish whether they saw an onboarding ad-removal offer, a trial screen or another app — §8.6 states on the purchase screen that every feature stays free.

<a id="c119"></a>
### C119 — Redesigns must not regress layout — ship a density / text-size option or an opt-out

**Certain** · 24 apps · 65 cards · positive in 7 apps · negative in 16 apps

*Why Certain:* 24 apps, same direction (act on it, 85%), 10 reports label it high-priority

A compact-list redesign produced a dated backlash (report 7) while a Liquid Glass refresh drew none (report 8); layout regressions hit neurodivergent users hardest (report 4); a Feb 2024 redesign and continuous UI churn drew a backlash cluster (report 10). Report 23: a list view or density control (45, 0.62%) must be opt-in — 8.9% of that theme's reviews are 1★ precisely because the app changed on them; the v3.0 feature expansion split reviewers the same week. Report 25: complexity is both the top praise and a top complaint (126 vs 27; 65 vs 'too many icons to pick from') — any simplification must be opt-in. Report 27: do not remove features in updates without an opt-out — restore the full-year grid as a selectable view and the 365-dot view as a choice. Report 28: UI bloat / update regression 6 (0.73%, mean 2.50); 'Seems like every update just brings more paywall and more forced advertisements'. Report 30: add a compact list density — rows too large once habit count grows. Report 36: a 2026 layout / scaling regression — font clipped on iPhone SE3, schedule options overflowing on iPhone 13 Plus / iOS 26.2 at first run (an immediate uninstall), an overview 'zoomed in like it was designed for desktop' — 4 of 6 UIBUG records in E5. Report 43: the Oct 2025 redesign split reviewers 4 positive / 7 negative — the negatives are a blocking journal-on-skip modal with no opt-out ('should have option to TURN OFF… the pop up is obscured by my keyboard'), a calendar header 'that takes up too much space', a removed pause button, a scheduling regression and three data losses at the moment the UI changed; the positives are reordering and the restructured routine screen; the report proposes an opt-in theme switch and a one-time 'what changed' screen instead of forced change. Report 48: the 2021 history-logging redesign is the one self-inflicted UX wound (see [[C264]]); 62 call the UI dated but the report advises against redesign for novelty. Report 50: repeated UI redesigns drew three long-term US users in five weeks (Jan–Feb 2025, all churn risk) — 'it's also counter intuitive to create an app about routine and habits and make your users keep adjusting to new layouts'; 'this was perfect as it was when I first downloaded it!… now it's messy' — not repeated in 19 months; 'do not redesign the UI again without a migration path'. Report 52: redesign complaints arrive in release bursts — Oct 2020 widgets (26), Jun 2021 a Success / Pending / Fail sheet on every check-in (29), Sep–Dec 2024 compressed layout (31), Feb–Apr 2026 AI note titles (20), Aug 2026 red focus page (12) — each about losing speed or calm, not a feature; a 5★ reviewer proposes decoupling front-end style from feature iteration; the report's R1: redesigns behind a setting for at least one release. Report 54: §8.5 'Do not redesign' — 128 praise the design and no 1★ criticises it. Report 71 (MyStreaks): 'the user interface can be clunky and unpolished at times. The menu can be slightly inconvenient to navigate' (ZA, 4★) beside 7 praising ease — the check-off and the navigation / social surfaces are different parts of the app; usability-test them separately. Report 75 (Habit Streak): the v1.57.1 'fresh look' widget redesign (2025-10-26) drew a 5★ asking for the old one back — 'earlier version of widget was very attractive. light screen and fire icon can you please bring that back'; widget demand climbed back from 5.6% to 23.5% of reviews; §8.3 #1 restore the look or offer it as a style option. Report 76 (Way of Life): the 2014-06 version 3.0 flat redesign split users — 'new version (3.0) looks awful' (2★), NEG_UPDATE_WORSE 8 of 17 in that era — and marks an era boundary in the review series; NEG_DESIGN 70 (0.90%) runs 2011 → 2023. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): the v2.1.0 overhaul (2026-02-11) produced 'UI bugs [that] have made it unusable' for a daily user (1★) and a reorder bug after a drag-and-drop rework — 'Do not rewrite the UI: 68.02% craft praise'. Report 85 (Habitica): the mid-2018 redesign removed sorting pets by colour; a 2026 redesign splits users (two like it, three do not); NEG_REDESIGN present across eras. Report 86 (Today): the November 2018 check-in redesign (NEG_REDESIGN 23, 3.22★) — single-tap check-in became multiple steps, the calendar mark shrank 'from a fully filled-in square to a TINY dot', no visual done-indicator so users tapped twice — was rolled back within months and reviewers upgraded in public: 'Dev Team reacted quite quick… Happy to have single tap check in back… Changed my rating to 5 stars ;-)' (edited 1★ → 5★); 'Thank you for listening!' — 'the corpus's clearest demonstration of responsiveness converting anger into loyalty'.

<a id="c142"></a>
### C142 — Surface existing features where users look

**Certain** · 24 apps · 72 cards · positive in 2 apps · negative in 22 apps

*Why Certain:* 24 apps, same direction (act on it, 87%), 10 reports label it high-priority

Features hidden behind 'Advanced Options' or unexplained modes are rated as missing — including by payers who bought and then believed the feature absent; report 7's weekly goals, multi-habit widget and notifications. Report 19: the only constructive reviewer found the product's real asset — a web course library — by accident, because the app never linked to it; the thirteen who called the product 'just a checklist' may have been describing the 10% they were shown. Report 23: a hidden backup/restore path, and edit/delete/undo actions hidden behind gestures — 250 UI-confusion reviews (3.44%, mean 2.66, 31.6% 1★) resolve into three actions: deleting a task, editing a task, undoing a completion; a single visible Edit / Delete / Undo affordance plus in-app text would address most of them. Report 26: a calendar/statistics view shipped ~late 2024 and users still cannot find it ('the calendar could be more easily accessible, I currently have to search for it') — a cheap discoverability fix on built functionality. Report 27: streak length is not readable from the day list (a full interaction spec given); a goal end date and archiving are on the listing and a reviewer could not find them; a streak freeze is listed and zero reviewers mention it; the website link in Settings points at a dead domain — the only support path. Report 28: an in-app 'Restore purchases' and 'Contact support' entry point is missing — four purchase failures and two 'where do I get help' reviews, while the developer answers e-mail within hours. Report 30: edit / delete / pause exist and three reviewers in three countries could not find them ('how do you pause a habit? how do you edit? I've looked everywhere'), one rating 1★ — a discoverability defect, not a missing feature. Report 31: misunderstandings about how to edit or delete a habit, what 'untracked' means, what colours and X/O marks mean and how 'quit' goals count — a UX problem, not a gap. Report 33: misunderstandings rise with feature count — a time-of-day filter hid habits and produced a false bug report; how to reorder or delete; skip vs cancel vs fail; 'every day starts skipped' (a setting); where the timer is; how to connect the Watch. Report 34: 'No widgets!!' two months after widgets shipped, and a request for an easier way to mark yesterday answered by the existing long-press ('That solves 90% of the struggle'). Report 43: roughly a tenth of scheduling complaints ask for shapes the app already has (custom days 'Monday and Wednesday's', timed tasks, untimed tasks) and land as 1★ / 2★; a Mac app is requested although the listing claims Mac. Report 47: the start date before creation exists but is hidden behind blank picker options — the second-largest request in the corpus (21) is a discoverability fix. Report 56: 'a feature-discoverability problem, not a feature-absence problem' — reminders requested twice after shipping (buried in the habit editor; v2.3.2 added a bell icon on every row), back-dating hard to find, widget transparency in the store preview but not findable — 'Shipping a feature is not the same as retiring its request'. Report 57: an AI habit-suggestion feature shipped in 2025 and both reviewers who mention it cannot find it; a Shortcuts 'Check-in ID' exists undocumented. Report 59 (Tappsk): NEG_UI_CONFUSING 152 (1.00%, rising to 1.4% in the latest era) — cannot find how to delete a habit or set a reminder on a habit ('не могу понять как удалить ненужную привычку'). Report 65 (Rabit): CONF_UX 12 (2.41%, mean 3.50) cannot find a control or how to mark a habit done; the timer is hard to find. Report 69 (TheFor): 'I am struggling to find the section of exploring popular routines' (4★). Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): a 2026-07-05 review asks for 'cloud sync, so data can be backed up and synchronized across devices' — iCloud sync has shipped since at least 2024-10-14, is praised by three reviewers and is a headed section of the description; an archive/restore feature (v2.3.0) is likewise unknown to a user asking for lost boards back. Report 84 (HabitGrid): MISUNDERSTAND_EXISTING 2 — a 4★ warns 'all your data will be deleted if you change your phone' while the listing advertises 'IMPORT AND EXPORT… restore it at any time' and zero reviews mention it; another asks for widgets five months after they were praised; 'discoverability problems, not missing features'; §8.3 surface export in onboarding and settings before building accounts — 'the cheapest change that answers both reviews'. Report 86 (Today): Restore Purchases exists in Settings and reviewers who lost premium on reinstall never found it (MON_RESTORE 18); statistics live in the profile screen and were found 'by accident' (UX_CONFUSE 74); a skip feature exists and 'nobody understands it' — 'fixing the explanation may be worth more than building anything'. Report 89 (Check Calendar): widgets and notifications are both in the listing and neither is praised in 253 reviews — five requests each stopped after they shipped, but no review says they were found; a widget shipped and never mentioned is a widget users may not know exists. Research: Quit Habit Decision.md — the inverse-reading rule: when the leader already ships a feature, its request count collapses and is replaced by complaint codes (164 of 56,653 reviews, 0.29%, almost all complaints), so a low count must never be read as low demand ([[C310]]).

<a id="c177"></a>
### C177 — One clear SKU shelf — every plan distinctly named, stating its period, and delivering exactly what its label says

**Certain** · 22 apps · 75 cards · positive in 3 apps · negative in 16 apps · tied to a purchase in 1 apps

*Why Certain:* 22 apps, same direction (act on it, 82%), 5 reports label it high-priority

Report 11: three SKUs shared the identical display name 'Habits PRO Functions' at $1.99 / $6.99 / $8.99 and none named a period, while reviewers described 'annual', 'VIP' and 'lifetime' purchases — neither the user nor support could tell what had been bought. Report 12: ten SKUs including three 'Weekly Subscription' and two 'One-Time Payment' entries at different prices, visible on the store page. Report 19: charged ≠ agreed ($29.99 annual agreed, $59.99/month billed) when the plan bought was never named back to the buyer. Report 30: Monthly $5.99, Yearly $44.99, a second Yearly $29.99 and Lifetime $59.99 — 'Te dicen que es de por vida el plan y es solo para un año' ('Cuidado, engañan'), and the monthly option could not be bought ('it charges for a year'); five of the six reviewers who reached payment had a bad outcome. Collapse the shelf. Report 41: the Lifetime SKU was intermittently invisible — 'I can no longer see the lifetime plan which I would like to purchase!'; 'When activated trial there was a lifetime subscription option. Now don't see it'; 'bummed I missed out on the lifetime deal'; and a Chinese user found no purchase entry at all — 'the cheapest revenue recovery in the report'. Report 42: seven concurrent IAPs, five near-identically named at $39.99 / $59.99 — reviewers quote wildly different prices by year and storefront. Report 43: the purchase sheet does not say 'one time' — 5 reviewers (mean 4.20) could not tell whether $2.99 was monthly or once, three of them 5★ users trying to buy ('can't seem to figure out if the $2.99 is per month or a one time purchase.?') and one who wrote a 2★ believing it was monthly; the thing the sheet fails to state is the product's most-praised attribute. Report 46: three concurrent premium SKUs (ED Premium Monthly, Everyday Premium Year, ED Full Year Access) beside a lifetime; a web price cheaper than in-app ('only $12 a year on the website, more in the app'). Report 49: the UK's advertised £1.99–£2/month resolves to a £24.99–£29.99 annual charge at checkout (misleading checkout 8.86% of GB, +7.48pp) while 'price too high' runs below global — 'the checkout presentation, not the price level, is what is generating one-star reviews'; a monthly plan costing more for two months than the annual for twelve (15). Report 52: two one-time tiers (小太阳 / 大太阳) with no upgrade credit between them; tier confusion carries a ×5.11 payer lift. Report 54: a one-time purchase that 5 reviewers think is a subscription ('the one time fee for a whole year'; 'is the ¥68 membership a one-off lifetime buyout?'). Report 60 (Mindway): 'When purchasing, it implies the option of monthly billing, but auto drafts the whole year' (1★, 'It seems scammy'); the annual is chosen to escape the weekly ('paid the $40 annual to avoid $7/week') and then regretted — plan clarity at purchase is one of the five paid-user issues; F2 includes the monthly-vs-annual selection screen. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): 'What is the difference between the 34 and 59 paid subscription?' — a buyer had to publish a 5★ review to ask, because the paywall did not answer it; M2: differentiate the two tiers on the paywall itself. Report 75 (Habit Streak): nine SKUs from $1.99 to $79.99, six named only 'Premium' or 'Premium access' with no period — 'A shopper cannot tell from the listing whether Premium — $11.99 is a month, a year or forever'; §8.1 #2 rename them (no reviewer complains — an external observation). Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): 10 IAP SKUs from $2.99 to $29.99 under three product names ('Momentumly Plus', 'Premium Habit Tracking', 'Premium'), none showing a billing period, beside a description whose only money paragraph is auto-renewal boilerplate with no price, tier, trial or one-time option — three reviews over 12 months hold three different beliefs about whether a lifetime purchase exists ('I've subscribed for the lifetime version', 2★; 'there is no possibility to get a lifetime version', 2★ — the entire review; 'The one time purchase rather than a subscription model is also a lovely thing', 5★); reviewers name the paid tier five different ways; 'a user who cannot tell what is being sold does not buy'; §8.1.2 show periods and cut the SKU count; §8.7 Q1 'does a lifetime SKU currently exist' is answerable in one minute in App Store Connect. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): five SKUs under three product names (Powerpack $9.99, Ripples Plus Lifetime $24.99, Plus Monthly $2.99, Plus Yearly $9.99, Powerpack Family $17.99) with no billing period shown against any; nine reviews use six different names for the paid tier and two incompatible billing models ('the premium subscription… a one time 10 dollar payment' in one sentence; '$10 for a lifetime subscription'; 'Чекер+'; 'die Vollversion'); 'A customer who cannot tell whether they are buying a subscription cannot consent to buying one'; a 'Чекер+' tier existed under the old app name before today's 'Ripples Plus'. Report 86 (Today): three IAPs — Today Premium Monthly $3.99, Today Premium Annual $9.99, 'All premium features' $299.99 — and reviewers cannot parse them: 'why is Today Premium $10 per year, but ALL Premium Features are $300 ❓ what is the difference' (2★); 'premium used to be $4.99 and now… $299.99' (gt 2★); §8.10 'whatever the intent — a lifetime tier, a price-anchoring device, a legacy artefact — it currently reads to users as either a mistake or contempt'. Report 89 (Check Calendar): one SKU, clearly named 'Premium (Pay Once)', and still five reviewers describe a subscription — the period must be stated where the price is seen, not only in the SKU list ([[C305]]).

<a id="c095"></a>
### C095 — Neutral, non-judgemental tone on failure

**Certain** · 21 apps · 49 cards · positive in 14 apps · negative in 6 apps

*Why Certain:* 21 apps, same direction (act on it, 80%), 6 reports label it high-priority

Reset without shame, no motivational pop-ups, keep history — the differentiation against apps that 'talk'. Report 23: a reminder framed as loss — 'You will lose your streak of X days if you don't do this today' — drew requests in four languages to reframe positively ('pedagogy from the early 20th century'); one string change per locale. Report 24: childish / condescending tone 304 (0.70%, mean 2.701); what paying users value includes that missing a day is not punished. Report 25: 'I clicked, paid £29.99 and I don't even know why. It's a list of aims for the day, I get to see all the things I haven't done and feel bad' — a checklist without a forgiving frame reads as guilt. Report 26: 'accountability and motivation without the shame' — gentleness, no streaks and a calm garden metaphor are the moat (25, mean 4.76; mental-health users 32, mean 4.66). Report 33: guilt copy backfires — 'Let's do better tomorrow, shall we?'; 'Yikes'; a Jan 2026 'Are you sure the day is over?' pop-up on fail/skip with no off switch ('infantilizing … Shipping annoying stuff without an off switch is a churn risk') — 43 reviews on unwanted or guilt notifications (mean 2.33). Report 36: 'As an easily discouraged perfectionist, I LOVE that if you miss a day (or a week) that it doesn't become the app of shame' (20 votes); the motivational text is 'encouraging but never guilt inducing' (13, all 5★). Report 46: 'not ticks to check off but areas that fill with beautiful colours — so I don't feel stressed about not managing something'; 'a triangle in that space… feels like neutral data instead of a personal failing'. Report 47: non-punitive framing praised — 'やったところが色が塗られるので加点方式な感じがして好き' ('what you did gets coloured in, so it feels like scoring points, not losing them'); the report: keep filled colour when a streak breaks, any missed-day marker optional. Report 48: non-punitive framing praised by 39 (0.89%, 4.90). Report 53: reminders phrased as questions — 'instead of stating what I'm supposed to do NOW, it asks questions — Have you walked today?' (REM_GOOD 67, 4.85). Report 55: quirky reminder messages liked by most ('I loved being called a tiger') but pet names drove churn ('Deleted when the reminder called me cutie'); R5: offer a neutral message tone. Report 68 (Ultiself): PR_GRACE 75 — 'doesn't make me feel bad when I mess up' — gentler than other trackers. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): the jokey voice reads as shaming to some — 'the badge makes me feel blamed all day and weighs on me'; 'The cheerleading energy and jokiness give me goosebumps' — on an audience that includes depression and ADHD recovery.

<a id="c216"></a>
### C216 — A forgiving long-run measure — cumulative or decaying credit that a missed day does not zero — alongside streaks

**Certain** · 18 apps · 46 cards · positive in 10 apps · negative in 9 apps · tied to a purchase in 1 apps

*Why Certain:* 18 apps, same direction (act on it, 71%), 8 reports label it high-priority

Report 20: a non-streak percentage that drops when a day is missed rather than zeroing — 'missing one day and breaking my streak tends to send me into a spiral where I give up'; described as logarithmic and 'much closer to psychological reality'. The product's one genuine differentiator (38 explicit, the highest-affection language in a 4,048-review corpus; unclaimed by any competitor), broken by a 2021 rewrite when the score stopped decaying and never restored — 'Please bring that algorithm back!' Users who asked for a streak counter asked for it alongside, never instead of, the strength score. Distinct from C201 (a day-level partial-completion threshold): this is the long-run measure. Report 10: replacing cumulative Journeys with consecutive-streak Self-Care Areas was the lowest-rated change in a 70,041-review corpus (mean 2.76, 21 of 49 one-star); chronic-illness and ADHD users say a streak-only model is structurally incompatible with their lives. Ship the forgiving measure next to streaks, not instead of them. Report 24: paying users name 'missing a day is not punished' among the things they value most. Report 25: a paying user describes the day view as 'all the things I haven't done' and feeling bad — the un-forgiving frame is a churn reason. Report 26: the garden only grows if every habit is checked that day — 'If I miss only one out of 6 of my habits, nothing happens. Behaviourally this means people will say it's not worth trying'; 'doing 90% should be rewarded'; 'No room for off days… I'm human' (20 verified, mean 2.80) — while 25 (mean 4.76) praise the app for being gentle and streak-free; partial credit as a setting reconciles the two. Report 28: decay that resets 'ALL of your progress' after a bad week is read as data loss; a gentler or optional decay with a visible backup state would separate punishment from bugs. Report 41: the non-binary percentage ring rather than streaks is why a perfectionist bought. Report 54: 'the evidence of consistency and the punishment for breaking it are separable, and this user base wants the first without the second' — colour-density calendars, per-habit completion counts and monthly totals, not a streak counter with a reset (D4, 48 reviewers). Report 57: 'This is the only habit-building app that didn't make me feel like a failure for missing a day'; a detailed proposal asks for a skipped / failed distinction to keep it that way. Report 58: 'an effective habit tracker that did not discourage me when I missed a day'. Report 65 (Rabit): streak-only scoring is 'too all-or-nothing' — a completion-% score alongside the streak requested by a payer (S7). Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): finishers want to keep counting past the fixed 30-day cycle ('I want to see how far I can extend the record beyond 30 days!'; REQ_PERIOD 13); the same 2018 update removed a 90-day option (NEG_90_REMOVED 3). Report 76 (Way of Life): the percentage/grid measure is what users protect — misusing skip to emulate a weekly habit 'distorts the percentages they value' (NEG_CHART 38); OUT_AWARENESS 181 (self-awareness) is the outcome the grid produces. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): a momentum score that decays instead of resetting is the whole product — 'the first habit tracker without streaks'; 19 of 71 (26.76%, mean 4.89★, zero below 4★) praise it by name: 'I used to drop habits the second I missed a day — all because of streak pressure'; 'removes all the frustration of having to start over from zero. It takes the 2-day rule even further'; 'motivates me to get things done but without the feeling of punishment when life gets in the way'; the streak is still visible alongside; 11 outcome reviews (15.49%) all 5★; PRAISE_MOTIVATING 11 all 5★, described as 'positive reinforcement', 'nudges that feel thoughtful, not annoying', 'without making me feel anxious'. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): v2.4.0 added a toggle to disable streak/consistency stats — a partial answer to weekly-schedule requests where a 3×/week habit 'can never build a streak'. Report 85 (Habitica): PR_GRACE 10 and PR_REST 6 vs NEG_PUNISH 23 — a health bar that regenerates and an inn to rest in are the forgiving elements; users ask for them to be discoverable and time-limited. Report 86 (Today): a skip day is used as a mental-health tool — 'to sort days when I felt bad out of the streak. Over time it became easier to assess my successes' (de 5★, depressive phases) — and the skip feature that exists is misunderstood by three reviewers and reported as damaging streak statistics. Report 90 (Quit Bad Habits & Addiction): a relapse zeroes a counter that reviewers describe as their whole motivation, and they work around it — logging a slip as a dated note rather than resetting two weeks — while REQ_RELAPSE_OPTIONS 4 ask for a pause that keeps progress ([[C308]]). Research: Quit Habit Decision.md — for quit habits the forgiving measure is 'best-ever vs current' shown together, so a relapse costs the current number without erasing the achievement; a relapse that wipes history is the most-repeated complaint across 10,621 reviews of the leading quit tracker.

<a id="c083"></a>
### C083 — Performance must not degrade with habit count

**Certain** · 16 apps · 32 cards · positive in 0 apps · negative in 16 apps

*Why Certain:* 16 apps, same direction (act on it, 97%), 7 reports label it high-priority

5+ second taps for the most engaged (paying) users; lag is a churn cause on its own. Report 30: above ~10 habits the list jumps back to the top after every tick and rows cannot be made denser — a defect that only paying users hit; fix it before raising the cap. Report 31: freeze / lag 404 (7.79%, mean 1.62) rising in every era to 26.6% of 2025–26 — '10 seconds for the sound effect, another 20 seconds for the colour to change'; '20-30 seconds per habit'; 'it now takes several seconds to add a single entry … can't cope with too many entries' (iPhone 15 Pro) — set a tap-to-register budget (<100 ms) and test with multi-year histories; some reviewers infer throttling of non-subscribers (untested). Report 42: lag scales with habit count ('the more goals you add the slower it gets'; hit at 15 habits) — 12 reviews (mean 2.58), 9 Brazilian, 4 payers — 'the users most affected are the ones who bought the app to have more than three habits'. Report 53: slowdown with many habits (24-vote jp review); the statistics crash tested against long histories and 20 habits. Report 56: the bottom menu bar blocks the habit list at 9+ habits — the scale 'unlimited habits' invites. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): UX_LIST_SCALE 2 (4.50★) — users with many boards find the single-page layout hard to manage; DEF_REORDER_BUG 1 after a drag-and-drop rework. Report 86 (Today): the sibling failure — latency growing with accumulated check-ins rather than habit count ([[C303]]); 'as my list of habits gets longer (and my dashboards get more complex), it gets very slow and the list gets very difficult to navigate' (za 3★); a performance fix in Mar/May 2020 was confirmed ('The latest update fixed the lag. I've dealt with that tedious issue every single day for months') and the complaint returned.

<a id="c152"></a>
### C152 — A promised pre-charge trial reminder must actually arrive — in-app, with amount and date

**Certain** · 15 apps · 29 cards · positive in 0 apps · negative in 12 apps

*Why Certain:* 15 apps, same direction (act on it, 96%), 6 reports label it high-priority

Report 10: 'you promised to remind me before charging' is the highest-intensity complaint in a 70,041-review corpus (billing-dispute family mean 1.97, 60% one-star, 17% of all payers); the reminder must be a blocking in-app card on next open, not only a push, and the exact amount and charge date must sit on the trial screen and permanently in Settings. For an ADHD audience the reminder is the feature, not a courtesy. Report 48: charged the full year at the start of a 7-day trial; a receipt shared by 'another active subscriber'. Report 50: no trial-expiry reminder before a ~$50 annual charge (AU) — fix F1 pairs it with the price mismatch. Report 59 (Tappsk): a confirmation e-mail with the renewal date is the report's first immediate fix (MON_AUTO_CHARGE 229, MON_CANCEL_TROUBLE 73). Report 67 (Habio): 'The day before my trial ended, they took the money and THEN emailed me and said my trial was up the following day'; MON_NO_RECEIPT 68 (3.32%); §8.3: a reminder 48 hours before conversion with the renewal amount in local currency and the plan length. Report 68 (Ultiself): no receipt or notice before charges (MON_RECEIPT 17); §8.2: show the renewal price and date on the intro-plan screen and in a receipt email. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): no in-app notice before the free window closed — 'why, with no notice at all?'; one reviewer reports three months instead of one week (unexplained). Report 82 (Lasting Change): BILL_NO_NOTICE 11 (1.00★) — no renewal notice before any charge; 17 learned of the charge from their bank.

### C077 — Purchase and signup flow must not leak buyers

**Certain** · 14 apps · 31 cards · positive in 0 apps · negative in 13 apps

*Why Certain:* 14 apps, same direction (act on it, 93%), 5 reports label it high-priority

People who try to pay and cannot (errors, rejected emails, promos that fail to apply) leave 2–4★ and money on the table. Report 14: two willing buyers in 2020 could not complete the purchase ('When I click upgrade button, it only appears an orange screen and then disappears') — the checkout broke in the app's final months. Report 53: an accidental purchase on first open (kr) and a crash right after paying ₩19,000. Report 55: the purchase button crashed in January 2018 — 'I want to give you money! I want more habits! But you're app crashes whenever I try to upgrade' (PAY_IAP_FAIL 14, 10 that month). Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): a 5★ Russian user cannot find how to pay — 「Кааак оплатить???????」 — 'Full intent, zero friction tolerance, no sale'. Report 76 (Way of Life): 'money were taken but nothing had changed' (ru 1★); BUG_PURCHASE 9.48× among purchasers. Report 82 (Lasting Change): DEF_LOGIN 14 (8.00%, all but one 1★) — people who paid on the web and could not get into the app: 'we recognise your email adress but the account registration is not complete — you took all the fee in öne min'; 'it says my account doesn't exist'; no create-account option on the sign-in screen; 'my email is not even registered. Then why was I even charged'; present in the first review of the corpus (15 days after release) and still in the last year; §8.7 every successful web payment must end in a usable app account linked by the purchase email. Report 85 (Habitica): BUG_SIGNUP 139 (4.03%, mean 1.55★ — the harshest code: 'people who never got in have nothing else to say'; 'they haven't been able to program a functional login screen in two years'), BUG_ACCOUNT 85: the onboarding Finish button, Google sign-in returning to the same screen, prefilled usernames that cannot be changed; the 2018-02-26 App Store feature day brought new users who could not reach the servers to register (22 reviews that day, 2018 the lowest-rated year at 3.32★); §8.2 'sign-up and login that never dead-ends'.

<a id="c255"></a>
### C255 — An in-app language selector that respects the user's choice — shipping a localisation must never trap someone in a language

**Certain** · 14 apps · 27 cards · positive in 2 apps · negative in 9 apps

*Why Certain:* 14 apps, same direction (act on it, 92%), 5 reports label it high-priority

Report 41: after Czech shipped, a Czech user wanted to keep English and 'there's no way to change the language' (13309363635, 5★); a French user's app switched itself to German — 'Why this language change to German??? I can't set it back to French? I'm so disappointed, I loved this app' (13509177027, 1★, Dec 2025). A regression introduced by localising, which converts a feature investment into a rating loss; the report's fix F5 is an explicit in-app language selector. Report 42: Ukrainian users served a Russian interface with no way to switch ('How to switch to Ukrainian/English interface?'). Report 43: 'The app is a mess, full of spelling mistakes' (GB, 1★) — localisation quality. Report 46: two German reviewers could not use the app because they do not read English (2020, Dec 2023) although German is listed. Report 47: notification options rendered as '汽車' and '手冊' in Traditional Chinese, mainland terms shown to Taiwan, a French machine translation that caused an immediate delete — translation quality 5, none Japanese. Report 52: Chinese-reading users on English systems ask for an in-app language setting independent of iOS; the Traditional setting in Taiwan still shows mostly Simplified. Report 56: the UI switched to Chinese unprompted and the user could not find how to change it back. Report 76 (Way of Life): reviewers ask for 'a working language switch' (REQ_LANG 13); BUG_LANG 15 (3.60★) across 8 languages. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): 10 localisations, 6 languages in the corpus, zero complaints about translation, missing languages or formatting. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): 13 days after a ten-locale bulk release, a Korean 4★: 'The Korean translation needs significant improvement. As it stands, it's worse than a machine translation' — the only translation-quality signal, pointing at the expansion release rather than a long-standing gap. Report 82 (Lasting Change): the app ships English only; 17 reviews (9.71%) are in other languages and the substantive ones are about billing consent, not language — §8.9 do not prioritise localisation. Report 83 (Roubit): the app spread internationally before it spoke other languages — English speakers arrived via Twitter in 2022 to a Korean-only app while the listing already claimed English ('inside the app you can only use korean'; 'tried my best to translate each part but its tiring'); LANG_REQUEST 11 (18.4% of E2); LOCALIZATION_INCOMPLETE 5 in 2023–2026 (Korean in the gacha and store: 'ハングルで読めない'; 'me aparecen letras coreanas'; no am/pm format); §8.7 string-coverage checks per release per shipped language. Report 84 (HabitGrid): a Vietnamese reviewer praises that the interface 'has Vietnamese' on a storefront where the listing advertises English only; Russian is written on five storefronts including us and ca. Report 85 (Habitica): translations are volunteer work and a volunteer reports the finished Ukrainian iOS translation had not shipped for months (2026-05-18) while 'Немає української мови' earns a 1★ — 'ship the translations volunteers already made'; a language setting that reverts to English and mixed-language screens are their own defect class. Report 86 (Today): a shipped translation criticised the day it arrived — 'what the hell is check-in translated as? If you can't translate, add a language option' (cn 5★); partial screens (3D Touch menu, widget) in English; Simplified only, no Traditional.
