<a id="c256"></a>
### C256 — Skip, miss and not-yet-logged are visibly distinct states, and the stats explain which is which

**Certain** · 14 apps · 29 cards · positive in 1 apps · negative in 11 apps

*Why Certain:* 14 apps, same direction (act on it, 73%), 5 reports label it high-priority

Report 41: a paying user never used the app because 'what does it mean when you forget to record a habit as completed, is that skipped or recorded as a miss. I don't understand how the stats work' (9373324084, GB, 3★); five years later 'when you go into a habit's history and see gaps, you don't understand whether you forgot to tick that day or whether it was a skip' (14303067862, UA, 4★); others ask for an explicit 'not achieved' (未達) state distinct from skip and to 'mark no if you missed it' (11107932681, 11725650343). Onboarding is the lowest-rated non-monetisation theme (8, mean 2.88). Report 43: a skipped vs missed distinction is part of the swipe confusion ('I was constantly marking things as done when I really wanted to mark them as skipped'). Report 46: 'missed' distinct from 'not recorded' requested by 6 (mean 4.67) — and the skip semantics confuse 19. Report 47: a note on a missed day that does not count as done requested by 4 (mean 4.50, 3 KR); show missed days 2 — the missed state needs its own visible, optional marker. Report 48: no vacation / illness handling that leaves a streak or an average intact (13); weekend 'misses' on weekday habits (21). Report 49: tasks marked done / partial / skipped by swipe; no pause for illness or absence (3). Report 50: skipped days should be visually distinct (1); a Skip that breaks daily completion is part of the pause request. Report 59 (Tappsk): 'чтобы можно было задачу пометить как НЕ сделанную' (so a task can be marked as NOT done) — a missed item cannot be marked as missed, only carried forward. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): 'unlimited back-dating makes streaks less meaningful' — a fan asks to mark missed days explicitly (a cross / red mark) and to lock past days; P4: streak integrity as an option, because some users need back-fill, and §8.5: do not remove back-dating — make it lockable. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): a blank cell is ambiguous — ○ / ✕ / △ marks would separate 'didn't do' from 'forgot to log' (mark types 5). Report 76 (Way of Life): the three-state grid (yes / no / skip) is praised (PR_SKIP 99, PR_YESNO 73), but without scheduled frequency skip becomes a scheduling method ('I try to only use skips for actual exceptions to habits, not as a scheduling method', 3★) and corrupts the stats (NEG_CHART 38); §8.4: non-scheduled days must be neutral and excluded from percentages. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): 'removing the streak also removed the obvious scoreboard, and a minority cannot find the replacement' — no tick-mark ('Daily habits, tick mark not available', a 1★ in a habit app over the core action), no achievement feeling ('lacks to give you the feeling of achievement for completing the tasks'), an unexplained momentum number and no monthly view of hits and misses ('difficult for you to know which days you have missed… from a monthly perspective') are four versions of one complaint (U:ux_friction 7, 9.86%, mean 2.57★ — the lowest mean of any union); §8.3.3 'a filled month is the achievement feedback the streak used to provide'. Report 86 (Today): 'I can not to figure out what different between skipped and not to check in' (tw 4★); REQ_FAILMARK 6 want to record a missed day explicitly; a skip that damages streak statistics (one report). Report 89 (Check Calendar): REPORT_ALL_MARKS_COUNTED 4 (1.58%) — reports count a ❌ day as done: 'I went to the gym 5 times this week… But I will also put 2 times the x… when I see the report, it shows 7 counts' (5★); one buyer gave 1★ for it and another wonders whether paying 600円 was a mistake; §8.6 count per emoji/mark in reports — 'for a record-keeping app these defects undermine the reason to pay'.

<a id="c123"></a>
### C123 — Notifications are few and finely user-controllable — per-type settings, escalation opt-in, never spammy and never silently retuned

**Certain** · 13 apps · 32 cards · positive in 1 apps · negative in 10 apps

*Why Certain:* 13 apps, same direction (act on it, 83%), 4 reports label it high-priority

Some users depend on an un-dismissable alarm, others are driven out by it; a global default serves both badly; removing it broke wake-ups for loyal subscribers. Report 24: all-or-nothing notification settings make users disable everything (744, 1.71%); per-type control is the fix. [Merged from C253: Report 36: notification restraint is praised by 12 (2.22%, mean 4.67) and framed as the reason people switched — 'fine-tuned control over the notifications you receive — probably the #1 reason I've deleted other habit apps was that they spammed me with a billion distracting notifications' (13967987039); a US talking point (3.97% vs 0.69% non-US). More / snoozable reminders are also requested (7) — make any escalation opt-in so the restraint is not lost. Report 43 (counter-case): the nag loop is the differentiator — user-controlled frequency ('as often as you want') is what makes heavy notification acceptable; one review in 638 finds it excessive. Report 46: a daily e-mail at exactly 12 with a new sender address each time (3, mean 1.67, 2020–23) was made switchable ('You can turn them off if you don't like it'). Report 48: notification overload 12 (2.33) against 224 reminder praise — custom text and per-tracker control keep the ratio stable. Report 50: per-habit reminders praised by 10 (4.90); notifications broken on the new Watch app (1).] Report 53: suppress reminders once the habit or its Health goal is met ('it should know based on my steps being tracked that I've met the goal'), several clock times per habit, snooze from the notification (R1); a burst of 10–15 notifications at 8 am ('64 notifications in just a few days'). Report 55: reminders only for undone habits, several per habit (R4). Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): notifications that continue after being switched off ('I definitely turned notifications off, yet they keep coming', 1★), remain for deleted goals and duplicate on a new cycle (BUG_NOTIF 38, 1.66%, mean 3.42); §8.2 honour notifications-off, allow weekday / weekend reminder times and later edits (REQ_NOTIF_EDIT 10). Report 76 (Way of Life): NEG_BADGE 13, NEG_NOTIF 11 (2.27★) sit beside NEG_FORGET 14 'forgets to log' — the reminder that nags and the one that is missed are the same design problem. Report 83 (Roubit): NOTIF_TOO_PERSISTENT 3 for alarms that repeat until done; BUG_REMINDERS 6. Report 85 (Habitica): BUG_NOTIF 50 vs PR_NOTIF 24; REQ_REMINDERS 20; pop-ups that derail the task are named by ADHD users. Report 90 (Quit Bad Habits & Addiction): the app has no notifications at all and REQ_NOTIFICATIONS 11 (1.79%) ask for them — 'Only downside is no notifications'; 'the app is forgotten very quickly'; 'no daily motivation, notifications or congratulations … after three days I forgot it existed' — while §8.4 still specifies them as optional and off by default. Zero notifications is also why no review in 614 complains of notification spam.

<a id="c188"></a>
### C188 — The app must open offline — never block launch on a network call

**Certain** · 12 apps · 41 cards · positive in 1 apps · negative in 11 apps · tied to a purchase in 1 apps

*Why Certain:* 12 apps, same direction (act on it, 87%), 7 reports label it high-priority

Report 13: a blocking in-app 'update in progress' migration bricked the app on launch in three waves (Nov 2019, Oct 2020 at 5.9% of that month's reviews, Sep 2025 → Aug 2026), destroyed data on reinstall ('lost almost 3 years of habit tracking') and locked out paying subscribers; 'Will not launch without internet'. Report 14: 'works fully offline' was one of two named reasons a reviewer chose this app over rivals already tried. Report 16: 'why in the world does ticking a box require connectivity!' — 9 reviews, zero 5★; a remote worker without internet for days could not use the app. Report 25: one reviewer names iCloud sync as the stuck state on first run ('shows synchronising with iCloud and nothing happens') — a first-run data path, not rendering; add a skip-setup / continue-offline path. Report 28: offline use is reported as paid and then removed; 6 complain about an internet requirement (mean 3.83). Report 46: free users cannot check off a habit offline ('ticking off habits while offline are locked behind a paywall', 7, mean 2.14) — the mechanism behind China's 'offline mode while online' cluster (16 of 17 Chinese, Sep 2019 – Apr 2020, consistent with the backend being unreachable from the mainland); the report's #14 allows offline check-off in the free tier. Report 47: a crash loop after logging in to the free backup (6, Feb 2024 – May 2025) with log-out as the only workaround; a white screen when typing a habit name (13, 2020–24). Report 53: in mainland China the launch screen hangs for seconds to 10+ minutes from build 2.8.0 (Dec 2022) through Aug 2026 — BUG_LAUNCH 30 of cn's 273 (10.99%); 'with a network connection it won't open; it only works offline' points at a blocking network call (analytics, paywall or ad SDK slow or blocked in China); F5: test cold start with no network and with blocked endpoints. Report 83 (Roubit): BUG_LAUNCH_LOAD 26 (5.20%, 2.85★; US 11.5%: 'i have never been able to use it because it does not load'; 'it just infinitely loads. Unusable.'); BUG_UPDATE_LOOP 7 — §8.2 instrument install → home screen (room loading, routine fetch, forced-update check) and fail open: show routines when the room or store cannot load; 'never block the app on an update that the App Store does not yet offer'. Report 85 (Habitica): NEG_OFFLINE 55 (1.60%) and BUG_SERVER 126 (3.66%) — a server-dependent client that cannot open or tick tasks during outages (2023-09-16: 20 reviews in a day, 17 server errors); NEG_CHINA_NET 16 unreachable from mainland China without a VPN ('翻墙连接也不行' — even using a VPN does not work). Report 90 (Quit Bad Habits & Addiction): the inverse case — the app only worked *offline* during the July 2026 crash week, because the ad load on launch was what crashed it ('airplane mode helps'; 'with the internet off it runs stably'); the listing promises 'works offline', and a network-dependent ad banner quietly broke that promise ([[C306]]).

### C223 — Undo / un-complete is a visible button — never a gesture-only path

**Certain** · 11 apps · 24 cards · positive in 0 apps · negative in 10 apps

*Why Certain:* 11 apps, same direction (act on it, 87%), 5 reports label it high-priority

Report 23: the only undo for an accidental completion was a shake gesture available immediately after the action; 77 reviews (1.06%, mean 3.38) across 12 storefronts called it unacceptable, several found the only workaround was resetting all history, and some deleted the app over it. Keep the gesture, add a button and a long-press-to-uncomplete path. Report 43: the Done and Info buttons sat adjacent for four years and swipes were mis-read ('I was constantly marking things as done when I really wanted to mark them as skipped… so I deleted it'; 'Tap targets for your most common actions… are tiny'); undo an accidental Done requested. Report 48: can't edit / delete a log 32 (3.22). Report 52: 'tap again to undo' was removed (2021) and a mistaken tap can only be marked 'failed'. Report 72 (Habit Hearts): 'eu cliquei numa tarefa errado e contou mas como eu desfaço isso???????' (4★); a slow undo, wants swipe-to-undo (4★); §8.2 #9 a fast, obvious undo. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): UX_NO_TICK — 'Daily habits, tick mark not available' (in, 1★): whether the tick is missing or merely hard to find, 'the outcome was a one-star review in a habit app over the core action'; §8.3.2 make the completion gesture unmissable. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): REQ_UNDO_CHECKIN / DEF_CHECKIN_SPAM — 'Check in too many times' (4★): a second tap should undo; v2.0.1 restored a long-press check-in configurator. Report 89 (Check Calendar): 'can't erase a check once entered' (jp, 4★, 2023) and a mis-tap confirmation dialog that 'appears too often' (jp, 4★, 2025) — undo must exist and must not become a modal on every tap.

### C139 — Cache entitlements locally — never block a paid surface on a live server check

**Certain** · 10 apps · 23 cards · positive in 0 apps · negative in 10 apps

*Why Certain:* 10 apps, same direction (act on it, 100%), 2 reports label it high-priority

Report 7: widgets that re-checked Pro against a network service showed 'Upgrade' to paying users for 15 months (100% payers, mean 2.25), 4× more often in markets with VPN/DNS filtering; render from the last-known-good receipt. Report 24: cannot log in / paid but no premium access 96 (mean 1.375, 78.1% 1★). Report 25: three independent reports in three storefronts (fr, fr, nl) that the app stopped working immediately after payment — specific enough to reproduce against the entitlement path. Report 28: 'I paid the 14.99 to unlock the full app 2 days ago and it's still saying I need to purchase it… Total scam'; carrots not delivered after 2–3 hours with restart and restore both failing. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): the clearest case — 'If I don't have internet access the app asks me to go premium, when I already bought the app. This is a headache. Can you fix this critical error!' (EC, 5★ despite the bug): a receipt check that requires the network re-paywalls exactly the offline moments (commute, flight, poor signal) when a habit app is used; I1: cache the receipt / entitlement locally and never re-paywall a verified purchaser because the network is unavailable — 'the single highest-severity non-burst finding in this report'. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): the developer's own v2.7.0 note (2026-09-03) — 'Fixed an issue where Ripples+ features would sometimes become locked while the device was offline' — corroborates MON_ENTITLEMENT_FAIL 3 (every one 1★, 33.3% of stated payers); §8.1.1 an offline grace period for verified entitlements and an in-app 'my purchases' state showing what is owned and when it was verified. Report 83 (Roubit): a Restore Subscription button resolved an entitlement/ad problem for a paying user who then moved to 5★; membership that 'sometimes drops' is the same class.

<a id="c183"></a>
### C183 — A pre-planned, structured day is the outcome ADHD and autistic users praise

**Certain** · 10 apps · 25 cards · positive in 8 apps · negative in 1 apps

*Why Certain:* 10 apps, same direction (act on it, 83%), 4 reports label it high-priority

Report 12: 'I lose track of time, forget to do things, and never have a plan, but that girl made sure I DID have a plan' — the one narrow, consistent praised outcome (22 reviews, mean 4.95) is being told what the day looks like. Report 25: an app titled 'Routine / Planner for ADHD' models whether a habit happened, not when — per-habit clock time with a notification at that time is the biggest unshipped feature (29, mean 3.41, 17 of them 4–5★; 9.0% of the 4★ band), clustering with one-off tasks (10), every-N-minutes reminders (4), an hour-by-hour agenda view (4) and long-term goals (7); buyers who expected time structure found a checklist ('Just a to-do list app'; 'I get to see all the things I haven't done and feel bad' — a £29.99 purchaser). Whoever ships routine scheduling rather than routine checking takes the ADHD-planner positioning. Report 43: a red / yellow / green time-window timeline and multi-step timers are what ADHD users name — 'when I don't have the brain power to think it just tells me what to do next'; an adult child with autism's morning routine on timers. Report 59 (Tappsk): the one-screen day plan with habits on top is what forgetful and ADHD reviewers credit ('keeps me together with my bad ADHD'). Report 60 (Mindway): organisation and structure is the most-cited benefit (15, 6.94%, mean 4.80, 13 at 5★): 'I used to be a mess, today I'm organised' (IL); 'Now I have a regular plan' (TR); 'You plan what you're gonna do at the next day'; the ADHD reviewers credit exactly this ('helps me stay on task instead of getting distracted'). Report 85 (Habitica): 'For people with depression, like me, this app is incredible' (18 votes, the most-voted purely positive review); 'Points go in where you can see them, so you want to do it even when you're not motivated' (jp) — instant visible reward as the executive-function aid.

**Certain** · 10 apps · 21 cards · positive in 0 apps · negative in 9 apps

*Why Certain:* 10 apps, same direction (act on it, 100%), 6 reports label it high-priority

Every charge produces a receipt that names the plan, the amount, the next charge date and links to the product; every renewal is preceded by a reminder. Related: C152 (the trial-end reminder) and C177 (SKU names). Report 10: a monthly event's 'grow potion' animation crashed the app on load for a large cohort (120 crash reviews in Feb 2026, 4–6× baseline), destroying 600-day streaks and locking paid users out for weeks; reviewers blame the event cadence for shipping untested code. Report 52: release waves recur on old OS versions (v2.41 on iOS 13 biometric unlock; iOS 14.x launch crash for 20+ days) — F5: a release gate for old iOS and data migrations, staged rollout, crash-safe local store before schema changes; target no month with ≥20 crash reviews. Report 55: F4 — test every build against current and previous iOS versions and screen sizes; staged rollout; halt on a crash spike (no month with >10 crash reviews). <a id="c193"></a>
### C193 — When a trial or subscription ends, the user lands on a usable free tier with read-only history — never a cliff

**Certain** · 8 apps · 24 cards · positive in 1 apps · negative in 8 apps · tied to a purchase in 1 apps

*Why Certain:* 8 apps, same direction (act on it, 100%), 3 reports label it high-priority

Report 16: a cancelled payer could not edit, view or even complete the one habit the free tier allows — 'It's my habit for walking my dog, who is recently deceased… I guess the app is bricked for me now.' A lapsed subscriber with read-only history is a resubscription candidate; one whose data is hostage is a permanent loss. Report 16 (trial side): a well-liked no-card 28-day trial that dropped to a one-habit tier read as a bait-and-switch — 'it encourages people to start habits and continue them for three weeks and then hits you with a steep bill' — and was the fastest-growing negative (2.4% → 7.2%). Taper, warn earlier and in-app, or keep the streak read-only. Report 60 (Mindway): with a free tier of 1–3 tasks there is no usable free tier to land on — a lapsed or refused subscriber has nowhere to go but the wall. Report 72 (Habit Hearts): a free-tier data reset after a month, unexplained — if free data expires, it must say so. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar, 151 reviews): the clearest cost of the cliff — at the end of an undisclosed ~1-week free window the app stops entirely ('after a week you can't even tap'; TRL_SUDDEN_LOCKOUT 20, mean 1.30) and read access to existing records is locked (TRL_DATA_HOSTAGE 6, mean 1.17 — 'the angriest theme'; 人質 'hostage' in two reviews and a title: 'holds the records you've built up hostage and presses you to pay'); the app is used for medication adherence and a locked-out user wrote 'I never thought it would go paid — I wish I'd written down what I'd been taking'; §8.1 #3 'Never lock read access to existing records. Let expired users read, scroll and export their history forever; gate only new entry and premium features' — the report's single highest-leverage change; #4 unconditional CSV export at trial end — 'A user who leaves with their data does not write scam'. Report 89 (Check Calendar): after the trial, previously entered checks and notes cannot be viewed or copied out — PAY_DATA_LOCKED 8 (3.16%, 1.75★): 'when it ends, you're basically unable to do ANYTHING without paying. I can't even copy the notes I had written down'; 'Holds your data hostage for money'; 'now I can't even see the information I entered in those 7 days; it's blocked' (br); 'it's sad that I can't even see the notes I've entered without paying' (jp, 2026-03) — 'this matters more for a medication tracker than for a to-do list' (USE_HEALTH 14); one reviewer said a January 2025 update made old records visible again and a March 2026 reviewer still could not read notes; §8.2 keep history readable and CSV export available (the export already exists) even if new checks require Premium.

### C217 — An unexplained number reads as broken — explain the score, and any rule that moves it by itself, on-screen

**Certain** · 8 apps · 20 cards · positive in 0 apps · negative in 6 apps

*Why Certain:* 8 apps, same direction (act on it, 94%), 5 reports label it high-priority

Report 20: a weekly habit completed once showed 4%, not 100%, and users could not work out why; the developer's answer (~91 repetitions to reach 100%) read as arbitrary. A documentation failure, not a maths failure — one explainer screen and an optional 'this period' toggle was the cheapest satisfaction win in the corpus (20 classified, undercounted). Report 59 (Tappsk): 'не очень понятно что значит 115' (not clear what 115 means) — the productivity score is unexplained on screen. Report 60 (Mindway): 'It's just a basic to do list' — the absence of any metric at all (no completion %, no consistency view) is read as the product being unfinished. Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): 'you see a sea of dots without being able to distinguish month, week and day' (IT, 1★) — the dot / heat-map grid others paid for carries no time axis, and a 4★ asks for the options to be explained: 'the UI is legible to people who already understand it'; P8: a visible month / week / day framing as a design test; P7: one-line hints on first use. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): the momentum number is unexplained in-product — 'I can't really tell on what basis momentum arises, or why it's good that it's displayed' (kr 3★) vs 'At first I had some trouble following the points logic, but now that I've grasped it, I'm thrilled' (de 5★) — 'same obstacle, two outcomes… the gap between those two reviews is the whole opportunity'; §8.3.1 a one-tap explanation where the number is displayed; U:comprehension 4 (5.63%, 3.00★). Report 86 (Today): the custom chart, counter and milestone cards go unexplained (UX_CONFUSE 74; NEG_FEATURE_UNUSED 15) and a skip state is misunderstood by three — the depth layer that converts power users confuses everyone else. Report 90 (Quit Bad Habits & Addiction): the goal ladder advances by itself and is not explained — U:goal_setting 25 (4.07%, mean 4.12★) from people who otherwise like the app: GOAL_HOWTO_QUESTION 13 ('tapped everything, can't see where to change the goal'; 'spent the first day trying to understand why my goal is one day and where to change it') and GOAL_STEPS_RIGID 15 (7 then 30 days is too far for a strong habit; 'a 100-year goal is somewhat unrealistic', de; a 13-year-sober reviewer wants 15 years, not 100; 'it sets a month automatically, I need a year'); one reviewer says custom goals used to work and were removed; §8.5 show on first run that goals advance automatically, allow a custom next milestone, and use a gentler ladder (1, 3, 7, 14, 30, 60, 90 days, then yearly) — and one reviewer likes the automation, so it stays the default. (Consolidation after report 90: title widened from 'An unexplained metric reads as broken' to cover automatic rules as well as computed scores — a target the app changes by itself needs the same one-line explanation.)

<a id="c012"></a>
### C012 — Week / month / year grid views

**Strong** · 36 apps · 107 cards · positive in 19 apps · negative in 23 apps · tied to a purchase in 3 apps

*Why Strong:* 36 apps, directions mixed (act 40, free 35, open 13)

'Filling the squares' is the retention mechanic and emotional payoff. Report 23: statistics limited to the current and previous month (46 requests); the most-requested visualisation is a year heat-map / GitHub contribution grid, the single most-named competitor gap (Habitify). Report 25: statistics weak/unreadable (8) — rework the screen around 'why did I miss it'; a heat-map widget like HabitKit/Ripples requested. Report 26: statistics/history/calendar per habit was the top unmet need (40, 1.04% — 'this is a cosmetic habit tracker, it does not offer really understanding of progress'), something shipped ~late 2024, and the rate returned to 4.26% of substantive 2026 reviews because it is hard to find and stats cannot be reset. Report 27: daily, weekly and yearly views exist and a monthly view is the missing rung — requested five times over four years, the only feature request that repeatedly costs stars (2 of 6 3★); the year grid is the app's signature and its de-emphasis was noticed. Report 29: statistics (bar, pie, weekly analytics, completion rings) is the one advanced surface praised unprompted (10, mean 4.60) and asked to be extended — all-time records, a monthly/yearly grid, export — the safest place to add depth without violating simplicity. Report 30: per-habit and per-day completion percentages requested; history editing works only within the current month. Report 34: the per-habit year grid / 'year in pixels' / GitHub-style heatmap is the differentiator — 105 reviews (14.13%, zero 1★), 'the only habit tracker I could find with a whole year view'; 'Don't Break The Chain only makes sense if you can actually see your chain!' Report 46: a habit × day grid whose squares deepen in colour with each consecutive completion is the product — 228 reviews (10.47%, mean 4.86): 'Because I don't want the gradient to break, I'm motivated to check in every day'; 'Anybody that like seeing a git commit graph will love this app'; 'not ticks to check off but areas that fill with beautiful colours — so I don't feel stressed about not managing something' — praised at a near-constant 9.68–11.62% for eight years. Report 47: a dot grid that fills — and keeps what was filled — is the retention mechanic: 67 (11.38%, mean 4.70), rising to 17.1% of 2025–26 reviews ('マスが埋まっていくのを見るのが、地味に達成感を感じてとても良い'); calendar / month view praised 9; a combined all-habit overview calendar requested 6 (mean 4.50); the month view showing only a week is a payer's bug. Report 58: daily / weekly / monthly / yearly progress views with unrestricted history are an adoption reason for 5 ('you can see all of your history not just a month back'). Report 59 (Tappsk): habits show a week, not a month — 'Не нашел полноценную сводную статистику по всем привычкам' (no proper summary across all habits, 3★); REQ_STATS 114 (1.3% of the latest era); the experiment is a month view per habit. Report 60 (Mindway): a routine planner sold without any consistency view is judged 'just a to-do list' by 10 reviewers including 5 payers; the minimal fix proposed is a completion % plus current streak plus a 30-day grid (E4). Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): statistics are not on the main screen and have to be sought out — named as a reason a 4★ is 'consider[ing] other options'; P6: reachable from the main screen without adding clutter. Report 69 (TheFor): the heat map is 'quite gimmicky' — tapping a day should show which habits were completed that day (REQ_DAY_DETAIL). Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): a History of completed cycles is praised (PR_HISTORY 31) while others want a calendar view (9) and a done list / time log (7). Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): the weekly grid is the unit people praise (5), and a monthly view is the third request (6) — 「月ごとの表示機能」 named as an immediate-purchase condition. Report 76 (Way of Life): the at-a-glance grid of green/red/grey cells plus charts is the second-largest praise (PR_INSIGHTS 838, 10.79%, 4.80★) and the #2 purchase trigger (14.3% of 349 purchasers: 'This is the only app I bought the paid version for, and I regret it not at all'); honesty through colour is the motivator — 'keeps me from fooling myself into thinking I did better than I really did'; 'I hate to break a winning steak'; PR_ACCOUNTABILITY 477 (6.14%). Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): a calendar exists but does not show hits and misses — U:calendar_gap 3 (4.23%, 3.33★): 'my habit in a calendar graphic'; 'the calendar part doesn't operate well' (kr); a monthly hit-and-miss view is what replaces the streak's achievement feedback. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): the GitHub-contribution grid is the product ('you've filled in every box for the first month, then you realise you've formed a habit'); PRAISE_ANALYTICS 9 (5.00★) after 'das neue Update mit den Analytics'; advanced analytics moved from paid to free in v2.4.0. Report 83 (Roubit): statistics and weekly reports ship; PRAISE_ALL_IN_ONE 23 — one user deleted separate to-do, goal and diary apps. Report 84 (HabitGrid): the grid is the app's name — 'remind me of github, very beautiful'; 'progress by day, week, for the year, clear statistics, beautiful visualisation. You can mark progress for past days and add a note. Ideal'; 'It is very motivating when you see your progress for the year'; U:visual_progress 16 (18.60%), free. Report 85 (Habitica): the avatar is the only progress view; REQ_CALENDAR 33 and REQ_STATS 71 ask for the grid/history that every other tracker in the series has. Report 86 (Today): the streak calendar card is the record users protect ('changed the check-in marks on the calendar from a fully filled-in square to a TINY dot', 2★); REQ_DASHBOARD 70 want all habits on one screen; statistics live in a profile screen found 'by accident'. Report 89 (Check Calendar): PRAISE_MONTH_VIEW 11 (4.91★) — 'see the whole month of the glance'; 'having a visual where I can see how often I accomplish my goals in a given month is helpful'; one monthly calendar per habit, several as tabs (PRAISE_MULTI_CALENDAR 11, 5.00★).

<a id="c143"></a>
### C143 — Intra-day completion: tap N times to fill N/N

**Strong** · 26 apps · 58 cards · positive in 5 apps · negative in 19 apps

*Why Strong:* 26 apps, directions mixed (act 26, free 13, open 7)

When a habit's target is more than once a day, each tap should count toward it; one binary tick per day is report 8's #1 unmet need, the only complaint theme still rising, and a stated uninstall. Report 20: multiple check-ins per day (water, medication, teeth) was requested 54 times (mean 3.87) and named as table stakes against Streaks and Productive; never shipped. Report 23: multiple-per-day / partial increments (111, 1.53%) largely shipped in 2016; residual complaints are about partial-progress display. Report 26: multi-count per day (5 glasses of water, 10 pages) requested by 7. Report 27: multiple completions per day shipped ~Aug 2025 and is praised ('the multiple check-ins per day feature is very handy'). Report 29: 'As someone who takes medication twice a day it would be incredibly helpful to mark the same habit done twice a day'. Report 33: multiple completions per day / quantities (water ×8, pills ×3) was the largest 2017–19 request (53, 50 before Aug 2020) and shipping multi-check-in goals in Habitify X retired it (2.9% of E1 → 0.1% of E5). Report 36: multiple completions per day requested by 5. Report 41: countable goals with over-achievement and partial credit ('if a habit needs a count of seven… and you have only performed it four times, you get credit for that'). Report 42: multiple completions per day for water, meals and reps do not exist — 6 reviews (all US, 13.0% of US, mean 1.50), two refund-seeking payers: 'Track your food? Great - you can track it ONCE/day'; 'So you're going to eat or drink water just once a day?' — the marketing promises a counter, the product delivers a daily checkbox. Report 43: 0/2 and 0/4 per-day counters with hourly nagging exist and sell the app. Report 46: several completions per day requested by 12. Report 52: multiple check-ins per day (237 — water × 8, meds morning and evening) and multi-check habits that force a detail sheet even with one-tap enabled. Report 53: brush teeth twice, meditate in two sessions (CORE_MULTI 12). Report 55: the same habit several times a day (CORE_MULTI 5). Report 57: multiple check-ins per day requested from 2019 ('stamping three or four times a day, like for medication'), shipped as 'goal', capped at 5 ('I need 10'), then tier-gated — producing the three angriest change complaints (24 requests). Report 62 (Streaks, yusuf kildan): within-day granularity is the largest coherent feature gap — 4 of 45 (8.89%) from four storefronts over eight months: count a habit N times a day and sum at day end, more than one reminder a day ('One reminder a day is not enough' for water and steps), a value per day ('walked 5k, then 7k'); two described use cases (water, steps) are currently unserviceable; P1 in the roadmap. Report 65 (Rabit): a times-per-day option that cannot be partially completed — 'tenho que tomar vitamina 2x ao dia, porém não consigo marcar caso eu tenho tomado apenas 1x. É tudo ou nada'; 'i'm not really sure what it is supposed to be used for' (S4). Report 72 (Habit Hearts): duration targets with partial completion — 'if your goal is 120 min, you can tick 20 min of it' — praised. Report 76 (Way of Life): REQ_COUNT 129 includes 'several times a day'; the yes/no/skip cell cannot hold a count. Report 83 (Roubit): '하루에 프랭크 10회 하기라면' (if it's 10 planks a day) — count-based routines requested (REQ_FLEX_SCHEDULE 10). Report 88 (GetHabit): counting habits ('8 glasses of water') cannot be tracked (FUNC_LIMITED); §8.8 count-based habits as table stakes.

<a id="c096"></a>
### C096 — Privacy and discretion stack

**Strong** · 10 apps · 28 cards · positive in 3 apps · negative in 7 apps

*Why Strong:* 10 apps, same direction (act on it, 75%)

Face ID / passcode lock, no account, discreet app name, alternate icons — zero negative reviews in report 3 and category-critical for recovery users on family phones. Report 33: privacy 23 reviews (mean 1.35) — the in-app help showed other customers' support conversations, e-mails and photos; goal-share URLs readable without login with no off switch; sync requiring Apple ID, Google account and e-mail; third-party analytics — audit support-conversation scoping and make sharing opt-in with unguessable, expiring links. Report 48: 25 reviews object to being forced to create an account and go online for a local tracker — a privacy objection distinct from price, strongest in Germany. Report 49: 20 frame the pre-paywall questionnaire as data collection (1.10) — one demands deletion. Report 52: a passcode lock that an ad dismissal bypasses (2025) — security-relevant despite being a single report. Report 56: no ads, no data collection, no account — 'Dots currently monetizes nothing', itself a differentiator and the credibility that makes a donation ask land. Report 76 (Way of Life): passcode / Touch ID / Face ID lock; PR_PRIVACY 12 ('local data, no account', 4.92★); a lock-out is a 1★. Report 86 (Today): the paid passcode / Touch ID / Face ID lock leaks the habit list — via the 3D Touch widget after force-close (ua 4★), on background resume ('no password is required to launch the app'), and for an instant before the fingerprint screen (jp) — three reports in three languages over three years; one reviewer objects on principle to paying for a lock.

<a id="c237"></a>
### C237 — The reward loop needs a content runway — finite gardens, themes or levels exhaust long-term users

**Strong** · 8 apps · 30 cards · positive in 5 apps · negative in 6 apps

*Why Strong:* 8 apps, directions mixed (act 8, free 7, open 7)

Report 26: garden-motivation praise declined monotonically 7.93% → 8.41% → 5.65% → 5.03% → 3.76% across five years while aesthetic praise strengthened, and reviewers report running out of gardens ('when I grew all the gardens, there is nothing to do'; 'YOU NEED MORE GARDEN DESIGNS!!'; 'I'll get bored if more aren't added'). For a product whose entire retention mechanism is the garden this is the most strategically important soft signal; per-habit gardens would also soften the all-or-nothing rule. Report 28: users complete all rooms and the motivation engine stops — 16 (1.95%), including a paying customer leaving ('this one doesn't motivate me anymore'), 'after level 200 you get items less frequently, and the hype is gone', 'incentives stop after level three hundred'; one specifies the remedy — reset the house and make it dirty again, counting resets like a prestige. Report 36: a 60-day monument that is the same journey for every habit — curiosity brings people back on day 3 ('I can't stop because I'm curious about what the next reward is'; GAME+ 74, mean 4.69) and the identical journey and hard stop drive them away around day 60–120 (17 distinct, mean 2.76: 'the story is repeated for all habits … pretty boring', 8 votes; 'it's a shame that it lasts only 60 days … I could have built something infinitely'). Report 49: 'what happens after day 66' and further programmes requested (5); several describe second, third and fourth 66-day cycles. Report 50: long-tenure reviewers (9) all rate 5★; requests deepen rather than stop. Report 54: more plants / a garden or shelf (9) and richer plant behaviour (9); growth stopping at 67 days — see [[C273]]. Report 65 (Rabit): the garden is the retention mechanic (GAM_PLANT 21, mean 4.62; MOT_GOOD 21, 4.86 — 'ver minhas plantinhas crescendo me incentiva a continuar') and under-built — more plant varieties (3), a placeable garden 'more like FarmTown' with tap-a-plant-for-detail, a widget that shows the garden and warns when a plant is near death; 'the cheapest available investment in the thing people already love'. Report 83 (Roubit): carrots → coins → fragments → gems spent on furniture, themes and outfits partly through a gacha; REWARD_ECONOMY_SLOW 7 ('It is so hard to get the coins'); PAYWALL_COSMETICS 4 ('A bit greedy' — fragments cannot buy Ultimate items); BUG_REWARDS 15 (2.80★); requests for more outfits, poses, rooms and seasonal themes (14, 5.00★) — the content runway is the ask. Report 85 (Habitica): the collection loop (eggs, pets, mounts: PR_COLLECT 88) retains after novelty fades, but REQ_CONTENT 79 (2.29%) — more content, actual battles, an endgame — and 'they are all essentially the same' show the runway ends; REQ_TRADE 12.

<a id="c254"></a>
### C254 — An all-habits overview with one-tap check-off — never force one-habit-at-a-time navigation

**Strong** · 8 apps · 27 cards · positive in 2 apps · negative in 5 apps

*Why Strong:* 8 apps, directions mixed (act 12, free 7, open 4)

Report 36: a full-screen one-habit canvas with names in a small strip at the top produced 27 distinct navigation complaints (5.00%, mean 3.56, mostly 4–5★), asked continuously from Dec 2021 to Apr 2026 (one review 45 helpful votes): the centre check button swallows horizontal swipes, the strip is 'quite a reach', and it gets worse with more habits — i.e. for the paying user ('I have to swipe through 16 habits. That alone is enough for me to not want to use this app anymore'); 12 ask for 'a consolidated list / calendar view of all of your habits' to 'check or uncheck' on one page. A Dec 2025 partial fix was praised the same week, but complaints continued. Report 43: groups / profiles that can be toggled on and off (e.g. weekday vs weekend sets) requested by 4 (mean 4.25). Report 47: a combined all-habit overview calendar requested by 6 (mean 4.50); a 'today / not yet done' list by 3 (4.67); today's status unclear 5 — the home surface must show every habit's state at once. Report 48: a Today list exists but is premium (tags / filters / Today); a 3-tracker free tier keeps the overview small. Report 59 (Tappsk): the one-screen today / tomorrow / later layout with habits on top is the praised overview (PR_SECTIONS 134, PR_ONE_SCREEN 82, PR_SWIPE 58 reschedule by swipe; 'Die Ansicht „heutige und zukünftige Aufgaben“ ist bei keiner Anderen App so gut und Übersichtlich aufgeteilt'). Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): glanceability 21 (13.91%, 4.95; UX_OVERVIEW 9, all 5★) — a week × every habit on one screen with no scrolling: 'There are lots of apps that fill in coloured blocks, but those take space per item so you can't see everything without scrolling. This app doesn't have that problem' — the product's differentiator. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): a multi-habit widget is the second repeated request — 'only able to select 1 habit to track at a time. So, I have to open the app to check which habits I have yet to complete' (5★); 'a widget what would show all Habbits at once' (4★); REQ_WIDGET_MULTI 2 (4.50★). Report 86 (Today): the one-page-per-habit model is the differentiator and the scaling ceiling — REQ_DASHBOARD 70 (3.92%, 2016-03-21 → 2026-07-13, ten years: 'see all habits at once'), BUG_SWIPE 39 (horizontal swipe fighting vertical scroll, 2016 → 2024 in seven languages, 'the single longest-running unfixed complaint'), UX_FRICTION 41 — 'Requiring each habit to be its own page makes this impractical for tracking more than a small number of items' (2★); 'I have more than 30 habits… please minimize that dashboard so i could see all my habits at once' (2026); users specify the fix — 'list as a default view; tap on an item will add a point; a habit image as a part of a row'; §8.8 'do not remove it; make it optional past a threshold'. Report 89 (Check Calendar): the one-calendar-per-habit design is praised (11 reviews at 5.00★) and its cost appears as REQ_MULTI_HABIT_VIEW 2 and a request to tick several habits from the widget (2026-07) — the same tension report 74 recorded for the sibling app.

<a id="c230"></a>
### C230 — Sync merges an append-only, timestamped event log — never last-writer-wins state replacement

**Strong** · 7 apps · 16 cards · positive in 0 apps · negative in 4 apps

*Why Strong:* 7 apps, same direction (act on it, 100%)

Report 23: after a 2022 migration to direct iCloud sync, complaint-framed sync went from 1.42% of 2015–17 reviews to 7.60% of post-2022 reviews (mean 2.90) and data loss from 0.33% to 4.62% of the era; failure modes were a device overwriting newer state with older state, deleted tasks resurrecting, Watch completions never reaching the phone, and completions un-completing seconds later. A customer review spells out the correct architecture: immutable timestamped events applied in order. Report 48: duplicate entries 32 (2.31), 20 of them in the 2015 sync rewrite. Report 50: to-do entries lost and unrecoverable for a Premium user (Apr 2026). Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): the recording tap is lost — tapping the ring shows the undo hint instead of recording ('A pop-up saying cancel with the top-right button appears; when I reluctantly delete it I'm back to day one'; BUG_INPUT 20, 2017 → 2026), counts stick at 7 or 4, and 'fairly often, wipes out the previous day's record' (BUG_COUNT 12, BUG_RESET 7); defects are in 48% of 1★ — 'For a product whose whole promise is an unbroken record, a lost day is the worst possible failure'; §8.1: log every tap so a lost day can be restored. Report 76 (Way of Life): no sync at all for 16 years — REQ_SYNC 139 — so this corpus has zero sync-conflict complaints; the data-loss path is the phone change, not the merge. Report 86 (Today): a restore flow that overwrote the backup it was reading and wiped the restore data (jp, 'Farewell, Today') — restore must be non-destructive.

**Strong** · 6 apps · 26 cards · positive in 2 apps · negative in 5 apps

*Why Strong:* 6 apps, same direction (act on it, 96%)

Report 10: 'overwhelm' is the largest UX complaint (1,046 reviews) — an app sold to people with executive-function difficulty accumulated six sequential screens (quote, mood prompt, event cutscene, visitor, chest, claim-confirm-claim) before the checklist. Report 24: an app sold as an ADHD focus aid is described as itself overstimulating ('This app literally GIVES me adhd') — cluttered/overwhelming 1,324 (3.05%, mean 3.068) and confusing navigation 1,507 (3.47%, mean 2.338), rising through the good eras too (1.90% → 4.26%); 46.1% of clutter requests come from 4–5★ users, so a low-stimulus home screen that opens on today's routine with coaching, Discover, Circles and cross-app promotion below the fold is a retention feature; checking off one habit takes 3–5 screens. Report 47: check-in takes 2–4 taps (long-press → record screen → done; a reviewer counts '記録したい項目を選択→＋→完了→＜') and one-tap logging has been requested since 2019 — too many taps 14 (2.38%, mean 2.86: '気軽にチェック入れたいのに何タップもアクションが多くて億劫になる'); the report's E4 is an optional one-tap mode with the memo screen skipped unless long-pressed. Report 48: 'open the app, click a check mark, exit' is what simplicity means to 817 reviewers — see [[C264]]. Report 65 (Rabit): BUG_ONBOARD 22 (mean 1.45, the lowest of any theme with n>10) — recommended installs that never got past the intro ('TODOS OS MEUS AMIGOS ME RECOMENDARAM'), twice as common outside Brazil, i.e. in the expansion audience. (Consolidation after report 90: distinguish [[C306]] — an ad SDK that crashes the app before the first screen renders is a reliability failure, not an attention one; the launch path must be both uninterrupted and unbreakable.)

<a id="c201"></a>
### C201 — A user-set partial-completion threshold — a 'good day' below 100%

**Strong** · 4 apps · 19 cards · positive in 2 apps · negative in 2 apps · tied to a purchase in 1 apps

*Why Strong:* 4 apps, directions mixed (act 9, open 6, free 3)

Report 18: a traffic-light day status that turns green at a user-chosen ~60–80% is the most-articulated praise in a 2,048-review corpus (92 reviews at 4.24★; explicit partial-completion praise at 4.80★): 'with percentage apps you aim for 100 and suffer; here you switch to "green is good enough"'; 'a 60% check feels like 100% achievement'; 'I never feel guilted or pressured'. Rest / postpone / skip options sit alongside it. Some users want it harder (a must-do habit that gates the light, a 90% threshold) — so the threshold is a setting, not a constant. Report 23: a 6-of-8 day rendered as ✗ is named as demotivating and the reason people keep a second app; render a partial ring, not a failure mark. Report 26: partial completion earns nothing (all-or-nothing garden growth, 20 reviews, mean 2.80); ship partial credit as a setting, with full completion still rewarded more — the existing 'no wither' option is the precedent. Report 41: a daily completion percentage ring with partial credit is the quiet differentiator (40, mean 4.67) — 'as someone who suffers from perfectionism and binary thinking… you're never thinking about the cliff edge of losing a streak… made this a thing i actually use and bought over the hundreds of habit apps i browsed'; 'a meh day means about 70%— C work, but a better baseline'; two want weighted habits, one dislikes 'out of 100%'.

<a id="c219"></a>
### C219 — A free cap must be concurrent, never lifetime — deleting a habit frees a slot

**Strong** · 4 apps · 11 cards · positive in 0 apps · negative in 4 apps

*Why Strong:* 4 apps, same direction (act on it, 67%)

Report 20: the 3-habit free cap behaved as a lifetime cap — users who deleted a habit to make room could not add a replacement and the add button routed to the paywall; this turned a pricing decision into a functional dead end and was the mechanic that converted annoyance into uninstalls. Report 31: a minority reported 2 or 4–5 free slots after deleting and re-adding, which the free tier did not always allow. Report 36: archived / completed habits counted against the cap — 'when I went to archive one of my completed habits and tried to make a new one it wouldn't let me … seems like kind of a ripoff'. Report 48: users who deleted a tracker to make room found the slot gone (23, mean 2.22, 'the most damaging variant') — fix #2: restore slots freed by deletion. Report 50: 'unlimited for the first few days' then 'keep only three habits' — the cap applied retroactively to habits already created.

<a id="c030"></a>
### C030 — Sync must work — and prove it

**Contested** · 30 apps · 109 cards · positive in 7 apps · negative in 27 apps · tied to a purchase in 3 apps

*Why Contested:* 30 apps; free vs paid genuinely split — 4 apps' cards say build-free, 6 say build-paid

The paid feature that breaks most; sync failure is ×12.8 over-represented among buyers. Report 13: iCloud sync complaints rose 10× from 2015 to 2021 and ran at 8.9% of 3★ reviews — the fastest-worsening dimension and the defect most likely costing renewals. Report 23: sync is the single largest reliability finding — 348 mentions (4.79%), 223 complaint-framed (3.07%, mean 3.08, 23.3% 1★), only 22 positive; the 2022 migration produced a spike (25 → 60 → 40 → 24 by year) with visible recoveries within weeks and a tail still visible in 2026 — a migration with a long, damaging tail; Germany 10.0%, Spain 10.1%, Sweden 9.7%. Report 25: cross-device sync not updating 14 (1.07%, mean 3.29), flat across eras. Report 27: sync that works but cannot be seen produces data-loss anxiety (4) and sync requests (3 — iPad; 'wish my goals were synced across my devices') in a corpus where the listing says iCloud sync already exists. Report 31: sync / backup / restore fails in 83 reviews ('Manual syncing is so 2010'); real-time iCloud sync across iPhone, iPad and Watch is requested with the iPad layout, concentrated in the 4★ band. Report 33: account-only (Firebase) sync replaced personal iCloud sync ('Original Habitify was able to sync … over personal iCloud. This has been removed'), with repeated logouts; sync failures 119 (3.02%), 7.9% of E4 — offer iCloud sync as an option alongside the account backend. Report 36: private sync is the resolution of the privacy-vs-sync tension — local-only praised ('not harvesting your data') while sync is the top request. Report 41: cross-device iCloud sync with no account is praised by 90 (11.04%) and fails for 13 (1.60%, mean 3.08) — four of them payers, because sync is the promise the app is bought on. Report 43: iCloud is simultaneously the advertised backup, an undismissable error banner ('iCloud Sign in Error - I can't turn off this message'; 'Constant iCloud Error… Sloppy code') and a backup that did not restore for a payer ('lost everything even though it was backed up to iCloud') — 5 reviews, mean 1.40, none after Aug 2022. Report 46: cross-device sync is a paid trigger ('I did upgrade so the data could be shown and updated on my watch') and a failure surface — sync 15 (mean 3.13), Watch and Mac disagreeing with the phone ('I paid a hefty price to sync with all my devices', subscriber 2★). Report 47: December 2019 sync hanging at 0% (7 reviews in 9 days); a crash loop after logging in to the free backup 6 (Feb 2024 – May 2025, log-out the workaround); registration / login failures 8, six of them from mainland China ('好像需要vpn'). Report 48: sync failure is the only reliability theme that never improved — 48 (1.09%, 2.65), flat at 11–13 per era since 2015, now the most common reliability complaint; the 2015 v3.0 sync rewrite shipped with crash-on-launch (29.55% of the era), duplicated trackers (20) and data loss (25). Report 52: sync is iCloud-only and fails across iPhone and iPad (147 reviews, 0.71%); reviewers ask for account-based sync (132). Report 55: partial, silent or 'only half' sync, a buried manual sync button; multi-device users pay for sync, open the iPad and see partial or no data — 'habitbull is a one device app only. And i have paid for pro. Unacceptable'. Report 56: 'the recent update about sync made my habits disappear, is there anyway I can get them back??' — six days after a sync request; F1: a local pre-sync snapshot and a visible restore path. Report 59 (Tappsk): BUG_SYNC 61 (5.71× among purchasers — sync is Premium-only) — 'На iphone не работает синхронизация'; the 2.6.2 release notes lead with 'iCloud sync more reliable'; a paid user lost everything and the account ('все записи удалились и больше не могу авторизоваться'). Report 69 (TheFor): an account system exists but habit data does not follow it — 'i've tried logging on and off and deleting and reinstalling the app but nothing works :/'; 'не могу синхронизировать… iPhone и iPad' (BUG_SYNC 3, mean 3.67). Report 72 (Habit Hearts): iCloud sync with no sign-in — only 3 mention sync, none negatively; 'nobody is fighting with it'. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): 7 say sync does not work, one Korean reviewer says iCloud sync links her devices, the listing claims cross-device restore — 'Determine which is true, then fix the capability or the discoverability'. Report 89 (Check Calendar): 'No login required' and 'stored only on your device' beside a backup that restores across devices — the developer replied in February 2025 that automatic sync between devices is being 'actively' looked into; REQ_SYNC_MULTI_DEVICE 3; every buyer problem in the corpus is a device change.

<a id="c153"></a>
### C153 — Automatic cloud backup on by default — never manual opt-in

**Contested** · 23 apps · 68 cards · positive in 3 apps · negative in 21 apps · tied to a purchase in 2 apps

*Why Contested:* 23 apps; free vs paid genuinely split — 3 apps' cards say build-free, 3 say build-paid

Report 10: progress stored on-device with a manual opt-in backup produced 551 data-loss reviews (9% of all 1★), a family rate that quadrupled in four years, and clinicians publicly withdrawing recommendations; 37 users did not know a backup was required until after the loss. Warn before any destructive path (delete for storage, phone change). Report 20: recovery from a developer-caused wipe was paywalled behind a manual premium iCloud backup; the recommendation is automatic daily local + iCloud snapshots with restore available to free users, and regression tests on the migration path. Report 23: Settings > Manage Data > Backups existed but was repeatedly discovered via support e-mail; several reviewers upgraded their rating on learning it existed — surface backups in the first-run tutorial, not a support reply. Report 27: iCloud sync exists ('seamless iCloud syncing'; the listing confirms) but is not legible — 'if my device gets reset all the data will be gone or I can recover it?'; a user will not reorder habits for fear of losing data; one churned after an update lost all progress; fix: a Settings line 'Backed up to iCloud · last synced <time>' plus an explicit restore path — a communication fix, not an engineering one. Report 29: optional iCloud backup, off by default and account-free, proposed against 9 data-loss reports and 3 sync requests — while one reviewer names 'I didn't even have to list my email' as the deciding factor. Report 34: a local-first no-account app praised for privacy loses data on reinstall and factory reset; optional iCloud sync would keep data off the developer's servers while fixing loss, multi-device use and exit. Report 41: a recoverable migration loss was recovered only by the developer by hand — the report asks for visible backup / restore with a 'last backed up' state. Report 42: no visible backup / restore; 'update → restart → history truncated' recurs across 2020–2026. Report 43: local-only storage with optional iCloud lost users four years of history in July 2026; the report's #1 fix is iCloud backup on by default with a visible restore path and a 'last backed up' time. Report 46: the report's #2 is a per-habit change history with one-tap 'undo last 7 days' and conflict resolution that never deletes a completed mark. Report 47: a free backup exists since Feb 2024 but the 2026 loss shows sync overwriting local history on update and recovery e-mails not arriving — backup is only as good as its restore path. Report 50: no backup or restore capability mentioned anywhere in 205 reviews after two data-loss reports. Report 69 (TheFor): a Pro purchaser: 'you have to back up you data in case your phone get lost … if auto backup option available on pro plan it wound be batter' — B4: automatic backup inside Pro closes the only paid-user request and mitigates reinstall data loss. Report 76 (Way of Life): cloud backup was a premium feature until v4.3.0 (2026) made 'Backup & Restore free for all users' — §8.2 notes that addresses cost, not the default: automatic, silent iCloud backup on by default and a restore check before any update migrates data; REQ_AUTO_BACKUP 12; NEG_BACKUP_MANUAL 13 (2.77★). Report 86 (Today): iCloud Drive / Dropbox backup was manual and paid; BUG_ICLOUD 17 — 'iCloud was clearly on but there was no automatic backup'.

<a id="c308"></a>
### C308 — Logging a lapse must not be the same action as destroying the count — a quit-tracker needs a way to record a slip, and non-judgemental wording around it

**Moderate** · 2 apps · 8 cards · positive in 1 apps · negative in 1 apps

*Why Moderate:* 2 apps

Report 90 (Quit Bad Habits & Addiction): the product's whole mechanism is loss aversion on a big number — 'breaking big numbers hurts far more than the urge to smoke'; 'one reason not to relapse was that all the days would reset' — and reviewers then route around the reset rather than take it: a Ukrainian user logged a slip as a note instead of resetting ('I didn't want one day's slip to wipe two weeks, so I just noted the day'), PRAISE_NOTES_LOG 21 (3.42%, mean 4.90★) is the relapse note with its reason and date ('the ability to write and save the reason when you relapse is wonderful', jp), REQ_RELAPSE_OPTIONS 4 ask for a pause that keeps progress ('you can't pause and keep your progress'), and REQ_MOTIVATION_CONTENT 14 ask for supportive wording — 'show a line saying how many days you could have been clean'; 'a button for почти сорвался (almost relapsed)'. The vocabulary itself is noticed: 'the words refusal, bad habits, relapse are so-so' (REQ_POSITIVE_HABITS 3). This matters most where the audience is at risk — USE_SELF_HARM 13 (mean 4.92★), USE_DRUGS 8, USE_TREATMENT_CONTEXT 3, one keeping the log for a psychiatrist. §8.4 and §8.7: a growth visual that does not wither on relapse, an 'almost relapsed' record, crisis and support resources in the relapse flow for every shipped language, and no ads in that flow. Related: [[C216]] (a forgiving long-run measure beside streaks), [[C157]] (every guilt mechanic optional), [[C016]] (pause without losing history), [[C103]], [[C262]] (recovery actions stay free). Research: Quit Habit Decision.md — 'a relapse must not wipe history' is named as the single most-repeated complaint in the 10,621-review corpus of the leading quit tracker, i.e. the defining failure mode of the whole quit category, and the specified behaviour is to log the slip, keep the record and show best-ever alongside current.

**Reports:** [90](<../App Store Reports/90. Quit Bad Habits & Addiction - Sobriety Counter & Tracker (REPORT).md>), [Quit Habit Decision](<../Research Reports/Quit Habit Decision.md>)

<a id="c306"></a>
### C306 — Third-party ad code never sits on the launch path — the core surface renders first and any ad failure fails open

**Moderate** · 1 apps · 6 cards · positive in 0 apps · negative in 1 apps

*Why Moderate:* 1 app, exceptional magnitude (lift x14; lift x30; mean 0.7★)

Report 90 (Quit Bad Habits & Addiction, 614 reviews, mean 4.40★): release 1.2.0 (2026-07-15) put an ad banner in the launch path and the app became unusable for a week — BUG_CRASH 65 (10.59%, mean 2.23★), 64 of them in the seven days 2026-07-16 → 07-22, 64 of the 69 reviews posted that week, mean 2.41★, 58.0% one- or two-star, and 40 of the corpus's 62 one- and two-star reviews for all time. Reviewers diagnosed it themselves: BUG_CRASH_AD_LOAD 14 ('After recent update the app constantly crashes after the advertisement screen tries to load!'; 'the ad tries to load as soon as I open the app, and it crashes at once') and CRASH_OFFLINE_WORKAROUND 3 ('airplane mode helps'; 'with the internet off it runs stably'); BUG_AFTER_UPDATE 21. For a counter app the crash is not an inconvenience — 'if a relapse happens I won't be able to log it'; one reviewer thought years of statistics and notes were lost; another switched to a competitor. The same crash hit the developer's other app, so the defect travelled with the shared ad integration. §8.1: initialise the ad SDK after the core surface renders, catch and fail open on every ad load error, test release builds with the network on and ads live, stage the rollout and watch crash rates by build for 48 hours. The recovery is the other half of the lesson: 1.2.1 shipped six days later and the wave stopped dead — the 30 reviews after 2026-07-22 contain no crash report and average 4.70★, and the cumulative public rating (4.913★ over 14,806 ratings) barely moved. Related: [[C031]] (crashes and launch failures), [[C188]] (the app must open offline), [[C275]] (an ad that fails to load must never block the core action), [[C156]] (a release needs a crash gate).

**Reports:** [90](<../App Store Reports/90. Quit Bad Habits & Addiction - Sobriety Counter & Tracker (REPORT).md>)

## Part 8 — Things to do and not to do, with the tactics that produced them

Everything around the product rather than in it: listing, pricing presentation, launch, support,
localisation, campaigns and programmes. Tactic cards keep the outcome attached, so this reads as
"what worked for whom", not just "do X".

<a id="c027"></a>
### C027 — Localise early — it unlocks revenue

**Certain** · 66 apps · 262 cards · positive in 24 apps · negative in 42 apps

*Why Certain:* 66 apps, same direction (act on it, 65%), 19 reports label it high-priority

Missing localisation is the biggest market-specific complaint and a stated purchase blocker; shipping a language visibly converts (Japan). Report 10: localisation is HIGH-PRIORITY at country level in eight storefronts at once (cn 26%, ru 18%, tr 19%, br 13%, es 12%); reviewers say they will not pay in English. Report 13: Arabic is the largest unserved language (20.5% of Saudi reviews); users were also served the wrong language ('I am from Turkey but this app language is Korean', 41 votes) and shown store screenshots in languages the app does not have. Report 18: Japanese Instagram ads led to an app that opened in Korean with a KakaoTalk login; Korean push notifications persisted a year after the UI was fixed, the terms page stayed English-only (one reviewer refused to trial for that reason), Traditional Chinese was largely Simplified wording, and a Dutch translation was unintelligible. Report 19: an Instagram ad ran in Spanish for an English-only app — 'tell me if there's a Spanish version and if not, refund the money'. Report 20: Russian-first UI leaked to Chinese, French and Swiss users, Chinese localisation existed and was later removed ('there was Chinese a few years ago'), and Ukrainian was requested and never added. Report 23: bad German localisation ('Die Übersetzung ins Deutsche ist total fehlgeschlagen') undercut the premium price in the corpus's worst large market (mean 3.62); machine-translated Chinese help text drew 52 upvotes and was still cited seven years later; localisation-quality complaints span de, ru, se, kr, cn, tw, jp and es (mixed EN/ES notifications, English-only icon search); a Hangul IME bug went unfixed five years. Report 24: the praise vocabulary (small steps, coaching, art, 'life-changing') appears in every language and the forced-water complaint in six; language requests concentrate in Vietnam, Uzbekistan, Russia, Brazil and Italy; Germany praises the app's craft at 19.61% (3× the corpus); China (1,250 reviews, mean 3.431, 28.6% 1★) is unreadable by an English-anchored classifier. Report 25: localisation demand is new and growing (0% → 1.0% → 2.7%; Turkish 9, Korean 3, Italian 3, Russian/Ukrainian 3, Chinese 2, Japanese 1); Korea and China are 100% 5★ and 75%/50% localisation requests ('If there is Chinese, it will definitely be loved by the Chinese market') — reached only by users tolerant of an English UI; Turkish shipped Jul 2026 and the review stream responded. Report 26: localisation requests in Arabic, Thai and Spanish; Russian localisation quality criticised in 2023 ('hire a competent localiser') and praised by 2025; the German store listing carried a typo ('Gewohnheitstrinker' — habit drinker); Chinese reviewers ask for the community features of a discontinued app ('种子习惯'); the cn aesthetic rate of 3.12% is a classifier artefact. Report 27: localisation is not an issue — zero complaints across seven non-English reviews; the two Monday-week-start requests (DE, AU) are the only regional-convention issue. Report 28: 21 localisation requests/defects (2.56%) — Spanish 5, Turkish 3, Chinese 3, Japanese 2, Russian 2, French, Thai, Arabic, Portuguese; two are defects on an existing localisation (Japanese glyphs rendered for Chinese, habit names truncated; untranslated English with Chinese selected) and a 2022 localisation update rendered every 'r' as a black square; rest-of-world markets rate higher (4.181 vs 3.956) and are 5× more blocked by language (5.56% vs 1.09%) — 'the cheapest lever in the highest-satisfaction segment'; two name language as why they leave. Report 29: the listing supports 8 languages and not Spanish or Russian, yet 8 Spanish-language reviews arrive from UZ/CL/MX/AR/ES/US and one is blocked ('No puedo cambiar la lengua, ayuden me por favor') — Spanish first is the cheapest defensible localisation case. Report 30: 13 languages functioning and one explicit localisation compliment from Chile; an Arabic onboarding blocker; 11 reviews in a language not matching their storefront. Report 31: 61 localisation requests (1.18%) and French and German reviewers say localisation is their purchase condition ('J'achèterai la version premium quand elle sera traduite en français'; didn't buy Pro because there was no German); China is the happiest storefront (4.09) and the loudest localisation demand (23.9% — '无中文无满分', no Chinese, no full marks); Ukraine 26.7%, Russia 13.6%, France 11.3%; recommended: Spanish, Portuguese, Chinese, German, French, Russian. Report 33: localisation grievances are about quality — 「たどたどしい日本語」 (halting Japanese), simplified-Chinese glyphs in Japanese, an offensive German UI string ('Pisst du dabei?'), a lost Russian UI, English-only support replies — 62 reviews (1.57%); Chinese reviewers praise the localisation; Arabic users ask for an Arabic UI; motivational copy read as 'far too American and over the top' in the Netherlands. Report 34: 19 polite localisation requests (none 1★) — Chinese 9, Russian 4, Spanish 2, French 2, Ukrainian 1 — 11 of them arriving in E3, starting the day a free-lifetime promotion reached br, vn, cn and co: promote into a market only once the app speaks its language. Report 36: localisation requests were 7.0% of E1 (six Chinese-market, May–June 2022, plus MX 1★ 'solo esté en inglés me hace perder el interés') and stopped after mid-2022, consistent with localisation shipping. Report 41: shipping Italian and Traditional Chinese (Jun 2026) brought reviewers straight back to rate 5★ ('I ran straight here to give 5 stars'); missing Spanish blocked a purchase ('es por eso que aún no acabo de lanzarme a comprarla'); Russian — requested from five unrelated storefronts — is the largest unserved language; non-English storefronts like the app equally (4.581) but self-report paying at 5.52% vs 9.9%. Report 42: Russian-language support was the original wedge in Russia ('the competitor has no Russian'), and Russia is both the most appreciative and the most defect-exposed market — where users now cannot pay at all. Report 43: all 10 language requests are non-US (4.37% of non-US reviews) — Arabic three times in fourteen months from Saudi Arabia and Oman, each capping the rating at exactly 3★ ('Nice app but it lacks Arabic support, so it deserves ⭐️⭐️⭐️'); Portuguese and Spanish requests appear answered by the listing's five languages; one 'full of spelling mistakes' (GB, 1★). Report 46: the UI reached 15 languages (Catalan praised by name; Turkish requested with 16 votes in 2020 and praised in Turkish by 2022) but the Learn content, videos and e-mails stayed English — 'all the support is in English, which surprised me because the developer is Spanish. If it were in Spanish, I'd consider subscribing' (ES); Arabic and Russian reviewers ask the same; the report: localise content, Spanish first. Report 47: machine-translated UI costs installs in every non-Japanese market — '적절한 한글화가 절실'; notification options rendered as '汽車' and '手冊' ('car' and 'handbook', TW); 'une traduction française faite de façon automatique et de très mauvaise qualité' — installed and deleted; mainland-Chinese terms shown to Taiwan (5 reviews, none Japanese); Korea's share fell from 32 (2020) to 1 (2025). Report 48: Russia (10.13% no-localization, requests 2013–17) and China (12.33%) are the clearest localization signals; a 2022 review celebrates Chinese localization arriving; rest-of-world raises localization four times as often as high-spend markets; the listing reached 10 languages. Report 49: German added May 2025 but 'sprachlich nicht ganz sauber'; the book summaries and meditations stay English-only — 'localise the content, not just the chrome' — requested in DE, KR, JP, ES, BR, PL; Korea reports unnatural translation in 18.2% of its reviews; behaviour-change praise runs 7.69% in Germany vs 18.13% in the US, plausibly a localisation-quality gap. Report 50: Korea — 4 reviews all 5★, two asking for Korean ('Add korean'; a detailed 5★ written in Korean that still cannot use the app in Korean) — the cleanest unmet-demand signal from a small storefront; experiment: localise into Korean. Report 52: incomplete English — notifications, pop-ups and ads still in Chinese on English devices — is the single largest theme in every eligible non-Chinese storefront (us 22.30%, ca 22.95%, au 20.75%; English-primary 22.1% at mean 3.00) and Traditional Chinese is missing in Taiwan (22.89%); unfixed since a 2020 peak; the ADHD / Focus store subtitle reaches a population that cannot read the app. Report 53: machine-translated or mixed-language UI in ru, br, it, se, kr and jp (DES_LOC 19 — 'you need to study more Japanese'; lock-screen reminders alternating Chinese and English). Report 54: habit lessons English-only inside localised UIs ('this software is all in English', CN; 'English texts are not translated', DE); Arabic and full Chinese requested; a German reviewer calls it 'the only habit tracker in German'; outcome language 16.9% in developed markets vs 4.6% elsewhere — 'a behaviour-change tool in developed markets and a cute utility elsewhere'. Report 55: Brazil — several give 4★ 'only because' there is no Portuguese (DES_LOC 8 of 21, 7.7% of br); a Spanish localisation that was available and then removed ('Antes estaba en español y ahora no'); R6: pt-BR first, then Russian. Report 56: the listing claims Korean and Japanese yet 24 of 43 polled storefronts, Japan included, returned zero reviews; non-English reviewers rate 5.000 vs English 4.882. Report 57: Japan is the most price-sensitive and least-localised storefront — 'settings has English and Korean mixed in'; 'I can't understand explanations written in English… the screen is so minimal that [features] aren't self-evident' (1★); incomplete Simplified Chinese (CN). Report 59 (Tappsk): Ukraine is the only storefront where a language request is distinctive — REQ_LANG 8 (7.75×) ask for a Ukrainian interface, which the 17-language listing does not declare (nor Kazakh); Russian is written from 46 storefronts including 59 reviews on the US storefront; BUG_TRANSLATION 7 (a German widget in Russian). Report 60 (Mindway): the paywall complaint appears in 13 storefronts and 6 languages with the same structure and the benefit claims in near-identical words across ten languages — 'Mindway's value proposition translates'; 59 bodies (27.31%) are non-English across 22 storefronts, and 90 of 125 polled storefronts (Japan, Korea, Spain, India, Russia, Indonesia, Philippines) returned zero reviews. Report 65 (Rabit): Spanish requested Dec 2020 ('Solo pediría añadir el español'), also German, Russian and Vietnamese (LOC_REQ 4); a Brazilian storefront user got English onboarding; being in Portuguese with a Brazilian developer is itself valued ('Amoo a pegada brasileirinha do app 😍 me sinto em casa'; DEV_LOCAL 2). Report 67 (Habio): REQ_LANG 41 (2.00%) — the only request at meaningful strength — from the free era onward ('ojalá pronto la pongan en español también'; 'Nur wie kann ich die App auf deutsch umstellen?'); France 13.19%. Report 69 (TheFor): English-only — 'No tiene en idioma español. No entiendo inglés.' (1★, the only 1★ with a cause the developer can remove entirely); 17 reviewers (21.25%) wrote in other languages and used it anyway — simplicity makes it usable without localisation; P3: Spanish, then Portuguese (12.5% of reviews). Report 72 (Habit Hearts): 27 languages including Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Thai and Vietnamese, yet zero written reviews in Japan, Korea, China, India or Turkey — 'the largest gap between what the app is localised for and where it is used'; no localisation complaint across 138 non-English reviews. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): emoji-search keywords stay English under a Japanese locale, raised by a paying customer — 「有料なのですから、対応お願いします」; a shorter home-screen app name requested. Report 75 (Habit Streak): 22 localisations and 24 of 41 non-English reviews, zero localisation complaints; 10 reviews written in English from non-English storefronts. Report 76 (Way of Life): 25 declared languages; REQ_LANG 13 ask for Chinese, Russian, Japanese, Korean, Kazakh, Galician or a working language switch; BUG_LANG 15 translation errors reported in 8 languages; English is the review language of 78 storefronts, Russian is written from 14. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): one request — '希望能增加中文' (cn 5★, 2025-03-02) — and ZH-Hans + ZH-Hant now ship; zero localisation complaints in six languages; 10 localisations ship but Japan, Australia and Taiwan produced no review at all despite a shipped Japanese localisation. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): 16 languages ship, 13 appear in the corpus; a Russian request (5★, 2026-04-24) shipped ~7 weeks later in a 'localized for 10 more countries' release; a UI of icons and grids draws no other language complaints; China produced zero text reviews despite a shipped Simplified Chinese localisation. Report 83 (Roubit): 247 of 500 reviews (49.40%) are non-Korean for an app shipping only English and Korean; Portuguese (26) and Spanish (22) reviews are among the warmest (4.08★, 4.41★) with neither language shipped; Chinese (3) and Vietnamese (1) requests open; §8.7 decide from install data. Report 84 (HabitGrid): release 1.0.9 'Added languages' (2025-10-29) was followed by a 2.7× rise in review rate (2.65 → 7.09 per 30 days) and a new dominant market — zero Russian-language reviews before it, 39 of 73 after, Russia now 43% of reviews and 44% of public ratings, all 5★ ('the best tracker in Russia'); the listing still says English only. Report 85 (Habitica): NEG_LANG 195 (5.66%) is the most-voted complaint in the corpus — four of the six most-voted reviews ask for Turkish (154 votes between them); Korea is a single-issue storefront (40 of 52 reviews, 76.9%, about the missing Korean translation — which exists on Android); the listing declares 18 languages but not Korean or Turkish ('Man, there's even Hebrew but no Turkish'); three problems share the code — no translation at all (Turkish, Korean, Arabic, Vietnamese), translated elsewhere but not on iOS, and broken language switching (screens mix languages or revert to English; BUG_DISPLAY 20 of 63 in cn); §8.3 publish a translation call inside the storefronts asking loudest. Report 86 (Today): Chinese and Japanese localisation shipped Sep 2016 and was immediately criticised ('what the hell is check-in translated as? If you can't translate, add a language option'; the 3D Touch menu and widget untranslated); Traditional Chinese still missing in 2018 and never added (tw 16 reviews); a user posted an iOS Settings walkthrough in a review to force the language; 1,112 reviews (62.3%) are in English but only 595 from the US — 'country-based segmentation and language-based segmentation are different operations'. Report 89 (Check Calendar): 24 listing languages and 12 review languages; the one Arabic request is written in English on the US storefront because Arabic is not shipped; DEF_LOCALISATION 1 — 'app name is in strange japanese characters' (br, 1★, 2022). Report 90 (Quit Bad Habits & Addiction): the store language field says English only while the description claims 70+ languages and 1.2.0's note was 'The app has been translated into more languages'; PRAISE_LOCALISATION 3, including 'Ukrainian is available'; the Ukrainian storefront splits 17 Russian / 13 Ukrainian reviews.
