<a id="c103"></a>
### C103 — Vulnerable users — recovery, mental-health and minors — are a sensitive surface

**Certain** · 33 apps · 75 cards · positive in 18 apps · negative in 18 apps

*Why Certain:* 33 apps, same direction (act on it, 88%), 15 reports label it high-priority

Alcohol, nicotine, self-harm (incl. minors), drugs, EDs, no-contact; monetisation moves land as 'preying on the vulnerable'; age rating is load-bearing. In report 4: 455 kid/teen reviews who cannot pay, and 89 shame / diet-framing reviews in a 4+ app. Report 24: a product marketed to people with executive dysfunction and low income priced as a premium wellness subscription; diet-culture / eating-disorder trigger complaints (61, mean 2.918); depression/anxiety users are 2.89% of the corpus. Report 26: users describing severe depression, being bedbound, three years clean and wartime anxiety ('This app helped me return to life') — the gentle, non-punitive frame is what serves them; children as young as 10 review the app. Report 28: an app rated 4+ with 40 reviews (4.87%) from or about children — 'I'm ten'; 'im nine'; 'I am a 8 years old' — serves untargeted network ads (AI homework-cheating apps, Temu wigs) and a 'watch an ad to double carrots' prompt; a brand and compliance exposure independent of the rating damage. Report 29: 'You're doing a great service to students who cannot afford to spend on applications' — free access matters to students; 4 student/budget reviews at mean 5.00. Report 31: sobriety, medication and mood-disorder trackers were hit by streak resets, removed quit-to-zero goals and upsells interrupting tracking. Report 49: the acquired audience is young and emotionally timed — 12 minors, 'I saw it on insta at 2am and got the 2am motivation to change my life so now I have a year of this app', buyers 'at the lowest point in life' or in severe depression; mental-health-benefit reviews carry the taxonomy's highest mean (4.94). Report 64 (Critique AI): the creator audience is young — 20 reviews (4.77%, mean 1.90) are minors or argue for them (ages 12–15 self-stated; 'everyone on it seems to be like 12-15 years old'), 13 of 20 in the US; a ~$40/yr annual-upfront plan needs a payment instrument they do not control; a parent bought it for a 12-year-old and asked for a refund; the most-upvoted review (9 votes) asks for an adult tier and a free teen tier; research: what share of installs are under 13 — 'a compliance question as much as a pricing one'. Report 65 (Rabit): medication adherence ('não estou mais esquecendo de tomar meus remédios') and depression ('m'aide à surmonter ma dépression seulement je ne reçois aucunes notifications') — for these users a reminder failure is not an inconvenience. Report 67 (Habio): USE_ACCESS 18 name vulnerability (disability, low income, student, mental-health crisis) and USE_MENTAL 40 — 'Shame on the developers for scamming people, like me, who are trying to work on their mental health' (the most-voted review, 16 votes). Report 68 (Ultiself): 'my first week of white knuckling sobriety, I found an ad for this app'; 'Instead of helping me to quit drinking it's making me feel like drinking even more' (OUT_HARM 2) — an addiction ad that sells a generic tracker to someone in early recovery. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): depression, ADHD, anxiety, autonomic disorders and binge eating named with recovery stories (USE_WELLBEING 25, 4.92: 'My depression has eased and I've been able to return to work'; 'day 15 since the stress-driven late-night binge eating I'd suffered for about eight years stopped') — the reason a quiet mode matters. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): medication adherence (5) — a dose titrated every two weeks tracked as 20 / 40 / 100 mg rows ('I've safely reached and held the final dose') — makes the tracker 'a clinical-adjacent record'; locking it behind a paywall is 'a materially different act from locking a feature'. Report 76 (Way of Life): USE_ADDICTION 46 (4.96★, 'Today marks 1 month clean'), USE_MENTAL 27, USE_ADHD 23 — the sobriety and mental-health cohorts rate highest in a 4.62★ corpus. Report 82 (Lasting Change): a mental-wellness-framed product (mood and stress check-ins, meditations, 'Contains Health or Wellness Topics', 'Data Linked to You: Health & Fitness') whose users report sobriety and productivity outcomes (OUT_WELLBEING 7 at 4.71★; 'haven't had alcohol for over 60 days') and whose billing is the most-complained-about in the series; one PRIV_CONCERN. Report 83 (Roubit): U:mental_health_any 68 (13.60%, mean 4.84★) — the highest-rated cohort; two suicidal-crisis disclosures credited to the app; a diary sent to an AI with an advertising-and-analytics privacy label and no review asking where the text goes; minors present (SEG_STUDENT_MINOR 13). Report 85 (Habitica): the mental-health cohort (USE_ADHD 71, USE_MENTAL 51) is both the most enthusiastic and the most exposed — a guild used as a support group was removed in 2023, and a punishment mechanic drove a struggling user out for three years; therapists recommend it to clients. Report 86 (Today): 'I started using this app to get a better grip on my depressive phases, and to sort days when I felt bad out of the streak' (de 5★) — a skip/forgiving state as a mental-health tool; accessibility is an evidence gap (2 mentions in 1,785; text over photos has obvious contrast risk, reported in 2016). Report 88 (GetHabit): USE_MENTAL_NEURO 5 — ADHD, OCD, brain injury, addiction recovery — reached a product that charged $7.99 a week before showing anything. Report 89 (Check Calendar): USE_HEALTH 14 includes insulin, medication and supplements — and PAY_DATA_LOCKED locks exactly those records; a reviewer tracking days 'clean' (2★) lost the app to the wall. Report 90 (Quit Bad Habits & Addiction): U:safety_sensitive 23 (3.75%, mean 4.96★) — USE_SELF_HARM 13 ('with this app I haven't harmed myself for a month'; 'with it I stopped crying and cutting', ua; 12 of the 13 describe holding back), USE_DRUGS 8 (cocaine, injected drugs, Lyrica, weed), USE_TREATMENT_CONTEXT 3 (two rehabs, a relapse log kept for a psychiatrist); the listing describes smoking, alcohol, gambling and nail-biting and never mentions self-harm, the app is rated 9+, and it served gambling ads ([[C307]]) — 'the app is already used for self-harm recovery by reviewers who are likely young; its content, relapse copy and any ads shown to them are a safety question'.

<a id="c104"></a>
### C104 — Never ship a paywall or feature-removal change silently

**Certain** · 32 apps · 76 cards · positive in 1 apps · negative in 27 apps

*Why Certain:* 32 apps, same direction (act on it, 84%), 17 reports label it high-priority

Undisclosed changes and 'it was a bug' replies that don't match what users see destroy trust for a year. Report 11: the store description still discloses no paywall at all (0 mentions of premium/subscription/free/unlock) after the retrofit; a grandfathering rule for pre-2026 users is the recommended fix. Report 20: the Feb 2021 restoration was never announced — '4 stars after premium was restored, but not 5 because the devs ignored us for so long and have not acknowledged the issue' — and the March 2025 wipe drew 'no communication whatever about this disaster.' Report 29: the bandwidth-sharing prompt arrived with no announcement; the report's first fix is 'decide and publicly disclose the web-indexing policy'. Report 30: the 2 → 3 cap change shipped without the listing being updated. Report 31: monthly/yearly frequency, streak display, swipe, quit-to-zero, Shortcuts, the tappable widget, 'last done' and day-start time were removed across v2 (Mar 2022) and v3.0 (27 Jan 2023) — feature removal 9.4% of E4, an update blamed for a regression 8.4%; the legacy Premium stopped being recognised in Apr 2023 with no notice. Report 33: Habitify X (~27 Aug 2020) removed time logs, yearly stats, CSV export, swipe, 'N per week', Shortcuts and the Watch app with 'no migration path' — 149 reviews in nine weeks, 42 UPDATE-. Report 36: the Oct 2023 widget gate was read as a bug for months ('the widget app has not been working properly … says that I have to unlock it') and the 2026 cap as 'extremely bugged. I cannot add a second habit'. Report 43: 'pause a habit' vanished in the 2026 update (2★) and 'every 2/3 weeks' schedules silently became weekly after the redesign (4★). Report 46: dark mode 'moved behind a paywall' in a June 2024 update ('Immediate deletion'). Report 47: the May 2024 changes arrived unannounced and the word reviewers use is 改悪 ('made worse', 23 reviews at mean 1.39); the listing still says 'unlimited task registration' while reviewers report a cap of 6 — the report cannot resolve which is current. Report 48: the 2015 conversion was announced as grandfathering prior purchasers and 14 say it was not honoured ('bait and switch', 'SCAM', 'Rent what you've paid for'); the cap reductions of 2018–20 arrived unannounced and were discovered by users deleting a tracker and finding the slot gone (23, mean 2.22). Report 50: the 5 → 3 cap cut reached users without notice — four say they were not told the terms before installing, and the angriest reviews are from people who lost capacity they already had. Report 55: the June 2018 switch from a $4.99 one-time unlock to $19/yr shipped with a release note that said only 'Changes'. Report 57: none of the tier changes was announced — 'there wasn't even an announcement — what's going on?' — F7: an in-app changelog before the next tier change. Report 59 (Tappsk): the January-2021 update capped the free tier at 20 tasks (reviewers also report 10, 3 and '2 habits, 2 recurring'), removed free habits for some ('раньше можно было использовать две, а теперь НИ ОДНОЙ' — before two, now NONE) and simultaneously stopped recognising existing purchases — MON_FREE_CUT 103 (80 in 2021-01→04), BUG_PURCHASE 57 in the era (its peak), any price objection 10.1% of the era (its peak), churn 2.2% (peak), the lowest era mean after launch (4.50★), the second most-voted review in the corpus (94 votes); the developer's reply ('it is 50') did not match the app ('only 20 are available'). Report 65 (Rabit): three model changes in six years each visible in the era means — free 4.49 → optional premium 4.19 → ads + cap 2.98 → notification outage 2.98; the E2 → E3 drop of 1.21 stars coincides exactly with ads plus the cap. Report 67 (Habio): 'I downloaded this app based on the pinned review that stated it had a free version' — the free tier disappeared in 2022 (hard wall 17.74% of that era) while older reviews still said free. Report 72 (Habit Hearts): all 21 release notes are the identical string 'Bug fixes and performance improvements' — nothing records when the free cap moved from 3 to 1 and back, so users discovered it at the paywall and the only record is the reviews; research: check remote-config history against 2024-12-18 and 2025-02. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): an ad-supported free app converted to a ~1-week trial with no notice around 2025-01-04 — zero grievances in 51 reviews over the prior 2.5 years, then 22 of 37 (59.46%); mean 4.43 → 2.78; 1★ from 1 to 17 in six months; still 22.22% of reviews twenty months later — 'an ongoing tax', not a one-off migration cost. Report 75 (Habit Streak): a free, ad-free app ('For a free app without adds, this is great', 2024-07-28) acquired a paywall by 2024-09-19 ('App payante désormais… dommage qu'elle soit devenue payante', 1★); money complaints went from 0 of 6 pre-paywall to roughly a third of every era since, the last review in the corpus (2026-07-15) being one — 'a steady state, not a spent event'. Report 76 (Way of Life): the 2023 move to a subscription was not dated by any reviewer and the corpus cannot say whether lifetime buyers were migrated automatically — the change arrived as a surprise on the restore path ('it said I had to buy premium again', 1★). Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): no reviewer claims the app used to be free and became paid — the complaint is that the free tier is too thin, not that something was taken away; no paywall-introduction event is visible. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): the widget moved behind the wall and subscription SKUs appeared with zero listing text — MON_UNEXPECTED 2 (2.00★: 'after a while it turns out I have to pay'), MON_BAIT_SWITCH 1 ('Just charge for the download instead of the bait and switch'); two reviewers describe the free tier incompatibly fifteen days apart ('not able to use the app whatsoever for free', 1★ vs 'De momento uso la opción gratuita… súper útil', 5★) — a disclosure problem. Report 84 (HabitGrid): §8.4 — if a charge is ever introduced, announce it in advance and measure the review stream for the first price complaints; the terms already reserve charging while the listing and reviews say free. Report 86 (Today): the Notification-Centre widget was removed in 1.9.55 (2021-09-02) with release notes that said nothing about it — 11 complaints in six languages in three months ('No more widget. Which is the main way i used the app. So, I probably won't keep up to be using it', 1★; 'Give it back'; '还我小组件') — restored two months later with a note ('Thank you for making the widget come back!'); photo covers were moved behind payment taking existing covers with them (2023). Report 89 (Check Calendar): the trial wall was applied to existing free users, not only new installs — the first trial-wall review (2024-01-06) came from someone who had used the app about two months ('2ヶ月ほど使っていましたが'); 2024-Q1 holds 21 reviews, 11 describing the wall, with three reviews on each of 01-06, 01-10 and 01-13 across jp, br and us; mean fell 3.78★ → 2.91★ and paywall share 11.1% → 56.7% between eras; PAY_FEATURE_REVERSAL 7 includes long-time users newly locked out ('Used this app around last year and it worked great, the premium features makes sense like more tabs… But recently… now you need to pay for the WHOLE features'); before 2024 the same app's complaints were freemium-shaped (two calendars free, dark mode moved to paid in 2022).

<a id="c085"></a>
### C085 — Address tracking / privacy visibly

**Certain** · 31 apps · 61 cards · positive in 10 apps · negative in 17 apps · tied to a purchase in 1 apps

*Why Certain:* 31 apps, same direction (act on it, 76%), 7 reports label it high-priority

One unrebutted 1★: 'a whole lotta tracking going on by the developer'. Report 13: a 2017 privacy-policy revision drew 11 reviews in a month; location prompts with no stated purpose ('No, you don't need it') and disclosure-to-law-enforcement language made long-time users delete. Report 24: privacy / personal data complaints 138 (mean 1.225, 87.7% 1★) — a long questionnaire and web billing that collects card data before install. Report 27: a no-data-collection privacy label and no account are praised as features (4, mean 5.00); data monetisation is contradicted by the evidence and the listing. Report 29: 'I also appreciate that there's no subscription fees or ads. Am I trading off data privacy for this?' — users of free apps look for the hidden price; the listing's privacy label did not obviously cover the bandwidth-sharing prompt that followed. Report 34: on-device data with no account praised as privacy (7): 'my data isn't stored on a server!'; 'hasn't been larded with privacy-invading trackers'. Report 36: 'Does what it's meant to do while respecting your privacy and not harvesting your data'; 'the developers don't collect your data'. Report 41: 'This app doesn't hoard your data'; privacy / no account 10 reviews, all 5★. Report 43: 'Great data privacy (no data collected)' is enumerated among purchase reasons; 'I want to support the excellent privacy and pricing policies!' Report 46: 'Completely functional without paying! No ads!' (chronic pain); no ads praised by 10 (4.90); no account needed by 2024. Report 52: untranslated Chinese UI plus a precise-location request led a US reviewer to title the review 'Malware?? DO NOT INSTALL'; 'still using location after uninstall'; a dead privacy-policy link. Report 53: reviewers who read the privacy policy object to Facebook pixel and Firebase SDKs in a health-adjacent app; unexplained Apple ID prompts on launch (PRIV 7, 1.86); R8: publish and minimise third-party analytics. Report 55: premium required an e-mail account or the purchase was lost; cloud storage of goal data questioned; 'no login needed' praised. Report 56: no data collection named as the primary value by an ES reviewer ('No recopila datos') and corroborated by the listing; adding analytics to learn about churn would contradict it. Report 64 (Critique AI): 'don't put your email in this app' — two German reviewers independently, three months apart; refusal to give card or personal details before seeing the product; a photo demanded before the price; German reviews 28.6% scam and 14.3% privacy (n=14) vs 5.01% / 1.19% globally. Report 68 (Ultiself): PRIV_DATA 18 treat the stored card as the risk — 'must delete your credit card after'. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): 'collects no personal data' named as a reason to trust (PR_PRIVACY 4); §8.9 keep no data collection. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): a user objects that cloud backup contradicts the listing's on-device privacy claim. Report 75 (Habit Streak): zero privacy, sync, account or data-loss complaints, consistent with 'stored securely on your device—no sign-ups or cloud storage required'. Report 76 (Way of Life): the same local-only design draws PR_PRIVACY 12 (4.92★, 'Local data, no account') and BUG_DATA_LOSS 38 — privacy praise and data-loss complaints come from one decision; the answer is default backup, not an account. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): zero privacy or data-sharing mentions in 71 reviews across six languages. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): 'PRIVATE BY DESIGN' is a headed section of the listing and 'Data Not Linked to You' the privacy label; PRAISE_NO_TRACKING 3, and three reviews volunteer privacy as the reason they chose the app; zero privacy complaints — 'Private by design is working'. Report 83 (Roubit): one tracking objection in 500 ('the app tracks you', 5★); the privacy label lists advertising and analytics uses and precise location; the diary — with crisis content — is sent to an AI and no review asks where it goes. Report 84 (HabitGrid): 'PRIVACY FOCUSED — No sign-in. No servers. No cloud.' is credited by two reviewers ('only anonymized data collection'; 'doesn't collect huge amounts of data') and questioned by none — but the privacy label lists analytics identifiers/usage/diagnostics, the policy is template text naming IP, approximate location, Amplitude and marketing, and the website offers cloud backup; §8.1 make the four sources agree: 'the risk is to a positioning that two reviewers already credit, not to a current complaint'. Report 86 (Today): the label declares no tracking; PR_PRIVACY 4, PR_NOADS 7, PR_SECURITY 3 vs PRIV_CONCERN 4; 'no ads, no account, on-device data — quiet assets that cost nothing and are named unprompted'. Report 89 (Check Calendar): the listing says 'Your data is stored only on your device. It is never sent to third parties' while the privacy label declares 'Data Used to Track You: Diagnostics', the policy says edited information is sent 'to the analysis service', and the app advertises backup and restore across devices — one reviewer notices ('the description mentions security being top priority… Yet the backup/restore option uses the privacy-invading cloud', 4★, asking for non-cloud export); §8.8 reconcile the statements — 'the risk is to a positioning a reviewer already questions'. Report 90 (Quit Bad Habits & Addiction): the privacy label declares Data Used to Track You (location, identifiers, usage data, diagnostics) and third-party advertising and analytics, in an app where reviewers log self-harm, cocaine, injected drugs and masturbation — and not one of 614 reviews raises privacy, tracking or data use; §8.8 asks how backup or transfer (REQ_BACKUP_SYNC 4) squares with a 'works offline' promise and a tracking label for sensitive habits.

<a id="c058"></a>
### C058 — Discovery runs through social video, Reddit, therapists (US) and Xiaohongshu / Bilibili (CN)

**Certain** · 27 apps · 61 cards · positive in 20 apps · negative in 5 apps · tied to a purchase in 6 apps

*Why Certain:* 27 apps, same direction (act on it, 89%), 10 reports label it high-priority

Plan marketing around where users say they found the app. Report 10: 381 reviews involve a clinician recommending the app; two clinicians publicly withdrew the recommendation over data loss. Report 19 (negative case): paid Instagram/YouTube ads → web quiz → web checkout → a checklist; six reviewers named the channel and the funnel, not the software, generated the corpus. Report 23: therapists and psychologists recommending it to ADHD clients (28, mean 4.50), Atomic Habits and habit literature (14, mean 4.79), podcasts and blogs (Daring Fireball, MacBreak Weekly, Do By Friday, Diary of a CEO; 12, mean ~4.6); Apple editorial / Design Award traffic was the worst channel (17, mean 2.53). Report 24: acquisition runs through Instagram / Facebook / X ads into a web questionnaire; credibility signals (Duke/Stanford framing, Atomic Habits adjacency) and 'the trial produced a result in days' are the conversion stories. Report 25: Instagram / TikTok / Reels ads are a stated acquisition channel for buyers; three arrive via a clinician. Report 31: TikTok / Instagram / YouTube / press named by 117 (mean 1.72), 81 of 98 TikTok mentions in 2022 — the channel that brought the largest audience arrived during a launch crash. Report 34: launched via Reddit (Jul 2018); 6 reviewers (mean 5.00) say they found it via Reddit, social or reviews; early Reddit adopters wrote long, personal reviews to the developer by name. Report 36: an App Store Awards / Apple Design Award feature drove discovery at launch (Jun 2022); a professional coach prescribes the app to clients. Report 55: a Reddit launch post with the developer answering in the thread produced 21 reviews on day two (4.71 for 2015), and BuzzFeed plus a TV review produced 105 in January 2016 (4.77); a Korean rapper's recommendation in 2019–20; therapists and a clinical psychologist recommend it to clients. Report 57: the only AI-discovery attribution in the corpus — 'I found it by asking GPT to recommend an app with the features I wanted' (KR, 2025); Korean word of mouth (24 advocacy). Report 58: founder TikTok is the only named channel — 8 of 91 ('I saw the creator talking about her app on TikTok'; 'thanks to that tik tok girl'), no reviewer names search, friends or ads; single-channel, founder-dependent acquisition that also inflates the mean via audience selection; attribution fell 13.3% → 4.3% between halves. Report 59 (Tappsk): Russian-language acquisition — the founder's vc.ru article (MKT_PRESS 13), bloggers (MKT_BLOGGER 19: 'посмотрел видео у Маргулана'; 'я смотрела тик ток'), word of mouth (MKT_WOM 41), ads only 9. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): new acquisition routes in 2025–26 — a YouTube appearance and an AI assistant's recommendation ('I asked an AI to recommend apps like this and picked from those'); the developer's book appears alongside the app. Report 71 (MyStreaks): a founder-led content channel — a book, a podcast and the founders (Jeff & Jami) — appears in 8 reviews (25.0%), every one 5★, from the first review (Feb 2021) to the last era: 'This concept, the book, and the app have done a 180 in how I see habits'; 'it wasn't until I found this App + Podcast…' — users 'already bought into the method before they open the app'; 'a durable acquisition advantage no habit-tracker competitor can replicate by shipping features'. Report 76 (Way of Life): press and podcasts are the named acquisition source — MKT_PRESS 51 (0.66%, mean 4.94★), 26 in E4 (Tim Ferriss's podcast with Kevin Rose, Ezra Klein), later Atomic Habits, and in ru/kz Margulan Seisembay ('Спасибо Маргулану Сейсембаю'); 6 purchasers cite press ('Used for one day then upgraded to the paid'); coaches and clinicians recommend it to clients (USE_COACH 20, 4.95★); gb 2.20×, au 3.11×. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): seven reviews name YouTube or Reddit as the acquisition channel ('The dev took feedback from me on Reddit and released my requested feature within a couple of weeks'); PRAISE_INDIE 9 (5.00★) with no entry after 2025-02-28 and CH_YOUTUBE none after 2025-11-25 — 'the early corpus is full of people who followed a developer; the recent corpus is full of people who found an app'; §8.4.4 rebuild the acquisition story or accept a harsher audience. Report 82 (Lasting Change): the funnel is Instagram → quiz → personalised-book checkout with a forced app bundle; every documented path to payment runs through the book, none through the app; U:acquisition_any 12 (6.86%, 1.33★). Report 84 (HabitGrid): the only acquisition channel named in 86 reviews is an LLM — 'GPT suggested I look at this app' (ru 5★) — plus one App Store search; no ad, article or social post is named; the developer runs Discord, Reddit, TikTok, Instagram, X and LinkedIn and none surfaces in a review. Report 85 (Habitica): therapists, a psychotherapist, a life coach and an autism/ADHD support worker recommend it to clients (SEG_PRO 16, 13 in the US); an AI assistant is a new acquisition route ('I asked ChatGPT for ideas on making my life more like a video game—enter Habitica', 5★, 2025).

<a id="c212"></a>
### C212 — No conditional refunds — no proof-of-use requirement, and an advertised guarantee is honoured on request

**Certain** · 26 apps · 77 cards · positive in 2 apps · negative in 23 apps

*Why Certain:* 26 apps, same direction (act on it, 90%), 10 reports label it high-priority

Report 19: refunds were refused for 25 of 105 (23.81%); a 'prove 14 consecutive days of use' condition (6), a 30-day money-back guarantee that was advertised and then denied (3 — all three bought because of it), and retention bots answering refund requests (5) turned refusal into fraud allegations, chargebacks and an FTC report. A guarantee you will not honour is a fraud allegation you have pre-purchased; the refund is cheaper than the dispute. Report 24: refund refusals (968, 2.23%, mean 1.070) quote near-verbatim T&C clauses across years and markets — 'the set-up fee for the trial period is non-refundable' and 'unless cancelled at least 24 hours before the renewal date'; 227 reviewers hold an e-mail or screenshot confirming cancellation and were charged anyway. When a refund is actually reached it works and reviewers upgrade in place (1★ → 4★), so the failure is reaching it. Report 30: 'quise cancelar suscripción… no puedo recuperar el dinero' — a refund dead end for an accidental subscription. Report 33: refunds routed to Apple, then refused — a child's 598 RMB refused twice; 45 refund reviews (mean 2.16), 13 from Korea. Report 43: a refund refused inside the EU 14-day withdrawal period (DE, 1★). Report 48: refund requests 23 at mean 1.04★ — the lowest-mean theme in the corpus with n > 10. Report 49: a marketed '66-day money-back guarantee' cited 13 times (1.85) with undisclosed conditions (66 logged days at ≥ 50% completion — 'Very misleading'), met conditions and no refund, a confirmed PayPal transfer that never arrived, 'nowhere to be found'; 21 of 36 refund requests refused or ignored (1.14) — 'a marketing promise generating one-star reviews at a higher rate than having no promise would'. Report 54: every refund request (5, all 1★) was caused by a failed entitlement, not dissatisfaction with the feature set. Report 55: refund requests 19 (1.11), 17 from payers, 9 from the UK. Report 59 (Tappsk): MON_REFUND 159 (1.05%, 1.94★) — refunds reported granted ('Все вернули! Оперативно') and refused ('техподдержка не видит причины возврата' — support sees no reason for a refund; 'I was rejected to refund of 20$ annual subscription'). Report 60 (Mindway): four refund requests, all 1★, all US, all after an annual charge — refused ('NO EXCEPTIONS OF A REFUND'), no route found, 'this needs to be reported', 'I wish I could get my money back'. Report 64 (Critique AI): a parent bought for a 12-year-old found it too advanced and asked for a refund in a review; 'would not let me have my money back' after a 'cancel anytime' promise. Report 67 (Habio): MON_REFUND_DENIED 242 (11.80%, mean 1.01); an advertised money-back guarantee cited as not honoured by 42 (2.05%) — 'Money back policy requires that you use the product for 21 days consecutively!'; 10 invoke the EU 14-day withdrawal right; refunds granted in 10 (mean 2.80), 3 of them via the bank or PayPal rather than the developer. Report 72 (Habit Hearts): a buyer who trusted the sister apps, disliked this one and was refused a refund (2★); an accidental purchase from a sale pop-up — 'If there's a way to get my money back please let me know😭. I'm to tight for money'. Report 76 (Way of Life): MON_REFUND 9 (0.12%, mean 1.89★) — drivers are a purchase that did not work, an unexpected subscription charge, or a product that did not meet the price ('got my money back', ch 1★); purchaser churn 3 of 349 (0.9%). Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): zero refund and zero cancellation mentions in six languages — 'read as unobserved, not absent'. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): zero refunds, cancellations or renewals reported in 172 reviews; one refund threat resolved by its own later edit. Report 82 (Lasting Change): REFUND_REFUSED 36 (20.57%, every one 1★), 12 shielded by pointing at the T&Cs or asserting the service was delivered ('no refunds as we delivered the service — which is simply not true'; 'they don't issue out refunds unless it's their fault directly'); several asked for a refund on the same day as the charge and were refused; one refund obtained 'after insisting' — and that reviewer was then charged 50€ months later; §8.5 experiment: refund any charge disputed shortly after renewal or after a documented cancellation, and measure the 1★ rate — 'the current policy produces the most-repeated public warning'. Report 88 (GetHabit): BILL_REFUND_REQUEST 64 (13.06%) vs BILL_REFUND_RECEIVED 4 and REFUSED 7 — 'tried to request a refund TWICE from Apple and was denied'; 'I was told I had to pruebe I used the app at least during 7 days'; the terms call fees 'non-refundable'; the two refunded quickly changed their tone ('they issued a full refund in under 24 hours'; 'que ladrones no son', 3★) — §8.4 a no-questions refund for double charges and charges after cancellation.

<a id="c056"></a>
### C056 — Don't build AI features on demand grounds

**Certain** · 23 apps · 33 cards · positive in 7 apps · negative in 9 apps · tied to a purchase in 1 apps

*Why Certain:* 23 apps, same direction (act on it, 62%), 3 reports label it high-priority

0.011% demand; users ask for the opposite. Report 23: exactly one review mentions the 'Break It Down' AI feature (May 2026) — and asks for it to be removed. Report 24: an AI chat/coach bubble added ~2025 is an unwanted addition for long-tenure users, and AI-generated art/copy is the worst-rated non-billing theme (64, mean 1.156, 90.6% 1★) — the theme did not exist before 2024. Report 28: zero of 821 reviews request AI features; the only AI mention is a complaint about AI homework-cheating ads served inside the app — 'no evidence of AI demand in this audience'. Report 33: AI 'smart fill' and AI / chatbot support (2025–26) drew mostly negative reviews — 'Stop shoving AI everywhere'. Report 34: across 743 reviews over eight years, no review mentions AI, ChatGPT or an AI feature. Report 36: exactly one review mentions AI — as a substitute after uninstalling over the cap ('doing it with AI daily tasks until I find an alternative'). Report 41: Apple Intelligence habit suggestions shipped (Sep 2025) drew one light positive ('I like the apple AI to help with ideas'), while 'an AI coach' is on the report's do-not-add list. Report 46: 'I'm really sick of apps with a million features and AI just to convolute things' (Apr 2026, 5★). Report 47 (counter-evidence): an AI coach replying to each check-in is the first premium feature reviewers praise unprompted (13, mean 4.69) — see [[C263]]; the objections are silent stops and a toggle bug, not the feature. Report 64 (Critique AI): the AI is the brand ('AI Coach' in the name) and 'among people who used it, the weakest part' — 19 AI reviews at mean 2.21 vs outcomes 4.92 and gamification 4.00; a paying 5★ splits the product: 'for the AI plan? No. For speaking coaching and challenges to improve overall? Yes'; the substitute named for the AI half is ChatGPT / Grok / Gemini. Report 65 (Rabit): zero AI mentions in 498 reviews spanning 2020–2026 — 'worth knowing before assuming AI features are table stakes in this category'. Report 68 (Ultiself): 'I don't really see where the AI is supposed to be working' — personalisation that feels generic (NEG_AI_POOR 23); PR_AI 20 (15 in E6) against NEG_AI_CONTENT 8 (all E6); §8.7: test a demonstrably personal plan against the library. Report 69 (TheFor): a $2.99 'Routine AI' purchase is listed and zero reviews in 3.5 years mention AI in any form. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): REQ_AI 1 (kr 3★) raises AI features as an expectation — single voice.

<a id="c178"></a>
### C178 — A quiet, adult, non-gamified tracker is a positioning some users actively seek

**Certain** · 23 apps · 62 cards · positive in 23 apps · negative in 3 apps · tied to a purchase in 1 apps

*Why Certain:* 23 apps, same direction (act on it, 70%), 19 reports label it high-priority

Report 11: 'Functional, no frills and no infantilization. I tested half a dozen similar apps before finding this one'; 'I hate apps that demand set times'; 'without any imposed junk' — four of 33 reviewers chose the app for what it refuses to do, and three switched from gamified competitors. A live tension with the pet/mascot category norm. Report 27: two reviewers name the absence of gamification as the reason they chose the app — 'There's not pets to take care of, there's no flashy graphics or anything, and that is just perfect for me'; 'it removes a direct emphasis on urgency and/or self-competition' — and 52 praise minimalism; in a category converging on pets, gardens and streak anxiety, deliberate plainness is a defensible position that any future monetisation must not contradict. Report 28 (counter-evidence): the gamified pet loop is what works here — 'especially having adhd, this gamification works so well for my brain'; one reviewer chose it because it is less feature-heavy than Finch; the plain/gamified split is a positioning choice, not a rule. Report 29: 'Everything that you need, nothing that you don't' — 119 praise simplicity against 3 wanting rewards or more features; do not add features to the main flow. Report 30: 'понятный и удобный интерфейс. Без заморочек' — a minimalist tracker's one proven strength; the thesis works and the packaging fails. Report 31: the simple, colourful adult tracker is loved consistently in every era, and contrasted with Habit-Bull's 'roided-out CrossFit guy'. Report 34: 'Feels like it was made by Apple'; 'Native iOS gem'; 'The whole app just feels calm and clear' — calm native design praised by 156 at 4–5★, gamification requests (5) outnumbered by praise for its absence. Report 41: 'What you will not find here: being told which habit to do. Challenges against other people'; the report's do-not-add list — to-do list, journal, pet, plant, challenges, social feed, AI coach. Report 43: 'not all illustrated with pink & blue kittens and ribbons, have a psychologist's daily thought for the day baked in, nor is it incessantly asking me to note my feelings for the day'; 'you don't have to read a bunch of flowery, condescending you can do it! messages'. Report 46: 'habitica but without the stupid game mechanics'; no gamification praised (3, all 5★). Report 52: SOC_NOSOCIAL 120 (4.85, payer lift ×4.55; 100% mainland) — 'please never add social features, I just want to check in quietly by myself' (48 votes); 'no ads, no noise' praise rose in 2024–26 as reviewers compared the new ad experience. Report 54: 'Unlike some other apps which include too many unnecessary settings, this app has just what you need. No distractions, and no complications'. Report 56: users praise absence — 'no random pop ups—just put your habits in and track them'; 'track their habits without the faff'. Report 58: 'no visual noise'; 'straight to the point of habit tracking'. Report 69 (TheFor): 19 reviewers (23.75%, mean 4.84) tried two to ten trackers first and kept this one — 'a habit-tracker refugee… looking for less product, not more'; P2: market relief from other apps, not 'Transform Your Life'. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): 'It doesn't reward you for streaks, or show you stats, or remind you to do anything. You don't even enter goals into the app. Everything else I tried failed at one of these points… but for what I need it's perfect' — UX_NO_PRESSURE 3 (5.00); simplicity 65 (43.05%) — do not add streaks, goals, nagging or complexity. Report 76 (Way of Life): 'I've possibly tried every habit app, and keep coming back to this one' (the most-voted review, 20 votes); 'I just always end up coming back to the simplicity of Way of Life'; PR_BETTER_THAN 428 (5.51%) is said comparatively; NEG_SIMPLE 43 / NEG_POINTLESS 15 ('I can do the same with a simple tally sheet', 2★) is the accepted price of the position. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): 'Momentum based habit tracking feels way more realistic and helpful… than the streak focus that is everywhere else'; COMP_TRIED_MANY 4 and COMP_BEST 3, all 5.00★ — the highest-intent reviews; 'It doesn't feel stressful, like other apps'. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): 'Others are way too expensive or overly animated and cute. This one strikes a great balance'; PRAISE_NO_GAMIFICATION 2 ('Minimal incentive to follow some arbitrary set of rules to make habits stick, leaving it up to the user instead'); a GitHub-contribution-grid identity (7 mentions at 5.00★, developers self-identify: 'As a SWE'; 'I'm a developer so I can definitely understand the GitHub feel'); U:competitive_win 27 (15.70%, 4.93★): 'Tried them all and this is by far the best'. Report 84 (HabitGrid): 'Nothing superfluous, aesthetic, beautiful, intuitive. What I was looking for!' (ru); 'without extra noise'; OUT_FOUND_IT 15 (17.44%) — the search ended here; ACQ_TRIED_MANY 16. Report 86 (Today): 'No frills, no fuss'; 'It doesn't give you confetti or a cookie but it helps form that path in your brain'; positioned against 'bubbly' rivals; reviewers say it is not a to-do list, calendar or workout tracker — 'Habits are different than to-dos and should be tracked differently'. Report 89 (Check Calendar): a calendar you tick, no streaks, no login, no social — zero streak, Apple Health or Family Sharing mentions in 253 reviews and no social request; PRAISE_NEED_FIT 31 ('Finally a calendar app where you can check off days'; 'I wanted a basic calendar with yes or no to track gym attendance this does exactly what I wanted'). Report 90 (Quit Bad Habits & Addiction): a quiet counter with no account, no social layer, no streak badges and no notifications carries a 4.40★ corpus and 77.52% praise; 'no subscriptions and no extra buttons'; the tree icon is praised as calm ('the idea of the tree as the main icon is simply beautiful').

<a id="c071"></a>
### C071 — Never ship and walk away

**Certain** · 22 apps · 65 cards · positive in 4 apps · negative in 18 apps

*Why Certain:* 22 apps, same direction (act on it, 83%), 12 reports label it high-priority

Abandonment is visible to users within a year; the app becomes an OS-release liability for paying users with no recourse, while the store rating quietly rises on survivorship. Report 8: a ~18-month pause let iOS updates break the create flow, widget and launch, and users publicly asked whether the app was abandoned ('Wrapped 2022' still in settings in 2025). Report 14: a solo-developer app broke at each major iOS transition ('Same thing happened with iOS 13 and it took them a while to fix it'), went five years without an update, and the last thing the corpus records is the product and its checkout failing at once. Report 17: a developer who in early 2022 emailed users personally when their feature shipped had gone silent by 2023 — not an absence of ability but its exhaustion; bug reports at each iOS transition then had nobody to fix them. Report 20: across 92 months no significant new capability shipped — the only material changes were the paywall, a widget that never worked and two data-destroying updates; 'ZERO updates, content, features… NOTHING that justifies a yearly subscription fee.' Report 25: a solo developer's fast turnaround (24-hour fixes) thinned across eras (support praise 3.0% → 0.9%) while a launch blocker survived two release cycles. Report 28: 'incentives stop after level three hundred… makes me assume the developers have taken their hands off the wheel'; the listing's last version is ten months stale. Report 31: after a Dec 2020 sale ('sold from Tree Betty to this new owner') the new operator went silent on support and legacy purchases while escalating monetisation — 'ever since the original designer/developer sold it … it's stopped working'. Report 47: stagnant development 3 ('作者好像不更新了', 2020; '評価が高いアプリなのに1年以上更新がないのも残念', 2023). Report 53: positives vanished before negatives peaked — SUP_GOOD none after Mar 2022, REM_GOOD none after May 2024, WATCH_GOOD 4.3% (2022) → 0% (2026) — while iOS releases broke widgets, Watch app and statistics for a year ('No update to fix issues on iOS 18 for about a year'). Report 54: abandonment 0.9% → 1.4% → 5.0% and support-unresponsive 0 → 0.7% → 4.2% across periods; reviewers escalate from inferring neglect ('after apparently a year since the last update') to reporting a closed channel; a six-year request backlog (widget since Oct 2020, long-range stats since Apr 2020); F6: publish any maintenance signal. Report 55: 'No updates have been issued in over half a year and the developers are no longer answering emails' (2016); no iPhone X layout from Nov 2017 to Dec 2020 (BUG_COMPAT 53); 'The last update was 9 months ago, this is unacceptable for a subscription based product' (2025). Report 57: 'people have been asking about iPad and Mac for years and you always say it's planned — is it ever actually happening?' — 6 told 'planned', never shipped. Report 59 (Tappsk): NEG_DEV_PROMISE 88 rising to 1.1% of the latest era, 4.43× among purchasers — 'there were added zero new features'; 'Два года прошу добавить эту простую фичу' (asking for this simple feature for two years, 1★); 'приложение вообще не меняется годами'; REQ_TIME, REQ_BACKFILL, REQ_PHOTO, REQ_STATS and REQ_SHARED never stop; SUP_NONE also peaks in the latest era (0.8%). Report 60 (Mindway): after a two-month acquisition burst the app produced roughly one review a month for 15 months with two four-month silences, and no reviewer in 750 days reports a problem being resolved (is_edited false on all 216) — the 2026 tail is 28.57% paywall complaints and zero benefit claims. Report 65 (Rabit): in-app copy still said 'start your 2024 year strong' in Feb 2025 and the purchase screen still said 2024 in Sep 2026 ('Poderiam verificar o anúncio de compra que está em 2024?'); 'Tinha tudo pra ser do topo de app de hábitos mas não atualiza' (DEV_STALE 5, all 2025–2026); review volume 120 → 106 → 67 → 30 → 12 per year with the mean not recovering — 'attrition, not repair'; F10: 'the clearest public signal that the app is abandoned' is a trivial string. Report 69 (TheFor): no update for ~9 months (1.4.6, 2025-12-21) while reviews fell 43 → 13 → 4 per year; no reviewer yet calls it abandoned, but 'the corpus can no longer detect a new problem quickly'. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): 2023 is the lowest year since launch (4.56 on 108 reviews), the year tone / notification complaints reached 7 and after the add-on went monthly; 2024 recovered to 4.75. Report 76 (Way of Life): NEG_SLOW_DEV 20 (3.50★) and NEG_DEV_PROMISE 6 (2013 → 2026) — 'Can't wait for the promised weekly/monthly options' (2016) is still unmet in 2026; PR_UPDATE 255 (4.91★, 'updates improve it') is the counter-signal in most eras. Report 86 (Today): the extreme case — 1,030 days between releases (2022-11-09 → 2025-09-04, zero releases in 2023 or 2024), beginning with a build that would not launch; DEV_STALE 67 (3.75%, 20.34% of E5 reviews); users audited the developer ('no update in 2 years… copyright dates only thru 2021… email bounces because the embedded address is toda@neybox.com… Odd because sister app Pillow is working well'); 'the pattern is latency, not absence' — dark mode two years after the request, a time-zone bug fixed six and a half years after the first report, and iPad / home-screen widget / bad-habit tracking / archive / overview never in ten years; 11 releases since Sep 2025 but only 13 reviews to judge by; 'what converts a category-leading app into abandonware'.

<a id="c209"></a>
### C209 — No sign-up wall before first use

**Certain** · 18 apps · 41 cards · positive in 8 apps · negative in 9 apps · tied to a purchase in 1 apps

*Why Certain:* 18 apps, same direction (act on it, 87%), 7 reports label it high-priority

Report 18: 'sign-up / login required or broken' was a very strong signal (70, 3.42%, mean 3.13★); a sign-up wall before any trial was a ranked purchase barrier, and Japan's form demanded e-mail, phone and real name before the product was visible. Distinct from having an account system: the account should be offered when there is something to protect. Report 27: 'no account required' is praised as a feature (4, mean 5.00 — 'so many habit apps are expensive and require an account'; 'All this without asking for my personal details') and the listing's no-data-collection label is part of the positioning; a required account 'rules out ad-funded or data-funded models'. Report 29: 'the fact I didn't even have to list my email sold me' — do not require an account; adding one for billing has its own cost. Report 41: 'No account or login is needed' is a reason to choose the app; one payer cancelled rather than enable iCloud. Report 48: 39 reviews (1.64) objected to a forced account on a local tracker in 2015–18; the complaint ended when iCloud sync replaced the account. Report 50: sign-in required before first use, Apple or Google only (see C035). Report 55: a registration screen first; F6 — never block first use. Report 56: 'I tried a couple of them on the App Store and hated them immediately. They usually ask 20 questions just to get started'; 'no sign-in wall' named as why it stuck. Report 58: §8.5 do not require an account to start. Report 76 (Way of Life): 16 years with no account — PR_PRIVACY 12 'local data, no account'; the cost is data loss on phone change (C034) rather than a sign-up complaint. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): no account, no login wall — zero complaints and one request for an account (as a sync/backup path). Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): no account, no login ('there's no subscription or sign in/up', 5★); PRAISE_NO_ACCOUNT 1; zero forced-account complaints; iCloud sync without an account. Report 82 (Lasting Change): the web purchase and the app account are two systems that disagree about who the customer is (DEF_LOGIN 14) — an account is required and it is the reliability failure. Report 85 (Habitica): an account is mandatory and sign-up is the harshest failure in the corpus (BUG_SIGNUP 139 at 1.55★); NEG_FB_LOGIN 18 when the rebuilt app launched without Facebook login. Report 86 (Today): no account, no login, no server sync for ten years — praised ('no account') and blamed in equal measure; REQ_ACCOUNT 3 arrive only from users who lost data; §8.4 'optional account-based sync — not mandatory'. Report 88 (GetHabit): no account or sync (NO_ACCOUNT_SYNC 9) — 'cannot login without having to pay full payment again' (sg); web buyers could not link their purchase to the app; one would pay for 'cross device syncing'.

**Reports:** [18](<../App Store Reports/18. MyRoutine - Organize your day - Built around your real life (REPORT).md>), [27](<../App Store Reports/27. <a id="c150"></a>
### C150 — Never ask for a rating before the user has used the app

**Certain** · 17 apps · 42 cards · positive in 2 apps · negative in 12 apps

*Why Certain:* 17 apps, same direction (act on it, 91%), 4 reports label it high-priority

Report 9 put the rating prompt inside sign-up: users were asked for 5★ before seeing the app, the public rating ran 1.35 stars above written reviews, and Apple's guidelines forbid it. Report 12: an in-app instruction to rate 5★ during onboarding — 'It said I had to give them 5 starts so here I am' — was called out by 23 reviewers, two of whom named the exact 4.8 store aggregate; 14 of 77 five-star reviews contradict their own rating. Report 25: eight reviewers say the app asked for a review before they had used it, and one says it would not proceed without a review — if that gate existed, the 5★ share is not a satisfaction measurement for that period. Report 28: 'Every time I checked something off it would ask me to rate it' (5★, asking it to stop) — a prompt fired on the completion tap. Report 29: 'It asks for you to review it the moment you check one thing off' — ratings from people who have not yet used the app. Report 33: prompts 'three in 10 seconds' in 2017–18. Report 43: rating prompts 'every time I open this app' and 'every 2 minutes'. Report 46: 'It's asking whether I like the app just as I downloaded it!'; 'every other time I marked a habit as complete the app popped up a window asking me to rate it'. Report 50: see C094 — a prompt during the intro produces 1★ from users with no opinion. Report 59 (Tappsk): 'Хватит меня каждую секунду просить оставить отзыв' (stop asking me every second to leave a review, 1★) — cadence, not just timing. Report 60 (Mindway): 'Good but forcing me to rate😅🙄 / ITS FORCING MEE' (5★); 28 reviews (12.96%) say the reviewer has only just started ('I'm ready / I'm excited'; 'Just getting started, figuring it out!'; 'Lo voy descargando y ya me esta gustando') — 20 of the 128 5★; two 1★ with neutral text ('To soon to say'; 'Not sure about app yet') look like users rating the experience of being asked to rate; D6: stop harvesting ratings from users who have not used the app — a prompt after a routine completed on the fifth consecutive day would produce fewer, better, more durable reviews (E5). Report 64 (Critique AI): 'it got me to rate it before it charged me money so I gave it a 5 thinking that it was free because I am 13 and broke' — the likely mechanism behind a −2.09-star gap (written 2.589 on 419 vs public 4.68 on 18,785, ≥ 1.84 in every storefront), with 57 reviews (13.60%, mean 4.54) rated without product experience; research: does the prompt fire before the paywall — 'it changes how every dashboard in the business should be read'. Report 76 (Way of Life): 'app solicited a review 3 days in, after I paid for the premium version' (4★) — prompting right after a purchase reads as a second ask. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): never re-prompt someone who has already rated — 'i already rated this highly, but now I keep getting the review prompt' (1★). Report 89 (Check Calendar): a review prompt that may fire inside the trial produces a 4.676★ public rating for an app whose written reviews are 42% paywall complaints — §8.7 research whether it fires before the wall.

<a id="c057"></a>
### C057 — Offer a non-pastel / premium design option

**Certain** · 16 apps · 30 cards · positive in 8 apps · negative in 6 apps · tied to a purchase in 1 apps

*Why Certain:* 16 apps, same direction (act on it, 62%), 4 reports label it high-priority

Recurring critique from men and users wanting a premium look. Report 25: native Apple design language reads as premium — ''Apple' design all over it'. Report 26: reviewers convert on beauty within minutes of install ('I bought premium within the first couple minutes of downloading'; 'as soon as I saw the visuals and music I bought premium') — aesthetic is the mechanism, not decoration, and 'It's not just an app it's a piece of art'. Report 29: UI/visual design praised by 45 (12.30%, mean 4.64); a font complaint (1); more colours / custom colours requested (4). Report 48: 62 call the UI dated (3.63, rising to 1.68% of E5) while 14 praise its plainness ('does not include "cute" graphics') — the report: do not redesign for novelty; the tap-count lesson is the larger risk.

<a id="c060"></a>
### C060 — Cross-sell an app family on brand trust

**Certain** · 16 apps · 31 cards · positive in 9 apps · negative in 9 apps · tied to a purchase in 6 apps

*Why Certain:* 16 apps, same direction (act on it, 79%), 5 reports label it high-priority

Under-used monetization asset. Report 23: Streaks is sold in a bundle with Streaks Workout and HealthFace. Report 24 (counter-evidence): a nine-app family (Clarify, Shape, Elixir, Lumière, Lune, Ambiance, Sphere, Mind, Enchant), each its own download and subscription, is experienced as advertising inside a paid product and as a billing trap; Clarify, the ADHD sister app, is named almost only inside billing complaints (mean 1.637). Cross-sell on brand trust works only while the trust and the billing are clean. Report 28: cross-promotion from the sibling app Study Bunny drove launch (31.8% of 2021 reviews, a beta-forgiving cohort with zero 1★) and still drives a tenth of reviews, but fell to 3.8% by 2026 — the app now acquires on its own store presence, so the rating and the ad policy are commercially decisive; users ask for single sign-on and a shared bunny across the family. Report 31 (counter-evidence): the Growth Bundle cross-sell became the only upgrade path and a post-purchase 'gift' upsell that broke entitlements — 36 bundle complaints (mean 2.03). Report 36: a 5-app 'Not Boring' membership — SUITE+ 34 (mean 4.41; 'I purchased the S2 for the weather app, but Habits is really the star for me'; 4 of 34 payers bought for the suite) vs SUITE- 9 (mean 3.22; 'Theoretically it includes 3 other apps, but this is the only good one … the calculator app … lags'): the weakest app in the bundle drags the perceived value of the price. Report 52: a studio family (布谷布谷, 须臾, 青子记账, 千结) with common cross-purchasers (USER_CROSSAPP 230, 4.57, payer lift ×3.49). Report 53: WaterMinder buyers arrive happy, but 2023–25 reviewers link the developer to the 'Done' app's degraded lifetime upgrades and call the whole portfolio a scam — 'I will be regretfully avoiding this developer because their pricing policies'. Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): 78 reviews (3.41%, 4.90) use or found the developer's other apps — from 2018-06 the sister app 「集中」 ('Focus'); cross-use peaked at 6.7% of 2020–22 reviews; one multi-app user warns 'after a few months, all of them start producing an absurd run of bugs'. Report 72 (Habit Hearts): 'From the makers of Fleur!' — the app family (Fleur, Floret, Nost) appears in 26 reviews (10.40%, 4.88), rising to 14.00% in 2026; 8 came because of a sister app and 3 of 12 payers bought on that trust ('Yo la compré sin apenas usar la versión gratuita… ya que uso desde hace tiempo Floret… y Fleur'); two ask for the next app (a notes app, a book tracker) — 'this audience asks for more products'; the same trust also produced the only refund request. Report 82 (Lasting Change): the counter-case — six sibling apps under one seller share a billing entity, and a charge that shows a sibling's name spends the family's trust: 'Walking Yoga a scam' in a review of a different app. Report 89 (Check Calendar): the same individual developer ships two habit apps (Habit Check Calendar, report 74, and Check Calendar) with the same undisclosed trial — 23.84% and 28.85% trial grievances — and reviewers notice the family (COMP_SAME_DEV_APP 2; REQ_MERGE_APPS 1 asks to merge them); a family repeats its flaw as readily as its trust. Report 90 (Quit Bad Habits & Addiction): DEV_OTHER_APPS 5 (0.81%) — one buyer downloaded 'all your apps', another wants widgets 'across the whole trilogy'; the same July 2026 ad crash hit the developer's good-habits app, so the family shares its defects as well as its goodwill. Research: Quit Habit Decision.md — the limit of the app-family play: a second, generic quit app gains almost no cross-sell because the audiences do not migrate (only 2.4% of quit-tracker reviewers ask for good-habit building), while costing two ASO efforts and two support queues; a second listing is only worth it when it is a genuinely different vertical product ([[C309]]).

<a id="c137"></a>
### C137 — Show the paywall at the moment of need, not on app open

**Certain** · 16 apps · 26 cards · positive in 4 apps · negative in 11 apps · tied to a purchase in 4 apps

*Why Certain:* 16 apps, same direction (act on it, 88%), 3 reports label it high-priority

Surface the upgrade when the user tries the gated action (the third streak, a freeze); an upsell on every launch reads as 'begs me for money' and feeds the greed cluster. Report 13: the paywall fired 3–15 times in the first three minutes while the real purchase trigger was hitting the cap after engagement; the report's experiment: delay the first interstitial until habits are completed on three separate days. Report 25: move the paywall to after first value, not after the onboarding survey — the survey-then-paywall sequence averages 1.17. Report 36: the report recommends never showing the upsell before the first habit is created. Report 55: M2 — show the upsell at the moment a sixth habit is added, not on every launch. Report 60 (Mindway): the counter-case — a paywall shown at the moment of need is fine only if the need is real; here the 'need' is the third task of a routine, so the moment-of-need paywall is the wall itself (19 blocked at 1.63★). Report 70 (Habit / 継続する技術): the purchase moment users choose is a completed 30-day cycle — 22 of 54 purchasers report a streak ('I kept it up for 30 days, so I bought the useless feature'; 'I'll buy the useless feature if I last a month'); §8.7: offer the support prompt there. Report 77 (Streak-Free / Momentumly): the subscription prompt fires repeatedly after the first habit is added — the moment of need becomes the moment of nagging when the cap is one. Research: Feature Gating vs Quantity.md — why capability gates draw less backlash than quantity gates: 'users expect to purchase non-essential extras (custom themes, widgets, advanced stats) once they've already invested time.' The expectation forms after the investment, so the same gate shown at install and shown at month two are different products.

<a id="c181"></a>
### C181 — If the app is paid-only or trial-gated, say so in the subtitle, first screenshot and first screen — a free download that stops after N days is 'paid-only' to the person who hits the wall

**Certain** · 16 apps · 39 cards · positive in 0 apps · negative in 15 apps

*Why Certain:* 16 apps, same direction (act on it, 88%), 6 reports label it high-priority

Report 12: the description already said 'purchase is required to access any content' but the price label read Free — 162 reviewers (40%) wrote a 1★ review having never seen the product. A discovery and framing failure fixable at the top of the funnel. Report 25: ~7 reviewers ask for the app to be paid up front instead of 'fake-free' — an honest paid listing is preferred to a free download that gates at habit four. Report 36: 'It's not free. You can't do more than 1 habit without paying'; 'Si c'est payant mettez le là c'est caché après avoir téléchargé' — DISCLOSE 6, mean 1.67. Report 43: 'If it's a paid app then say so. You can only add 3 items before you have to upgrade' (1★); 16 'deceptive free' reviews (mean 1.25), zero after Oct 2021. Report 46: 'free forever' on the listing and website with a 3-habit tier is the angriest cluster (27, mean 1.85 — 'Potential but FREE FOREVER description is misleading'; 'IS NOT A FREE APP, it just has a free try-it-and-see mode'; 'not a one [screenshot] shows what the free version looks like'); the report's #5: remove 'free forever' and add a screenshot of the free tier. Report 50: a listing that says 5 free habits while users get 3; journal-app sync 'as advertised' that does not work; templates the listing 'promises' — fix F7. Report 59 (Tappsk): 'Пишите сразу, что ПО платное, а не встроенные покупки' — reviewers want the paid nature stated in the listing, not hidden as 'in-app purchases'. Report 60 (Mindway): 'Put the price next to your product in the App Store' — a paywalled app advertised as a free planner produced five misleading-advert reviews and five scam accusations, every one 1★. Report 74 (Habit Check Calendar): a free-download listing on every storefront that enumerates notifications, backup, CSV export and unlimited tabs 'with no statement of a trial, a time limit, or any feature being paid-only' — TRL_NO_DISCLOSURE 23 (15.23%, mean 1.52), 27 of 30 1★ are trial grievances; 14 reviewers write the fix: 'This is a paid app. After the free period ends you need a paid plan to keep using the service'; 'free for one week only, paid after that'; 14 propose selling it as a paid app outright; the most-voted review: 'The listing says in-app purchase, not paid app. It isn't a lie, but I can't see it as anything other than deliberate misleading to grow the user base'; §8.1 #1 state the model — free for N days, then a one-time purchase, price named — in the description and first screen. (Consolidation after report 75: title widened from 'If the app is paid-only, say so in the subtitle and first screenshot' to cover trial-gated apps; the original evidence stays in the statement.) Report 89 (Check Calendar, Naoki Otsu — the same developer as report 74, with the same omission): a free download whose checking stops after 4 days to a month, with no mention of a trial, Premium or a price in the store description captured 2026-09-13 nor in the archived 2024 and 2025 descriptions — PAY_TRIAL_WALL 73 (28.85%), PAY_UNDISCLOSED 27 (10.67%; 26 of them also describe the wall), U:paywall_any 107 (42.29%) explaining 64 of 71 one-star reviews; 'It was very cleanly, organized and easy to use. However, it says nothing about a trial'; 'NOT A SINLGE WORD was said about the need to pay'; 'Secretly paid app' (2026-08); reviewers write the fix themselves — 'If the app was upfront and said in the future, I'd have to pay I would have because I really like the app, but the dishonesty has made me delete the app'; 'if I had been told at the start, I would have paid right away' (jp, 5★); §8.1 put the trial length and the one-time price in the first lines of the description and on the first screen after install, with a visible countdown from day one and a reminder the day before it ends.

<a id="c076"></a>
### C076 — Never seed the launch rating — templated or bought reviews decay and leave the markets they cover unmeasurable

**Certain** · 14 apps · 44 cards · positive in 8 apps · negative in 5 apps

*Why Certain:* 14 apps, same direction (act on it, 77%), 2 reports label it high-priority

Users spot it in week one and say so; it contaminates the analytics baseline permanently. Report 16: a reviewer alleged the beta list was asked to 'overcome outdated reviews'; 23 self-identified beta testers were strongly bimodal and the launch rating was spent within six weeks. Report 19: all eight 5★ reviews in a 441-day corpus landed in one nine-day December window, all US, 44–74 characters, morning-UTC, generic register, one containing a homoglyph ('recọmmend') — the report treats them as unable to bear analytical weight and states every positive figure with and without them. Report 30: two dated phrase-bank campaigns seeded 50% of all reviews; when they stopped the rating fell toward 3.0★ and the organic 1★ rate tripled. Report 30: 83 of 166 reviews (50%) came from a five-phrase list in several languages, all 5★, in two dated campaigns; when they stopped the half-year mean fell 4.65 → 3.00, the organic 1★ rate rose 12.5% → 44.4%, and the US and GB storefronts were left commercially unmeasured (the high-spend group yielded 8 substantive reviews at 3.50 against a 4.79 headline). Report 43: 13 US 5★ reviews within 24 minutes on 10 Oct 2016 ('Use!!', 'Best!!', 'Helful'), three days after the first review — lifted 2016's mean 4.45 → 4.58 and the ten-year mean by 0.02; detected by timestamp clustering, not votes. Report 48: 3 reviews claim fake reviews (1.33); no burst or brigading pattern found — the Jan 2015 spike spans 20 storefronts with unrelated texts. Report 49: 27 reviews invert their stars as a signalling channel ('THIS is actually a one star review. I just wanted you to see it'; 'Gunna remove the one Star as soon as I know you got the message'). Report 60 (Mindway): a 45% two-month burst of very short, very positive, mostly non-English reviews with no duplicated authors or bodies — read as a paid acquisition push plus a first-session rating prompt rather than a farm — is disclosed as 'the single most distorting structural fact in the dataset'; the mean it bought decayed to 3.21 within weeks of the push ending. Report 67 (Habio): SUS_SEED 589 (28.72%, mean 4.91, 2024-03-11 → 2025-02-18) — 94.2% on the US storefront, 33.6% Cyrillic author names vs ~1% elsewhere, 3.1% with any helpfulness vote vs 28.3% of other 4–5★, zero mentions of charges or support; a developer reply pasted into a 5★ body, one paragraph split across three accounts in the same hour, six bodies posted twice by different accounts, referral spam, praise aimed at the complaint ('Cancelled my subscription with no issues at all'), praise for frequent updates while the current build dated from 2024-05-15; they supply 545 of 668 praise codes and coincide with a 4.28 US public rating against a non-seeded mean of 1.31; genuine reviewers cite the gap as proof of fraud ('These scammers pay to have their ratings boosted'); §8.7: stop any programme that sources, incentivises or scripts reviews. Report 68 (Ultiself): E5 (Apr–Sep 2025) holds 2,363 of 4,511 reviews (394 a month vs ~100 either side, mean 4.03 vs 2.23 before) with 230 of 238 generated author names ('nashayla*mogenot@1987qmnp'), 59 of 60 bodies using a look-alike letter 'ọ' to evade duplicate detection, most cross-author duplicate bodies (identical one-liners the same day in Mexico and Uzbekistan) and 1,544 of 1,885 very short 5★; Hebrew, Kazakh, Uzbek, Lithuanian and Latvian reviews almost all E5 one-liners; without E5 the corpus is 41.8% billing complaint and 47.3% praise (mean 3.02) — 'the public rating is not evidence of satisfaction'; earlier, three pairs of long identical US 5★ under different names in 2022-10 → 2023-01. Report 84 (HabitGrid): the soft form — six of the first 13 reviews come from the developer's home region (Romania 4, Hungary 2), two authors carry the developer's surname, none from either storefront appears after month five, and the website's testimonials ('John Harris', 'Maria Smith') match no App Store reviewer; disclosed not adjudicated; excluding the six moves the corpus mean 0.005★; §8.7 'the earliest ratings are the least independent… store rules on reviews from the developer's own circle should be checked, and the website testimonials should be real or removed'.

<a id="c180"></a>
### C180 — No 'wait, don't go' exit discounts or countdown timers on the paywall

**Certain** · 14 apps · 34 cards · positive in 3 apps · negative in 11 apps · tied to a purchase in 3 apps

*Why Certain:* 14 apps, same direction (act on it, 94%), 7 reports label it high-priority

Report 12: a lifetime offer at 17.99 that drops to 5.99 when the user tries to close, a '90% off' timer that still grants no access, and a 10× regional price jump were described as 'gross' and 'another major red flag'; 42 reviewers used the word 'scam'. The ladder is also visible to every prospect as ten SKUs on the store page. Report 13: 'Here's one star for you. You can buy the rest at a 49% discount' — the exit-intent discount tells every full-price buyer they overpaid. Report 19: customers charged $98.50/month and $99 were offered $5 and $49 lifetime plans on cancelling; all three left 1★ and one wrote 'That is probably the real value of the service' — a save-offer at 5% of the charged price converts a pricing objection into a fraud belief. Report 24: the cancellation flow offers progressively lower prices and reviewers publish it as a trick ('keep opting for cancel, you'll eventually get $5/month') — it converts some but establishes that the list price is not the real price. Report 31: countdowns that reset — 111 reviews (2.14%) — '72 hour countdown and reset back to 72 hrs'; 'like the DFS adverts, constantly on sale'; 'ran for months'; 'I'm pretty sure this type of fake sale is actually illegal'; fake urgency backfires in a self-improvement category. Report 59 (Tappsk): 'Предложение куда-то исчезло и желание купить пропало' (the offer vanished somewhere and so did the wish to buy, 2★); 'нажимаю на купит, а кнопка не активная' — time-boxed discounts that disappear lose the sale. Report 64 (Critique AI): an exit-intent 'one-time offer' after dismissing the first paywall — 80% / 75% off, '$2/month' — splits 5×1★ / 3×5★ (PAY_DISCOUNT 9, 2.15%, mean 2.44): it produced the only clean purchase-trigger record in 419 reviews and it reads as 'Preis 80% Rabatt, wenn man Zahlung abbricht. Unglaubwürdig.'; a second paywall 8 (1.91%, mean 1.25); M7: at minimum show the billed total on the discounted offer. Report 82 (Lasting Change): descending-price urgency in the web funnel — ACQ_PRESSURE 4 ('offer at lower and lower prices until you bite'; 'pseudo last time offers'). Report 88 (GetHabit): PAY_COUNTDOWN_OFFER 46 (9.39%) — a half-price lifetime offer on a one-hour timer shown before or right after another purchase; 40 of 46 accepted it and 13 were charged twice ([[C304]]); PAY_UPSELL_NAGS 36 — 'I've seen 4 attempted at making me buy upgrades in the first 1 minute'.

<a id="c026"></a>
### C026 — Handle markets where card payment fails (RU, AR, TR, DZ, PK)

**Certain** · 13 apps · 28 cards · positive in 2 apps · negative in 8 apps · tied to a purchase in 1 apps

*Why Certain:* 13 apps, same direction (act on it, 68%), 2 reports label it high-priority

Users who want to pay cannot; a discount/hardship path doubles as the workaround. Report 26: 16 reviews (mean 4.06 — willing buyers, not complaints) cannot pay — 8 Russian ('the trial button is not clickable… possibly because I live in Russia'; cards cannot be linked), 3 Chinese/Taiwanese ('tap subscribe and nothing happens'; a ¥38 tier shown with no in-app path), 2 Vietnamese (ShopeePay / MoMo requested); Russia is 19.18% of the corpus and its highest-satisfaction market — the highest-yield-per-effort monetisation item. Report 42: 'there's no way to pay from Russia' (Jun 2026) — a market with the worst defect exposure receiving paywall pressure it cannot convert. Report 49: dollar-pegged pricing in Türkiye, sanctions blocking cards, no UPI / local payment method (7). Report 52: 2018 purchase flow broken — 112 billing reviews that year, including no Alipay or WeChat Pay. Report 59 (Tappsk): the largest documented case — App Store payment became unavailable to Russian users from 2022-03; MON_PAYMENT_METHOD 74 (72 on the ru storefront, 54 of them 5★ because the reviewers want to pay and ask how — 'не могу оплатить премиум - версию, с кем мне связаться'; 'Вы теряете живые деньги' — you are losing real money); support arranged card or carrier billing case by case within minutes ('в течении 10-20 минут решили'; 'у меня мобильный оператор Megafon') and from 2024 a direct bank-card route is praised ('спасибо, что можно оплачивать напрямую по банковской карте'; 'за возможность альтернативной оплаты подписки для РФ'); the same era brought switchers from Trello and Notion after those services left Russia; the cost is the cancellation gap ([[C210]], [[C112]]). Removing the Russian storefront drops payment-access complaints from 0.7% to 0.0% and billing from 3.2% to 1.4%. Report 72 (Habit Hearts): Apple payment methods blocked from Russia and operator billing stopping in March 2026 made the app unpurchasable there — 'Не показывает цену, выдает ошибку'; 800 ₽ then 1,490 ₽ quoted on two cards, both declined; 'интерфейс красивый, но приложение абсолютно бессмысленно без платной версии'; 5 ru reviews, four in 2026, on the third-largest storefront (any_negative 27.59% vs 14.80%); support granted access case by case; §8.1 #5: fix purchase on ru or route those users to the grant path automatically. Report 76 (Way of Life): the Russian-speaking group (ru + ua + kz, 584 reviews) over-indexes on purchase/restore failures (ru BUG_PURCHASE 3.29×), subscription objections (2.83×) and platform requests (6.5% vs 4.3%) — and thanks the developer most (ru 1.99×, kz 4.06×).

<a id="c054"></a>
### C054 — Never run incentivised / review-for-premium campaigns

**Certain** · 13 apps · 43 cards · positive in 11 apps · negative in 4 apps

*Why Certain:* 13 apps, same direction (act on it, 90%), 4 reports label it high-priority

Bought rank and a fake average, 0.86% purchase signal, reputational backlash, unreadable data. Report 26: a review-for-cosmetic-unlock reward produced reviewers who volunteer they have not used the app; the ≤25-char 5★ tier doubled to ~35% of the corpus. Report 33: review solicitation — a founder-named 5★ burst (12 Oct – 1 Nov 2018: 110 reviews at mean 4.64 vs 3.30 before), 'a strange email … asking for a rating', a free-lifetime link after reviewing, contests awarding Premium, and a CEO asking for 5★ — 'Who the hell is peter?'; the burst left no durable effect and the report's last cheapest win is to stop it. Report 34: a free-lifetime giveaway (~29 Jun 2023) produced 27 short, mostly 5★ reviews in three days (55.6% ≤ 25 characters) and moved the mean by ~0.01. Report 42: six US 5★ reviews in three days (Aug 2020) with 13–30 helpful votes each and nonsense titles ('Hgfgg', 'Bdbdbd'), and eleven of Canada's twelve reviews 5★ generic praise in 13 days (May 2021) — 17 reviews (8.25%) that inflate the mean from 2.968 to 3.136 and leave Canada unmeasurable. Report 43: a launch-week burst of 13 seeded 5★ reviews inside 24 minutes moved a ten-year corpus by 0.02. Report 46: an aggressive in-app rating prompt produced 297 reviews (13.64%) in 44 days in May–June 2023 at mean 4.58 vs 4.29 — permitted by Apple, not fake, but it tripled volume with contentless 5★, diluted every later negative rate and 'made the post-2023 corpus less informative per review'; 17 reviews say they are writing only to make it stop. Report 52: a 2017 review-to-unlock gate (reminders unlocked by writing a review, with a length check) produced 462 unlock reviews, 427 in 2017, all 15 busiest days of nine years, keyboard-mash filler and 5★ reviews reading 'please stop forcing people to write reviews' — the launch year is unusable as a baseline. Report 68 (Ultiself): in 2026 named support agents ('Nick', 'Emma', 'Michael', 'Sam') resolved complaints with refunds and free lifetime access and asked for reviews — 14 of 45 E6 named-agent reviews report a refund or gift ('He canceled my subscription, issued a refund, and even upgraded me to lifetime access'); 'My feedback goes to Michael who asked me to write it'; 'Please post one review per day' inside a 5★; PR_SUPPORT rose from 9 reviews before 2025-10 to 62 of 1,238 after; §8.4: stop asking support contacts for reviews. Report 83 (Roubit): four reviews from January–March 2022 were written during a developer survey or for an in-app 'review-writing mission', and three post invite codes for in-app rewards — U:solicited_signal 7 (1.40%), all 5.00★; kept at the star given. Report 88 (GetHabit): REVIEW_GATE 13 (2.65%) — the app made users rate it before unlocking a challenge, 8 of 13 before they had used it ('it forced me to leave a review to unlock the first habit tracker'; 'writing a review in exchange for trying the app'; 'Just needed to rate to unlock'); the helpful-vote pattern runs backwards (5★ 2.74 votes vs 1★ 0.37; 11 one-line US 5★ with five or more votes); REVIEWS_DISTRUST 11 ('I'm assuming those are paid reviews'; 'I was a fool for trusting the 4.4 star rating'); §8.5 ask for ratings only after a completed streak, never as a condition — 'none of this proves manipulation. It is enough that the 4.355★ public rating should not be used as evidence of satisfaction'.

<a id="c067"></a>
### C067 — Fitness / health tracking use case

**Certain** · 13 apps · 23 cards · positive in 11 apps · negative in 2 apps

*Why Certain:* 13 apps, same direction (act on it, 67%), 7 reports label it high-priority

Very strong US use case. Report 31: health and medical routines praised by 36 (hip-surgery physio, Ménière's, a 95-day medication streak); life outcomes 113 (34 kg, 15 lb). Report 33: life outcomes 205 (on the way to 100 books; out of depression; quitting smoking; 1,000+ gym days); medical / mental-health use 20 (mean 4.70). Report 47: fitness / diet users 24 (4.07%, mean 4.08) are the largest named audience. Report 48: fitness / weight 95 (2.16%, 4.87) is the largest segment — 80 lbs lost, 31 lbs and 26 inches; behaviour-change claims 267 (4.95) rising to 8.18% of 2022–26. Report 60 (Mindway): 'Makes me hydrated makes me work out in a lot'; 'work out, drink more water, make my bed, do good in school, and tidy up my room' — health routines are the concrete outcomes named. Report 64 (Critique AI): fitness outcomes carry the corpus's highest mean (12, 4.92); requests for a calorie tracker beside the food scanner, Apple Health and Hevy sync, exercise animations and bodyweight / muscle-group tracking; outcomes run 5× higher in volume markets (11.4% vs 2.2%). Report 76 (Way of Life): USE_FITNESS 98 (1.26%), USE_HEALTH 71, USE_DIET 56 — 'go from 210 pounds to 164 pounds'; OUT_HEALTH 16 at 5.00★. Report 79 (Ripples / Checker): OUT_USE_CASE 13 — study hours, gym, medication, workouts, strength training, coding lessons, driving-theory mock tests; a general-purpose 'board' fits any of them. Report 88 (GetHabit): a cleaning-checklist ad drew USE_CLEANING 12 (11 in the US) — the advertised use case the app did not contain. Report 89 (Check Calendar): USE_FITNESS 18 (7.11%) — gym attendance, swimming, stretching, strength training; 'I wanted a basic calendar with yes or no to track gym attendance this does exactly what I wanted'; a Japanese buyer paid for a diet habit, reached the goal, and came back for exercise.
